# Townwise client portal and staff console: build spec

Status at merge into `develop` (2026-11-04): the API this spec describes is built in `api/`; `api/README.md` lists what is built and what is not yet. The client screens are not built; their mockups are on the Townwise design canvas, in the three "Client portal" and "Staff console" rows. Branch facts below (`feature/townwise-web`, the `kit-infra` and `portal-api` worktrees, `feature/infra` with MongoDB Atlas) describe the repository before those branches merged; production now runs on Azure DocumentDB (`infra/README.md`). The three source designs this spec cites were working files and are not in the repository.

Original status: spec, 2026-11-04, revised the same day after a critic review (Section 23 lists the changes). Synthesized from the three designs in this folder (`design-security.md`, `design-product.md`, `design-minimal.md`). Nothing in this document is built unless it is marked **Exists**. Spec verbs (“returns”, “refuses”, “shows”) say what the build must do.

Markers:

- `[CONFIRM: …]` is a default the build ships with; the user can change it. Lead defaults say “lead default”.
- `[DECISION NEEDED: …]` has no default; the build shows the honest gap until the user decides.
- On mockups, both render as Placeholder chips (design system), so nobody mistakes them for final copy. Neither ever ships.

Facts marked **Exists** were checked in these files for this spec, not copied from the designs:

- Kit, in the `portal-api` worktree: `api/kit/auth/MODULE.md` (never its Changes from source section); `api/kit/auth/src/create-auth.ts` (`AuthContext`, `revokeAllSessions`, optional `onUserCreated`); `src/middleware.ts` (`authenticatedAt` is `session.createdAt`, and refresh never moves it); `src/totp/factor.ts` (confirming TOTP revokes the user’s other sessions and keeps the current one); `src/sign-in.ts` (`onUserCreated` failures are logged and swallowed); `src/stores/types.ts` (`users.findById`, `users.findByEmail`, `totp.get` with `status` and `enabledAt`; no user listing); `src/routes.ts` (`AUTH_ROUTES`, including `/auth/logout-all` and `/auth/me`); `api/kit/server-core/MODULE.md` (per-router body parsers, CORS allows only `Content-Type` and `Authorization`, request logs keep `url`, query key `q` is redacted); `api/kit/mongo/MODULE.md` and `src/documentDb.ts` (partial filters may not use `$or`, `$not`, `$nor`, `$xor`, `$all`, `$mod`; no collation); `api/kit/rate-limit/MODULE.md`; `compose.yaml` (standalone Mongo, no replica set); `api/src/main.ts`; `api/package.json`; `package-lock.json` (`express` 5.3.0, `mongoose` 9.11.2, `vitest` 5.0.5, `testcontainers` 12.2.1, `@testcontainers/mongodb` 12.2.1 and `@types/express` 5.0.6 are already installed).
- Client: `client/README.md` says the client is `client`. On `feature/townwise-web` (staged in the `kit-infra` worktree, not committed): routes `/` (marketing home), `/about`, `/privacy`, `/security` (the marketing Security page), `/terms`, `/sign-in`, `/totp`, `/dashboard`, `/settings/security`, a Google button that reads “Continue with Google” on web and native, and self-hosted fonts.
- Design: `townwise-ds/project/README.md`, `tokens.json`, and the Nav, AppFrame, Button, StatusTag, FormField, Placeholder, NumbersTable, Toggle and Section READMEs; `ConsoleV2.dc.html`, `SignIn.dc.html`, `Privacy.dc.html`.
- Data: `townwise-home.json` (schema 1, year 2024, generated 2026-11-03): twelve towns with ids `hanover-nh`, `amherst-ma`, `ithaca-ny`, `burlington-vt`, `middlebury-vt`, `state-college-pa`, `bar-harbor-me`, `stowe-vt`, `conway-nh`, `north-elba-ny`, `provincetown-ma`, `nantucket-ma`. Conway, North Elba and Provincetown have one driver and no dates; Nantucket has neither.
- Checked again for the revision: `api/kit/auth/src/stores/types.ts` (`UserStore` has `findById`, `findByEmail`, `findByGoogleSubject`, `create`, `linkGoogleSubject` and `updateEmail`, and no delete; `TotpStore` has `startEnrollment`, `confirmEnrollment({ userId, step, recoveryCodeHashes, now })` and `remove`); `create-auth.ts` (`AuthDeps.now`, `revokeAllSessions`); `src/limits.ts` (`auth:ml-send-ip`, 20 per hour); `src/tokens.ts` (access tokens last 600 seconds); `api/kit/auth/package.json` (exports only `./src/index.ts`; the test helpers in `api/kit/auth/test/helpers/` are not exported); `api/kit/redis` (`RedisHandle.client`); `api/kit/rate-limit/src/limiter.ts` (keys are SHA-256 hashed before storage); `eslint.config.js` (`import-x/no-extraneous-dependencies` with `includeTypes: true` and devDependencies allowed only under `**/test/**`, `**/*.config.{js,ts}` and `tooling/**`; `import-x/no-relative-packages`); the installed `mongodb` driver is 7.7.0 and accepts `monitorCommands` in the connection string. On `feature/townwise-web`: `TownPanel.web.tsx` takes `cardRef` and `onBack`; no DeltaChart, MonthScrubber or NumbersTable component exists; `package.json` has no `react-native-svg`; `towns.ts` is staged, not committed; the privacy, security, terms and home copy quoted in Sections 17 and 22.4. On `feature/infra`: `infra/README.md` plans a MongoDB Atlas M0 cluster with a `readWrite` user on `townwise`.

## 1. Judging the three designs

### 1.1 Scores (1 to 10)

| Criterion | Security-first | Product-first | Minimal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Correctness against the requirements | 8 | 9 | 7 |
| Security | 10 | 7 | 6 |
| Clarity for restaurant owners | 7 | 10 | 7 |
| Simplicity | 4 | 6 | 9 |
| Fit with the kit | 7 | 8 | 6 |
| **Total, of 50** | **36** | **40** | **35** |

**Security-first.** It has the strongest isolation. Invitations are per organization, so adding an email never reveals or blocks anything in another organization. It also has one route table, GET-only view-as and audit written before the effect, and it noticed that server-core redacts the `q` query key. It costs too much for a beta: a hash-chained audit log with a verify endpoint, a Mongoose tenant-guard plugin, ESLint bans, a mirrored view-as namespace, eight limiters, an org Activity log, multi-location upload batches and per-location time zones. Its Overview at `/` collides with the marketing homepage on `feature/townwise-web`. It defers “Continue with Google” as a kit change, but that branch already renders it. Its staff check (“TOTP on, session under 60 minutes”) accepts the session that enrolled TOTP, which passed a code only to enroll, never at sign-in. Removed members land on Request access with no explanation.

**Product-first.** It has the clearest owner path. Approval creates the first location. The Waiting page shows the requester’s town. No access explains rejected, removed and paused separately, and the Forecast tab mirrors the homepage’s four steps. Its routes match the `(gate)` and `(app)` groups on `feature/townwise-web`. It reads the kit precisely: “session created after `enabledAt`” is exactly “this session passed a code”. Its weaknesses:

- It allows one live invitation per email across all organizations. That gives org admins an “unavailable” oracle and lets a hostile org admin squat a stranger’s address.
- It sets a 365-day calibration threshold that the homepage says is still being tested.
- It sums every row per date, which inflates guests on item-level exports.
- Its People page reads the kit’s `users` collection directly.

**Minimal.** It is the smallest build, and it has two ideas worth keeping. It asks whether a row is a day or a check, because item-level exports repeat the check’s guest count on every line. It reports file errors by row and column, never by value. Its weaknesses:

- View-as rides a `?viewAs=` query parameter authorized by any audit row from the last hour, so it is bound to the staff user, not the session.
- Membership is resolved by email on every request, so a Google email change loses access.
- It allows one email per organization, with the same oracle and squatting.
- Home at `/` and staff setup at `/security` both collide with marketing routes.
- An “In progress” tag on the client’s calibration step reads as work on their own model.

### 1.2 Base and grafts

The base is **Product-first**: its flows, pages, copy, routes, access-state model and per-session staff gate.

Grafted from Security-first:

- per-organization invitations with no cross-organization uniqueness, and a chooser when several organizations invited one email;
- change, recount, revert for the last admin;
- author-or-admin note edits, with `canEdit` on each note;
- uploads recorded as `applying`, then `applied`;
- the `q` key for email lookup;
- a 60-minute staff window;
- “Sign out everywhere” for staff;
- a log line per view-as read;
- product denials that are never 401;
- per-route body parsers;
- a branded `OrgScope`;
- a `strict: 'throw'` sales schema.

Grafted from Minimal:

- the day-or-check question and the refusal of item-level exports;
- errors by row and column;
- the `tw_` collection prefix;
- status derived from the data, with no stored calibration record in v1.

New in this synthesis:

- a Leave action and a one-time “Not your team?” notice after an automatic join that names who added the person, and a press-to-join screen for anyone who already has a pending request (the auto-join risk in F1);
- org admins see every Townwise staff action on their organization, view-as included;
- honest calibration states with no day threshold;
- a daily guests chart on the Sales data tab, on web, with a text and table fallback on native (D21);
- a staff-only deletion path for a person or a suspended organization (D22).

Not taken, and why:

- The hash-chained audit, tenant-guard plugin, ESLint import bans and mirrored view-as namespace are strong but heavy. The branded `OrgScope`, one route table, and isolation and view-as tests generated from that table cover the same failures for a beta. They are listed in Deferred.
- Security-first’s audit-before-the-effect for every action. This spec writes only staff actions first, refusing the action if the write fails (9.3, a [CONFIRM]). Client actions keep Product-first’s order: written after the effect, with a failed write logged at error level.
- The `?viewAs=` query parameter is not bound to a session.
- One live invitation per email creates an oracle and allows squatting.
- A 365-day threshold is an input claim the homepage says is untested.
- “Approve into an existing organization” is unnecessary: staff add the requester’s email on that organization instead (F2b).
- Reading the kit’s `users` collection touches a kit internal. The spec uses exact-email lookup through `users.findByEmail` instead.
- A `web_only` rule for staff is unnecessary: a 60-minute window behind TOTP already bounds a native session.
- Per-location time zones and archived locations are not needed: business dates are strings, and deleting an empty location is simpler.

## 2. Decisions at a glance

| # | Decision | Why | Marker |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Three roles: `superadmin` (Townwise staff), `org_admin`, `member`. A staff address never resolves as a member. | Staff manage any organization’s team, name and status from the console, and each of those actions is shown to that organization’s admins (D9). They read sales figures and note text only through audited view-as (D7), or by opening an organization as its admin (D25). | [CONFIRM: lead default, the three roles] |
| D2 | Staff are listed in `TOWNWISE_SUPERADMIN_EMAILS`. Every staff request needs TOTP enabled, a session created after TOTP was enabled, and a session at most 60 minutes old. | The kit cannot check a code per action without a kit change (Section 19). Once TOTP is on, every new session passes a code at sign-in. Confirming TOTP revokes the other sessions and keeps the current one, so “created after `enabledAt`” means “passed a code”. 60 minutes is as close to “every action” as the kit allows. | [CONFIRM: lead default, staff by config and TOTP for every staff action, read as a code at sign-in no more than 60 minutes ago] |
| D3 | An email on an organization’s list joins it automatically, with no click, the first time that person continues with Google. Anyone else lands on Request access. Staff approve, which creates the organization and makes the requester its org admin. One exception: a person who already has a pending request presses Join, and only then is the request withdrawn (F2b). | Lead default. The exception keeps an invitation the person never chose from skipping staff review. | [CONFIRM: lead default, auto-join, request access, approval. Conflict: the critic review recommends a one-click Join screen for every invitation, because auto-join lets an org admin pull a stranger into their organization (F1).] |
| D4 | Invitations are per organization. Two organizations may invite the same email; the person chooses. | No add result depends on another organization, so an org admin learns nothing about other customers and cannot block a stranger. | [CONFIRM: per-organization invitations] |
| D5 | One active organization per person. | A restaurant group is one organization with several locations. One unique index replaces an organization picker. | [CONFIRM: one organization per person] |
| D6 | Approval creates the organization, its first location and the requester’s admin seat. | The owner’s first page already shows their town and the upload step. | [CONFIRM: first location at approval] |

The setup panel’s routes (D23) give staff no read access; D25 does. | One audited exception to “visible only to that client”. | [CONFIRM: staff see values only through view-as] |
| D8 | View-as is bound to the staff session, lasts 30 minutes, needs a reason, refuses every write and every console route, resolves exactly as the target user, gate pages included, and ends when the target’s organization changes. | “Exactly what the client sees.” | [CONFIRM: lead default, read-only, audited, bannered; 30 minutes; any non-staff user as target] |
| D9 | Org admins see every Townwise staff action on their organization: each view-as with the staff email and reason, and every team, name and status change staff make. | Trust around private data. Not requested by the user. | [CONFIRM: show staff activity to org admins, with staff emails] |

The homepage says the history needed is still being tested. | [CONFIRM: lead default, honest states] [DECISION NEEDED: minimum days of history before calibration] |
| D13 | Tuning is structured notes per location: closure, private event, opening, other. An AI chat waits. | Lead default. | [CONFIRM: lead default, notes first, AI chat later] |
| D14 | Townwise sends two emails, each only to the person it concerns and only after the change it reports is written: request received (F2) and you’re in (F3, from the call that seats the requester). They come from `no-reply@townwise.tech` through Azure Communication Services, sent with the API’s managed identity, with Reply-To from `TOWNWISE_EMAIL_REPLY_TO`, no images and tracking off. Invitations, rejections, view-as and every other flow send none. A failed send is logged as a code, with no address, and never blocks, fails or retries the action. Email is on when `EMAIL_ENDPOINT` is set: in production from this release (2026-11-09), whose F2, F3, P3, P4 and C3 copy says so; locally, when `EMAIL_ENDPOINT` is set in `api/.env.local`, it sends through the developer’s `az login` instead of the managed identity. | Owner decision, 2026-11-05. People are held until staff approve, so they need to hear when they’re in. A rejection email waits on an owner question (whether it quotes the staff message). | Decided (owner, 2026-11-05) |
| D15 | An organization has one or more locations. Sales, uploads and notes belong to a location. | Lead default. | [CONFIRM: lead default, per-location data] |

Replacing history is as destructive as deleting it, which is admin-only. | [CONFIRM: member permissions; members add new days only] |
| D17 | No multi-document transactions. Writes are ordered so a retry completes them, and unique indexes catch races. | Local Mongo is standalone (`compose.yaml`), and production DocumentDB sets `retryWrites=false`. | none (a fact) |

| D19 | Product denials are 403 or 404, never 401. | The shell refreshes on any 401 (kit client contract). | none (a kit contract) |

Each setup write is recorded before it takes effect and shown to the organization’s admins once they join (D9), and the uploads it makes read “Townwise staff”, never the staff email. | D30 | Notes in the forecast. From the town's today on, a location's saved notes adjust its published forecast on every read (14.5): a private event with a guest count adds its guests to the day's range, a buyout (a private event, closed, now allowed a guest count) books the day, a closure closes it, and each shows as a reason labeled in code, never from its detail or its title; where a reason comes from a note that has a title (12, D49), the Calendar, Home and TownwiseAI's cards may show the title after the label as the person's own words ("Your private buyout, 70 guests: Holiday party"), never in its place. Runs are never rewritten; past days, `inRange` and live accuracy stay the model's. Notes take optional local hours (12), shown in the reason; there is no hourly forecast. Adjusting on read keeps frozen runs auditable and scorable, and an edit or delete shows everywhere through one function. | [CONFIRM: notes change the forecast from today on, never a past day] [CONFIRM: a buyout books the whole day] [CONFIRM: an event with hours ends by midnight on its own day] [CONFIRM: the Calendar and Home show a published forecast day's middle figure, with its range beside it; TownwiseAI, citations and the TownwiseAI landing keep ranges only] |
| D31 | Business rules. A location keeps a short list of standing facts about how it runs (“Closed Mondays”, “Brunch only on weekends”): at most 30, each one line of 1 to 200 characters, and a rule already saved in another case or spacing is refused (6.24, 10.16). Any member adds one; its author or an org admin edits or deletes it, as with notes. TownwiseAI reads them with every message the person sends: the location's current list goes into the person's stored message as a `business_rules` block whenever it differs from the last list on the conversation's path, and the conversation view never shows the block (`tuning-chat.md` section 3). A rule may carry a schedule, its forecast effect: a note's fields but the detail (kind, effect, weekdays, start and end dates, an optional guest count and hours), checked with a note's rules (12) by the same code, with an end date that may be left empty for no end ("ongoing", for a rule like “Closed Mondays”). The forecast read applies a rule's schedule from the town's today on exactly as it applies a note with those fields (14.5): its closure closes the day, its buyout books it, its private event with a guest count adds its guests, and every other schedule is listed with why it changed nothing; rules and notes on one day all apply (guests add up), except that a note covering the day beats a rule: a note that decides the day (a closure, a buyout, or one that says it is open: an opening, a private event, or more or fewer guests) sets aside every covering rule's closure and buyout (outcome `overridden`), so a one-day opening or party note opens a day a standing closure rule would close. Before the town's today a rule's closure holds only on a day whose guests are missing (no row, no guest count or 0) or under the likely-closed line (D32): real recorded guests beat a standing rule, so the day classes count them and the lab trains on them; closure notes and a rule's buyout keep closing past days. Each covering rule is a reason worded from its schedule (“Your rule: closed on Mondays”), never from its text, at most 6 a day (`moreRules` counts the rest). The lab's input reads a schedule's flags as a note's (10.15), with that same precedence, and its more or fewer guests say a near-empty history day was open (D32). A rule without a schedule is for TownwiseAI only and never changes the forecast, and P29 says which each rule is. The `business_rules` block puts a scheduled rule's summary on its own line, so TownwiseAI knows which rules change the forecast. | D32 | Likely closed. A past day whose guests are under 10% of its weekday's typical guests counts as likely closed: the restaurant was most likely shut, and the guests a staff meal or a stray check, not a very slow day. The typical guests are the median (the mean of the middle two for an even count) over the open days, those with guests above 0, among the 8 same weekdays before the day by date (the 8 weeks before it), so the line scales with the restaurant; with fewer than 3 such days there is none, and only the closed rule applies (a closure note, or an all-zero row). Past means before the town's today: today's row and any later one are never likely closed, since today's upload may be partial. A note covering the day with more guests or fewer guests says it was open, so a slow storm day stays a real day; a closure note (one of kind closure, whatever its effect, or any note whose effect is closed: the forecast's and the lab's `isClosure`) or an all-zero row keeps the day closed, never “likely”. A business rule's schedule (D31) closes the day too, unless a note covering it decides the day, and before today only when the day's guests are missing or under the line; its more or fewer guests say the day was open as a note's do. The rule reads guests only: a day with net sales and no guest count is never likely closed, and one with 0 guests and some net sales is, given typical guests. One pure rule in `api/src/closed-days.ts`, mirrored in `client/src/portal/analytics/days.ts`, both held to the shared `day-classes.json` fixture. The forecast lab never learns from a likely-closed day: the lab input (10.15) marks it closed with no guest count, so the lab neither trains on it nor counts it as a day with guests when it finds closed weekdays and closing holidays. A likely-closed day is closed in every day class: Analytics leaves it out under “Closed days” (P24), and your history by term state (13.2) and Home's usual and past Novembers skip it. The Calendar (P28), Home's This month, its day detail and This week's past years (P11), and Analytics' day panel and heatmap label call it likely closed and keep its count (“Likely closed (1 guest recorded)”), and TownwiseAI's `get_sales_days` and `get_day` mark it `likelyClosed` (`tuning-chat.md` section 4). | Owner decision, 2026-11-12: “if there are no guests on a day maybe that day is closed so we need to factor that in correctly”, after two history days with 1 guest each showed as real, very slow days. | D41 | Reading the ordering setup with TownwiseAI. On Ordering setup (P31), on the web and in the iOS and Android apps, a member (or staff opened as admin; never under view-as) drops or chooses one file (a PDF, an Excel `.xlsx` or Word `.docx` file, a CSV or text file, a file that is text under another name (`.json`, `.md`, `.rtf` or `.xml`, each sent as text), or a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP picture, or an iPhone’s HEIC photo, which the browser turns into a JPEG before it is sent, on the web only) or pastes text, and presses Read. The browser or app sends it once, in the request (`org.orders.setup.read`, 10.17): a file as base64 with the kind its extension names, never its name. The server sends it to Claude Opus 5.5 once, with the saved setup's supplier and item names and nothing else (never a point-of-sale name, the file's name, the organization's or location's name, or an email), a picture without its metadata; a PDF goes byte for byte, so its document properties, which can hold a title or an author's name, go with it. It answers checked suggestions: suppliers with the delivery and order-by days the content gives, and items with name, supplier, category, unit, servings per unit (an estimate marked as one), deal size and point-of-sale names, each marked when its name isn't written in the content's text. Never a par or never run out; email addresses and formatted ten-digit phone numbers are replaced (a seven-digit local number or digits run together are not caught, so the prompt is the main guard), and an item's supplier is one of the suggested suppliers or none. Nothing is stored: no file, no blob, no Your data item, no log of the content. The page merges the suggestions into the unsaved draft through the sheet import's merge, by item name: a new item keeps a blank par, category, unit, servings or supplier blank, so the checks name it at Save; a replaced item keeps its own value for each blank and always its par and never run out; proposed deliveries fill only a supplier with none. Each read is charged to the files AI budget (`TOWNWISE_FILES_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD`, shared with D34 reads and the AI column step, reserved before the call and corrected after it: a call that fails is charged what its stream reported, one the time limit or the person leaving ended before anything streamed keeps its whole reservation, and an API error before the stream is charged nothing) and shares the `ai_reads` limiter; it is off without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or with that budget at 0 (`canReadWithAi` false, and the page shows no section), whether stored files are on or off. The apps choose the file through the system file picker (no drop), check it by its name and size before anything is read, read the picker’s copy in the app’s cache when Read is pressed and delete it once its bytes are read, and refuse a HEIC photo, since the converter is web only (2026-11-18). Unlike the item sales upload (D35), a register export read this way sends its item names and quantities to Anthropic; the section says so before Read, and the privacy page says so. `order.setup_read` and the log lines carry kinds, codes and counts only. The change: `openspec/changes/read-setup-with-townwise-ai/`. | Owner request, 2026-11-15, while looking at P31: “shouldn't the ordering setup support just throwing any data into an agent that extracts the information?”, then “add these”. | D42 | Autonomous forecasts (OpenSpec change `autonomous-forecasts`). Every location of an organization whose forecasts are on (G1; on by default for every organization by the owner’s directive of 2026-11-16) keeps a published forecast reaching 91 days past today, refreshed every week with no person starting anything, for any organization and location: nothing in the code names a town, an organization or a location. The rules are 14.6. (1) A weekly refresh run by a background worker, not a timer in the API: a Container Apps scheduled job, `caj-townwise-forecasts`, runs `api/src/workers/weekly-forecasts.ts` from the API image every hour (one pass, then it exits), and the pass holding the lease on `tw_forecast_schedule` (6.25) starts a calibration (via `scheduled`, role `system`) for each location whose lab input changed since its last meaningful calibration, once a week per location, from 03:00 on Monday in the town’s time zone, recording each start once in `tw_forecast_weeks` (6.26). Scheduled calibrations are paid by Townwise (not charged to the organization’s TownwiseAI month, not counted in its 4 a day), at most 3 live at once and roughly 200 a week. Three ways stop it: `TOWNWISE_WEEKLY_FORECASTS` (on by default, 18), a staff pause in the console (P21) and G1 off for one organization. (2) Two engines in the lab: the trained model, which needs a 595-day span, and a baseline (each weekday’s recent level times last year’s seasonal shape times the location’s own calendar effects, model family `seasonal_baseline`), which a scheduled calibration may run from a 230-day span [Build note, 2026-11-19: a calibration a person starts may too, and the lab, handed the same input whoever started it, picks the same engine: the baseline alone under 595 days; the gate, the charge and the limits are unchanged]. Both are backtested on the same weeks, and the current engine sticks unless the other is at least 0.5 points of weekly WAPE better. The lab input moves to `townwise.lab-input/2`, adding the town calendar’s entries (never a title or URL) and the current engine. (3) One set of publish rules for every calibration, scheduled or started by a person: a same-engine refit against the best recorded backtest in its streak, with 0.5 points of tolerance and ties publishing; each engine’s absolute checks; a draft that moves the next 28 days by more than 25% held for staff; a model run never replaced by a baseline because the model could not run. (4) Runs reach today plus 91 days, capped at 182 days after the last day of sales; the gate keeps judging 28 days ahead. [Build note: D52 amends (4): runs are to reach today plus 365 days, capped at 400 days after the last day of sales, the days after a D42 run’s end being an outlook (release B, 2026-11-19); since release A (2026-11-17) “current”, the streak, refits of unchanged data, the jump guard and live accuracy read only a run’s forecast tier, its first 91 days, so a year-long run lapses and is judged as a 91-day run was (14.6).] (5) Reads of up to 92 days, with the window’s own `accuracy`, each day’s `scored` and each run’s `engine` (14.4, 10.13). (6) Home’s Last week shows the published forecast’s error on days with a guest count and the published forecast on days without one (P11); Home’s “never a guess” becomes “never an unpublished guess”. (7) The reserved `calibrated` and `stale` states are built as derived states (14.3). Built in phase 1 (2026-11-16): this spec and its docs, (5), the engine’s words, `seasonal_baseline` as a model family, and the client and the staff view accepting the new states and fields; everything else lands in later phases of the change, each on by default and inert while the lab runner is off (its `design.md`, decision 15), and is tested end to end before it is pushed. The “agentic rules” half of the request, TownwiseAI suggesting notes and rules from the town calendar each week, is the follow-up change `weekly-forecast-suggestions` (`openspec/changes/weekly-forecast-suggestions/`), which runs on this change’s weekly tick. [Build note: `weekly-forecast-suggestions`, built 2026-11-16 on a branch of its own, not yet merged: the same worker pass, after its calibrations and under the same lease, makes one TownwiseAI call per location a week (from 03:00 on Monday in the town; a location missed then is caught up later that week), with or without the lab, while `TOWNWISE_WEEKLY_SUGGESTIONS` is true (default true, 18) and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, for every location of an active organization whose weekly suggestions are on (`tw_orgs.weeklySuggestions`, absent reading as on; an org admin turns them off, 10.12; G1 does not apply, since a suggestion changes no forecast until a person accepts it). The call has no tools and answers in structured output: it sends the next 91 days of the town’s calendar (titles, dates, kinds, public source URLs, and each holiday’s and town event’s history at the location as a percent and day counts, never a guest count), the location’s notes and scheduled rules covering those days as written, and its earlier suggestions, and never a sales figure, an email, a person’s, organization’s or location’s name, or an id but calendar ids. It reserves $0.30 of the organization’s TownwiseAI month before the call, or the request’s ceiling at the most expensive model’s prices when that is more (skipped, `budget`, when less is left), holds the reservation on the week’s pass row and corrects it to the call’s cost when the row is finished; a row a dead pass left running longer than a lease is resolved by the next pass, which hands its reservation back once. The organization’s switch is read again right before each location, so an org admin’s off stops the locations not yet reached, and the staff pause (P21) pauses the whole worker, weekly suggestions included. A location deleted while its call runs keeps nothing of it. At most 5 suggestions are read, each checked by Section 12’s rules or D31’s and dropped when it starts before tomorrow or after the 91 days or repeats a note, a rule or an earlier suggestion; kept ones are stored open (6.27) and change nothing until an org admin accepts one, which writes the note or rule as that admin with the suggestion’s id. The week’s pass is recorded in `tw_suggestion_passes` (6.28), not on `tw_forecast_weeks`, whose row would stop that week’s calibration retries. | D43 | Home leads with This week’s forecast (OpenSpec change `home-week-forecast`). At a glance’s first tile, with a published forecast that gives at least 5 of This week’s seven days (from today) a figure in the Forecast row, is **This week’s forecast**: those figures added up, each rounded as the row shows it (an open day’s middle, 0 for a closed day, a buyout’s party), so the row adds up to the total. With all seven, it carries the week’s 80% range: the run’s own weekly band from its backtest (`backtest.weeklyRangePct`, the 10th to 90th percentiles of its past weekly errors, 14.4), applied to the estimated part of the total (open days’ figures less the guests notes and rules add), with those guests and buyouts’ parties added as the exact numbers they are, the low rounded down and the high up: daily 80% ranges don’t add (a week of every day’s low almost never happens), and the run’s week rows run Monday to Sunday (14.4, Weeks). With 5 or 6, the total names the days it leaves out and carries no range, since the band is for whole weeks. Then today’s figure and range, the busiest day and the quietest open day (a buyout as the busiest reads as its party, with no “about”), and the same 7 days last year beside it. Otherwise (nothing published, under 5 days with a figure, or a location without guests) the tile is This week, last year, unchanged. A day has no figure when the run doesn’t cover it, when it is booked for a private event that isn’t your buyout with a party, or when your buyout has no party. The Last week tile’s forecast-only words become “No guest counts for these days yet. Upload your sales to see how Townwise’s forecast did.”; it still shows no total over forecast days (D42). The member forecast read already carried each run’s `backtest`; the client now keeps its `weeklyRangePct`. | Owner question, 2026-11-17: “for the home page should I show the number of estimated guests today, this week and last week? what would have the most value?” Claude recommended leading with this week’s forecast, today as a line, and no estimate for last week; offered the run’s Monday-to-Sunday week with its own range, the owner asked “can’t we just sum up a different number of people over the next week and show that because isn’t that more intuitive?”, and chose the seven days from today, added up. | D45 | TownwiseAI turns that outlive their connection (OpenSpec change `resumable-chat-turns`; contract `tuning-chat.md` sections 2, 3, 5 and 7). (1) A turn runs on the server whatever its connection does: once `POST .../chat/turns` (10.12) has passed its checks and holds both live-turn claims, it runs to its end on the replica that took it, and closing the connection no longer aborts it. Every bound holds as before: 150 seconds from the claims, 8 model calls, the monthly budget before every call after the first, 60 turns an hour, one live turn per person and per conversation. (2) Its progress is kept in `tw_chat_turns` (6.29), one record per turn: its state, a 30-second lease the running replica renews, a stop flag, the person’s message and the events its stream sent, numbered from 1, text and thinking joined in batches of at most 200 ms or 4 KB. The conversation is still written once, when the turn finishes, so nothing partial ever reads as a saved turn, and the record never holds the raw API messages, so nothing D28, D36 or D39 elides is kept. A record goes 15 minutes after its turn ends, and with its conversation, location, organization or author. (3) The page reattaches: `GET .../chat` names the person’s running turn at the location, which the page opens on load; the conversation GET reports a running or interrupted turn with the person’s message; and `GET .../chat/:conversationId/turns/:turnId?after=<n>` (limiter `chat_tail`, 300 an hour) replays the events after a number, then follows the record, from either replica. Each event carries its number as the SSE id, so a dropped stream, a refresh, a second tab or a phone back from the background resumes where it stopped and never repeats text. (4) Stop is a request, `POST .../turns/:turnId/stop`, from any of the author’s tabs to either replica; the replica running the turn sees it within about a second, and a stopped turn saves nothing but its cost, as before. (5) A turn whose replica dies or restarts is not continued elsewhere: it ends `interrupted`, the page says “TownwiseAI was interrupted. Your message and this reply weren’t saved. Try again.”, and the person sends again. A replica shutting down refuses new turns (503 `chat_restarting`, “TownwiseAI is restarting. Try again in a moment.”) and settles its own running turns after the drain; a sweep in each replica settles a dead replica’s within about 45 seconds and releases its claims. (6) Server-sent events stay: no websocket, change streams or message broker. | D46 | Suggested closure rules (OpenSpec change `suggest-closure-rules`). TownwiseAI suggests the days a location is regularly closed as business rules (D31), which change nothing until someone on the team confirms them. (1) **From a file.** A file read (D34, 11A.9) also answers `closedPatterns`, at most 5: a closed weekday, the restaurant’s own opening hours for the whole week (the days with no hours are closed), or a closed season, `yearly` only when the file says it recurs; never a meal’s, bar’s or menu section’s hours, days missing from a sales table, or a one-off date, and no words from the file are kept for them. Townwise checks each against the read’s today and builds it into a closure schedule, and the read’s actions store it as an open suggestion (`tw_agent_suggestions`, 6.27, `source: 'file'`) worded by Townwise from the schedule (“Closed on Mondays”, “Closed Jan 1 to Mar 31 every year”). A closure event the read may not write as a note only because it spans over 14 days, and that ends today or later, becomes one too. Undoing the read removes its suggestions still waiting and keeps the rules already confirmed. (2) **From the sales history.** The weekday question (10.12) is replaced by a suggested standing rule, “Closed on {weekday}s”, when 60% of at least 4 counted days of that weekday have no sales and so do its last 4; the rule starts the day after the weekday’s last day with sales, so it never covers a day with recorded sales. It is computed on read and stored only when someone decides it. (3) **Yearly seasons.** A rule’s schedule may carry `season: { repeat: 'yearly', from, to }` (months and days, crossing the new year when `to` is before `from`), which covers those months and days every year from its start until the rule is deleted, wherever a schedule applies (14.5); P29’s form gets an Every year box. Notes never have one. (4) **Deciding.** Any member outside view-as, staff open as admin included, confirms, edits or dismisses one through two new `member` routes (10.12); weekly suggestions stay with org admins. A location keeps one suggestion per closure key in any status, so a dismissed one is never suggested again. At most 5 a read from its patterns, 10 open from files per location, and one per weekday from the sales history; pending ones don’t count toward the 30 rules. They show in P29’s “Suggested by TownwiseAI” group, P25’s Suggested rules, Home’s question count (P11) and P27. Nothing new reaches Anthropic: the sales source calls no model, the file source asks one more question of a file already sent whole, and the weekly pass leaves file and sales suggestions out of its request. On by default, with no env flag. | Owner request, 2026-11-17: “improve the data extraction agent to know when certain days are closed and create those rules automatically so the owner / manager just has to confirm them”, each with “confirm, edit or dismiss”; then “dive in” (keeping the sales history as a source), “sure add seasons” and “update privacy policy etc”. A file’s “Closed Mondays” ended up only as a fact in the read’s summary, a closed season over 14 days was dropped by the read’s guard, answering the weekday question `closed` saved a note over past days only, so nothing closed the next Monday, and a rule could not say “every year”. | Decided (owner, 2026-11-17): the file source, the sales source and seasons. | D50 | Staff can see how a forecast run was trained. In the console’s Forecasts (P21) a run’s model name opens a panel under its location’s table: the code commit and the days it learned from, its method and settings, its backtest and each half-year fold, and, for a model run the forecast lab made, the trees’ loss on training and on held-out days after each boosting round, drawn as two lines and said in words. The model has no epochs: its linear baselines are solved exactly and its trees are fitted in 400 boosting rounds, so a round is the unit. The loss is the mean absolute log residual, a ratio, so the panel keeps D7: percentages, counts, dates, settings and ratios, never a guest figure, and never the scorecard’s weekly series. The lab records the curve from now on, only for model runs (`scorecard.learning`, optional); a seasonal baseline has no rounds, and an imported run or an earlier lab run says no curve was recorded. | D52 | A year of forecast: the outlook (OpenSpec change `forecast-year-outlook`). A published lab run reaches the calibration’s today plus 365 days, capped at 400 days after the last day of sales (the run file’s own limit), in two tiers derived from the run and never stored (`api/src/forecasts/tiers.ts`): its forecast tier ends where a D42 run made that day would have ended, `min(madeAt + 91, dataThrough + 182)`, and every later day is its **outlook**. (1) Days 1 to 91 stay exactly as D42 built them: the lab’s forecast tier and its stops; “current” (the streak, refits of unchanged data) judged by the forecast tier’s end (`forecastThrough`); the jump guard reading only the compared run’s forecast tier; outlook days left out of live accuracy. (2) Outlook ranges: two outlook horizons, 182 and 365 days of lead, interpolated on the square root of lead between them and grown by it past 365; as first decided, a horizon’s band is its own backtest from 26 backtest weeks, the larger of that and square-root-of-lead growth from 8 to 25, the growth alone under 8, with backtest ratios taken per side; as built in release B (2026-11-19, after that rule failed the coverage check, and waiting for the lead’s decision, 22.3), the square-root-of-lead growth always, widened by a band of the engine’s own weekly misses at that lead, read the same on both sides and counted as independent windows, and every outlook week the same on both sides; never narrower with lead; reported in the scorecard’s `horizonOutlook`, never gated. A coverage check on four-year synthetic histories, built to be able to fail, must pass before runs grow. (3) The baseline reads two years back for leads of 358 to 400 days. (4) The trained model’s outlook stops at the town’s last researched term (`termsThrough`); the baseline’s does not. Dartmouth’s winter and spring 2028 terms are researched into the town calendar (13.1). (5) Lab input version 3 (`horizonDays: 400`, `termsThrough`), `LAB_MODEL_VERSION` `v10` (develop’s `v9` became the closed-weekday fix of 2026-11-18). (6) The gate checks the outlook for sanity only: `outlook_too_far`, `widening_out_of_order` and `outlook_past_terms` refuse a result (10.15). (7) Reads keep 92 days and 400 days ahead; the reader chooses each date’s run from run metadata and reads rows only of the runs it chose (14.4). (8) The Calendar, Home and TownwiseAI say “Outlook” for an outlook day, with its range and no “8 in 10” (P11, P25, P28); the model card and the public and privacy copy change once runs reach a year. Weekly suggestions stay at the next 91 days. Two releases: release A (2026-11-17, built) reads, judges and labels year-long runs while every run is still 91 days, so it changes no answer: (1), (6)’s first two checks, (7), (8)’s words but the model card’s and the public ones, and the 2028 terms; release B (2026-11-19) makes runs a year long under a paused weekly schedule (its range rule waits for the lead’s decision, 22.3, and its words for the owner’s), and rolling it back is reverting it. Contract: the change’s `design.md`. | Owner request, 2026-11-17: “also let's increase the forecase to one year out and then forecasts can become more precise as we get more data”. | D53 | Calendar event suggestions (OpenSpec change `calendar-event-suggestions`, built on `weekly-forecast-suggestions`; contract: the change’s `design.md`, decisions 1 to 16, with the Done lines of its `tasks.md` where the build differs). (1) A note remembers the owner-calendar event it came from (6.7, 12). Make a note on the Calendar, or accepting a spotted event, stores `fromEvent` (the calendar’s id, the event’s stored UID, its dates and hours at that moment, and `linkedAt`), read by the server from the event’s stored row and never from the request, and only for a keyed event, one whose key survives a refresh (10.18). An event that is gone or unkeyed leaves the note saved with no link. No title is stored on a note or a suggestion. TownwiseAI chat’s `propose_note` stays unlinked, so the chat’s frozen prefix is untouched. (2) Follow-ups, with no model call (10.18, 6.27, 10.12). After every switch of a calendar’s events (the refresh loop, Refresh now, an add), a note linked to an event that moved gets a `move` suggestion (while the note is still on its link’s dates and hours) and a note whose event went gets a `remove` suggestion (only for an event ending today or later, a note starting after today, a calendar under 2,000 events, and a refresh that kept a source-stated UID of the events it replaced when they had any, so a feed that rewrites its UIDs suggests no deletions). They run whatever the weekly switch, `TOWNWISE_WEEKLY_SUGGESTIONS` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` say, show in TownwiseAI’s panel only (P25) and in Home’s count (P11), and change nothing until an org admin accepts one, by compare-and-set on the note’s `updatedAt` (409 `note_changed` when someone edited the note, or a refresh rewrote the follow-up after the accept read it). (3) Spotted events (10.12; `tuning-chat.md` section 9). The weekly call also sends the location’s keyed owner-calendar events of the next 91 days, titles included, at most 150, soonest first, with every email address and phone number in a title replaced by `[removed]` and never a calendar’s name, kind or id or an event’s UID; a calendar’s events go only when the screen it was added or connected from said so: a file or link holds `titlesNotice: 1` when its add came from the Your calendars popover that shows the weekly sentence, and a Google connection when its connect came from the explainer that does (`WEEKLY_TITLES_NOTICE`), so a stale tab or an older app that never showed the words sends none, and a Google calendar’s go only while its connection is not revoked. It may answer at most 5 `event` suggestions, apart from the pass’s 5 notes and rules, with dates and hours taken from the event and a guest count only when the sent title states that number beside a guest word (40 guests, party of 8, for 12). The card asks an org admin whether the event takes “The whole restaurant (a buyout)” or runs “Alongside regular service”, with neither chosen, and Accept writes a private-event note linked to the event; a spot another note now covers (one linked to the same event, or a private-event or closure note over its days) is hidden and its accept answers 409 `event_changed`. Code drops any private-event note or rule on such a pass, any note or rule citing no town calendar entry the request sent, and any item repeating a word of a sent title (however spelled, cased, split, joined or accented) or holding 7 digits in a row, so no title is stored; a card’s words are written by code and read the title from the live event, which staff read as “Google calendar event” on a Google calendar (D39). (4) Sending titles is on by default (the owner’s rule of 2026-11-16) with an org admin’s switch, `tw_orgs.calendarTitlesToAi` (6.1, 10.12); staff open as admin may turn it off but not on. (5) The privacy page, the Google connect explainer, the file and link add screens (P28), `estimates.md` section 5 and 17 say that titles of owner-calendar events reach Anthropic weekly unless an org admin turns it off; those words await the owner, and titles must not be sent in production before the owner approves them (18). This reverses `weekly-forecast-suggestions`’ non-goal of reading owner calendars (D42’s build note). | Owner request, 2026-11-17: “have an agent to add in events around specific days right? e.g., if we know there is a private event and we need to account for moving that private event or cancelling it and whether not that event is exclusive for the whole restaurant or not”. The owner approved the plan after being told its privacy cost: owner-calendar event titles reach Anthropic once a week with nobody pressing anything. Until now a private event on the owner’s calendar changed a forecast only through a note someone made by hand, and that note kept no tie to its event: when the party moved or was canceled the note stayed where it was and the forecast kept a booked or busier day that no longer existed, and nobody was told. Weekly suggestions read only the town’s calendar, so they could not spot a private party. | D59 | TownwiseAI works on its own: slices 1 to 5 of OpenSpec change `auto-apply-agent-reads` (contract: the change's `design.md`, decisions 1 to 16, with the Done lines of its `tasks.md` where the build differs). (1) **The switch.** `tw_orgs.agentAuto` (absent reads on), turned off or on by an org admin with `PATCH /api/org/agent-auto` (staff open as admin may turn it off only), and the deploy switch `TOWNWISE_AGENT_AUTO` (default true; `false` in `api/production.env` until the owner approves the privacy wording). Both on, TownwiseAI reads each stored file on its own; either off, every flow is as before, except that refits after training changes (7) run whatever the switches say, since they send nothing anywhere. (2) **Automatic reads** (11A.9). A file Townwise finished storing (a reference item kept, or a dropped file read, kept or failed with its original) is queued `auto` for its adder, unless it was read into sales days, is a calendar export, is a summary or item TownwiseAI kept, is turned off, or did not finish with its box checked (`aiAuto: true` on the upload's complete; an upload with no box never sends it). The reader skips one whose bytes a read file of the location shares (`duplicate`), the 21st of a day per organization (`daily_auto_limit`; a retry of a read is not counted against itself), one turned off since it was queued (`turned_off`), and one that would leave $1 or less of the files month (`budget_spent`), before anything is reserved; a press is never held back by them. (3) **One writer and one ledger.** Every change TownwiseAI saves goes through `api/src/agent/apply.ts` into `tw_agent_changes` (6.31), ordered for retries with no transactions: the row `applying` under the planned target id and a dedupe key unique per location in every status, the target, the row `applied`, the audit event. It only adds: a note, a summary item or sales days the location lacks (slice 2: also a calendar file's labels, then its confirm for forecasts, only while every label on it is TownwiseAI's); never another change to or a deletion of anything that exists. (4) **The confidence bar** (11A.9). While the switch is on, a read's event becomes a note only when the model rated the event and the whole read `high`, it passes Section 12's rules and D34's guards, it disagrees with no note or rule a person made on its days, and its key was never used; any other event waits as a note suggestion from the file, decided by any member on P25. A pressed read follows the same bar. An automatic read writes as TownwiseAI and starts no calibration. (5) **Owner beats agent** (14.5): a person's note that decides a day sets aside TownwiseAI's notes on it, in the forecast read and the lab input; a TownwiseAI note a person edited is theirs. (6) **Undo** (10.12): each change shows in TownwiseAI's activity with Undo (any member for a note, the file's adder or an org admin for a summary, an org admin for days; never under view-as), which removes the target only while unchanged since (409 `changed_since` otherwise, the row then `adopted`); a log page lists every change with its why. D34's per-file undo marks the file's rows undone, and an undone change is never made again. (7) **Refits** (14.6), whatever either switch says: a change touching a day on or before the location's last stored sales day, and every sales upload, marks the location; the hourly worker pass refits it as the system after 15 quiet minutes, at most once a day, inside the live and weekly caps, or clears the mark when nothing the lab reads changed. (8) **Privacy** (17, P25, P26): the privacy page, How TownwiseAI works and the Add a file box (checked by default while the switch is on) are reworded, awaiting the owner. (9) **Slice 2: calendars** (10.18). A file calendar imported while both switches and its organization's `calendarTitlesToAi` are on (and not by staff open as admin) is sorted once with no press by the TownwiseAI reader's loop, D58's sort on the TownwiseAI month; its labels (never `unsure`, never over a person's; a calendar someone sorted, labeled or confirmed first, even during the call, is left to them, skipped `already_sorted`) are one `booking.label` change with the calendar's key, confirmed by TownwiseAI (`confirmedBy: 'townwise_ai'`), and its upcoming buyouts and parties get linked notes, each a `note.add` change; no calibration starts, a past booking wants a refit. Undo per calendar takes back the notes nobody changed, the labels nobody changed and the confirm (the calendar reads unsorted when no label is left), and is refused while the sort still runs. (10) **Slice 3: suggestions applied** (10.12). The weekly answer rates each item's `confidence` and a spotted event's effect; while both switches are on, the pass saves as TownwiseAI's a note rated `high`, a closure rule rated `high` (`rule.add`, at most 2 rules a week per location, both sources) and a spotted private event rated `high` whose effect the model chose (linked to the event; alongside regular service only with the count its title states), each through the one writer and stored `accepted` by TownwiseAI; one a person's note or rule decides differently, whose key was used, or past a file read's closure guards (14 days, 31 a pass), waits open. Before the call it adds a closed weekday the sales history is sure of (at least 90% of at least 8 counted days with no sales, beyond D46's bar; `sourceKind: 'sales'`). A link or Google calendar refresh that adds or moves a keyed event in the next 91 days brings that location's weekly pass forward, at most once a day, while the calendar titles switch is on too. (11) **Slice 4: chat and pasted text** (10.12, 11A.9). `propose_note` takes `plain`, the model's mark that the person's own message in the turn stated the note; while both switches are on, a plain note is saved by the tool itself through the one writer (`sourceKind: 'chat'`), as the person's note with TownwiseAI's mark, unless the turn read a file, a picture, a web page, a calendar event's title or a note TownwiseAI wrote from a file or a calendar, the caller is staff open as admin, the location is at the note limit, or the note conflicts with a person's or was undone before; its card then shows it saved with Undo, and otherwise it is the proposal card as before. This changed the chat's frozen prefix (the system prompt's notes lines and the tool's schema). Text pasted on Your data with its box checked (shown, checked, only while TownwiseAI works on its own) is read on its own as a stored file is. (12) **Slice 5: a calendar answers open questions** (10.12; owner, 2026-11-18: “if he connects his google calendar and puts in that they are closed then the question should go away about the rule in all places”). With no model call, wherever a calendar's events switch (an add, the refresh loop, Refresh now), after a file read or a sales upload, and after each weekly pass whatever its outcome, the location's keyed all-day events whose titles plainly say closed (a fixed word rule) answer its open closure suggestions: a dated closure rule or closure note every day of which they cover, and a standing closed weekday whose next 8 days of each weekday they cover; never a season, a booking or a D53 kind, and never one a person's note or rule decides differently. Gap and likely-closed questions do not ask about a day such an event covers, on every read. While both switches are on, TownwiseAI first saves a closure note linked to each answering event whose days closure notes do not all close yet (`sourceKind: 'calendar'`, D53's follow-up moves or removes it), or a standing weekday's rule, with Undo, and leaves the suggestion open when one is not written and still applied; removing the calendar takes back the notes nobody changed since; while either is off, nothing is saved and a standing weekday stays open. D28’s items open and edit (owner request, 2026-11-11: “let the user view and edit different kinds of data as much as possible”). A reference item kept with its original can be renamed (its extension stays) and edited: the browser stores the edited content as a new reference file through the chunked upload, and `POST .../data/:ref/replace` puts that file in the item’s place, keeping who added it, when, how it arrived and whether it is off, and recording when and by whom it was edited (6.11, 10.14). The old file is removed as a deleted file is, so the item has one version, the latest. Sales uploads, sales files and items whose original is gone cannot be renamed or edited. An Excel workbook whose every sheet fits the same is saved as a values-only copy, “{name} (edited).xlsx”, beside the original, which stays, since the browser writes cell values only, not formatting, formulas or charts. Each item has its own page, P27 (`/locations/[id]/data/[ref]`, read with `org.data.get`, 10.14), opened from its row: its details and downloads, an upload’s days on every platform, and on the web a stored file drawn in the browser, or a PDF opened in a new tab (11A.7).

## 3. Roles and permissions

| Capability | Staff | Staff in view-as | Staff open as admin (D25) | Org admin | Member | Signed in, no organization |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Read own access state (`GET /api/me`) | yes | the target’s | the org admin’s, with `openAsAdmin` | yes | yes | yes |
| Send an access request | no | no | no | no | no | yes, in `no_org`, `rejected`, `removed` |
| Join, or decline, an organization that invited their email | no | no | no | no | no | yes, in `invited` |
| Read the organization, locations, town profiles, sales, notes, calibration | team emails, location names and towns, counts and date coverage (D7) | read-only | yes | yes | yes | no |
| Upload sales | only during setup (D23), new and replaced days | no | yes, new and replaced days | yes, new and replaced days | yes, new days only | no |
| Delete all sales for a location | only during setup (D23) | no | yes | yes | no | no |
| Add notes; edit or delete own notes | no | no | yes | yes | yes | no |
| Edit or delete anyone’s notes | no | no | yes | yes | no | no |
| Add, rename, change the town of, or delete (when empty) a location | only during setup (D23) | no | yes | yes | no | no |
| Rename the organization | any | no | the one open | own | no | no |
| Read the team | any | read-only, if the target is an org admin | no (the console) | own | no | no |
| Add emails, change roles, remove people | any | no | no (the console) | own | no | no |
| Leave the organization | no | no | no | yes, unless last admin | yes | no |
| See Townwise staff activity on the organization | audit log | read-only, if the target is an org admin | yes | yes | no | no |
| Approve or reject requests; create, rename, suspend, reactivate organizations | yes | no | no (409 until End) | no | no | no |
| See everyone across organizations; sign a person out everywhere | yes | no | no (409 until End) | no | no | no |
| Read the audit log | yes | no | no (409 until End) | no | no | no |
| Delete a person’s records, or a suspended organization’s (D22) | yes | no | no (409 until End) | no | no | no |
| Start view-as | yes | no | no (409 until End) | no | no | no |
| End view-as | yes | yes | yes (End ends open as admin) | no | no | no |
| Two-step sign-in (`/settings/security`, **Exists**) | required | not applicable | required (the staff member’s own) | optional, recommended | optional | optional |

Rules behind the matrix:

- An organization always keeps at least one active org admin. Demoting, removing or leaving as the last one answers 409 `last_admin`, for org admins and staff alike.
- A staff email can be invited like any other, but it never resolves as a member, because the staff branch runs first.
- Only the addresses in `TOWNWISE_SUPERADMIN_EMAILS` are staff. Any other address a staff member adds to an organization, a personal Gmail included, joins as an ordinary member with full member access, no banner and no time limit. That row shows “Added by Townwise staff” on Team (P17), and the add appears in the organization’s staff activity (9.3).
- Every staff action on an organization (team, name, status, view-as, setup, opening it as its admin) is recorded before it takes effect and shown to that organization’s admins (9.3). The changes staff make while open as admin (D25) are recorded after they take effect, as an org admin’s are (9.3).
- Removed people keep their kit user. They may request access for another organization, or join another that invited them.

## 4. Access states and routing

### 4.1 Types

```ts
type Role = 'org_admin' | 'member';

type Access =
  | { state: 'staff' }
  | { state: 'staff_setup_required' }                          // staff email, TOTP not enabled
  | { state: 'staff_reauth_required'; reason: 'session_before_codes' | 'session_too_old' }
  | { state: 'member'; org: { id: string; name: string }; role: Role }
  | { state: 'invited'; invitations: InvitationView[]; pendingRequest: AccessRequestView | null }
  | { state: 'pending'; request: AccessRequestView }
  | { state: 'rejected'; request: AccessRequestView }
  | { state: 'removed'; org: { name: string }; removedAt: string; byYou: boolean }
  | { state: 'org_suspended'; org: { name: string } }
  | { state: 'no_org' };

interface InvitationView {
  inviteId: string; orgName: string; role: Role;
  invitedBy: { staff: boolean; email: string | null };  // email: the org admin's current kit email;
                                                         // null when staff added it, or that account no longer exists
}

interface MeResponse {
  user: { id: string; email: string };        // always the signed-in person; during view-as, built from the staff actor (7.2)
  access: Access;                              // during view-as: the target's access
  viewAs: ViewAsView | null;
  openAsAdmin: { id: string; org: { id: string; name: string }; startedAt: string } | null;   // D25: set while staff have
                                               // the organization open as its admin; `access` is then its org admin's
  staff: { verifiedUntil: string } | null;    // set whenever the signed-in person's own state is 'staff'
  welcome: { firstName: string | null; restaurant: string } | null;   // GET /api/me only (15.8); null in every other answer
}
```

### 4.2 Resolution order (`resolveAccess`)

Input: the kit’s `AuthContext` (`userId`, `sessionId`, `platform`, `authenticatedAt`). Output: `{ self: Access; effective: Access; grant: Grant | null }`. `self` is the signed-in person’s own access, computed before any view-as substitution; `effective` is what policies evaluate. Every read is from the primary. The resolver never writes. It reads the time only from the injected `now` (7.1).

1. Load the kit user (`users.findById`). If it is missing, answer 401 `unauthenticated`, the kit’s own answer for a deleted user, through the one helper `userGone()`. No other product code answers 401 (D19).
2. **Staff branch**, when the user’s current email is in `TOWNWISE_SUPERADMIN_EMAILS`:
   1. `totp.get(userId)` is not `enabled`: `staff_setup_required`.
   2. `authenticatedAt <= factor.enabledAt`: `staff_reauth_required`, reason `session_before_codes`.
   3. `now − authenticatedAt > 60 minutes`: `staff_reauth_required`, reason `session_too_old`.
   4. Otherwise `self` is `staff`, with `verifiedUntil = authenticatedAt + 60 minutes`. If a grant for this `sessionId` is live by time (Section 8), resolve its target with steps 3 to 7 (never step 2). The target’s resolved organization id is the organization of its active seat (step 3, active or suspended), or null. If that id equals `grant.orgId` (null equals null), the target’s access is `effective` and the grant is returned, so `viewAs` is set. Otherwise the grant is ignored exactly as an expired one, and `effective` is `self`. An open-as-admin grant (`kind: 'open_as_admin'`, D25, Section 8a) is live by time and while its organization exists and is in setup (D23); then `effective` is that organization’s `member` access with role `org_admin`, `openAsAdmin` is set, and steps 3 to 7 do not run. Otherwise it is ignored the same way.
3. An active seat (`tw_members.activeUserId == userId`): `member` if the organization is `active`, `org_suspended` if it is `suspended`.
4. Open invitations for the user’s current email (`tw_members.inviteEmail == email`, `status: 'invited'`) in active organizations: `invited`, listing all of them.
5. A pending request by this user: `pending`.
6. The newer of the latest rejected request and the latest removed seat: `rejected` or `removed`.
7. Otherwise `no_org`.

Outside the staff branch, `self` and `effective` are the same access.

An invitation outranks a pending request, so a second employee who requested access by mistake sees their team on `/joining` as soon as an admin adds them. With a pending request, the state carries it as `pendingRequest`, and `/joining` never joins on load: the request is withdrawn only when the person presses Join, and “Not my team” deletes the invitation and returns them to Waiting (F2b).

### 4.3 Client routing

The client calls `GET /api/me` after restore, after sign-in, after join and after leave. It calls it again whenever an `/api` call answers 403 `no_access`, `forbidden`, `staff_setup_required` or `staff_reauth_required`, or 409 `view_as_active` or `open_as_admin_active`. It clears cached organization data before it re-routes. When a read of `GET /api/me` shows open as admin gone (someone joined, the organization was suspended), the client sends `POST /api/admin/view-as/end` once, with the grant id it showed, because the resolver never writes and a reactivation inside the staff window would otherwise bring the grant back.

| State | Route |
|---|---|
| `staff` | `/admin/overview` (Overview, P32, D48); with `viewAs` set, the target’s route under the view-as banner; with `openAsAdmin` set, the organization admin’s route under the open-as-admin banner (D25) |
| `staff_setup_required` | `/settings/security` with the staff notice (**Exists**; notice added) |
| `staff_reauth_required` | none: the client signs the session out to `/sign-in`, with the reason as its notice (P8). `/settings/security` stays open |
| `member` | `/dashboard` |
| `invited` | `/joining` |
| `pending` | `/waiting` |
| `rejected`, `removed`, `org_suspended` | `/no-access` |
| `no_org` | `/request-access` |

The gate also allows `/request-access` from `rejected` and `removed`, when the person chooses it on No access. Any other route opened in the wrong state redirects to that state’s route. Route names extend the `(gate)` and `(app)` groups on `feature/townwise-web`. [CONFIRM: route names]
