## 5. Flows

### F1. First sign-in with an invited email

1. An org admin adds `{email}` on Team. A `tw_members` row is created with `status: 'invited'`, `inviteEmail: {email}` and the chosen role (default `member`). Audit `member.invited`.
2. The admin tells the person. Townwise doesn’t email invitations (D14), and the Team page says so.
3. The person presses “Continue with Google”. The kit creates or finds their user (**Exists**).
4. `GET /api/me` answers `invited`. With one invitation and no pending request, `/joining` shows “Joining {org}…” and who added them, and calls `POST /api/me/join { inviteId }` at once (lead default). With a pending request, or with two or more invitations, `/joining` lists them and waits for a press: Join on one, or “Not my team” on any (P6).
5. The server compare-and-sets the invitation to `active`. It matches `_id`, `status: 'invited'`, `inviteEmail` equal to the caller’s current email, and an active organization. It sets `userId`, `activeUserId` and `joinedAt`, and unsets `inviteEmail`. Then it withdraws any pending request of the caller (`withdrawnReason: 'joined_org'`), audits `member.joined`, and answers the new `MeResponse`.
6. `/dashboard` shows once: “You joined {org}. {inviter} added {email}. Not your team? Leave {org}.” {inviter} is the org admin’s email, “Townwise staff”, or {org} when that account no longer exists. Leave is on Settings.

[CONFIRM: lead default, auto-join without a click. Conflict: the critic review recommends dropping the automatic join for every invitation. The attack it describes: the org admin of any vetted organization renames it to a stranger’s business name (`PATCH /api/org`, not unique, not reviewed), adds a location in the stranger’s town, and adds the stranger’s Gmail address, often published on a restaurant’s website. The next time the stranger continues with Google, they join silently, see their own business name and town and the upload step, and cannot see the team (members have no Team page). Anything they upload, the org admin reads. Staff vetting covers the org admin’s own organization, not a right to enroll strangers, and the Leave notice shows once. A joined invitation also turns Active on the inviter’s Team page, which tells the inviter that the address uses Townwise. The recommended alternative: `/joining` always shows a one-click screen naming the organization and who added the person, with the primary “Join {org}” and the text link “Not my team”, and a test that join never runs from `GET /api/me` or on page load. It still needs no email and no approval, only one press. This spec keeps the lead default and narrows it: the notice names who added the person, and a pending request is never withdrawn without a press (F2b).]

Branches:

- **Different Google account than the one invited:** the state is `no_org`, so Request access. That page leads with “Joining a team that already uses Townwise? Ask an admin there to add {email}.” and ends with “Signed in as {email}. Using the wrong Google account? Sign out and continue with another one.”
- **An address Google is not authoritative for** (not Gmail, not Workspace): the kit refuses sign-in with 403 `google_email_not_authoritative`, and the sign-in page shows its existing message (**Exists**). Team warns admins before they add an address.
- **Already active elsewhere:** the update hits the unique `activeUserId` index, which answers 409 `already_in_org`. The client re-reads `/api/me`.
- **Invitation removed meanwhile:** 409 `no_invite`. The client re-reads `/api/me`.
- **Not my team:** `POST /api/me/decline { inviteId }` deletes that invitation, matching it exactly as join does. Audit `member.declined`. The row disappears from the inviter’s Team page. The client re-reads `/api/me`.

### F2. Request access

1. A person in `no_org` lands on `/request-access`. The form asks for organization name, their name, their role, the town (one of the twelve, or another town and state), number of locations and an optional note. The business can be found on Google Places first (10.2a), on the same page as the form (D29); the request then also carries the places the person checked, `places` (each `{ placeId, name, kind, town }`), optional (D24).
2. `POST /api/access-requests`. A unique partial index allows one pending request per user. Audit `access_request.created`, with `hasPlace`, `placeCount` and never a place id or name. [CONFIRM: a request keeps the place the requester picked; staff check it by hand]
3. `/waiting` shows what was sent, “We’ll email you when you’re approved.”, and the public profile of the town they named. [CONFIRM: town profile while waiting]

**F2b. Invited while pending.** At the next `GET /api/me` the person is `invited`, with `pendingRequest` set. `/joining` does not join on load. It names the organization and who added them, and offers “Join {org}” and “Not my team”. Join withdraws the request. “Not my team” deletes the invitation, and the request stays with staff, so an invitation the person never chose cannot skip staff review. This is also how staff place a requester into an existing organization: they add the requester’s email on that organization’s page, and the requester presses Join.

### F3. Staff approve a request

1. Staff open `/admin` (Requests, Pending) and read the request: organization, contact name and role, email (and the email at request time if it changed), town, location count, note, the place id when there is one, sent date. A warning shows when the requester already holds a seat.
2. Staff validate the person by hand, outside Townwise: for example, the email domain matches the restaurant, or a phone call. [CONFIRM: what “validated manually” means in practice]
3. “Approve” opens a dialog with the organization name and first location name, both prefilled and editable, and the town shown. The first location name starts as “{organization name}, {Town}” (D29). For a request with places, the dialog shows a Location name per place instead (prefilled “{Google name}, {Town}”, or “{organization name}, {Town}” for a street address or a place stored before places had names) with the place’s town, and “Each location needs its own name.” stops an empty or repeated name (C3).
4. `POST /api/admin/requests/:requestId/approve`, with `{ orgName, locationName }` for a request without places and `{ orgName, locationNames }` for one with them (`locationNames` in the same order and number as the places, each 1 to 80, unique by name key, 6.4; any other body is 400 `invalid_request`, before anything is written):
   1. Load the request (404 if missing). If it is `approved` with an `orgId`, skip to step 6 (a retry completes the work).
   2. If it is not `pending`: 409 `request_not_pending`.
   3. If the requester holds an active seat: 409 `requester_has_org`.
   4. Generate `orgId`. Audit `access_request.approved` with it, before the change (staff events are written first, 9.3).
   5. Compare-and-set the request from `pending` to `approved`, with `orgId`, `decidedAt` and `decidedBy`. No match: 409 `request_not_pending` (another staff member got there first), and the server writes `staff_action.not_applied`.
   6. Upsert the organization `{ _id: orgId }` with `$setOnInsert`: name, `active`, `createdAt`, `createdBy`, `fromRequestId`. Audit `org.created` on insert.
   7. Without places: upsert the first location keyed by `{ orgId, nameKey }` with `$setOnInsert`: name, the town from the request, and `placeId` null. Audit `location.created` on insert. With places (D24), while the organization is new or nobody has ever joined it (no `firstJoinedAt`, 6.1, and no member row with `joinedAt`, active or removed, as staff setup reads it): upsert one location per place the same way, with its name, the place’s town and its `placeId`, skipping places that already have a location in it, and audit `location.created` on each insert. So a retry fills only the missing ones; a retry whose name is on another place’s location answers 409 `location_name_taken`, never a merge.
   8. Insert the requester’s seat: `role: 'org_admin'`, `status: 'active'`, `userId`, `activeUserId`, `joinedAt`, `email` (the requester’s current kit email). A duplicate key in this organization counts as success. A duplicate in another organization (the requester joined elsewhere in the gap) answers 409 `requester_has_org`; the organization then exists with no admin, and its detail page shows “No admin yet”. Audit `member.joined`. [Build note: after inserting the seat, the server reads the request again. Gone means the requester was deleted meanwhile (10.7, Deletion): the seat is deleted, and, when nobody else is in it, the organization and the locations made for the request, with their names redacted as in an organization deletion; no `member.joined` is written, and the answer is 404, with `staff_action.not_applied` (`not_found`) for the approval event this call wrote.]
5. The requester sees their organization at their next `GET /api/me`, and gets the you’re in email (D14).

### F4. Staff reject a request

1. “Reject” opens a dialog with an optional message of up to 500 characters, which the requester will see.
2. `POST /api/admin/requests/:requestId/reject { message? }` audits `access_request.rejected` with `hasMessage` (never the message) first (9.3), then compare-and-sets `pending` to `rejected`. No match: 409 `request_not_pending`, and `staff_action.not_applied`.
3. The requester sees `/no-access` (rejected variant) with the message and “Send a new request”. [CONFIRM: rejected people may send a new request]

### F5. Org admin adds emails

1. On `/team` the admin pastes up to 20 addresses (one per line, or comma separated) and picks a role (default Member). [CONFIRM: role chosen at invite, default member]
2. `POST /api/org/members` normalizes each address exactly as the kit does (`trim().toLowerCase()`, then `z.email().max(254)`) and collapses duplicates. Each address gets one outcome, which never depends on any other organization:
   - `invited`: a row was created. Audit `member.invited`.
   - `already_invited`: this organization has an open invitation for it.
   - `already_member`: an active member of this organization has that email.
   - `invalid`: not an email.
3. The page lists the outcomes and the updated team.

Staff do the same for any organization from its detail page. Those rows carry `addedByStaff: true`, Team shows them as “Added by Townwise staff”, and each add appears in the organization’s staff activity (9.3).

### F6. Org admin edits the team

- **Change role:** `PATCH /api/org/members/:memberId { role }`. For a demotion, update, then count active admins. If the count is zero, set the role back and answer 409 `last_admin`. Audit `member.role_changed`.
- **Remove an invitation** (never joined): delete the row. Audit `member.removed` with `wasStatus: 'invited'`.
- **Remove a member:** set `status: 'removed'`, `removedAt` and `removedBy`, unset `activeUserId`, then count active admins. If zero, restore the row and answer 409 `last_admin`. Audit `member.removed`. An admin may remove themself when another admin exists.
- Change, recount, revert never ends with zero admins, needs no lock, and two concurrent demotions either both revert or one wins. [Build note: this holds for staff edits and for leaving (F7) too, against any mix of concurrent demotions and removals. A demotion from org admin marks the row (`demotingSince`) in the same write and clears the mark after its recount or revert; a removal recounts when the seat was an org admin or carried that mark, read in the same write as the removal, so a member can still leave, and be removed from, an organization with no active admin yet. A demotion recounts only when the row was an active seat at its write, so an invitation’s role never counts. A demotion’s revert matches the row by id, organization and the role it set, whatever its status, so a seat removed meanwhile gets its admin role back and the removal’s own recount puts the seat back. When a seat can’t be put back because the person took a seat in another organization meanwhile, the removal stands and is answered and recorded as done.]

### F7. Losing access, and leaving

- **Removed by an admin:** the person’s next `/api` call answers 403 `no_access`. The client re-reads `/api/me` (`removed`), clears cached organization data and shows `/no-access` (removed variant). Their session stays (D18).
- **Leave:** `POST /api/org/leave` from Settings. It is the same as remove, for oneself, with `byYou: true` and audit `member.left`. The last admin gets 409 `last_admin`.
- **Organization suspended by staff:** members see `/no-access` (paused variant). Data is kept, and reactivation restores access with no other step.
- **Rejected request:** `/no-access` (rejected variant).
- **Compromised account:** staff use “Sign out everywhere” on People (kit `revokeAllSessions`, **Exists**).

### F8. View-as

1. Staff pick a person (on People, a request’s detail, or a member row on an organization’s page) and press “View as”. A dialog asks for a reason (5 to 200 characters) and says it is recorded.
2. `POST /api/admin/view-as { userId, reason }`. Staff targets get 400 `invalid_target`; unknown users get 404. The server clears any grant still holding this session, expired or not (Section 8), writes audit `view_as.started` first, and then inserts the grant. If the audit write fails, no grant exists.
3. The response is a `MeResponse` with the target’s access and `viewAs` set. The client renders the target’s screens under a banner that cannot be dismissed.
4. While the grant is live, every route with the `staff` policy, any method, answers 409 `view_as_active`. Every other non-GET answers 403 `view_as_read_only`. `POST /api/admin/view-as/end` (policy `staff_self`) is exempt from both (7.2).
5. “End view-as” ends the grant (audit `view_as.ended`) and returns to the console’s Overview (`/admin/overview`, D48). The resolver ignores a grant past its end, and a grant whose target has joined, left or changed organization since it started. The next request returns staff access, and the client shows “View-as ended at {time}.” on `/admin/overview`.

### F9. Staff first sign-in, and the hourly sign-in

1. A staff email continues with Google, and `GET /api/me` answers `staff_setup_required`. The client opens `/settings/security` (**Exists**) with the notice “Townwise staff accounts need two-step sign-in. Set up your authenticator app, then sign in again with a code.”
2. After enrollment the kit shows recovery codes once and revokes the other sessions (**Exists**). This session predates `enabledAt`, so the resolver answers `staff_reauth_required` (`session_before_codes`), and the client offers “Sign in again”. The second sign-in goes through the code step, which also proves the authenticator works.
3. Every 60 minutes the client signs staff out to the ordinary sign-in page (P8), where they sign in again with a code. The shell has no return-to route (expo-shell Known gaps, **Exists**), so staff land on `/admin`.

Runbook line: add a staff email only when that person will sign in and enroll within minutes. Until they enroll, anyone who takes over their Google account could enroll a factor of their own. People shows each staff email’s two-step status.

### F10. Staff create an organization directly

For an organization signed outside the app: on `/admin/orgs`, “New organization” asks for the name and the first admin’s email. `POST /api/admin/orgs` creates the organization and an invitation with `role: 'org_admin'` and `addedByStaff: true`. That person joins as admin the next time they continue with Google (F1). [Build note: the request may carry `id`, a 24-hex id the client generates once per new organization. A repeat with that `id` (a retry) creates nothing new: it answers 200 with that organization and writes no second `org.created`. It is a repeat only for an active organization made this way (no `fromRequestId`) with the same name, whose team holds the same admin address or nobody yet; any other organization with that `id` is 409 `conflict`. The one thing a repeat adds is the admin invitation of a create that stopped before it, with `member.invited` written before the insert. A repeat that races the first past its check loses on the unique `_id`, and its `org.created` is followed by `staff_action.not_applied` (`conflict`).] No location is created yet; the admin’s first page asks for one. The organization’s staff activity lists its creation and the invitation. [CONFIRM: staff can create organizations without a request]

### F10b. Staff set up an organization nobody has joined yet

For a client whose daily totals Townwise already holds, used only with that client’s consent (D23). While the organization is active and nobody has ever held a seat in it (after F10 it has only its admin invitation), staff add, rename and delete its locations and upload or delete their daily totals from its console page (P21), through the setup routes of 10.7. The checks are the org admin routes’ (10.3, 11.3), town and place included, and an upload replaces the days it covers, as an org admin’s does. Each write is recorded before it takes effect (9.3), and staff see the result as counts and date coverage only, never a figure (D7). Once anyone joins (F1) or is seated by approval (F3), every setup route answers 409 `org_not_in_setup` for good, even after everyone has left or been removed and their records are deleted; so does a suspended organization. The admin who joins finds the locations and their days, sees each staff upload as by “Townwise staff”, and finds every setup write in their Townwise staff activity (D9). [Build note: setup is checked before the event, with no lock, so a join that lands between the check and the write is accepted; the write is still recorded and shown in staff activity.]

### F11. Upload sales history (web)

Rules are in Section 11. The entry points are Home’s history step and upload links (P11), the Sales data tab, and its empty state. An org admin’s upload replaces the days it covers; a member’s adds new days only and leaves existing days unchanged (D16, 11.4).

### F13. Delete a person or an organization (staff)

Rules are in 10.7 (Deletion). Staff delete a person from People (P22) after removing any active seat, or delete an organization from its detail page (P21) after suspending it. Each writes its audit event first, deletes the Townwise records, and replaces the email or names in older audit events. A deleted person’s kit user record is then deleted by hand (Section 19, item 7).

### F12. Add a note

Rules are in Section 12. The entry points are the Notes tab and “Add a closure note” beside the missing-days count on Sales data, which prefills kind `closure` and effect `closed`.

## 6. Data model

All collections take the `tw_` prefix, so they never collide with the kit’s `users` and `auth_*`. Each is a Mongoose model with a fresh schema built inside a factory, registered on `mongo.connection` before `ensureIndexes` (**Exists**). Schemas use `strict: true` (`strict: 'throw'` for sales), `versionKey: false` and `read: 'primary'`. Ids are ObjectIds, and `userId` is the kit’s user id string (24 hex). Business days are `'YYYY-MM-DD'` strings with no time zone. Money is integer cents. Partial indexes use only `$type` and equality filters; DocumentDB 5.0 rejects `$or`, `$not` and others (**Exists**).

### 6.1 `tw_orgs`

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `_id` | ObjectId | |
| `name` | string | 2 to 120, trimmed, not unique |
| `status` | `'active' \| 'suspended'` | |
| `createdAt`, `createdBy` | Date, userId | |
| `fromRequestId` | ObjectId or null | set when created by approval |
| `suspendedAt` | Date or null | |
| `forecasts` | `{ on, at, by }`, or absent | whether staff have switched the organization’s forecasts on (D27, G1), when, and by which staff user id (null once that person is deleted, 10.7); absent until first switched, which reads as off. Nothing is published, by staff or by a calibration, while it is off [Build note: D42, built in autonomous-forecasts phase 3b: absent reads as on, by the owner’s directive of 2026-11-16 (G1’s build note), and the staff console shows it “On (default)”; `{ on: false }` set by staff keeps it off] |
| `weeklySuggestions` | `{ on, at, by }`, or absent | whether TownwiseAI’s weekly suggestions run for the organization (D42’s build note, 10.12), when an org admin last turned them off or on, and that admin’s user id (null once that person is deleted, 10.7); absent until first switched, which reads as on (owner directive, 2026-11-16). Built in `weekly-forecast-suggestions` |
| `calendarTitlesToAi` | `{ on, at, by }`, or absent | whether the weekly suggestions call may read the titles of the location calendars’ events (D53, 10.12), when an org admin last turned it off or on, and that admin’s user id (null once that person is deleted, 10.7); absent until first switched, which reads as on (owner decision, 2026-11-17). Built in `calendar-event-suggestions` |
| `firstJoinedAt` | Date, or absent | when someone first took a seat: set only while unset (a compare-and-set) right after the seat write of a join (F1) or an approval (F3), and by a person deletion, from the person’s earliest `joinedAt` there, before it deletes their removed seats (10.7); never cleared, so staff setup never reopens (D23). Absent on organizations nobody has joined and on documents from before the field |
| `lastSuspendedAt` | Date, or absent | when it was last suspended: set at each suspension, never cleared (a reactivation clears only `suspendedAt`), so an open-as-admin grant started at or before it is never live again (8a, D25). Absent until the first suspension, and on older documents. |

Indexes: `{ createdAt: -1 }`.

### 6.2 `tw_members` (invitations and memberships, one collection)

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `_id`, `orgId` | ObjectId | |
| `email` | string | normalized; the invited address, or the requester’s email for an approval seat; kept for history |
| `role` | `'org_admin' \| 'member'` | |
| `status` | `'invited' \| 'active' \| 'removed'` | |
| `inviteEmail` | string, present only while `invited` | |
| `userId` | string or null | set on join |
| `activeUserId` | string, present only while `active` | |
| `invitedAt`, `invitedBy` | Date, userId | `invitedBy` is the org admin or staff member who added it |
| `addedByStaff` | boolean | true when a staff principal added the address (F5 from the console, F10); false for org admins’ invitations and for the requester’s seat at approval |
| `joinedAt` | Date or null | |
| `removedAt`, `removedBy` | Date or null, userId or null | `removedBy == userId` means they left |

Indexes:

- `{ orgId: 1, inviteEmail: 1 }` unique, `partialFilterExpression: { inviteEmail: { $type: 'string' } }`: one open invitation per address per organization.
- `{ activeUserId: 1 }` unique, `partialFilterExpression: { activeUserId: { $type: 'string' } }`: one active organization per person (D5).
- `{ inviteEmail: 1 }`: the resolver’s invitation lookup.
- `{ orgId: 1, status: 1 }`: team lists and admin counts.
- `{ userId: 1, removedAt: -1 }`: the `removed` state.

Email changes: the kit updates `users.email` when Google is authoritative for a new address (kit T27). A seat is bound by `userId` after joining, so access survives the change, and the display uses the current kit email.

| Field | Type | Rule |

Null otherwise: a location added without the search, a `placeId: null` write, or a town changed by hand. Older documents read as null |

### 6.5 `tw_sales_days`

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `_id`, `orgId`, `locationId` | ObjectId | `orgId` and `locationId` come from the location the server read, never from input |
| `date` | `'YYYY-MM-DD'` | |
| `guests` | integer or null | 0 to 20,000 |
| `netSalesCents` | integer or null | 0 to 100,000,000 |
| `uploadId` | ObjectId | the upload that last wrote this day; for a member’s add-only upload (D16), the upload that first wrote it. A day belongs to that upload alone (D28): turning the upload off leaves the day out of every read below, with no fallback to another upload’s values |
| `updatedAt` | Date | |

Indexes: `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, date: 1 }` unique; `{ orgId: 1, uploadId: 1 }` (D28: the days an upload still holds, for Your data’s counts and deleting one upload). The schema is `strict: 'throw'`, and the write path builds documents field by field, so no other field can be stored.

**One read rule for “off” (D28).** `SalesDayStore.coverage`, `coverageByLocation`, `months`, `days` and `history` leave out days whose `uploadId` is a turned-off upload (6.6); `hasAny`, `hasAnyForOrg`, `ownedDayCounts` (Your data’s counts), `apply` and the deletes see every day, and `disabledDates` gives only the days that are off (TownwiseAI’s questions). Two counts outside the store also see every day, and return counts and dates only, never a figure: the found days on an import’s drop screen (`ImportStore.found`, `stores/imports.ts`) and the staff console’s day count per organization (`adminOrgStats`, `stores/cross-tenant.ts`; the same console’s per-location coverage follows the rule). Every reader of figures (Home, Analytics, Sales data, `GET /api/org`, forecast scoring, people in town, the agent panel and every TownwiseAI tool) goes through those methods, so turning an upload off is one update with no fan-out. Published forecast runs are trained off-platform (6.20) and cannot change; their live accuracy scores against days that are on. TownwiseAI’s questions (10.12) treat a turned-off upload’s dates as explained, not as gaps.

### 6.6 `tw_uploads`

`_id`, `orgId`, `locationId`, `uploadedBy` (userId), `uploadedAt`, `status` (`'applying' | 'applied'`), `dayCount`, `inserted`, `replaced`, `kept` (days a member’s upload, or a TownwiseAI read’s upload of anyone’s, 11A.9, left unchanged because they already had data; always 0 for an org admin’s own), `firstDate`, `lastDate`, `hasGuests`, `hasNetSales`, and `byStaff: true` only on an upload staff made during setup (D23) or while open as admin (D25, including the file reader’s record for a file staff stored), whose `uploadedBy` is the staff user id. It holds no file name (file names can contain people’s names), no column names and no row count. Index: `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, uploadedAt: -1 }`. `disabledAt` and `disabledBy` (userId) are set while the upload is turned off (D28) and absent otherwise; index `{ orgId: 1, disabledAt: 1 }` (partial, on dates). A stored file's days (11A) get their own record too, written by the file reader; until this record gains a `fileId` (with the sales history work, 10.10), the link is the file's `uploadId` (6.11). `source: { via: 'ai_file', fileId }` is set only on an upload TownwiseAI wrote from the daily totals of a file someone let it read (D34, 11A.9), and absent otherwise: Your data lists it as `townwise_ai` with that file as `fromAiRead` (10.14), and the file's `uploadId` stays null, so deleting the upload never takes the file. It is turned off and deleted as any upload is, and undoing the read deletes it.

### 6.7 `tw_notes`

Fields are in Section 12, and `byStaff: true` only on a note staff wrote while open as admin (D25), whose `createdBy` is the staff user id. `source: { via: 'ai_file', fileId }` only on a note TownwiseAI made from an event in a file someone let it read (D34, 11A.9), whose `createdBy` is the person who asked; absent otherwise. An edit keeps it, so undoing the read deletes the note even after the person edited it. `fromEvent: { calendarId, uid, startDate, endDate, startTime, endTime, linkedAt }` only on a note made with Make a note from a keyed owner-calendar event, or by accepting a spotted event (D53, 10.5, 12): the calendar’s id, the event’s stored UID and its dates and hours when the link was made or last followed, never its title; absent otherwise, which reads as unlinked, with no backfill. An edit keeps it. It has no index of its own: a location’s linked notes are read on the index below (at most 1,000 notes), and `NoteStore.moveIf` and `removeIf` set or delete a linked note only while its `updatedAt` matches. Index: `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, startDate: 1 }`. Limit: 1,000 per location. [CONFIRM: 1,000 notes] [Build note: from the calendar change (D30) a note also stores `startTime` and `endTime`, local wall-clock `HH:MM` (24-hour), each `null` by default; a note stored before them reads as null (no hours), with no backfill. The forecast reader reads the notes overlapping a window (`NoteStore.overlapping`: `startDate <= to` and `endDate >= from`, sorted by `startDate`, `createdAt`, `_id`) on the same index; no new index.]

Fields are in Section 9. Indexes: `{ at: -1 }`, `{ orgId: 1, at: -1 }`, `{ actorUserId: 1, at: -1 }`, `{ orgId: 1, actorRole: 1, at: -1 }` (staff activity for org admins). No TTL. The only update is the deletion redaction (9.3). [CONFIRM: keep audit events indefinitely]

### 6.10 Isolation rules

1. Every tenant document (`tw_members`, `tw_locations`, `tw_sales_days`, `tw_uploads`, `tw_notes`, `tw_files`, `tw_imports`, `tw_upload_days`, `tw_file_entries`, `tw_files_usage`) carries `orgId`. Every tenant compound index leads with `orgId`, except the two seat indexes, which are keyed by the person.
2. Tenant store functions take a branded `OrgScope` as their first argument and add `orgId: scope.orgId` to every filter, update, delete and insert. Only `api/src/access/policy.ts` can mint an `OrgScope`, and only through these eight functions:
   - `scopeOf(memberPrincipal)`: member routes (rule 3).
   - `scopeForStaffOrg(staff, orgId)`: `/api/admin/orgs/:orgId/*` (rule 5). It reads the organization first and answers 404 if it is absent.
   - `scopeForNewOrg(staff, orgId)`: approval (F3) and staff creation (F10) only, for the organization those handlers just created.
   - `scopeForJoinedInvite(invite)`: the join handler only, after its compare-and-set succeeds.
   - `scopeForClaimedImport(claim)`: the file reader only (`files/worker.ts`, 11A), for the organization of the import it just claimed.
   - `scopeForSweep(found)`: the daily file sweep only (`files/sweeper.ts`, 11A.7), for the organization of a file, an import or a blob it found.
   - `scopeForClaimedAiRead(claim)`: the TownwiseAI reader only (`files/ai-reader.ts`, 11A.9), for the organization of the file whose read it just claimed.
   - `scopeForOpenAsAdmin(grant)`: the resolver only (`access/resolve.ts`), for the organization of the open-as-admin grant holding the staff session (D25, 8a).
3. Handlers on `/api/org/*` take the organization only from the principal. No member route takes an organization id from its path, query or body. In open as admin (D25), `PATCH /api/org` and `POST /api/org/locations` carry the `orgId` the page shows, which is only compared with the grant’s and refused when it differs (8a).
4. Location-scoped routes first load `{ _id: locationId, orgId }`. Another organization’s location answers 404 `not_found`, exactly like a location that does not exist. Children (sales, uploads, notes) copy `orgId` and `locationId` from that read.
5. Staff routes on `/api/admin/orgs/:orgId/*` mint a scope from the path through one function that requires the `staff` principal and reads the organization first (404 if absent).
6. Responses never include another organization’s ids or names, except the invitation list shown to its invitee.
7. Path ids are parsed with the mongo module’s `objectId` schema, so a malformed id is 400. Filter values are zod scalars. The only operators are built in code and wrapped in `trusted(...)` (**Exists**).
8. Operations keyed by a person, or spanning organizations, live in one file, `api/src/stores/cross-tenant.ts`, with a closed list: `findActiveSeat(userId)`, `findOpenInvites(email)`, `claimInvite(inviteId, email, userId)`, `declineInvite(inviteId, email)`, `latestRemovedSeat(userId)`, `adminOrgStats()`, `peopleRecords()`, `deletePersonRecords(userId, email)` (10.7, Deletion), the file reader's `claimNextImport()` (11A), the TownwiseAI reader's `claimNextAiRead()` (11A.9) and the daily file sweep's `claimFileSweep()`, `finishFileSweep()`, `sweepCandidates()`, `removeOldUploadDays()` and `existingFileIds()` (11A.7). Only `access/resolve.ts`, the join and decline handlers, the staff handlers, `files/worker.ts`, `files/ai-reader.ts` and `files/sweeper.ts` import it, and a test enforces that list. [Build note: `resumable-chat-turns` (D45) adds the TownwiseAI turn sweep’s `staleChatTurns(now, limit)` and `removeEndedChatTurns(before)`, imported by `chat/turn-sweeper.ts` only, which mints its scope with `scopeForStaleChatTurn(found)` in `access/policy.ts`; `deletePersonRecords` also deletes the person’s `tw_chat_turns` records (6.29) in every organization.]
9. Stored files' blob names are ids only, `{orgId}/{locationId}/{fileId}`, built in `api/src/files/blobs.ts` from the scope's `orgId` and ids the files store already checked belong to it; no request value becomes a path. `blobs.ts` is the only file that imports the Azure SDK, and `chat/*` imports no file code (test-enforced). The one door (D28) is `ctx.items.readText`, built in `app.ts` from `files/items.ts`: TownwiseAI’s `read_data_item` reaches the text of a turned-on, `kind: 'text'` reference item through it, the first 64 KiB decoded and at most 20,000 characters, and a turn reaches a file attached to its message through `ctx.items.readForModel` on the same reader (D36: that text, or a picture's bytes without its metadata, for that turn only, and only for the person who added the file or an org admin), and `api/test/isolation.test.ts` pins that no `chat/*` file touches `ctx.files` or `stores.files`. A sales file is never read by a model, and a file name or title is never sent. The one exception to the first is a file whose uploader or an org admin let TownwiseAI read it (D34, 11A.9): that file, and only that one, is sent whole; for every file nobody opted in this rule holds as written, and no file name or title is sent either way. One API identity reaches every organization's blobs, so isolation is in code and tests; the custom role keeps the API to the two client-file containers, and the private endpoint keeps the data plane off the internet.

### 6.11 `tw_files`

One row per stored file (11A). `_id` (the file id, used in blob names), `orgId`, `locationId`, `importId`, `purpose` (`'history' | 'reference'`; D28: a reference item is any file, or text pasted on Your data or kept from TownwiseAI as a `.txt` file named from its title, kept as it was sent and never read for sales), `disabledAt` and `disabledBy` (userId; set while a reference item is turned off), `addedVia` (`'townwise_ai'` when kept from a TownwiseAI card, else absent), `replacedBy` (D28: on a reference item while an edit is being saved, the id of the file taking its place; absent otherwise), `replacedAt` (D28: when `replacedBy` was set, and absent with it; a claim older than two minutes, or with no `replacedAt`, is stale, 10.14), `replaces`, `editedAt`, `editedBy` (userId) and `editedByStaff` (`true` only for staff open as admin) (D28: on the file an edit put in an item’s place, which also took the item’s `uploadedBy`, `uploaderRole`, `uploadedAt`, `byStaff`, `openAsAdminGrantId`, `addedVia`, `disabledAt` and `disabledBy`; absent otherwise; 10.14), `uploadedBy` (userId), `uploaderRole` (`'org_admin' | 'member'` at upload; decides replace or add, 11.4), `byStaff` (`true` only on a file staff stored while open as admin, D25: it reads “Townwise staff”, and the file reader records its upload as staff’s), `openAsAdminGrantId` (on such a file only, the grant it was stored under, so the reader’s `sales.uploaded` carries it in `viewAsGrantId` too), `uploadedAt`, `name` (the original file name: last path part, control characters removed, NFC, at most 255 characters; shown to the organization only, never logged, audited, put in a blob name or a URL, or sent to a model), `kind` (`'text' | 'xlsx' | 'xls' | 'pdf' | 'docx' | 'doc' | 'zip' | 'other'`), `sizeBytes`, `fingerprint` (SHA-256 over the chunk size and each chunk's SHA-256 in order, `townwise-chunks-v1:{chunkSize}:{hashes}`, so the same file uploaded again matches; it is not the file's plain SHA-256), `upload` (while uploading: `{ chunkSize, chunkCount, chunks: ({ bytes, sha256 } | null)[], head (first 8 KiB, base64), expiresAt }`; null after complete), `status` (`'uploading' | 'stored' | 'queued' | 'reading' | 'waiting' | 'read' | 'kept' | 'failed' | 'deleting'`), `outcome` (11A.6; `reference` for a reference item, shown as Kept for reference), `progress` (while reading: `{ phase, done, total, unit, phaseStartedAt, updatedAt }`), `readStartedAt`, `readMs`, `answers` (per sheet index), `uploadId`, `result` (counts and dates), `report` (11A.5), `cleanBytes`, `rawDeletedAt` (the name becomes the kind's label then, a workbook's sheet names in `report.sheets` become `Sheet 1`, `Sheet 2` and so on, and a ZIP's entry paths are cleared), `attempts`, `entries` (a ZIP's `{ total, used, kept }`, once listed), `modelCalls` and `costMicroUsd` (the AI column step's calls for this file, 11A.4), `aiChoices` (each call's answer, column indexes only, keyed by a SHA-256 of the redacted profile it was asked about, so a re-read of the same table reuses it without a call), `purgeRaw` (set by a staff purge while the file was busy, 10.7), `ai` (D34, 11A.9: absent until someone lets TownwiseAI read the file, then `{ status ('queued' | 'reading' | 'done' | 'failed' | 'skipped' | 'undone'), requestedBy (userId), requestedByRole, requestedByStaff (open as admin), requestedGrantId (that grant, or null), requestedAt, attempts (also the claim's token: every write under a claim matches the count it set), leaseUntil, notBefore (a read put back after an attempt stopped is not claimed before it: 1, 2, then 4 minutes; null otherwise), startedAt, finishedAt, reason (a code, 11A.9), partial (the text sent was cut), costMicroUsd, result ({ kind, confidence, summary, facts, events, days (at most 1,500, newest first), daysCut, eventCount, dayCount, daysBorneOut (the places in `days` of the days the file's text bears out, checked when the answer was saved; null for a picture) }, checked, capped and redacted; null until the model answered; the summary, facts, events and days are cleared when the original is deleted, the days once the actions have used them, and the whole of it on an undo), actions (null until the answer is acted on, and after an undo: { plan: { noteIds (one per event, in order), uploadId, itemId, calibrationId }, saved first by compare-and-set so a retry writes under the same ids; outcome: null until every action is done (a read that failed or was skipped with a plan and no outcome may have written some, and can be undone), then { notes (the ids it created), notesSkipped { duplicate, cap, invalid, guard }, uploadId (null without one), daysWritten, daysAlreadyHad, daysReason, itemId, itemReason, calibration { status, id } } }), undoing (`true` only while an undo runs) }`), and `source: { via: 'ai_file', fileId }` (only on the summary item a TownwiseAI read kept, naming the file it was read from; an edit of that item carries it on, D28). The person's answers are keyed by sheet index, or `family:<signature>` for a family of a ZIP's tables. `strict: 'throw'`. Indexes: `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, uploadedAt: -1 }`, `{ orgId: 1, importId: 1, uploadedAt: 1 }`, `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, fingerprint: 1 }`, `{ status: 1, 'upload.expiresAt': 1 }`, `{ status: 1, uploadedAt: 1 }` and `{ purgeRaw: 1 }` (sparse) (the sweep), `{ orgId: 1, uploadId: 1 }` with a `$type: 'objectId'` partial filter (D28: the file each upload on Your data was read from), and `{ 'ai.status': 1, 'ai.requestedAt': 1 }` (sparse; the TownwiseAI reader's claim across organizations, 11A.9). D60: `calendarImport` (`{ state, code?, at }`, absent until tried): `added` once a calendar was made from the file, or `refused` with `code` `calendar_limit`, `too_large`, `not_calendar` or `unavailable`; the calendar it made keeps the file’s id (`tw_calendar_sources.fromFileId`, 10.18), which says whether that calendar still exists. D61: `folder` (absent, or one of `menus`, `inventory`, `staffing`, `notes`, `other`, `unsorted`): the Your data folder the file was filed in, which outranks a TownwiseAI read’s kind but never Sales (an upload or a sales file) or Calendars (a calendar file) (10.14). Saved text (pasted on Your data, kept from TownwiseAI, or a read’s summary item) is written with `notes`; `FileStore.setFolder` writes or clears it (the hook for D59’s agent); an edit carries it to the file that takes the item’s place. Text pasted before D61 has none and is filed Not sorted yet.

### 6.12 `tw_imports`

A batch of files dropped for one location (11A). `orgId`, `locationId`, `createdBy`, `createdAt`, `lastDropAt`, `status` (`'open' | 'queued' | 'reading' | 'waiting' | 'done'`), `activeLocation` (equals `locationId` until done, then unset), `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, `question` (11A.4, while waiting), `appliedVersion` (+1 each time a file's days are written), `drops` (+1 each time a file completes into it), `lease` (`{ owner, until }`), `claimedAt`, `bytesRead`, `msRead` (over its finished files, for the reading speed). Indexes: `{ activeLocation: 1 }` unique with a `$type` partial filter (one active import per location; two first drops race on it and the loser reads the winner), `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, createdAt: -1 }`, `{ status: 1, startedAt: 1 }` (the reader's claim).

### 6.13 `tw_files_usage`

What the file reader's AI column step (11A.4) and reading with TownwiseAI (11A.9) have cost each organization per UTC month: `{ orgId, month (YYYY-MM), costMicroUsd, updatedAt }`, unique `{ orgId: 1, month: 1 }`, only ever `$inc`'d. A TownwiseAI read reserves the most its call can cost with an `$inc` filtered on the month staying within the budget (so concurrent reads cannot pass it together), then a second `$inc` corrects it to what the call cost (11A.9). Apart from `tw_chat_usage`, so neither budget eats the other's. Deleted with the organization.

### 6.14 `tw_file_sweeps`

One document, `{ _id: 'sweeper', owner, leaseUntil, lastRunAt }`: the daily file sweep's leader lease across replicas (11A.7). Cross-tenant by nature, so only `stores/cross-tenant.ts` reads or writes it.

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `_id` | ObjectId | |
| `orgId` | ObjectId | the organization the welcome was shown in |
| `userId` | string | the person it was shown to |
| `seenAt` | Date | when the client started showing it; a later record keeps the first time (`$setOnInsert`) |

Index: `{ orgId: 1, userId: 1 }` unique. A display marker, not an action, so it has no audit event. Deleted with the organization (10.7) and with the person, in every organization. [Build note: numbered 6.15 by the build plan, which reserves 6.11 to 6.14 for stored files.]

### 6.16 `tw_chat_proposals`

What the author did with each note, or each text item (D28), TownwiseAI proposed in their conversation (10.12). One document per proposal they acted on; none means the proposal is still open.

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `_id` | ObjectId | |
| `orgId`, `locationId`, `conversationId` | ObjectId | from the caller's seat and their own conversation |
| `userId` | string | the conversation's author |
| `proposalId` | string | the `propose_note` or `propose_data_item` call's id, 1 to 128 of `A-Za-z0-9_-` |
| `kind` | `'item'` | D28: set only on a `propose_data_item` call’s row, whose `noteId` is the kept file's id; absent on a note’s row |
| `status` | `'saving' \| 'saved' \| 'dismissed'` | `saving` between the claim and the note's write; reads as open |
| `noteId` | ObjectId | set when the document is inserted, a dismissed one too, so every try of a save writes the same note |
| `edited` | boolean | the saved note differs from the proposal ("Edit first") |
| `changeId` | ObjectId, or absent | D59 slice 4: the `tw_agent_changes` row (6.31) of a note `propose_note` saved itself because the person stated it plainly; such a row is claimed inside the turn and marked `saved` once the note is applied, or removed when it was not, so the card reads open |
| `createdAt`, `updatedAt` | Date | |

Indexes: `{ orgId: 1, conversationId: 1, proposalId: 1 }` unique; `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1 }`. It never holds the note's content or an item’s title or text. Deleted with the conversation, the location, the organization (10.7) and the author's person deletion (10.7, by `userId`); notes saved from proposals stay with the organization. Rows left by a crash during a conversation's delete, or by a Save racing it, hold only ids and go with the location, the organization or the person (`tuning-chat.md` section 5).

### 6.17 `tw_agent_answers`

The answers to TownwiseAI's questions about a location's days with no sales or almost no guests (10.12). One document per question answered; none means it is still asked.

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `_id` | ObjectId | |
| `orgId`, `locationId` | ObjectId | from the caller's seat and the location route |
| `questionId` | string | `weekday_{0-6}_{from}_{to}`, `gap_{from}_{to}` or `likely_closed_{date}`: dates and a weekday number only |
| `answer` | `'closed' \| 'open' \| 'not_sure' \| 'other'` | a later try of a `saving` answer may change it, unless its note is written (then it is the answer that note stands for); a `done` one stands, except that a try whose note is written overrules a different answer finished at the same moment |
| `noteId` | ObjectId | set when the document is inserted, whatever the answer, so every try of an answer that saves a note (`closed`, or `open` on a likely-closed question) writes the same note |
| `status` | `'saving' \| 'done'` | `saving` between the claim and the end; the question is still asked until `done` |
| `createdAt`, `updatedAt` | Date | |

Index: `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, questionId: 1 }` unique. No person id (the audit event `agent.question_answered` carries the actor) and no text: `other` stores the answer only. Deleted with the location's sales data (10.4: an answer was about those days, so the same days uploaded again are asked about again), the location and the organization (10.7); a person's deletion has nothing of it to delete. Notes saved from answers stay with the organization, as every note does.

### 6.18 `tw_file_entries`

One row per entry of a stored ZIP (11A.4): `{ orgId, locationId, fileId, index (central-directory order), path (sanitized: control characters removed, NFC, at most 300 characters; shown to the organization only, null under view-as, cleared when the ZIP's original is deleted), depth (1 or 2), kind, sizeBytes (declared, uncompressed), status ('used' | 'kept' | 'failed'), outcome, family (its table's header signature), dayCount }`. Unique `{ orgId: 1, fileId: 1, index: 1 }`; `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1 }`. Written in batches of 500 when the ZIP is read, replaced on a re-read; deleted with the file, the location's sales data and the organization.

### 6.19 `tw_upload_days`

`{ orgId, day (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC), bytes, updatedAt }`, unique `{ orgId: 1, day: 1 }`. Creating an upload reserves its size with a conditional `$inc` that fails past the daily cap; canceling an unfinished upload the same day gives it back.

### 6.21 `tw_forecasts`

[Build note: D52: a row’s tier (forecast or outlook) is never stored; the reader derives it from its run’s `madeAt` and `dataThrough` (14.4). Once runs reach a year (release B) a run adds about 365 day rows and 52 week rows instead of about 93 and 13, with no new index and no migration.] One row per day and per week of a run: `orgId`, `locationId`, `runId`, `span` (`'day' | 'week'`), `from`, `to` (equal for a day), `status` (a day's `open | closed | booked`; null for a week), `low`, `mid`, `high` (null on a closed or booked day), `baseline` (null unless the run recorded one), `openDays` (a week's), `reasons` (`{ kind, ref, effectPct }[]`, kind `weekday | term | event | holiday | level | closure | booking`; `ref` a town calendar id or group, kept only when it names an entry on that day). Labels are never stored. Indexes: `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, runId: 1, span: 1, from: 1 }` unique; `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, span: 1, from: 1 }`; `{ orgId: 1, runId: 1 }`. Strict (`'throw'`); rows are built field by field and upserted on their key, so a retried import writes only what is missing.

### 6.22 `tw_profiles`

The name a person gave Townwise for Home's greeting: `userId` (the kit user id, a string), `displayName` (a string or null; a null row is on purpose: “no name”), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Account-level, one row per person, never per organization, and read and written only for the caller's own `userId`, like `tw_access_requests`. It is not the kit's user record and not from Google. Index: `{ userId: 1 }` unique. Strict (`'throw'`); `PATCH` is an upsert with `$setOnInsert: { createdAt }`. No audit event. Deleted with the person (10.7), never with an organization.

The staff view and the console accept both from phase 1 of `autonomous-forecasts`, and the staff view names the requester “Townwise (weekly)”; nothing writes them until a later phase] |
| `regimeStart` | `YYYY-MM-DD` \| null | the first day of a lasting change in the weekly pattern the owner described |
| `status` | `'queued' \| 'running' \| 'succeeded' \| 'failed'` | `queued` until the job fetches its input, `running` until it posts its result; each change is a compare-and-set |
| `failure` | `start_failed \| timeout \| job_failed \| not_enough_history \| invalid_result` \| null | |
| `championRunId`, `runId` | string \| null | the published run it was compared with when it started, and the draft run it made |
| `dataThrough`, `inputSha256`, `imageDigest`, `codeVersion` | string \| null | the last day of sales the job was given, the hash of its input, the job image digest and the lab's code version (G3) |
| `dataSha256` | string, or absent | [Build note: D42, built in phase 3a of `autonomous-forecasts`, recorded at the job's input fetch; the weekly refresh compares it since phase 3b] the fingerprint the weekly refresh compares (14.6): the sha256 of the lab input’s canonical JSON without `calibrationId`, `today` and `champion`, with the input schema version and `LAB_MODEL_VERSION`; recorded on every calibration, a person’s too, and absent on one made before it, which counts as changed |

The console accepts them from phase 1 of `autonomous-forecasts`; the gate gives them since phase 3a. Phase 3b adds `engine_switched`, an engine switch the lab decided on the same weeks, published on its absolute checks, whose words name the engine and its margin (“Townwise switched to its demand model: it was 0.6 points better on the same held-out weeks, so Townwise published it.”)] |
| `chargedMicroUsd` | number | 100,000 (\$0.10) once the job has started, charged to the organization's `tw_chat_usage` month [Build note: 0 on a scheduled calibration (D42), built in phase 3a of `autonomous-forecasts`] |
| `requestedAt`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt` | Date \| null | |

Indexes: `{ liveLocation: 1 }` unique, partial; `{ orgId: 1, requestedAt: -1 }`; `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, requestedAt: -1 }`; `{ _id: 1, tokenSha256: 1 }`. Strict (`'throw'`). A live calibration older than 20 minutes is failed `timeout` by compare-and-set on the next start or read (no background loop). ### 6.24 `tw_business_rules`

A location's business rules (D31, 10.16): standing facts about how it runs that TownwiseAI reads with every message. One document per rule.

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `_id` | ObjectId | the rule id |
| `orgId`, `locationId` | ObjectId | from the caller's seat (`OrgScope`) and a location of that organization |
| `text` | string | normalized by `ruleTextOf` (`api/src/handlers/rules.ts`): NFC, every run of whitespace (newlines included) one space, trimmed; then 1 to 200 code points with no control or format character (`\p{Cc}`, `\p{Cf}`) |
| `key` | string | `text.toLowerCase()`: the duplicate check |
| `addedVia` | `'page' \| 'townwise_ai'` | how it was added; the rules route writes `page`, and accepting one of TownwiseAI’s suggestions (weekly, from a file or from the sales history, 10.12) writes `townwise_ai`, as does TownwiseAI adding one on its own (D59 slice 3, with `createdBy: 'townwise_ai'`) |
| `schedule` | object, or absent | the rule's forecast effect (D31): `{ kind, startDate, endDate, weekdays, effect, expectedGuests, startTime, endTime, season? }`, a note's fields (6.7) but `detail`, with `endDate` null for no end; checked by `readRuleSchedule` (`api/src/handlers/notes.ts`) with a note's rules. `season` (D46) is `{ repeat: 'yearly', from, to }`, `from` and `to` `MM-DD`, only on a schedule whose `endDate` is null; a schedule without one has no `season` field, read as none. A rule without a schedule has no `schedule` field at all, and taking a schedule off unsets it |
| `createdBy` | string | the kit user id of its author |
| `byStaff` | `true`, or absent | only on a rule staff added while open as admin (D25), whose `createdBy` is the staff user id; shown as “Townwise staff” |
| `agent` | `{ changeId, at }`, or absent | D59 slice 3: a rule TownwiseAI added on its own (`createdBy: 'townwise_ai'`, shown as “TownwiseAI”): its ledger row (6.31) and its `updatedAt` then; once someone edits it, it is theirs |
| `createdAt`, `updatedAt` | Date | |

Index: `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, key: 1 }` unique, which refuses a rule that differs from a saved one only in case or spacing and also serves the list and the forecast read's scheduled rules (`BusinessRuleStore.scheduled`: filtered on `orgId`, `locationId` and a `schedule` present, sorted by `createdAt`, `_id`, at most 30 rows in the query, so no other index is needed). Strict, `versionKey: false`, read from the primary, like `tw_notes`. Limit: 30 per location. [CONFIRM: 30 business rules per location, 200 characters each] No transactions: an add checks the count, inserts, then counts again and deletes its own row when the location went over 30 (change, recount, revert), so two adds racing at 29 never leave 31. Deleted with the location and the organization (10.7); rules never block deleting a location (staff setup's `location_has_data` counts sales days, notes and stored files, never rules; the org admin's delete takes them all, D44). Not deleted with a person: like a note, the rule keeps `createdBy` and shows its author as “Deleted person”. The text never reaches a log line or an audit event (9.2, 17).

### 6.25 `tw_forecast_schedule`

[Build note: D42, built in phase 3b of `autonomous-forecasts`: `api/src/stores/forecast-schedule.ts`, not a tenant store (it holds no organization’s data), read by the worker, the staff pause and the next refresh date; `paused` is `{ at, by, email }`, with `by` null and `email` “Deleted person” once that staff member is deleted (D22). `weekly-forecast-suggestions` adds `suggestionsAt`, when a pass last ran the weekly suggestions (null or absent before the first), which P25’s panel reads; the pause pauses the whole worker, weekly suggestions included.] One document, `{ _id: 'weekly', owner, leaseUntil, paused }`: the weekly refresh’s lease across replicas (14.6), claimed by compare-and-set for 10 minutes as `tw_file_sweeps` is (6.14) and renewed by compare-and-set before each location, and the staff pause, `paused` being `{ at, by }` (when, and the staff member who paused it) or null, absent read as not paused. Cross-tenant by nature, so only `stores/cross-tenant.ts` reads or writes it.

### 6.26 `tw_forecast_weeks`

[Build note: D42, built in phase 3b of `autonomous-forecasts`: `api/src/stores/forecast-weeks.ts`, a tenant store; the weekly cap’s count and the rows left `starting` are read across organizations in `stores/cross-tenant.ts`.] One row per location per week the weekly refresh considered it (14.6): `orgId`, `locationId`, `week` (the Monday, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the town’s time zone), `status` (`'starting' | 'started' | 'start_failed' | 'unchanged' | 'not_enough_history' | 'cap_reached'`), the calibration id once `started`, and the input fingerprint (`dataSha256`, 6.23). Unique `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, week: 1 }`, so a location starts at most once a week. A row goes `starting` before the calibration starts, then `started` or `start_failed`; a `starting` row older than the lease is resolved by the next holder (14.6). A location skipped because 3 scheduled calibrations are live, or because a calibration of it is live, gets no row, so a later tick tries again. Ids and codes only, never a figure. Deleted with the location and the organization (10.7).

### 6.27 `tw_agent_suggestions`

[Build note: `weekly-forecast-suggestions`, `api/src/stores/agent-suggestions.ts`, a tenant store.] TownwiseAI’s weekly suggestions for a location (D42’s build note, 10.12): `orgId`, `locationId`, `week` (the pass’s Monday in the town), `type` (`'note' | 'rule'`, or one of the three kinds of the second build note), `content` (a note’s fields, or a rule’s schedule with `detail` null and `endDate` null for no end), `text` (a rule’s words, null on a note), `why` (TownwiseAI’s one sentence, at most 280 characters), `calendarIds` (the town calendar entries it rests on, at most 5), `status` (`'open' | 'accepted' | 'dismissed' | 'expired'`), `decidedBy` and `decidedAt` (the org admin who accepted or dismissed it; null once that person is deleted, 10.7), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Index `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, status: 1, 'content.startDate': 1 }`. An open one whose first date is today or past in the town is never listed and is set `expired` by the location’s next pass. Accepting writes the note or rule with the suggestion’s id, then sets `accepted` by compare-and-set from `open` (or `dismissed`, when a dismiss raced an accept that had already written it); dismissing is `open` to `dismissed`. Deleted with the location and the organization (10.7). [Build note: `calendar-event-suggestions` (D53), the same store: `type` also `'event'` (a private event spotted on an owner calendar), `'move'` and `'remove'` (the follow-ups of a note linked to an event that moved or went). `why` is null on all three: their words are written by code at read time (10.12), never by the model and never stored. An `event` holds `event: { calendarId, uid, startDate, endDate, startTime, endTime }` (never a title) and a `content` that is a `private_event` note on the event’s dates with effect `unknown` and the guest count to prefill; a follow-up holds `follow: { noteId, calendarId, change: 'moved' | 'gone', from, to, noteUpdatedAt }` (`to` null when gone; `from` and `to` the event’s raw dates and hours) and a `content` that is the note as accepting would leave it (as it is, for a `remove`), so listing and expiry read `content.startDate` as for the others. A follow-up’s `week` is the town’s Monday of the day it was made, and it holds `openFollowFor` (its note’s id) only while open, `$unset` on every change of status, under the unique partial index `{ openFollowFor: 1 }` with `partialFilterExpression: { openFollowFor: { $type: 'objectId' } }` (the pattern `tw_calibrations.liveLocation` uses on DocumentDB), so a note has at most one open follow-up; a newer change updates the open row in place by compare-and-set, and a change an org admin dismissed (same note, kind and target) is not made again. A `move` or `remove` the next refresh finds nothing to suggest for is set `expired`. There is no hook on the paths that remove notes or calendars: GET .../agent neither lists nor counts, and accepting answers 404 and sets `expired`, a `move` or `remove` whose note is gone, any of the three kinds whose calendar is gone, and a spotted event whose live row is gone or at other dates (10.12). A deletion of the location deletes them with it, as the other kinds.]

[Build note: `suggest-closure-rules`, D46.] Suggested closure rules share the collection, as `type: 'rule'` rows with optional fields: `source` (`'file' | 'sales'`; absent on the weekly pass’s rows, read as `weekly`), `fileId` (the file a `file` row was read from), `evidence` (a `sales` row’s `{ noSalesCount, weekdayCount, lastSalesDate }`: counts and one date, `lastSalesDate` null when the weekday had no sales) and `closureKey` (file and sales rows only, `agent/closure-suggestions.ts`: the weekdays, sorted, or `*`, then a dated range’s start and end, a season’s `yearly=` months and days, or `ongoing` for a standing rule, as in `closed|w=1|ongoing`, `closed|w=*|2027-01-04..2027-03-31` and `closed|w=*|yearly=01-01..03-31`; a standing or yearly rule’s key ignores its start, so a file’s “Closed Mondays” and the sales history’s Mondays are one rule). `why` is required on a weekly `note` or `rule` row only (the three kinds of the second build note carry no `source`, so they read as `weekly`, and have a null `why`) and null on these, whose origin is worded from `source`, `fileId` and `evidence`; their `text` is Townwise’s words from the schedule, never the file’s or a model’s; their `week` is the town’s Monday of the day they were made; and their `content` may carry the schedule’s `season`. Index `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, closureKey: 1 }` unique, partial on `closureKey` being a string, so a location holds one suggestion per key in any status and a dismissed one is never suggested again. They are inserted one at a time under a given id (`insertOne`; the weekly pass’s batch insert is unchanged). A file or sales row is open while its `endDate` is null or not before today in the town: one whose end has passed is never listed and is refused on decide, and the weekly pass’s expiry sets it `expired`, never an ongoing one; the weekly pass’s list and expiry by first date take weekly rows only. Undoing a file read deletes its rows still open (10.14), and deleting a location’s sales data deletes its `sales` rows not accepted.

[Build note: D59 slice 3.] A weekly `note`, `rule` or `event` row TownwiseAI saved on its own (10.12) is stored `accepted` with `decidedBy: 'townwise_ai'` under the id of the note or rule it wrote, so it is never listed, suggested or sent again; a `sales` row for a closed weekday it added on its own likewise, with its closure key. A pass brought forward stores its rows under the town's day as `week`.

[Build note: D59 slice 5.] A row one of the location's calendars answered (`api/src/calendar/answers.ts`, 10.12) reads `status: 'answered'` with `decidedBy: 'calendar'` and `decidedAt`, set by compare-and-set from `open`; a computed sales suggestion it answered is stored `answered` under its closure key. It is not a person's dismissal and not an accept: it is never listed, counted or expired, its closure key keeps the same rule from being suggested or added from the sales history again, and it stays answered when the calendar changes later.

### 6.28 `tw_suggestion_passes`

[Build note: `weekly-forecast-suggestions`, in `api/src/stores/agent-suggestions.ts`.] One row per location per week its weekly suggestions call was made or skipped: `orgId`, `locationId`, `week`, `status` (`'running' | 'suggested' | 'none' | 'budget' | 'failed'`), `suggested` (how many were stored), `reservedMicroUsd` (what the running call reserved of the organization’s TownwiseAI month, 0 once settled) and `month` (the month it was reserved in), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Unique `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, week: 1 }`, inserted `running` before anything else, so a week makes at most one call per location however passes overlap; finishing the row hands its reservation back in the same write. A call that fails before reporting anything costs nothing, and its row is removed with its reservation handed back, so a later pass that week makes the call. A row still `running` a lease (10 minutes) after it was last written belongs to a dead pass, and the next pass resolves it by compare-and-set: `failed`, handing back the reservation it held once, which leaves that week without a call; or, when it held none (no call was made), removed, so the week still runs. Indexed `{ status: 1, updatedAt: 1 }` for that lookup. Counts and codes only. Deleted with the location and the organization (10.7).

### 6.29 `tw_chat_turns`

[Build note: `resumable-chat-turns` (D45), in `api/src/stores/chat-turns.ts`; contract `tuning-chat.md` section 5.] One record per TownwiseAI turn while it runs and for 15 minutes after it ends: `orgId`, `locationId`, `conversationId`, `userId` (the conversation’s author), `turnId` (the live-turn claims’ id), `state` (`'running' | 'done' | 'failed' | 'stopped' | 'interrupted'`; a refused turn ends `done`), `leaseUntil`, `stopRequested`, `startedAt`, `endedAt`, the turn’s nodes (`userNodeId`, null for a regenerate; `replyNodeId`; `parentId`), `message` (the person’s text and their files as `{ ref, kind }`; null for a regenerate), `events` (`{ seq, type, data }`, the stream’s own events, numbered from 1), `eventCount` and `releasePending` (set while the sweep has yet to release the claims of a turn it ended). Unique `{ orgId: 1, turnId: 1 }`; indexed `{ orgId: 1, conversationId: 1 }`, `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1 }`, `{ userId: 1 }` (person deletion), and `{ state: 1, leaseUntil: 1 }` and `{ endedAt: 1 }` for the sweep. Inserted after both claims are held and before the first event. Every write is a compare-and-set on the record still `running` (a batch also on `eventCount`, so an ambiguous write is never doubled) and renews `leaseUntil` to 30 seconds ahead, with a heartbeat while nothing is written that renews it once 10 seconds of it are used; the last event and the last state are written in one update. A running record whose lease has passed reads as interrupted to every reader, and the sweep (`chat/turn-sweeper.ts`, every 15 seconds in each replica) settles it: the record to `interrupted` with its `error` event first, by a compare-and-set that also requires the lease still passed (a renewal that got in first leaves the turn running with its claims), then the conversation’s claim and the person’s; the record keeps `releasePending` until both are released, so the next sweep completes a sweep that stopped between its steps. It holds what the stream showed (text, thinking summaries, tool views, visuals, proposals, suggested questions), never the raw API messages, so nothing D28, D36 or D39 elides is kept; never logged or audited. Deleted with its conversation (after it), its location (10.3, D44, after its conversations), its organization (10.7, in the first sweep) and its author’s person deletion (10.7, by `userId`, not counted), and by the sweep 15 minutes after `endedAt`; the saved conversation is then the only copy.

### 6.30 `tw_activity_days`

[Build note: D48, OpenSpec change `staff-overview`: `api/src/stores/activity-days.ts`, a tenant store; the Overview’s read across organizations, old-row removal and person deletion are in `stores/cross-tenant.ts`.] One document per person, organization and UTC day on which a member or org admin used the app: `{ _id: '<orgId>:<userId>:<YYYY-MM-DD>', orgId, userId, day }`, nothing else. The `_id` is built from the three, so no time is kept (a default ObjectId would carry the second of the day’s first request); no path, route, page, IP address, device or count. Written by the recorder in the route chain (7.2, D48) with `$setOnInsert`; a duplicate key from a race is success. Indexes `{ orgId: 1, day: 1 }` (an organization’s window), `{ day: 1 }` (the Overview’s read and old-row removal) and `{ userId: 1 }` (person deletion). Rows dated before the 180 days kept (today and the 179 before) are deleted by the first write of each UTC day in each replica, so it needs neither stored files nor the weekly worker. Deleted with the organization, in both of its sweeps, and with the person in every organization (10.7); a member removed from an organization keeps theirs there until they age out.


### 6.31 `tw_agent_changes`

[Build note: D59, OpenSpec change `auto-apply-agent-reads`, in `api/src/stores/agent-changes.ts`, written only by `api/src/agent/apply.ts` and Undo.] One row per change TownwiseAI saved at a location: `orgId`, `locationId`, `sourceKind` (`'file'`, (slice 2) `'calendar'`, or (slice 3) `'weekly'` and `'sales'`; (slice 4) `'chat'`, a note the person stated plainly in a TownwiseAI message), `sourceId` (the file's, calendar's or (slice 4) conversation's id, or null), `action` (`'note.add' | 'item.add' | 'sales_days.add' | 'booking.label' | 'rule.add'`, the last since slice 3), `targetId` (the note, rule, summary item or upload it added, under the id planned before any write; for `booking.label`, one change per calendar sorted on import, the calendar), `dedupeKey` (a SHA-256 of the action and its content normalized: a note's kind, dates, weekdays in order, effect and folded title; a closure rule's closure key, which leaves out a standing closure's start, or another rule's schedule; an item's or days' file; a calendar sort's calendar), `confidence`, `why` (TownwiseAI's words, at most 200 characters, or null; shown only in the log, outside view-as), `onBehalfOf` (the file's adder), `status` (`'applying' | 'applied' | 'undoing' | 'undone' | 'adopted'`), `targetUpdatedAt` (the target's `updatedAt` when applied; Undo removes it only while unchanged), `startDate`, `endDate`, `noteKind` and `weekdays` (for the activity's words; a rule's schedule kind, and a null end for a standing rule; `weekdays`, slice 3, the note's or rule's weekdays sorted, absent for every day; a calendar sort's dates are the first and last of the buyouts and parties it wrote), `count` (slice 2: how many labels a calendar sort wrote, counted once they are written; absent otherwise), `appliedAt` (for a calendar sort also the labels' `bookingAt`, planned before any write), `statusAt`, `statusBy`. Unique `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, dedupeKey: 1 }` in every status, so the same fact from two sources is written once and an undone change is never made again; `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, appliedAt: -1, _id: -1 }` for the activity and the log; `{ orgId: 1, locationId: 1, sourceKind: 1, sourceId: 1 }` for a file's undo and a calendar's. Every change of status is a compare-and-set. Before a note or rule's row, its conflict check reads a person's notes and scheduled rules on its days, from its start to its end or, with no end, to 400 days from its start or from today, the later. A weekly or sales row left `applying` for an hour or more (its pass died; those sources plan a new target each pass, so nothing retries one) is finished by the location's next weekly pass (`finishStaleChanges`): marked applied as TownwiseAI when its note or rule was written as planned, removed (freeing its key) otherwise. Never logged; audit events carry its action and source kind only. Deleted with the location (D44) and the organization (10.7, in both sweeps).

## 7. Authorization in one place

### 7.1 Module layout

All of it lives under `api/`; nothing changes in `api/kit/*`.

```
api/
  src/
    main.ts            Exists. Composition root: builds config, logger, Mongo, Redis and auth as today, calls
                       createTownwiseApi() before ensureIndexes, and mounts its router at /api
    app.ts             createTownwiseApi({ config, logger, connection, authStores, auth, redis, now }): registers the
                       Townwise models on `connection` and returns the /api router. main.ts and the tests both use it
    email.ts           Exists. Unchanged (the kit's magic-link sender, which rejects every send)
    mail/              templates, layout, the Communication Services transport and the mailer (D14)
    azure-identity.ts  managed-identity tokens for Azure services (locally, the developer's az login), cached per resource (D14; file storage too)
    config.ts          Townwise env schema (TOWNWISE_SUPERADMIN_EMAILS), spread into the one loadEnv call
    towns.ts           the twelve { townId, name, state, kind } (Section 13) and the US state codes
    normalize-email.ts the kit's email rule, repeated and pinned by a parity test (Section 19)
    access/
      resolve.ts       resolveAccess(): the only code that decides staff, membership, organization and view-as
      policy.ts        Principal, the five policies, the view-as guard, the four OrgScope mint functions (6.10)
      routes.ts        TOWNWISE_ROUTES and mountTownwiseRoutes()
    stores/            one file per collection; tenant stores require OrgScope; cross-tenant.ts (6.10 rule 8)
    handlers/          me, requests, org, locations, sales, notes, team, admin, view-as, deletion
  test/                integration tests against Mongo and Valkey in Docker, as the kit's are; helpers/ (Section 20)
```

**One clock.** `now` is the same function `main.ts` passes to `createAuth` (`AuthDeps.now`, **Exists**), and Townwise code reads the time only from it: the staff window, view-as grants, the upload date rule and audit timestamps. A test clock then ages kit sessions and Townwise rules together.

**Types without new packages.** The Redis client is typed `RedisHandle['client']` from `@ckeith26/redis`, and driver types come from `mongoose.mongo.*`, so `src/` imports no `ioredis` or `mongodb` types (Section 19, item 5).

### 7.2 The route table

```ts
type Policy = 'signed_in' | 'member' | 'org_admin' | 'staff' | 'staff_self';

interface TownwiseRoute {
  readonly id: string;                          // 'org.locations.create'
  readonly method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE';
  readonly path: `/${string}`;                  // under /api
  readonly policy: Policy;
  readonly bodyLimit: 'none' | '2kb' | '32kb' | '256kb'; // 'none' for GET and DELETE; '2kb' only on the two Places routes; '256kb' only on the upload route
  readonly limiter?: 'uploads' | 'requests' | 'view-as' | 'chat' | 'places';   // 'writes' applies to every non-GET automatically, before resolveAccess
  readonly handler: (req: Request, res: Response, principal: Principal) => Promise<void>;
}
```

`mountTownwiseRoutes(router, TOWNWISE_ROUTES)` builds every route with the same chain:

1. `auth.requireAuth` (kit): 401 `unauthenticated`; 403 `origin_not_allowed` for a cookie request without an allowlisted Origin (**Exists**).
2. **`townwise:writes` limiter**, for every non-GET, keyed on `acct:<userId>` from `authOf(req)`. It runs before any read or parse, so refused and probing writes count too.
3. `resolveAccess(authOf(req))` produces the `Principal` (from `self` and `effective`, 4.2).
4. **View-as guard**, in this order, when the principal is in view-as:
   1. A route with policy `staff`, any method, answers 409 `view_as_active`.
   2. Any other non-GET answers 403 `view_as_read_only`.
   3. The route with policy `staff_self` (`POST /api/admin/view-as/end`) is exempt from both.
   
   Each GET that passes logs `townwise.view_as_read { grantId, routeId }`.

   Then the **open-as-admin guard** (D25, 8a), when the principal is in open as admin: `staff_self` passes; a route with policy `staff`, any method, answers 409 `open_as_admin_active`; a route not marked `openAsAdmin` answers 403 `open_as_admin_refused`, GETs included; a marked route goes on. So a new route stays closed in that mode until someone marks it.
5. **Policy**, evaluated on `effective` except `staff_self`:
   - `signed_in`: anyone who passed step 1.
   - `member`: `access.state === 'member'`, else 403 `no_access`.
   - `org_admin`: `member` and `role === 'org_admin'`. A member gets 403 `forbidden`; anyone else gets 403 `no_access`.
   - `staff`: passes only for a principal of kind `staff`, which never carries view-as. `staff_setup_required` and `staff_reauth_required` answer 403 with those codes. Everyone else gets 403 `forbidden`, and the staff checks run after the email check, so a non-staff caller never learns anything about staff two-step state.
   - `staff_self`: the signed-in person’s own staff gate (`self`: TOTP enabled, session created after `enabledAt`, under 60 minutes), computed before the view-as substitution. It passes for a `staff` principal and for any principal in view-as or open as admin, because a grant is live only while its actor passes that gate. Otherwise it answers exactly as `staff` does. Used only by `POST /api/admin/view-as/end`.
6. **Body parser**, `express.json({ limit })`, when the spec names a body limit. The guard and the policies never read the body, so a refused request is never parsed. On the ordering setup's read alone (`org.orders.setup.read`, D41, 10.17), the route's `beforeBody` step runs right before the parser: it holds the replica's 16 MiB byte gate for the body's `Content-Length` (413 `payload_too_large` without one or over 8 MiB, 503 `extract_busy` when the gate is full), and `assertRouteTable` refuses the step on any other route. The `/api` router mounts no router-wide parser, so the upload route’s 256 KB parser never widens the others (server-core: body parsing is per router, **Exists**).
7. **Route limiter**, when named (`uploads`, `requests`, `view-as`, `places`; Section 10.8; `chat` in `docs/portal/tuning-chat.md`), keyed on `acct:<userId>`.
8. The handler receives the principal. For member routes, `principal.scope` is the only organization it can use.

Boot throws if two specs share a method and path, if a GET spec names a body limit, if any route other than `view-as/end` uses `staff_self`, or if a `staff` or `staff_self` route is marked `openAsAdmin`. Paths not in the table reach server-core’s `notFound` (**Exists**).

```ts
interface StaffActor { userId: string; email: string; sessionId: string; verifiedUntil: string }
interface ViewAsContext { grantId: string; actor: StaffActor }   // the staff member doing the viewing
interface OpenAsAdminContext { grantId: string; actor: StaffActor }   // D25: the staff member with the organization open

type Principal =
  | { kind: 'staff'; actor: StaffActor }
  | { kind: 'member'; userId: string; email: string; scope: OrgScope; role: Role; memberId: string | null;   // null only in open as admin
      viewAs: ViewAsContext | null; openAsAdmin: OpenAsAdminContext | null }
  | { kind: 'other'; userId: string; email: string; access: Access; viewAs: ViewAsContext | null };
```

In view-as, `userId` and `email` are the target’s, and `viewAs.actor` is the staff member. `MeResponse.user` and `MeResponse.staff` are built from the actor whenever there is one (`actor`, or `viewAs.actor`). `view-as/end` takes the session id from `viewAs.actor.sessionId`. Audit events use the actor, and view-as writes nothing except its own start and end. In open as admin (D25), the principal is the grant organization’s org admin, with the staff member’s `userId` and `email`, `memberId` null (they hold no seat), the resolver’s scope, and `openAsAdmin.actor` the staff member; the changes it makes are recorded with actor role `superadmin` and the grant id (9.3).

### 7.3 GET is side-effect free

Every GET handler only reads (kit Security 5: GET handlers must be side-effect free). A test runs every GET route with Mongo command monitoring and fails on any `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `findAndModify` or `bulkWrite` (Section 20). One exception, outside the handlers (D48): a member’s or org admin’s first request of a UTC day, a GET included, writes one `tw_activity_days` row (6.30) from the route chain, after the policy and before the handler, and that replica’s first write of the day deletes the rows older than the 180 days kept. The test lets those writes through and fails on any other (`api/test/chain.int.test.ts`).
