| 503 | `files_unavailable` | every stored-files route while `FILES_BLOB_ACCOUNT_URL` is unset; deleting a location's sales data, or an organization, that has stored files while they are off | the browser upload (P13) instead |
| 503 | `uploads_busy`, `storage_unavailable` | a replica at 12 chunk streams (`Retry-After: 2`); blob storage refused or failed (`Retry-After: 5`) | the upload queue waits and retries |

Not HTTP errors, and never in a response's `error`: a TownwiseAI read's codes on the item (`ai.reason`, `ai.daysReason`, 10.14, 11A.9), which the item page says in plain words. Among them `answer_too_long` (failed: the answer reached the output limit, so none is kept; “a shorter file, such as one year of sales, will work”), `requester_gone` (skipped: the person who asked left the organization, or staff's grant ended, before anything was written) and `already_had_days` (no days written: the location already has every verified day, and TownwiseAI never changes one).

### 10.10 Calendar and sales history

Two reads for Home, Analytics and TownwiseAI. Both are `member` GETs in `TOWNWISE_ROUTES` with no body and no route limiter (`app:api-ceiling` still applies). Both are allowed during view-as, where the chain logs `townwise.view_as_read` with the grant id and route id only. Neither handler logs or audits anything, and neither imports `stores/cross-tenant.ts`.

| Method and path | Policy | Request | Success | Extra errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/sales/history` | member | | 200 `SalesHistory` | 400 (malformed id); 404 |
| `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/calendar?from=&to=` | member | `from` and `to` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, exactly those two keys; `from` on or after 2010-01-01; `from <= to`; `to` at most 400 days after the server’s UTC day; a span under 7,320 days | 200 `LocationCalendar` | 400 `invalid_request`, with no field details; 404 |

```ts
interface SalesHistory {
  coverage: Coverage;
  uploadsOff: boolean;                 // D28: no day shows because every upload holding days is turned off (10.4)
  days: {                              // columns of equal length, oldest first, one entry per stored day
    date: string[];
    guests: (number | null)[];
    netSalesCents: (number | null)[];
    upload: number[];                  // index into `uploads` of the upload that last wrote the day; -1 if it has no record
  };
  uploads: {                           // every upload some day references, newest first
    id: string; uploadedAt: string; uploadedByEmail: string; status: 'applying' | 'applied';
    firstDate: string; lastDate: string;
    file: null | { id: string; name: string | null; kind: 'text' | 'xlsx' | 'xls' | 'pdf' | 'docx' | 'doc' | 'zip' | 'other' };
                                       // the stored file (11A) the upload was read from: null for a browser upload, a
                                       // deleted file, and every upload while stored files are off; name null in view-as
  }[];
}

interface LocationCalendar {
  town: Town;                          // the location's town
  researched: boolean;                 // the town has at least one researched event (13.1)
  covers: { from: string; to: string } | null;   // the span of the town's researched events, all years; null when none
  events: TownEvent[];                 // overlapping [from, to], sorted by start, then id
}

interface TownEvent {
  id: string;                          // stable: 'us:thanksgiving:2026', 'hanover-nh:2026-11-17:fall-term-classes-end'
  title: string;
  start: string; end: string;          // inclusive; a single day has end === start
  kind: 'holiday' | 'event' | 'term' | 'season';
  scope: 'national' | 'town';
  group: string | null;                // a recurring kind ('us:thanksgiving', 'hanover-nh:classes:fall'); null for a one-off
  groupLabel: string | null;
  confidence: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low' | null;  // the research's rating; null for holidays and key dates
  sources: { label: string; url: string }[];     // at least one
}
```

- The history route exists because `sales/days` caps at 366 days, and the heatmap and year over year need every year. It reads the days and the referenced uploads in two queries, and one current email per distinct uploader (10.1, “Deleted person”). Aggregates (weekly shape, months, drivers) are computed in the client from this one response.
- `file` is always null until stored files link uploads to files; then `name` is null during view-as.
- The calendar is location-scoped, not `/towns/:townId`, so a town outside the twelve still gets its holidays. A restaurant’s own calendars have routes of their own (10.18).

### 10.11 Files and imports

All under `/api/org/locations/:locationId`, all members, all 503 `files_unavailable` while stored files are off; every non-GET also passes `townwise:writes`, and view-as refuses every non-GET (403 `view_as_read_only`) and both downloads (403 `view_as_no_download`). The full table, with each route's errors, is `api/README.md` (Stored files); the shapes are in 11A.

| id | Method and path | Who | Body | Limiter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `org.files.create` | `POST /files` | member | 2 KB `{ name, sizeBytes, purpose: 'history' \| 'reference' }`; answers `autoRead` (D59) | `files` |
| `org.files.chunk` | `PUT /files/:fileId/chunks/:index` | the uploader | raw, exact `Content-Length` (`bodyLimit: 'stream'`, this route only) | `file_chunks` |
| `org.files.complete` | `POST /files/:fileId/complete` | the uploader | 2 KB `{ aiAuto? }` (D59: `true` lets TownwiseAI read the file on its own) | |
| `org.files.list` | `GET /files?before=` | member | | |
| `org.files.get` | `GET /files/:fileId` | member | | |
| `org.files.entries` | `GET /files/:fileId/entries?after=` | member | | |
| `org.files.raw` | `GET /files/:fileId/raw?part=` | the uploader or an org admin | | `downloads` |
| `org.files.clean` | `GET /files/:fileId/clean` | member | | `downloads` |
| `org.files.remove_raw` | `DELETE /files/:fileId/raw` | the uploader or an org admin | | |
| `org.files.remove` | `DELETE /files/:fileId` | the uploader or an org admin | | |
| `org.originals.remove` | `DELETE /originals` | org admin | | |
| `org.imports.current` | `GET /imports/current` (declared before `:importId`) | member | | |
| `org.imports.get` | `GET /imports/:importId` | member | | |
| `org.imports.start` | `POST /imports/:importId/start` | member | 2 KB `{}` | |
| `org.imports.answer` | `POST /imports/:importId/answer` | member | 2 KB `{ questionId, choice }` | |

A `reference` file (D28, 10.14) takes the same chunks and caps but joins no import and is never read for sales: `complete` sets it `kept` with outcome `reference`.

`PUT` is allowed only with `bodyLimit: 'stream'` (the file chunk) or `'1mb'` (the ordering setup’s save, `org.orders.setup.save`, 10.17: 300 items with 10 point-of-sale names each can pass 256 KB), and `'stream'` only on `org.files.chunk` and `'1mb'` only on the setup’s save (boot refuses anything else). One `POST` takes `'8mb'`: reading the ordering setup with TownwiseAI (`org.orders.setup.read`, D41, 10.17), a file of up to 5 MB as base64 or pasted text; boot refuses `'8mb'` on any other route. The staff purge of an organization's originals is `admin.orgs.originals.remove` (10.7). The chunk handler reads the body itself after the policy passed, and a chunk it refuses is answered with the connection closed, unread.

### 10.12 TownwiseAI proposals and side panel

`POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/chat/:conversationId/proposals/:proposalId` (`org.chat.proposal`, member, body `8kb`, `writes` only). The conversation's author saves a note TownwiseAI proposed, as shown or edited first, or sets it aside. Contract and views: `docs/portal/tuning-chat.md` section 2.

| Request | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `{ action: 'save', note?: NoteInput }` (`note` is the author's edit) or `{ action: 'dismiss' }` | 200 `{ proposal: { id, status: 'saved' \| 'dismissed', noteId, edited }, note: Note \| null }` | 400 `invalid_request` (body, malformed id, or an edit that breaks a Section 12 rule); 404 (the location is not the caller's organization's, the conversation is not the caller's in this location, or no proposal with this id was shown in a stored turn); 409 `note_limit`; 403 `view_as_read_only`; 429 |

- Only the author's press saves a note, and only a proposal they were shown: a `propose_note` call with valid input and a result that is not an error. The note goes through Section 12's rules again and is audited `note.created`, as from the notes route.
- Only a proposal in a stored turn: a turn is stored when it ends with `done` (not `refusal`), so a proposal streamed during a live turn is 404 until then, and one from a turn that failed, was refused, was stopped or was interrupted stays 404. That is unchanged by D45: a turn the page reads again after a refresh, or follows in a second tab, is still live until its `done`, and its cards stay disabled until then. The client keeps the card's actions disabled until `done`, and after a failure offers the notes route instead (`tuning-chat.md` section 2).
- No transactions (DocumentDB): the save claims the proposal in `tw_chat_proposals` (6.16), writes the note with the claim's `noteId`, then marks it `saved`. A retry, a crash between the steps or two tabs pressing Save end with one note; only the request that wrote it records `note.created`. Saving a saved proposal again, or setting it aside, answers its saved state.
- `GET .../chat/:conversationId` shows each proposal's `status` (`open`, `saved` or `dismissed`) and `noteId`. One with no record reads as saved when a note the author wrote at the location says exactly the same, so a proposal added with the notes route is not offered twice; a colleague's note never counts (`tuning-chat.md` section 2, [CONFIRM]).
- Logged as `townwise.chat_proposal { orgId, locationId, conversationId, status, edited }`, never the note's text.
- D59 slice 4: a note `propose_note` saved itself (the person stated it plainly; 10.12's TownwiseAI working on its own) streams its `proposal` event with `saved: { noteId, changeId }`, and `GET .../chat/:conversationId` shows that proposal `saved` with `auto: { changeId, status, undoable, target? }`, its change's status, whether the caller is offered Undo (agent/changes.ts, false under view-as and for anyone but the note's author or an org admin) and, while the change is `applied`, `target` `changed` or `gone` once someone edited or deleted the note on Notes, which the card says. Its Undo is the change's own route below. A turn that fails after the save is not stored, so its card goes, and the note stays in the activity and the log with Undo; one that failed between writing the note and marking its change applied is finished by the next weekly pass (`finishStaleChanges`, an hour on).

**Feedback.** The author rates a reply with `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/chat/:conversationId/feedback/:nodeId { rating: 'up' | 'down' | null, reason? }` (`org.chat.feedback`, member, body `1kb`, `writes` only): `null` clears it, `reason` is one of six fixed values and goes only with `down`, and `nodeId` must be a reply of the caller's conversation on any branch (else 404). It is stored in the conversation document as an enum and a time, never text, shown in the conversation view (staff in view-as read it, and the guard refuses the write), and logged as `townwise.chat_feedback { orgId, rating, reason }`; no audit event.

**Versions.** A conversation is a tree of the person's messages and TownwiseAI's replies (`tuning-chat.md` sections 2, 3 and 5). Edits and regenerates are turns on `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/chat/turns` (`org.chat.turn`): an edit sends `parentId`, the edited message's parent (null for the first message), and a regenerate sends `{ conversationId, replyTo }` for a new reply to the person's message `replyTo`. So each one takes the live-turn claims, counts toward the 40-turn and 1.5 MB caps (every branch counts), is checked against the monthly budget and spends `townwise:chat` and `writes`, and each sends the model only its own path, byte for byte. `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/chat/:conversationId/active { nodeId }` (`org.chat.active`, member, body `1kb`, `writes` only) stores the newest leaf under that node as the version shown and answers the conversation as `GET .../chat/:conversationId` does; `PATCH /api/org/locations/:locationId/chat/:conversationId { title }` (`org.chat.rename`, member, body `1kb`, `writes` only; trimmed, 1 to 60 characters, no control characters) answers `{ id, title }`. Neither moves the conversation in the list, records an audit event or logs; an unknown node or another person's conversation is 404, and under view-as `?node=` reads any version while the guard refuses both.

**Attachments (D36).** A send on `org.chat.turn` may carry `attachments`, 1 to 5 distinct `f_` refs of Your data at the location (a regenerate carries none and reads its stored message's files again; an edit sends the edited message's refs again). Before any claim, from each file's record and first bytes: stored files off is 503 `files_unavailable`, a file not at the location (or another member's still uploading) 404, a sales file 400 `invalid_request`, one of the caller's own still uploading 409 `attachment_not_ready`, one the caller didn't add, unless an org admin, 403 `attachment_not_allowed`, and files that would take the replica past 64 MB held for turns 503 `attachments_busy`. The bytes are read after the claim. The conversation's person entries gain `attachments: { ref, kind, name, state }[]`, `name` null under view-as. What is sent and stored: `tuning-chat.md` section 3.

**Keeping text (D28).** `GET` and `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/chat/:conversationId/item-proposals/:proposalId` (`org.chat.item_proposal.get`, `org.chat.item_proposal`, member, body `2kb`, `writes` and, on the POST, `files`, the budget Paste text uses) are the card of a `propose_data_item` call: GET shows `{ proposal: { id, title, text, status, item } }` (a read that writes nothing and logs nothing), POST `{ action: 'save' }` keeps the text and `{ action: 'dismiss' }` sets it aside. Save writes exactly the text of the stored call, never text from the request, as a `.txt` reference item added via TownwiseAI (6.11), claiming the proposal first (6.16) so a retry or a second tab ends with one item; it answers 503 `files_unavailable` while stored files are off. Only the conversation’s author reaches it; anything else is 404. Contract: `docs/portal/tuning-chat.md` section 2.

**Side panel.** `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/agent` (`org.agent.get`, member, no body, no limiter) and `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/agent/questions/:questionId` (`org.agent.answer`, member, body `1kb`, `writes` only). Both work whether or not the chat is on. Contract: `docs/portal/tuning-chat.md` section 8.

| Route | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| GET | 200 `{ questions: Question[], activity: ActivityItem[], suggestions: Suggestion[], weeklySuggestions: { on, available, canChange, calendarTitles }, ruleSuggestions: RuleSuggestion[] }`, the first two computed at read time (`ruleSuggestions`, D46, below) | 400; 404 |
| POST `{ answer: 'closed' \| 'open' \| 'not_sure' \| 'other' }`, exactly that key | 200 `{ question: { id, answer }, note: Note \| null }` | 400 `invalid_request` (body, any other key, or an id that is not `weekday_`/`gap_`/`likely_closed_` with dates); 404 (the location, or a question not asked now, which since D46 includes every weekday question not answered before); 409 `note_limit` (`closed`, or `open` on a likely-closed question); 403 `view_as_read_only`; 429 |

- **Questions** are rules over the location's own days, never an estimate, over the last 365 days of coverage (from the later of the first day and 364 days before the last day with sales, to that last day); the days read reach 56 days before it, for each day's typical guests (D32). Each question carries the numbers behind it (dates, day counts and guest counts, never net sales or a note's text). A business rule's schedule (D31) explains a day differently from a note, only as it decides the day: a closure schedule (kind closure or effect closed) explains the days it covers, those with no sales (gap questions) and a likely-closed day, which D32 then reads as closed; a schedule with more or fewer guests explains only a likely-closed day, which D32 then reads as open, never a day with no sales (no sales under "busy Fridays" is more suspicious, not less); any other schedule explains nothing, and a rule with no schedule changes nothing. A yearly schedule (D46) explains only the days of its season from its start. No weekday question is asked (D46): a weekday with no sales on at least 60% of its counted days, with at least 4 of them, is a weekday the location is usually closed on, and the sales history suggests it as a standing closure rule instead (Suggested closure rules, below). Weekday questions answered before keep their answers and notes. A day counts from the first day with sales in the window, and only when its week (Monday to Sunday) has sales on another day, so a week with no data at all never makes a weekday look closed. Gap and likely-closed questions ask only about usually busy days not on a weekday the location is usually closed on: a day is usually busy when its weekday had guests on at least 5 of the 8 same weekdays before it, with typical guests of at least 10, so a location with no guest counts is asked no questions (the sales history may still suggest a closed weekday). [CONFIRM: a day is asked about only when its weekday had guests on at least 5 of the 8 same weekdays before it, with typical guests of at least 10] A gap question (`{ id, kind: 'gap', from, to, dayCount, typicalGuestsLow, typicalGuestsHigh }`) asks about a run of consecutive days with no sales that no note and no earlier answer explains, when at least one of its days is usually busy, with the lowest and highest typical guests of those days, rounded; a weekday the location is usually closed on (the 60% rule over all its counted days) bridges a run but never starts or ends one, and a run the window cuts off before its first day with sales is not asked. A likely-closed question (`{ id: 'likely_closed_{date}', kind: 'likely_closed', date, guests, typicalGuests }`) asks "Were you open?" about a usually busy day D32 calls likely closed that no note of any kind and no earlier answer explains, with its recorded guests and its typical guests, rounded. At most 5, gaps and likely-closed days together, newest first by their last day. An answered question's days, whatever the answer, are not asked about again until the location's sales data is deleted, which deletes the answers too. [CONFIRM: 60% of a weekday's days, at least 4 of them]
- **Answers.** `closed` saves a closure note (`effect: 'closed'`) over the question's days, the weekday only for a weekday question, the one day for a likely-closed question, through Section 12's rules and the note limit, recorded `note.created`. On a likely-closed question `open` ("Yes, it was just slow") saves the open-day note the same way: an `other` note for that day with `effect: 'fewer_guests'`, no expected guests and the detail "Open, with very few guests (your answer to TownwiseAI).", which D32 reads as open. [CONFIRM: "Yes, it was just slow" saves an Other note with fewer guests and the detail "Open, with very few guests (your answer to TownwiseAI)."] `open` on a weekday or gap question (the data is missing), `not_sure` and `other` save nothing. `other` is Something else: the client sends the person's words to TownwiseAI as a chat message, then answers `other`; the body is the answer alone, so the words never reach this route, a store, a log or an audit event. The answer belongs to the location: answering one already done, by anyone, answers what was saved. No transactions: the answer claims its question in `tw_agent_answers` (6.17), writes the note the answer saves with the claim's `noteId`, then marks the answer `done` and records `agent.question_answered` once. A retry, a crash between the steps or several tabs end with one note, and the note with the row's id decides the answer (a likely-closed question's `closed` and `open` both write with it, so the one written first stands). A question whose claim stopped before `done` is still asked, and its next answer finishes it, with that answer, while the question is still asked; a stopped claim whose note is written finishes as the answer that note stands for, whatever the next answer is. An answer is marked `done` only while the row still holds it, and the request answers with what the row holds; an answer whose note is written overrules a different answer sent at the same moment (the note exists), as a saved proposal overrules Not now.
- **Activity** (`ActivityItem`, newest 20) lists only real, dated records of the location: `{ at, kind: 'upload_applied', firstDate, lastDate, dayCount }` for applied uploads, `{ at, kind: 'note_saved', via: 'chat' | 'question', noteId, noteKind, startDate, endDate }` for notes the caller saved from their own proposals and notes saved by answers (closure notes and open-day notes; left out once the note is deleted), and `{ at, kind: 'question_answered', questionId, answer }` for `open` on a weekday or gap question, `not_sure` and `other`, and (F3) `{ at, kind: 'file_processed', fileId, firstDate, lastDate, dayCount }` for stored files Townwise read, dated when the read ended, in place of the upload record that read wrote. Later sources append their own kinds (forecasts' `forecast_made`); a client shows a kind it does not know as nothing. Never a file name (the panel is read under view-as too), a note's detail or a figure.
- Logged as `townwise.agent_answer { orgId, locationId, answer }`. Under view-as the GET is logged `townwise.view_as_read`, and the POST is refused by the guard.

**Weekly suggestions** (`weekly-forecast-suggestions`, D42’s build note; contract `docs/portal/tuning-chat.md` section 9). GET .../agent’s `suggestions` are the location’s open ones whose first date is after today in the town, soonest first: `{ id, type: 'note', note, why, calendar, createdAt }` or `{ id, type: 'rule', text, schedule, scheduleSummary, why, calendar, createdAt }`, `calendar` being `{ id, title, start, end }` of the town calendar entries it names. `weeklySuggestions.on` is the organization’s switch, `available` whether passes run here (`TOWNWISE_WEEKLY_SUGGESTIONS` true, the weekly worker ran them within the last 3 hours by the schedule’s `suggestionsAt` (6.25), and staff have not paused it; the API’s own TownwiseAI key does not count, since the worker makes the calls) [CONFIRM: TownwiseAI’s panel says weekly suggestions run only when the worker ran them within the last 3 hours], `canChange` whether the caller is an org admin outside view-as.

| Route | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `POST .../agent/suggestions/:suggestionId/accept {}` (`org.agent.suggestion_accept`, org admin, body `1kb`, `writes`, runs in open as admin) | 200 `{ suggestion: { id, status: 'accepted' }, note: Note \| null, rule: Rule \| null }`: the note (Section 12) or the rule (10.16, `addedVia: 'townwise_ai'`) written as that admin with the suggestion’s id, so a retry or a second tab writes it once; one already accepted answers what it wrote | 400 (a body); 403 `forbidden` (a member), `view_as_read_only`; 404 (another organization’s or location’s, unknown, dismissed, or its first date today or past); 409 `note_limit`, `rule_limit`, `rule_exists` (it stays open) |
| `POST .../agent/suggestions/:suggestionId/dismiss {}` (`org.agent.suggestion_dismiss`, as accept) | 200 `{ suggestion: { id, status: 'dismissed' }, note: null, rule: null }`, or the accepted state when an accept got there first, also when an accept wrote the note or rule but never marked it accepted (the dismiss then finishes the accept, recording `agent.suggestion_accepted`) | as accept, without the 409s |
| `PATCH /api/org/weekly-suggestions { on, orgId? }` (`org.weekly_suggestions.switch`, org admin, body `2kb`, `writes`, runs in open as admin with the tab’s `orgId`, D25) | 200 `{ weeklySuggestions: { on } }`; a change records `org.weekly_suggestions_changed` before it is applied | 400; 403; 409 `open_as_admin_active` |

Logged as `townwise.agent_suggestion { orgId, locationId, suggestionId, decision }` and `townwise.weekly_suggestions_switched { orgId, on }`; the worker’s pass logs `townwise.weekly_suggestions_pass { state, passes, suggested, none, budget, failed, ownerEvents, applied, early, ms }` (`state` `ran`, `off`, `paused`, `lease_held`, `lease_lost` or `deadline`), and `townwise.weekly_suggestions_location_failed { orgId, locationId }` for a location whose turn threw. Never a date, a note’s text, a rule’s words, a why, a prompt or an answer.

**Suggestions applied (D59 slice 3, `api/src/lab/suggestions.ts`, `api/src/calendar/early-pass.ts`, `api/src/lab/schedule.ts`).** The weekly answer's every item carries a `confidence` (`high`, `medium` or `low`; required in the schema sent, and an item without a known one is not sure), and a spotted event's `effect` says whether the title makes it a buyout (`closed`), a party alongside regular service (`more_guests`) or neither (`unknown`); the stored event suggestion keeps `effect: 'unknown'`, as an org admin still chooses. While `TOWNWISE_AGENT_AUTO` and the organization's `agentAuto` are on (read once a location's pass), the pass saves through the one writer (6.31, `sourceKind: 'weekly'`, as TownwiseAI, the why its own, none for an event) what it is sure of: a note rated `high`; a rule rated `high` whose schedule is a closure (`rule.add`, any other rule waits); and a spotted event rated `high` whose effect was chosen, as a private-event note with that effect, the event's dates and hours and its link (`fromEvent`), alongside regular service only with the guest count its title states. [CONFIRM: TownwiseAI saves a weekly suggestion it rated high on its own: a note, a closure rule, or a spotted private event whose effect it chose] Each saved one is stored `accepted` by `townwise_ai` under its note's or rule's id, so it is never listed, suggested or sent again; one the writer refuses (a person's note or rule decides its days differently, its key was used, D31's limit or words) is stored open as before, and so is one past the closure guards of a file read (11A.9): a closed note over 14 days, a closure rule closing more than 14 days in a row (one with no end closing every day included), or a closed note past 31 closed days the pass saved. An earlier weekly closure rule's closure key, in any status, drops a rule with that key as a file or sales suggestion's does (above), so one someone dismissed is not asked or saved again when the model words it again or moves its start. At most 2 rules are added a week per location, counted on the ledger over the last 7 days in any status, the sales history's included. [CONFIRM: at most 2 rules applied a week per location] Before the call, a closed weekday the sales history suggests (D46) whose evidence is sure, at least 90% of at least 8 counted days with no sales, and whose closure key no row holds, is added as TownwiseAI's rule (`sourceKind: 'sales'`, its why Townwise's own counts, “No sales on 12 of 12 counted Mondays in your sales history.”) and stored as the sales suggestion `accepted`; one someone undid keeps its key and is never added or suggested again. [CONFIRM: TownwiseAI adds a closed weekday on its own when at least 90% of at least 8 counted days had no sales] The pass line gains `applied` and `early`. **Brought forward:** a link or Google calendar refresh (the loop or Refresh now) whose switched events add a keyed event, or move one (its dates or hours), on a day from tomorrow to today plus 91 in the town marks the location (`tw_locations.earlyPass.wantedAt`, `$max`; logged `townwise.weekly_pass_brought_forward { calendarId, changed }`). After the week's locations, the worker's pass takes each marked location of an organization with weekly suggestions on: with `TOWNWISE_AGENT_AUTO`, `agentAuto` or `calendarTitlesToAi` off, or a pass of the location made since the mark, it clears the mark; with a pass made earlier that town day, it keeps it for tomorrow; otherwise it runs the location's pass (above) keyed by the town's day (`tw_suggestion_passes.week`), so a day makes at most one call per location, and clears the mark by compare-and-set on the value read. [CONFIRM: a calendar change brings the weekly pass forward at most once a day]

**TownwiseAI working on its own** (D59, `api/src/handlers/agent-changes.ts`, `api/src/agent/changes.ts`). GET .../agent also answers `agentAuto: { on, available, canChange }` (`on`, the organization's switch; `available`, `TOWNWISE_AGENT_AUTO` true and TownwiseAI reading files here; `canChange`, an org admin outside view-as), `noteSuggestions` (the events a file read wasn't sure of, open while they end today or later: `{ id, source: 'file', note, file: { ref, title } \| null, canDecide }`, the title and detail null under view-as), decided by any member through the suggested rules' accept (an empty body only) and dismiss routes below, and `waiting` (those and the suggested rules, counted). Activity gains `{ at, kind: 'agent_change', changeId, action, sourceKind, status, startDate, endDate, noteKind, weekdays, count, undoable, sourcePasted }`, never a title, why, file name or figure (UI review 2026-11-19: `sourcePasted`, on the log's rows too, is true for a `file` change whose file is text pasted on Your data, `files/items.ts` isPastedText: a text item with no adder of TownwiseAI's and no read it came from, filed in Notes and pasted text; the client then says “from text you pasted”) (`weekdays`, slice 3, the weekdays a note or rule covers, 0 being Sunday, null for every day, so a weekday rule does not read as every day; `count`, slice 2, is how many labels a calendar sort set, null otherwise; the log's view carries it too); `undoable` is false under view-as, once a person changed the target, and for a caller the action's role refuses, and a `sales_days.add` change shows in place of its upload. D59 slice 4: while both switches are on, `propose_note` saves a note whose `plain` the model set (the person's own message in the turn stated it) through the one writer as `sourceKind: 'chat'` with `sourceId` the conversation's id: as the person's note (`createdBy` the caller, the audit actor the caller) with TownwiseAI's `agent` mark, `why` null; never for staff open as admin (view-as sends no turn), never in a turn that read a file, a picture or a web page (`ToolContext.turn.readUntrusted`) or a calendar event's title or a note TownwiseAI wrote from a file or a calendar (`turn.readNotTyped`, set by `get_owner_calendar` once it lists an event and by `list_notes` and `get_day` once they list such a note), never at the note limit, and never past a person's conflicting note or a key used before (the card then shows as a proposal, and its Save note saves a person's note). Its result to the model says it was saved, and it is logged `townwise.chat_note_stated { orgId, locationId, conversationId, outcome }`. The activity lists it as `agent_change` with `sourceKind: 'chat'`, not as a saved proposal; its Undo is offered to the note's author or an org admin. [CONFIRM: a note a person states plainly in TownwiseAI chat saved with Undo, as theirs]

| Route | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /api/org/agent-auto { on, orgId? }` (`org.agent_auto.switch`, org admin, body `2kb`, `writes`, runs in open as admin with the tab's `orgId`) | 200 `{ agentAuto: { on } }`; a change records `org.agent_auto_switched { on }` before it is applied | 400; 403 (a member; `open_as_admin_refused` for staff turning it on; `view_as_read_only`); 409 `open_as_admin_active` |
| `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/agent/changes?before=` (`org.agent.changes`, member, no body, runs in open as admin) | 200 `{ changes: [{ id, at, action, sourceKind, sourceRef, sourcePasted, status, startDate, endDate, noteKind, weekdays, count, why, undoable, targetId }], next }`, newest first, 50 a page (`next`, `<ISO time>_<id>`, reads the older page; null on the last); `why` null under view-as | 400 (a bad cursor); 404 |
| `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/agent/changes/:changeId/undo` (`org.agent.change_undo`, member with the action's role: any member for a note, the file's adder or an org admin for a summary item, an org admin for sales days and (slice 2) a calendar's labels; no body; `writes`; runs in open as admin; refused under view-as) | 200 `{ change }`, now `undone` (a retry that finds it undone answers the same and records nothing); `agent.change_undone { locationId, action, sourceKind }` once | 400; 403; 404 (an unknown id, or another location's or organization's); 409 `changed_since` (a person changed the target since: the row reads `adopted`, and the target stays theirs), 409 `change_in_progress` (still being applied) |

Undo is ordered for retries: the row `applied` to `undoing` by compare-and-set, the target removed only while its `updatedAt` is still `targetUpdatedAt` (a note by compare-and-set; a summary item through the file removal; days through D34's upload removal), then `undoing` to `undone`. A target deleted since answers 200 and the row reads `undone`. Undo per calendar (slice 2, a `booking.label` change): first each `note.add` change from that calendar still applied goes through the same steps (one a person changed since reads `adopted` and stays theirs, and the calendar's undo goes on), then the labels that sort set that are still TownwiseAI's at its `bookingAt` are cleared (the events read as never labeled), and a confirm TownwiseAI made is taken back by compare-and-set (`bookings.state` back to `sorted`, so the calendar waits for Use for forecasts, or `bookings` removed when no row holds a label any more, so it reads unsorted and its page offers Sort again); a person's labels stay. While the calendar's sort still runs (`autoSort.status` `sorting`) the Undo answers 409 `change_in_progress`, and a sort writes no further note once its labels' change is no longer applied. The change is offered for Undo while any label of that sort is still TownwiseAI's. [CONFIRM: Undo per calendar takes back the notes, labels and confirm TownwiseAI made that nobody changed since] Undoing a change on a training day marks the location for a refit (14.6). A calibration already started is never undone. Logged as `townwise.agent_auto_switched { orgId, on }`, `townwise.agent_change_undone { orgId, locationId, changeId, action, removed }` and `townwise.agent_change_adopted { orgId, locationId, changeId, action }`. [CONFIRM: Undo removes only what TownwiseAI added, only while nobody changed it since] [CONFIRM: the panel's and switch's words]

**A calendar answers open questions (D59 slice 5, `api/src/calendar/closed-events.ts`, `api/src/calendar/answers.ts`, `api/src/agent/question-input.ts`).** Code only, no model call and nothing sent anywhere, so it runs whatever the weekly suggestions and calendar titles switches say. A calendar event counts as closed when it is keyed, all day, its dates make a closure note (Section 12) and its title plainly says closed: folded (accents and apostrophes dropped, other marks spaces), no `?` or digit, optionally "we are", "we're", "restaurant", "cafe", "shop", "store" or "business", then "closed", then only words from a fixed list: joining words, days, holidays and plain reasons a whole business shuts (the list is in the OpenSpec change's design decision 16), so "Closed-door meeting", "Closed session", "Closed for catering" or "Closed road" never count. A repeating event on a link or file calendar is never imported (`calendar/ics.ts`), so it answers nothing; Google expands repeats into single events. [DECISION NEEDED: whether repeating events on link and file calendars are expanded so they can answer a closure question] (22.3). GET .../agent's gap and likely-closed questions treat a day such an event covers as explained, as a covering closure note does. The location's open closure suggestions (D46's file and sales rules, D53's weekly notes and rules, D59's file note suggestions) are checked for the whole location right after `followLinkedNotes` at every switch point (the add, including D60's import of a stored calendar file, the refresh loop and Refresh now), after a file read, after a sales upload (the route, staff setup and a sales export read into days), and after each weekly pass whatever its outcome: a dated closure rule or closure note is answered when every day it closes is covered; a standing closed weekday when the next 8 days of each of its weekdays from tomorrow are covered; never a yearly season, a private event or buyout, more or fewer guests, a spotted event or a follow-up; and never one a person's own note or rule decides differently on one of its days (owner beats agent). While `TOWNWISE_AGENT_AUTO` and `agentAuto` are on, the answer is first saved through the one writer as TownwiseAI's (`sourceKind: 'calendar'`, `onBehalfOf` the adder of the answering calendar, no why): a closure note with no title for each answering event whose days closure notes do not all close yet (a note over part of it, a weekday-only note or a booking's note does not count), linked to the event so D53's follow-up proposes its move or removal, and the same for the events over the days a current question asks about (so the lab reads what the panel stops asking; a history day wants a refit); or, for a standing weekday, its own rule (not counted in the 2 a week). At most 20 notes a run; a suggestion is answered only once everything it needs is written and still applied, or was made before by another source and is still applied, so a conflict, a limit, or a note a person undid or changed leaves it open. Undo on a calendar's booking labels takes back only the sort's own notes, not these. Removing a calendar, or its Google access ending, takes back as TownwiseAI the closure notes its answers saved that nobody changed since (`agent.change_undone`, logged `townwise.calendar_answers_taken_back { locationId, calendarId, undone }`). While either switch is off, nothing is saved, a standing closed weekday stays open, and the forecast reads those days as it did while the question was open; the Calendar's Make a note puts the closure in. A location deleted during a run keeps nothing it wrote. The suggestion then reads `answered` (6.27). A run that answered any records `agent.calendar_answered { locationId, count }` as TownwiseAI (each note or rule also records `agent.change_applied`) and logs `townwise.calendar_answers { locationId, answered, notes, rules, held }` (failures `townwise.calendar_answers_failed { locationId }`); never a title, uid or date. The activity words each calendar change "from your calendar". [DECISION NEEDED: whether a calendar event that plainly says open answers a likely-closed question] (22.3).

**Suggested closure rules** (`suggest-closure-rules`, D46; `api/src/handlers/rule-suggestions.ts`, `api/src/agent/rule-suggestion-views.ts`). GET .../agent’s `ruleSuggestions` and GET .../rules’ `suggested` (10.16), built by one function, list the location’s open file and sales suggestions, oldest first, then the sales history’s not stored yet. A `RuleSuggestion` is `{ id, source: 'file' | 'sales', text, schedule, scheduleSummary, file: { ref, title } | null, evidence: { noSalesCount, weekdayCount, lastSalesDate } | null, canDecide }`: `text` is Townwise’s words from the schedule (`closureRuleText`: “Closed on Mondays”, “Closed on Mondays and Tuesdays”, “Closed Jan 4 to Mar 31, 2027”, “Closed on Mondays, Jan 4 to Mar 31, 2027”, “Closed Jan 1 to Mar 31 every year”, “Closed on Mondays, Jan 1 to Mar 31 every year”), never the file’s or a model’s; `file` is a file suggestion’s file, its Your data ref (`f_` or `u_`) and its name (`title` null under view-as), or null once the file is deleted; `evidence` is a sales suggestion’s; and `canDecide` is true outside view-as. Both reads write nothing (7.3).

- **From the sales history.** `weekdayEvidence` (`api/src/agent/questions.ts`) counts each weekday’s days as the questions count them (from the first day with sales in the window, in weeks with sales on another day, turned-off days left out), a day having sales when it has guests or net sales. A weekday is suggested when at least 60% of at least 4 counted days have no sales and its last 4 counted days have none, so a past or seasonal pattern never becomes a standing rule; `lastSalesDate` is its last counted day with sales, or null. [CONFIRM: 60% of at least 4 days, and the last 4 counted days without sales] The suggestion is a closure on that weekday with no end, starting the day after `lastSalesDate` (at the first day with sales in the window when it had none), so it never covers a past day with recorded sales, guests or net sales. None is suggested when the weekday’s earlier weekday question was answered `open`, `not_sure` or `other` (an earlier `closed` does not stop it). It is listed as `sales_weekday_{d}` (`d` 0 for Sunday to 6) while no suggestion holds its closure key, under its stored id while that one is open, and not at all once it is decided. [CONFIRM: the sales history suggests standing closed weekdays]
- **From a file**, the read’s actions store them (11A.9).
- **One per rule.** Each has a closure key (6.27), unique per location in any status. None is made when a closure rule of the location already covers it (for a standing one, an ongoing closure on the same weekdays or more; otherwise one with the same key), or when a rule with a schedule has its words in any case. A rule with the same words and no schedule closes nothing, so it does not block one; confirming then answers 409 `rule_exists`.
- **Nothing changes until someone decides.** The forecast read never reads `tw_agent_suggestions` (14.5): only an accepted suggestion has a rule. Pending ones don’t count toward the location’s 30 rules. [CONFIRM: suggested rules don't count toward a location's 30 until confirmed]

| Route | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `POST .../agent/rule-suggestions/:suggestionId/accept` (`org.agent.rule_suggestion_accept`, member, body `2kb`, `writes`, runs in open as admin), `{}` to confirm or `{ rule: { text, schedule } }` to save an edit (`text` at most 2,000 characters before `ruleTextOf`; `schedule` a `RuleSchedule`, or null or left out for none; checked as P29’s add checks them) | 200 `{ suggestion: { id, status: 'accepted' }, rule: Rule \| null }`: the rule (10.16, `addedVia: 'townwise_ai'`) written as the caller with the suggestion’s id, so a retry or a second tab writes it once; one already accepted answers what it wrote (`rule` null once that rule is deleted) | 400 `invalid_request` (the body, a malformed id, or a text or schedule the rules refuse); 403 `view_as_read_only`; 404 (another organization’s or location’s, unknown, a weekly suggestion, dismissed, expired, open with its end before today in the town, or a `sales_weekday_` id whose evidence no longer holds); 409 `already_decided` with `rule`, the stored rule (a rule already under the suggestion’s id has other words or another schedule than this request would write); 409 `rule_limit`, `rule_exists` (it stays open); 429 |
| `POST .../agent/rule-suggestions/:suggestionId/dismiss {}` (`org.agent.rule_suggestion_dismiss`, as accept) | 200 `{ suggestion: { id, status: 'dismissed' }, rule: null }`, or the accepted state with its rule when an accept got there first, also when an accept wrote the rule but never marked it accepted (the dismiss then finishes the accept, recording `agent.suggestion_accepted`) | 400; 403 `view_as_read_only`; 404 as accept; 429 |

- `:suggestionId` is an ObjectId or `sales_weekday_[0-6]`. Deciding `sales_weekday_{d}` recomputes its evidence (404 when it no longer holds, as for a stale question), then stores it open (`source: 'sales'`, its closure key and evidence) under a new id, or finds the row already holding its key (a file’s, or a racing decide’s), and goes on with that row, so two tabs end with one row and one rule. A weekly suggestion is 404 here before any write, and the weekly routes answer 404 for a file or sales suggestion.
- No transactions: Confirm and Edit write the rule through the rules code (`addRule`) with the suggestion’s id, recorded `rule.created { via: 'townwise_ai' }`, then mark the suggestion accepted by compare-and-set from `open` or `dismissed`, and only the request whose compare-and-set lands records `agent.suggestion_accepted { locationId, suggestionId, type: 'rule', source, edited }`, `edited` worked out from the stored rule against the suggestion, not from the request. A Confirm racing an Edit leaves one rule, and the request that lost answers 409 `already_decided`. Dismiss marks it dismissed by compare-and-set from `open` and records `agent.suggestion_dismissed { locationId, suggestionId, type: 'rule', source }` once. [CONFIRM: any member confirms, edits or dismisses a suggested closure rule; weekly suggestions stay with org admins]
- Logged as `townwise.agent_suggestion { orgId, locationId, suggestionId, decision, source, edited }` (`edited` on an accept only). Never the rule’s words, its schedule, a file name or an evidence date.

**Calendar event suggestions** (`calendar-event-suggestions`, D53; contract `docs/portal/tuning-chat.md` section 9). Three more kinds share the routes above. GET .../agent’s `suggestions` also lists them with `why` null and `words`, the card’s one sentence, written by the server at read time and never stored: `{ id, type: 'event', words, note, event, calendar: [], createdAt }` (`note` is the note accepting writes, a `private_event` with effect `unknown` and the guest count to prefill; `event` is `{ calendarId, title, titleHidden, startDate, endDate, startTime, endTime }`, the title read from the live event row, or “Google calendar event” with `titleHidden` true to staff under view-as or open as admin when the calendar is a Google one (D39), and no UID); `{ id, type: 'move', words, noteId, note, from, calendar: [], createdAt }` (`note` as accepting leaves it, `from` the note’s dates and hours now); and `{ id, type: 'remove', words, noteId, note, calendar: [], createdAt }`. A follow-up’s words come from the note’s kind and dates alone, never a title (“The private event on Sat, Jun 13 moved to Sat, Jun 20 on your calendar.”, “The private event on Sat, Jun 13 is no longer on your calendar.”); an event’s read “From your calendar: {title}, Sat, Jun 13, 6 pm to 10 pm”, and to staff on a Google calendar “From your calendar: Google calendar event, Sat, Jun 13, 6 pm to 10 pm. Ask your client’s team what this event is.” The list neither shows nor counts one that rests on something now gone: a `move` or `remove` whose note is gone, any of the three whose calendar is gone, and a spotted event whose live row is gone or at other dates, or that another note now covers (a note other than its own linked to the same event, or a private-event or closure note over its days). `weeklySuggestions` also carries `calendarTitles` (the organization’s titles switch, true when never set).

| Route | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `POST .../agent/suggestions/:suggestionId/accept { effect: 'closed' \| 'more_guests', expectedGuests: integer 1 to 20,000 \| null }` on an `event` (strict; the one accept with a body) | 200 as accept above, `note` the `private_event` note written as that admin with the suggestion’s id: the event’s dates, its hours when Section 12 allows them (else all day), `weekdays` null, `detail` null (never a title), the chosen effect and count, and `fromEvent` set; the server reads the event again first, so a retry or a second tab writes one note | 400 `invalid_request` (`more_guests` with no count, or any other body); 404 (its calendar is gone: it is set `expired`); 409 `event_changed` (the event is gone, no longer keyed or at other dates, or another note now covers it as above: it is set `expired`); 409 `note_limit` (it stays open) |
| `POST .../agent/suggestions/:suggestionId/accept {}` on a `move` or `remove` | 200 as accept above. A `move` sets only the note’s dates and hours, its link’s dates and `updatedAt` (`NoteStore.moveIf`), never writing back its kind, guests or detail, and answers the note as moved, recording `note.updated`; a `remove` deletes the note (`removeIf`, `note` null), recording `note.deleted`. Both are compare-and-set on the note’s `updatedAt` as the follow-up recorded it, after reading the suggestion again; it is marked accepted only while its own last write is the one the accept read, or, when the accept’s own note write landed, from `expired` too (a refresh may expire it meanwhile), so `agent.suggestion_accepted` is written once and a retry answers accepted; a retry after the accept’s own write (the note is at the move’s dates with a later `updatedAt`, or already gone) is accepted with no second note event | 403; 404 (as accept, and its calendar is gone, or for a `move` its note: it is set `expired`); 409 `note_changed` (the note’s `updatedAt` differs, say after someone edited its guest count, or a refresh rewrote the follow-up since the accept read it; the suggestion stays open and the next refresh recomputes it) |
| `POST .../agent/suggestions/:suggestionId/dismiss {}` on any of the three | 200 as dismiss above | as dismiss; 404 also when its calendar (or, for a follow-up, its note) is gone, which sets it `expired` |
| `PATCH /api/org/weekly-suggestions/calendar-titles { on, orgId? }` (`org.weekly_suggestions.calendar_titles`, org admin, body `2kb`, `writes`, runs in open as admin with the tab’s `orgId`, D25) | 200 `{ calendarTitles: { on } }`; a change records `org.calendar_titles_ai_changed` before it is applied, and the same state again writes nothing | 400; 403 (a member; and `open_as_admin_refused` for `on: true` while open as admin, whatever the current state, after the tab check); 409 `open_as_admin_active` |

Only an org admin outside view-as accepts or dismisses any of them (staff open as admin borrow the role, D25), and nothing changes until one does. The titles switch is on unless an org admin turned it off; staff open as admin may turn it off and not on, since turning it on is the organization’s consent to send its customers’ names to Anthropic. While the organization’s weekly suggestions and its titles switch are both on, the weekly call also sends each location’s keyed owner-calendar events of the next 91 days, soonest first, at most 150, leaving out events linked to a note, events an earlier `event` suggestion named in any status, a Google calendar’s events unless its connection is not revoked and holds `titlesNotice: 1`, which a connect stores only from the explainer that says titles go weekly (D39), and a file’s or link’s events unless the calendar holds `titlesNotice: 1`, which an add stores only from the Your calendars popover that says so (P28), so a calendar added or connected from an older screen (a stale tab, an older app) comes in by being added or connected again (`WEEKLY_TITLES_NOTICE`, 10.18). It may answer up to 5 `event` suggestions beside its 5 notes and rules, each kept only for a ref the request sent, with no private-event or closure note over its days, its dates and hours from the event, a guest count only when the sent title states that number beside a guest word (N guests, people, ppl or pax; party of N; for N), and none of the model’s words. On a pass that sent owner events, every private-event note or rule, every note or rule citing no town calendar entry the request sent, and every note or rule whose why, detail or words repeat a word of a sent title or hold 7 digits in a row is dropped: words are compared after NFKD with marks stripped, lowercased, with punctuation inside a word removed and one trailing s off, each pair of words side by side also joined, and a title word counts from 3 characters, apart from `GENERIC_TITLE_WORDS`, `COMMON_WORDS` and the words of a town entry the item cites. The title of a card is never stored or logged.

Logged as `townwise.calendar_titles_switched { orgId, on }`; a follow-up run logs `townwise.calendar_followups { calendarId, moved, gone, expired }`, only when one is non-zero, and `townwise.calendar_followup_failed { calendarId }` (warn) when it fails, which never fails the refresh; the worker’s `townwise.weekly_suggestions_pass` also carries `ownerEvents`, how many owner-calendar events its calls sent, summed. Never a title, a UID, a calendar’s name or an owner event’s date or guest count.

### 10.13 Estimates

People in town and "How Townwise estimates" (13.2), and the published forecast (14.4). All three are `member` GETs in `TOWNWISE_ROUTES` with no body and no route limiter (`app:api-ceiling` still applies), allowed during view-as, where the chain logs `townwise.view_as_read`. None logs or audits anything. The build contract, with every field, is `docs/portal/estimates.md`; the staff routes that import and publish forecast runs are in 10.7.

| Method and path | Policy | Request | Success | Extra errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/people-in-town?from=&to=` | member | `from` and `to` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, exactly those two keys; `from` on or after 2010-01-01; `from <= to`; at most 92 days counting both ends; `to` at most 400 days after the server’s UTC day | 200 `PeopleInTownWindow` | 400 `invalid_request`, with no field details; 404 |
| `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/estimates/about` | member | | 200 `EstimatesAbout` | 400 (malformed id); 404 |
| `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/forecast?from=&to=` | member | as people in town (at most 92 days, so today and the next 91 days are one read, D42) and `from` at most 400 days before the server’s UTC day | 200 `ForecastWindow` (14.4) | 400 `invalid_request`; 404 |

[Build note: D52 (release A, 2026-11-17): the forecast read’s days and weeks carry `outlook` (14.4); its limits are unchanged, 92 days a read, `from` at most 400 days back and `to` at most 400 days ahead, so a month in 2027 on the Calendar is still one read of its grid’s 42 days.]

```ts
interface PeopleInTownWindow {
  available: boolean;                  // false only for a town outside the twelve
  reason: 'town_not_researched' | null;
  from: string; to: string;
  town: { name: string; state: string; kind: 'college' | 'seasonal' | 'event' | null };
  timeZone: string;                    // the town's IANA zone
  periods: {                           // consecutive days with identical components, merged
    from: string; to: string; fromWeekday: Weekday; toWeekday: Weekday;
    termState: 'in_session' | 'finals' | 'between_terms' | 'summer_session' | 'unknown';
    termLabel: string | null;          // 'Fall term classes', 'Between terms (from the term dates)'
    termSourceIds: string[];
    headcount: { low: number; high: number; sourceIds: string[]; excludes: string[] } | null;
    headcountWhy: 'no_population' | 'visitors_unknown' | 'no_term_dates' | 'no_enrollment' | null;
    events: { id: string; title: string; kind: 'event' | 'holiday'; attendanceHigh: number | null; sourceIds: string[] }[];
  }[];
  season: { month: string; countyFoodServiceJobsIndex: number; baseYear: number; county: string; sourceIds: string[] }[];
  visitors: { month: string; label: string; perDayAverage: number; sourceIds: string[] }[];
  yourHistory: {                       // this location's open regular days with a known term state
    metric: 'guests' | 'netSales';     // mean: whole guests, or whole US dollars
    cells: { state: TermState; weekday: Weekday; days: number; mean: number | null }[];   // mean null under 3 days
    first: string | null; last: string | null;
  };
  sources: { id: string; label: string; url: string; confidence: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low' | null }[];
  caveats: string[];
}

interface EstimatesAbout {
  version: string;
  card: { estimates: string; inputs: string[]; cannotSee: string[]; limits: string[]; checked: string; whoCanSee: string };
  location: { name: string; town: { name: string; state: string } };
  today: { date: string; weekday: Weekday; timeZone: string; approximate: boolean };
  forecast: { run: ForecastRunView | null; live: LiveAccuracy | null };   // the newest published run (14.4) and its own live accuracy, or both null
  calendar: { researched: boolean; covers: { from: string; to: string } | null };
  people: { headcountInputs: ('residents' | 'studentHousing' | 'enrollment' | 'housingCloses' | 'eventAttendance' | 'visitors')[]; sources: PeopleSource[] };
}
```

TownwiseAI reads the same window through `get_people_in_town`, the calendar through `get_town_calendar` and the published forecast through `get_forecast` (`tuning-chat.md` section 4), and its "today" is the town's local date (13.2). Home and Analytics keep the device's local date; both are Eastern for the twelve towns.

[Build note: from the calendar change (D30) the forecast read includes the location's notes from the town's today on (14.5). Each `ForecastDayView` adds `model: { status, low, mid, high }` (the run's own figures, always present, equal to the day's when no note changed it), `noteGuests` (the guests notes add on an open day, or the buyouts' party on a booked day; 0 when none) and `moreNotes` (note reasons past the first 6, still counted); from the business rules (D31), `moreRules` (rule reasons past the first 6, still counted). A reason is `{ kind: ReasonKind | 'note', label, effectPct, sources, note: { id, guests, outcome } | null }`: `note` is null on the run's reasons, and a note's reason has `effectPct` null and `sources` empty. A `ForecastWeekView` adds `noteGuests`, and its `low`, `mid`, `high` and `openDays` shift by its days' note and rule changes (14.5, Weeks). The status codes are unchanged, and the read still logs and stores nothing.]

[Build note: from the reason effects change (14.4) each reason also carries `effect: { direction: 'more' | 'fewer' | 'same', pct, basis: 'model' | 'history', days } | null`, set on the run's reasons from the town's today on and null on a note's or a rule's reason and on every day before today; since D40 the effect also carries `averageGuests` (14.4). The range limit went from 31 to 42 days, so the Calendar can read a six-week grid at once; `get_forecast` keeps 31.]

[Build note: from D42 (phase 1 of `autonomous-forecasts`) the range limit went from 42 to 92 days, as people in town, so the next 91 days are one read; the Calendar keeps reading six-week grids, and `get_forecast` reads 92 too (14.4). `ForecastWindow` adds `accuracy`, each `ForecastDayView` `scored` and each `ForecastRunView` `engine` (14.4). The status codes are unchanged, and the read still logs and stores nothing. The ranged read of 14.6, which changes no answer, comes in a later phase.]

### 10.14 Your data

The list and the actions of P26 (D28). All members; view-as lists with names hidden and is refused every write (403 `view_as_read_only`); every non-GET also passes `townwise:writes`. Another organization’s location or item answers 404, exactly like an unknown one. Names travel only in JSON bodies, never in a path, a log line or an audit event. The full table, with each route’s errors, is `api/README.md` (Your data).

| id | Method and path | Who | Body | Limiter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `org.data.list` | `GET /api/org/data?locationId=&after=` (D59: also answers `agentAuto`, whether TownwiseAI reads a file added here on its own) | member | | |
| `org.data.get` | `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/data/:ref` | member | | |
| `org.data.update` | `PATCH /api/org/locations/:locationId/data/:ref` | the person who added it or an org admin | 2 KB `{ enabled }` or `{ title }` | |
| `org.data.replace` | `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/data/:ref/replace` | the person who added it or an org admin | 2 KB `{ fileId }` | |
| `org.data.ai_read` | `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/data/:ref/ai` | the person who added it or an org admin (an org admin only, for a Townwise staff upload) | 2 KB `{}` | |
| `org.data.calendar` | `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/data/:ref/calendar` | member (as Your calendars) | 2 KB `{}` | |
| `org.data.remove` | `DELETE /api/org/locations/:locationId/data/:ref` | an upload: org admins; a file: the person who added it or an org admin | | |
| `org.data.text` | `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/data/text` | member | 32 KB `{ title, text, aiAuto? }` (D59 slice 4: `true` lets TownwiseAI read the text on its own) | `files` |
| `org.chat.item_proposal.get` | `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/chat/:conversationId/item-proposals/:proposalId` | the conversation’s author | | |
| `org.chat.item_proposal` | `POST` the same path | the conversation’s author | 2 KB `{ action }` | `files` |

- `ref` is `u_` plus an upload’s id or `f_` plus a stored file’s id. The list merges `tw_uploads` and the `tw_files` rows that wrote no days (a stored file that wrote days shows once, as its upload, with its file’s actions), newest first by time and id, 100 a page, with `next` as the cursor `<ISO time>_<24 hex id>`. Each item has its kind (`daily_totals` or a file kind), how it arrived (`browser`, `file`, `staff`, `townwise_ai`), who added it (a current email, “Townwise staff” or “Deleted person”), its size, `enabled`, its state, its days (`count`, `inUse`, `firstDate`, `lastDate`), when and by whom it was last edited (`editedAt`, `editedByEmail`, named as who added it) and what the caller may do (`canTurnOff`, `canDelete`, `canEdit`).
- **One item** (`org.data.get`, P27) answers `{ item }` exactly as the caller’s list shows it, plus `calendar` (D60, below). An item the list leaves out answers 404 like an unknown one: every stored file while stored files are off, a stored file that wrote days (its upload is the item), a file being deleted and someone else’s unfinished upload; a malformed ref is 400. An upload answers with stored files off. A read: it logs nothing and records nothing.
- **Turn off or on** sets or clears `disabledAt` and `disabledBy` in one update on an upload (6.6) or a reference item (6.11), then records `data.turned_off` or `data.turned_on`. Asking for the state it is already in changes nothing and records nothing. A sales file that wrote no days cannot be turned off (400 `invalid_request`); an item Townwise is still reading is 409 `item_busy`; anyone but the person who added it or an org admin (an org admin only, for a Townwise staff upload) is 403.
- **Rename** (`{ title }`, 1 to 120 characters, trimmed) is for a reference item kept with its original still stored, by the people who may turn it off (403 otherwise). The new name is the title made a file name as Paste text makes one (slashes to hyphens, control characters and runs of spaces to one space, `sanitizeName`), with the current name’s extension (from its last dot, unless that is its first character) after it unless the title already ends with it in any case. An upload, a sales file, an item whose original is gone and a title of no words are 400 `invalid_request`; an item not kept is 409 `item_busy`, and so is an item while an edit of it is being saved (a live claim, below), because the edit’s file keeps its own name and the rename would be lost. It is a compare-and-set on the item still being kept with its original and with no live claim, so a purge’s label is never overwritten and no rename lands while an edit is being saved. The same name changes nothing and records nothing; otherwise it records `data.renamed`. 503 `files_unavailable` while stored files are off.
- **Edit** saves the edited content as a new file and puts it in the item’s place. The browser stores it through the chunked upload (10.11) as a `reference` file, then calls `replace { fileId }`. The item (A) must be one that can be renamed, and `canEdit` also needs no edit being saved (no live claim: A’s `replacedBy` absent, or its claim stale). The new file (B) must be at the same location (another location’s, another organization’s or an unknown id is 404), kept for reference, stored by the caller in the last 24 hours, not A, with its original, and in no other item’s place (400 `invalid_request` otherwise). There are no multi-document transactions (D17), so three steps run in an order a retry finishes: (1) a compare-and-set claims A for B, setting `replacedBy` to B and `replacedAt` to now (already B: a retry, which renews the claim; another file: below); (2) a compare-and-set gives B A’s `uploadedBy`, `uploaderRole`, `uploadedAt`, `byStaff`, `openAsAdminGrantId`, `addedVia`, `disabledAt` and `disabledBy`, with `replaces` A, `editedAt` and `editedBy` (and `editedByStaff` open as admin), while B is still kept with its original, in no item’s place and replacing nothing or A; if B changed meanwhile A’s claim is undone and the call answers 404 or 400; (3) A is removed as `DELETE /files/:fileId` removes a file, a removal that stopped after its claim being finished. A gone whose place B took answers B. It answers 200 `{ item }`, B’s, whose ref is `f_` plus B’s id, and records `data.edited` (target B, `replaces` A) when it found A still there, so a retry once done records nothing. **A claim a stopped call left.** A claim is live for two minutes (`REPLACE_CLAIM_MS`); an older one, or one with no `replacedAt`, is stale. When A is claimed for another file X, the edit reads X once: X gone or being deleted can never take A’s place, so the claim is released at once (a compare-and-set on `replacedBy` still X) and A is claimed again, once; so is a stale claim whose X has not taken A’s place (X is left as it is). A stale claim whose X did take A’s place (`replaces` A) left A behind after step 2: the edit removes A as step 3 does and answers 409 `item_changed`, B staying a new item. A live claim answers 409 `item_changed`. An edited item keeps its first upload time (B takes A’s `uploadedAt`), so retention (365 days, 11A.7) still counts from when the item was first added. If the item is deleted while an edit is being saved, the edit can still take its place (the last save wins). B keeps its own name, kind and size; an edit with no change is refused when its upload completes, 409 `file_duplicate`, and B counts toward the caps (11A.2) until A goes. 503 `files_unavailable` while stored files are off. [CONFIRM: editing replaces the item with a new upload that keeps who added it, when and its on/off state]
- **Let TownwiseAI read it** (`org.data.ai_read`, D34, 11A.9) queues a read of the item’s stored file: an `f_` item’s, or for a `u_` upload the file it was read from. In order: 400 `invalid_request` for a body that is not `{}` or a malformed ref; 404 for another organization’s or an unknown location or item; 503 `files_unavailable` while stored files are off; 503 `ai_unavailable` while reading with TownwiseAI is off; 403 `forbidden` for anyone but the people who may turn the item off; 409 `ai_read_running` while a read is queued or reading; 200 `{ item }` unchanged once a read is done (a second press records nothing); 400 `invalid_request` for an upload with no stored file, a file whose original was deleted, or one Townwise is still uploading or reading. A compare-and-set queues it (a fresh `ai`, 6.11), so of two presses one wins and the other answers as above; then it records `file.ai_read_requested`, wakes the reader and answers 202 `{ item }`. Before the write, 429 `ai_read_queue_full` while the organization already has 10 reads queued or reading; the route's own limiter (`townwise:ai-reads`, 10.8) answers 429 `rate_limited`, or 503 `unavailable` while Redis is down. A failed, skipped or undone read may be asked for again. Every item carries `canAiRead` (the same rules, outside view-as, with stored files and reading on) and `ai`: null until asked, then `{ status, reason, partial, kind, summary, facts, daysCut, notes, notesSkipped, daysWritten, daysAlreadyHad, uploadRef, itemRef, daysReason, itemReason, calibration, canUndo, rulesSuggested, rulesWaiting }`, with `kind`, `summary`, `facts` and `daysCut` only once done and `summary` and `facts` null under view-as (once the original is deleted, the summary is empty and the facts none). What the read made, once recorded (11A.9): `notes` (`{ id, title, startDate, endDate }[]`, the notes it created that still exist, each with its dates as they are now and the title of the event it was made from; titles null under view-as or once the original is deleted), `notesSkipped` (`{ duplicate, cap, invalid, guard }`), `daysWritten` (the days its upload held once written), `daysAlreadyHad` (verified days the location already had), `uploadRef` (`u_<id>`) and `itemRef` (`f_<id>`, its summary item) while they exist, `daysReason` and `itemReason` (why it wrote no days or kept no summary item, 11A.9's codes, else null), and `calibration` (`{ status, id }`, 11A.9); `[]`, null, 0, 0, null, null, null, null and null before that and once undone. D46: `rulesSuggested`, how many suggested closure rules the read stored, and `rulesWaiting`, how many of them are still open (what an undo removes); 0 and 0 before that and once undone. `canUndo` is true outside view-as for the person who asked or an org admin, on a done read that made a note, an upload, a summary item or a suggested rule, or on a failed or skipped read whose actions began (a plan with no outcome). Every item also carries `fromAiRead`: on an upload or a summary item a TownwiseAI read made, the ref of the item it was read from (`f_<id>`, or the `u_<id>` of a file that wrote days of its own), and null otherwise, once that file is gone, and while stored files are off; such an upload has `via: 'townwise_ai'` and kind `daily_totals`.
- **Undo what TownwiseAI made** (`org.data.ai_undo`, `DELETE .../data/:ref/ai`, D34, 11A.9) removes what the read of the item's stored file made: the notes it made from the file (one the person since edited goes too: an edit keeps its `source`), its upload with the days that upload still holds (only days it added, since it never replaces one; days a later upload replaced stay), through the same upload delete as below, and its summary item (an edit of it too), through the file removal. Its suggested closure rules (D46) still open go one at a time, each by compare-and-set, except one whose rule a confirm already wrote under its id, which is finished as accepted (recording `agent.suggestion_accepted` by the person undoing); accepted and dismissed ones stay, so a confirmed rule stays the team’s and a dismissal is remembered. [CONFIRM: undoing a read removes its suggested rules still waiting and keeps rules already confirmed] A calibration it started is not undone: it runs on, and publishes only as any calibration does (staff's forecasts switch, 14.4); the answer names it. The person who asked for the read or an org admin; view-as refused by the chain. In order: 400 `invalid_request` for a malformed ref; 404 for another organization's or an unknown location or item; 503 `files_unavailable` while stored files are off (it works while reading with TownwiseAI is off); 400 `nothing_to_undo` for an item with no stored file or no read; 403 `forbidden` for anyone else; 409 `ai_read_running` while the read is queued or reading; 200 `{ item, calibrationKept: null }` unchanged once it is undone (a retry after it finished records nothing); 400 `nothing_to_undo` for a read whose actions never began (no plan) or whose recorded outcome made nothing (no note, upload, summary item or suggested rule). A read that failed or was skipped after its actions began can be undone, since it may have written some. With no multi-document transactions the order lets a retry finish the work: a compare-and-set marks the read `undoing` (6.11) while it ended (done, failed or skipped) with a plan; the notes, uploads and summary items that carry the file as their `source` are removed, each by filter, so a step runs twice harmlessly (and anything an earlier attempt of the read left goes too); then a compare-and-set marks the read `undone` and clears its actions and its answer (`ai.result`), and only that call records `file.ai_undone { locationId, notes, days, items, suggestions }` (what it removed) and logs `townwise.ai_read_undone { fileId, notes, days, items, suggestions }`. Answers 200 `{ item, calibrationKept }`, `calibrationKept` the id of the calibration the read started (left running), else null. The read may then be asked for again.
- **Delete** of an upload (org admins only, even a member’s own, D16): its stored file, then the days it still holds (days a later upload replaced stay), then its record last, so a retry finds it; answers `{ deletedDays, deletedFiles }` and records `sales.upload_deleted`. Delete of a file works as `DELETE /files/:fileId` and answers `{ deletedDays: 0, deletedFiles: 1 }`.
- **Paste text** keeps text of 1 to 10,000 characters with a title of 1 to 120 characters as a `.txt` reference item under the stored-files caps and retention (11A.2, 11A.7); 503 `files_unavailable` while stored files are off. The list, turning an upload off or on, and deleting an upload work with stored files off, because an upload holds only days.
- **A calendar file** (D60). One item’s view (never the list’s) carries `calendar`: `{ status: 'added', calendarId, label, eventCount }` while the calendar the stored file made exists (found by its `fromFileId`, also when the file’s own record was never written), `{ status: 'removed' }` once it was removed, `{ status: 'refused', reason, retry }` with the file’s code and whether Try again may mend it (`calendar_limit` or `unavailable`, with the original still stored), or null. `org.data.calendar` imports the file again: 400 `invalid_request` for a body that is not `{}`, a malformed ref or an item that is no calendar file; 404 for another organization’s or an unknown location or item; 503 `files_unavailable` while stored files are off; then 200 `{ item }` with its `calendar` as it is after: a retry refused again says so there, and an item added, removed or refused for good answers as it is, so a double press never imports a file twice. It records `owner_calendar.added` when it adds one (10.18). UI review 2026-11-19 (Import as a calendar, P27): it also imports, for the first time, a calendar file kept before D60, one with no import record and no calendar, kept for reference with its original (an `.ics` or `.ical` file of kind `other`); the calendar’s unique index on the file’s id still holds two presses at once to one calendar, and one whose original was deleted answers 400 `invalid_request`. Such a file’s `calendar` stays null until then.
- **Folders and calendars** (D61, `api/src/data/folders.ts`). Every item (on the list and on its own) carries `folder`: `sales`, `calendars`, `menus`, `inventory`, `staffing`, `notes`, `other` or `unsorted`, from what Townwise knows of it and never its name: an upload or a sales file (`purpose: 'history'`) is `sales`; a file with a `calendarImport` other than `refused`/`not_calendar` is `calendars`; else the file’s own `folder` (6.11); else `notes` for text TownwiseAI kept (`addedVia` or `source`); else a done read’s `kind` (`sales`, `calendar` to `calendars`, `menu` to `menus`, `inventory`, `staffing`, `other`); else `unsorted`. The list also answers `calendars`, the same on every page: the scope’s calendars (the location’s, or every location’s without `locationId`, each location’s oldest first), each `{ id, locationId, label, kind, host, eventCount, skippedRepeating, status, lastSuccessAt, createdAt }` as Your calendars shows it (never an address; to staff a Google calendar is “Google calendar”). A stored file a calendar was imported from (that calendar’s `fromFileId`) is left out of `items` while the calendar exists, so it shows once, as the calendar; a page may then hold fewer than 100 items with more to come. The file’s own page still answers (`folder: 'calendars'`, `calendar.status: 'added'`). A client older than D61 ignores both fields.
- Downloads keep the existing routes (10.11) and their log line; a GET never writes, so a download records no audit event (7.3).

[Build note: D49 (P27) the single item's read, `GET .../data/:ref`, adds `ai.events` to a done read: `{ title, startDate, endDate, kind, effect, expectedGuests, noteId }[]`, the events TownwiseAI read, `effect` one of `closed`, `more`, `fewer` or `unknown`, `noteId` the note made from it while that note exists (else null), `title` null under view-as, and an empty list once the original is deleted (its events go with it). The list (`GET /api/org/data`) and a PATCH's answer leave it out, so a client never takes the events from either.]

### 10.15 The lab callback (`/lab`)

The forecast lab's job (D27, `modeling/lab`) calls back to the API on two routes mounted at `/lab`, outside `/api` and outside the kit's auth: the job holds no session and no secret, only its calibration's id. It signs in with its managed identity: before each call it asks Entra for a token for the lab callback app (`townwise-lab-callback`, a credential-free app registration whose only role is to be this audience) as the lab identity, and the API (`api/src/lab/caller.ts`) checks the token's RS256 signature against the tenant's keys, its issuer (`https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0`), its audience (the app's client id), its tenant (`tid`) and its caller (`oid`, the lab identity's object id), with 5 seconds of clock tolerance. Any principal in the tenant can get a token for the app; only the lab identity's passes. Locally the job sends the API process's own random secret instead, compared in constant time. They are the only routes outside `/auth` and `/api` (`api/test/routes.test.ts`), and sit outside `TOWNWISE_ROUTES`. The identity token is not tied to one calibration, so the input is fetched once, by compare-and-set, and the result is bound to that fetch: the input answer carries a fresh result token in `X-Townwise-Result-Token`, stored only as its sha256 (6.23), and a result needs it with the identity token; a second fetch, by anyone, is 404. Whoever fetches first gets the result token, so code running as the lab identity that fetches another calibration's input first can read it and post a forged result for it (a known risk the owner deferred, `infra/README.md`). The identity is checked first, then the live calibration is found by id within its 20-minute callback window (and, for a result, by the result token's hash), and `access/policy.ts` mints the `OrgScope` from the calibration, so the job reads and writes one location of one organization. The body is parsed only after both checks pass. Every refusal is 404 `not_found`: a missing or wrong token, an unknown id, another calibration's result token and a finished calibration look alike (never 401); while the lab is off (no runner) both routes answer 404 to everything. Every refusal while the lab is on logs `townwise.lab_callback_refused { route, reason }`, never an id or a token: the identity check's reason (`missing`, `malformed`, `signature`, `expired`, `issuer`, `audience`, `tenant`, `caller`), then `not_live` for a signed-in caller naming no live calibration or one whose input was already fetched, and `result_token` for a result whose token is missing or not that calibration's, so probing calibrations shows in the log. Only when Entra's keys cannot be fetched do they answer 503 `lab_auth_unavailable` (and warn `townwise.lab_callback_unavailable`). A job that cannot sign in or fetch its input posts nothing, so its calibration fails `timeout` after 20 minutes.

| Method and path | Request | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
