| `GET /lab/calibrations/:id/input`, once | `Authorization: Bearer {the lab identity's token for the lab callback app}` (locally, the API process's secret) | 200 `townwise.lab-input/2` (D42), with the result token in `X-Townwise-Result-Token`: `calibrationId`, `metric`, `today`, `dataThrough`, `horizonDays` (182), `regimeStart`, `days` (guests per day with term, week of term, event groups and three flags from the notes, which after `dataThrough` leave out the notes the forecast read applies, 14.5; never a note's text, a calendar title or a name), `calendar` (the town calendar's entries, below), `champion` (the published model's forecast to compare with, its `engine` and `recordedWeekdayBiasMeanAbs`, its calibration's recorded backtest weekday bias, null for an imported run; or null). A queued calibration becomes running here | 404; 503 `lab_auth_unavailable` |
| `POST /lab/calibrations/:id/result` (up to 256 KB) | `Authorization: Bearer {the lab identity's token}` and `X-Townwise-Result-Token: {result token}` (so nothing is taken before the input was fetched); a lab result: a success (a run file with `trainingSource: 'townwise_lab'`, the scorecard, the code version and parameters) or a failure code | 200 `{ status }` once stored | 400 `invalid_lab_result` `{ issues: { path, code }[] }`, which fails the calibration `invalid_result`; 404; 503 `lab_auth_unavailable` |

[Build note: D52 (release A, 2026-11-17): a result’s scorecard may carry `horizonOutlook` (an array of at most two `{ horizon: 182 | 365, weeks, weeklyWape, coverage80, ratio, basis }`, optional until release B makes it required) and its params’ `widening` up to 8 entries, each with an optional `horizon` naming an outlook anchor. `checkLabResult` refuses, as `invalid_lab_result`, a run ending after `min(madeAt + 365, dataThrough + 400)` (`outlook_too_far`, path `run.days`) and widening whose `fromLead` does not strictly increase, whose ratio falls under 1 or decreases, or whose outlook anchors differ from `horizonOutlook`’s ratios when it is reported (`widening_out_of_order`, path `params.widening`). Release B (2026-11-19): the input is `townwise.lab-input/3`, `horizonDays` 400 and `termsThrough` (the town’s last researched term day, classes or finals, or null; `termsThroughOf` in `api/src/lab/input.ts`), and the lab refuses versions 1 and 2; `LAB_MODEL_VERSION` is `v10`; a result’s scorecard must carry both outlook reports, 182 then 365, with anchors equal to their ratios; and `checkLabResult` takes the calibration’s `termsThrough` and refuses a model run ending after the later of its forecast tier’s end and `termsThrough` (`outlook_past_terms`, path `run.days`), never a forecast-tier day and never a baseline run (6.23). The golden year-long result is 99,671 bytes as compact JSON, so the 256 KB limit stands. [CONFIRM: the gate judges nothing about the outlook but these sanity checks]]

Ingesting a result follows D17, in an order a retry completes: the draft run upserted on its file hash (the lab never changes a run that exists), its rows, `draft`, the result on the calibration, the gate (set once, by compare-and-set), the publish the gate decides, and the finish. The gate (`api/src/lab/gate.ts`, G2) publishes only when forecasts are on for the organization and it is active (G1), the published forecast did not change meanwhile, and the draft beats the current forecast on at least 12 held-out weeks by at least half a point of weekly WAPE, with 80% ranges holding 65% to 95% of weeks and weekday bias no more than 2 points worse; with no current forecast it needs 12 backtest weeks with an 80% range (595 days of history always gives them) with coverage in band and weekly WAPE at least half a point under a weekday-median baseline. Either way coverage is judged on at least 12 weeks that have a range (`too_few_weeks` or `not_enough_history` otherwise). Ties do not publish. A duplicate or retried POST ends with one run, at most one publish and one `calibration.finished`; a retry that finds the gate recorded as publishing and the run still a draft (an outage between the two) publishes it. The job retries its POST once on a connection error, a lost answer or a 5xx. The job's log lines carry counts and codes only (`fetched input: {n} days`, `posted result: ok`).

[Build note: D42 (14.6). Built in phase 2 of `autonomous-forecasts` (2026-11-16): the input version 2, the lab's two engines and the result's new scorecard fields below; the gate's new rules came in phase 3a, and since then 14.6's publish rules judge every draft. The input moved to `townwise.lab-input/2` in one step, the API and the lab built from the same commit, and the lab refuses version 1 (`invalid_input`). Version 2 adds `calendar`, every town calendar entry overlapping the input’s days as `{ id, group, kind, start, end, confidence }` (`kind` `event`, `holiday`, `term` or `season`; never a title, URL or source label; only the US federal holidays for a town with no researched calendar), and `champion.engine` (`model` or `baseline`), the engine of the current published run. `horizonDays` stays 182. The result’s scorecard adds `engine`, `engines` (each engine’s backtest metrics, the model’s null when it did not run), weekly bias, `horizon91` and `horizonReach`, and the gate becomes 14.6’s publish rules for every calibration.]

### 10.16 Business rules

A location's standing facts (D31, 6.24): “Closed Mondays”, “Patio opens in May”. Four routes in `TOWNWISE_ROUTES` (`org.rules.list`, `org.rules.create`, `org.rules.update`, `org.rules.remove`), each `member`, `openAsAdmin: true` and with no route limiter (the writes spend `townwise:writes`, as every non-GET does); `api/src/handlers/rules.ts`. TownwiseAI’s suggested closure rules (D46) are confirmed, edited or dismissed through two more, `org.agent.rule_suggestion_accept` and `org.agent.rule_suggestion_dismiss` (`POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/agent/rule-suggestions/:suggestionId/accept` and `.../dismiss`, each `member`, `openAsAdmin: true`, body `2kb`), whose table is in 10.12.

| Method and path | Policy | Request | Success | Extra errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/rules` | member | | 200 `{ rules: RuleView[], limit: 30, suggested: RuleSuggestion[] }`, oldest first; `suggested` (D46, 10.12) the location’s open suggested closure rules, which P29 lists above Add a rule | 400 (malformed id); 404 |
| `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/rules` | member; body `2kb` | `{ text, schedule? }`, strict: `text` at most 2,000 characters before `ruleTextOf`; `schedule` a `RuleSchedule` or null (or left out) for none | 201 `{ rule }` | 400 `invalid_request` (the body, a text `ruleTextOf` refuses, or a schedule `readRuleSchedule` refuses); 404; 409 `rule_limit`; 409 `rule_exists` |
| `PATCH /api/org/locations/:locationId/rules/:ruleId` | member (author or org admin); body `2kb` | `{ text?, schedule? }`, strict, at least one: a field left out keeps what it holds; `schedule: null` takes the schedule off | 200 `{ rule }`; only the fields that differ from the stored rule are written, and nothing different writes nothing and records nothing | 400; 403 `forbidden`; 404; 409 `rule_exists` |
| `DELETE /api/org/locations/:locationId/rules/:ruleId` | member (author or org admin) | | 204 | 400; 403 `forbidden`; 404 |

`RuleView` is `{ id, text, addedVia: 'page' | 'townwise_ai', createdByEmail, createdAt, updatedAt, canEdit, schedule, scheduleSummary }`: `createdByEmail` is the author's current email, “Townwise staff” for a rule staff added while open as admin (D25), “TownwiseAI” for a rule TownwiseAI added on its own (D59 slice 3), or “Deleted person” when the author's account is gone, as for notes; `addedVia` is `townwise_ai` both for a rule written by accepting a suggestion and for one TownwiseAI added on its own, which the author tells apart; `canEdit` is true for the author and for org admins (only org admins for one TownwiseAI added); `schedule` is the rule's `RuleSchedule` or null, and `scheduleSummary` its plain words, built in code from the fields only (`scheduleSummary` in `api/src/forecasts/reasons.ts`: what it does, its weekdays Monday first, its dates and its hours, as in “Closed on Mondays from Jan 5, 2027” or “Adds 40 guests on Fridays from Jan 2, 2026, 6 pm to 9 pm”), or null.

`RuleSchedule` (D31) is `{ kind, startDate, endDate, weekdays, effect, expectedGuests, startTime, endTime }`, a note's `NoteInput` (Section 12) but `detail`, which it never has. `readRuleSchedule` (`api/src/handlers/notes.ts`) checks it with the code that checks a note (`validDays`): the start from 2010-01-01 to today plus two years, the end on or after it and at most 366 days later, unique weekdays, guests only on a closed schedule that is a buyout, hours both or neither, start before end, none on a closure. `endDate` may be null or left out for no end. [CONFIRM: a rule's schedule may have no end date ("ongoing"); one with an end keeps a note's 366-day span] A schedule may also carry `season: { repeat: 'yearly', from, to }` (D46), or null or left out for none: `from` and `to` are `MM-DD`, and the schedule then covers a day on or after its start, on its weekdays, whose month and day fall from `from` to `to`, crossing the new year when `to` is before `from` (`12-20` to `01-05`), every year until the rule is deleted. `readRuleSchedule` refuses (400) a season whose months and days are not real, one that starts or ends on Feb 29 (a season that spans Feb 29 includes it in leap years), one of a year or more (more than 364 days counted in a non-leap year) and one on a schedule with an `endDate`; the start keeps its rule, and the other fields keep a schedule's other rules. A note never has one (12). [CONFIRM: a yearly rule runs every year from its start until it is deleted; Feb 29 can't start or end a season; a season is shorter than a year] `scheduleSummary` words it: “Closed Jan 1 to Mar 31 every year, from Nov 17, 2026”, “Closed on Mondays, Dec 20 to Jan 5 every year, from Nov 17, 2026”. An Other schedule needs no detail, since the rule's own text says what it is. [CONFIRM: an Other schedule needs no details, since the rule's text says what it is] Any other key, a `detail` included, is 400.

- **The text rule** (`ruleTextOf`): NFC, every run of whitespace (newlines included) one space, trimmed; then 1 to 200 code points with no control or format character left. The stored text is that normalized form, and its lowercase is the duplicate key, so a rule that differs from a saved one only in case or spacing is 409 `rule_exists`, on an add and on an edit (the unique index, 6.24).
- **The limit.** 30 rules per location: an add at 30 is 409 `rule_limit`. The add then inserts and counts again, deleting its own row and answering 409 `rule_limit` when the location went over 30, so two adds racing at 29 never leave 31 (both may be refused). [CONFIRM: 30 business rules per location, 200 characters each]
- **Who changes a rule.** Any member adds one; its author or an org admin edits or deletes it. Another location's or organization's rule id is 404, checked before 403 `forbidden`, as `editableNote` does.
- **Edits racing.** PATCH reads the rule, then writes only the fields that differ from what it read (`BusinessRuleStore.update`, one `findOneAndUpdate` that `$set`s the text or the schedule, or `$unset`s the schedule), so an edit of the text and an edit of the schedule racing both land, and a field a request sends unchanged keeps whatever a racing edit wrote. Two edits of the same field are last writer wins, as for notes. Pinned in `api/test/business-rules.int.test.ts`.
- **Audit.** `rule.created { locationId, via: 'page', scheduled }` (`via: 'townwise_ai'` for a rule written by accepting a suggestion, 10.12), `rule.updated { locationId, scheduled }` (only when the text or the schedule changed; `scheduled` is whether the rule has a schedule after it) and `rule.deleted { locationId }`, target `rule`, written after the effect (9.2, 9.3). In open as admin (D25) the rule is marked `byStaff` and its events are staff events, so they show in Townwise staff activity as “Added a business rule”, “Edited a business rule” and “Deleted a business rule”. The routes log only the request line (route id and status); the text never reaches a log line or an audit event.
- **View-as.** Staff read the list; the guard refuses every write with 403 `view_as_read_only`.
- **TownwiseAI.** A turn that sends a new message (not a regenerate) reads the location's rules after the budget check and before the live-turn claim, so a store failure there needs no release. When the list differs from the last `business_rules` block on the turn's path, the person's stored message starts with a new block holding it (with no rules after earlier ones, the line “There are no business rules for this location now.”); unchanged rules, and a location that never had any, add nothing. In the block a rule's `<` and `>` become the full-width `＜` and `＞`, so no rule can close it early: any member writes rules, and every member's chat at the location reads them, an org admin's included. The stored rule and P29 keep the text as written. [CONFIRM: rule angle brackets sent to TownwiseAI as full-width look-alikes, rather than refused when the rule is saved] Only the newest block on the turn's path (the new message's included) is sent in full; each earlier one is sent as “[Earlier business rules, replaced by a later list.]”, so a deleted or edited rule's text is not sent again, while the stored messages keep their blocks. Contract: `docs/portal/tuning-chat.md` section 3. A rule with a schedule has a second line in the block, “  Forecast schedule: {scheduleSummary}”, which a rule's one-line text can never forge; with no schedule anywhere the block is what it was before schedules. The text and the schedule never reach a log line or an audit event.
- **The forecast.** A rule's schedule changes Townwise's forecast from the town's today on as a note with the same fields does (14.5), except that a note covering a day that decides it beats the rule's closure or buyout there; a rule without one never changes it.

### 10.17 Orders (D35)

Every route is under `/api/org/locations/:locationId`, `member` (the item sales delete is `org_admin`), open to staff opened as admin (D25) and refused under view-as for a write, reading the setup with TownwiseAI (D41) included. The routes, their bodies, limiters and error codes are in `api/README.md` (Orders); the collections `tw_order_setups`, `tw_item_sales`, `tw_order_counts`, `tw_order_decisions`, `tw_order_rules` and `tw_order_cards` and their deletion are in its Data section. Audit actions: `order.setup_saved`, `order.item_sales_uploaded`, `order.item_sales_deleted`, `order.count_saved`, `order.decision_saved`, `order.rule_saved`, `order.rule_turned_off`, `order.card_saved`, `order.card_dismissed` and `order.setup_read` (D41: whether a file or pasted text was read, the call's outcome, and how many suppliers and items it suggested), each with ids, dates, codes and counts only (never a name, a quantity, a reason or the content).

| Route id | Request | Policy | Body | Limiter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `org.orders.get` | `GET .../orders[?sample=true]` | member | none | |
| `org.orders.decision` | `POST .../orders/decisions` | member | 2 KB `{ itemId, delivery, quantity, reason }` | |
| `org.orders.rule` | `POST .../orders/rules` | member | 2 KB `{ itemId, situation }` | |
| `org.orders.rule_off` | `POST .../orders/rules/off` | member | 1 KB `{ ruleId }` | |
| `org.orders.setup.get` | `GET .../orders/setup` | member | none | |
| `org.orders.setup.save` | `PUT .../orders/setup` | member | 1 MB `{ expectedVersion, setup }` | |
| `org.orders.setup.read` | `POST .../orders/setup/read` | member | 8 MB `{ source }`: a file `{ type: 'file', kind, data }` (base64; `kind` `pdf`, `xlsx`, `docx`, `text` or `picture`, from the extension) or pasted text `{ type: 'text', text }`; no other key | `ai_reads` |
| `org.orders.item_sales.upload` | `POST .../orders/item-sales` | member | 256 KB `{ from, to, days }`, `to` before the town's today | `item_sales` |
| `org.orders.item_sales.remove` | `DELETE .../orders/item-sales` | org admin | none | |
| `org.orders.counts.save` | `POST .../orders/counts` | member | 32 KB `{ date, items }` | |
| `org.chat.order_proposal.get` | `GET .../chat/:conversationId/order-proposals/:proposalId` | the conversation’s author | none | |
| `org.chat.order_proposal` | `POST` the same path | the conversation’s author | 2 KB `{ action, quantity?, reason? }` (a change), `{ action, situation? }` (a rule: the situation its card showed, else 409 `rule_changed`) or `{ action: 'dismiss' }` alone (a setup card, D56: it is never saved) | |

**How ordering works, in plain words.** A member sets up a location once: the suppliers, the days each delivers and the day and time to order by, and the items (name, supplier, unit, how many servings a unit holds, the par, the deal size, whether it must never run out, and the names the register uses for it). They can type the items or import a filled sheet. They upload an item sales export from the register for the last weeks, which the browser reads and matches to those names, so only servings per item per day are sent. They count what is on hand, in whole or half units, as often as they like. From these Townwise builds, for each supplier, the next order: when to order by, the delivery it is for, the delivery it lasts until, and a quantity for each item with the reason in a sentence. The owner can change a quantity and say why, and can ask Townwise to remember the reason; a remembered change applies to every later order of that item until they turn it off. Nothing is ordered or sent anywhere.

**Reading the setup with TownwiseAI (D41), in plain words.** On the web or in the apps, a member gives Ordering setup one file or some pasted text and presses Read. The page sends it in that one request; the server reads it into text (a PDF as it is, its document properties included, and a picture without its metadata), asks Claude once for the suppliers and items in it, checks the answer itself, answers, and keeps nothing. The answer is suggestions only: suppliers with the delivery days and order-by days the content gives, and items with their supplier, category, unit, servings per unit (marked when TownwiseAI estimated it from a standard container, such as about 124 pints in a half-barrel), deal size and point-of-sale names, each marked when its name isn't written in the content. It never holds a par or never run out, and email addresses and formatted ten-digit phone numbers in it are replaced (not a seven-digit local number or digits run together, so the prompt is the main guard); an item's supplier is one of its suggested suppliers, or none. The page merges it into the unsaved draft as it merges a sheet, so nothing is saved until the member saves the setup and the checks name anything missing. A read takes up to 150 seconds from the handler's start, after the upload (then 503 `extract_timed_out`; the page waits 230 seconds, inside the ingress's 240). It is charged to the organization's files AI budget, shared with reading stored files (11A.9): a refusal or a cut answer is charged; a call that fails is charged what its stream reported, one the limit or the person leaving ended before anything streamed keeps its whole reservation, and an API error before the stream (503 `extract_failed`) is charged nothing. A replica holds at most 16 MiB of reads' bodies, two full ones, counted by their `Content-Length` right before they are parsed: past it 503 `extract_busy`, so ahead of the `ai_reads` limiter and every check of the handler, and a body with no length or over 8 MiB is 413 `payload_too_large`. It is off, and the setup GET's `canReadWithAi` false, without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or with that budget at 0. Its caps, codes and charges are in `api/README.md` (Ordering and Orders).

**Ordering setup suggestions in TownwiseAI (D56), in plain words.** On the web, a member attaches an order guide, an invoice or a price list from Your data to a message and asks TownwiseAI to set up their orders from it. TownwiseAI already has the file’s content for that reply (D36), so it writes what it found, the suppliers with their delivery days and the items, and the server checks it the way it checks a read on Ordering setup, with two differences: at most 60 items, and no register names. The reply shows a card. The card compares the suggestions with the setup as it is saved now and says what is new and what would change in an item already there, field by field. It never saves anything. **Review in Ordering setup** opens Ordering setup with the suggestions in the draft, unsaved, where the person sets each new item’s par and presses Save; **Not now** sets the card aside. The card’s read (`org.chat.order_proposal.get`) answers `{ kind: 'setup', status, read, readWeb }`, `status` being `open` or `dismissed`, and 404 once the file the suggestions came from is turned off or deleted, or is not the caller’s to read. Under view-as it answers `{ kind: 'setup', status, counts: { suppliers, items }, readWeb }` in place of `read`. Setting it aside writes `order.card_dismissed` with `kind: 'setup'`; nothing writes `order.card_saved` for it. It costs the chat turn’s tokens only, within the TownwiseAI month.

**How the board gets a quantity.** For an item, Townwise takes the average servings it sold on each weekday over the last 8 weeks of item sales, adds up the days between the order-by day and the next delivery after this one, and turns servings into units after the category's usual loss. On days a published guest forecast covers, a day's servings are scaled by the forecast's guests over the location's own average guests for that weekday. The cushion is the spread of how far past orders' use missed the same estimate; it is left out until there are two past orders to learn from. The quantity is what is needed to reach a target chance of not running out (98% for an item that must never run out, else 95% for bottles, cans and draft, 92% for liquor, 88% for cocktail ingredients), less what was counted, never under the par less what was counted, rounded to the deal size by cost, or up to a whole unit without one. With no count, or a count older than 7 days, the quantity follows the par. A day the forecast marks closed expects no sales; a booked day keeps the weekday average. An item no day of the 8 weeks sold follows the par. A draft item's par is one higher when the days ahead use more than one keg, as the Python engine's backup keg rule has it. A line holds at most 999. Confidence is low with no fresh count or no item sales, medium for a count 3 to 7 days old or under 28 days of item sales, else high. The math is the Python engine's (`reorder/reorder/engine.py`) ported to `api/src/orders/engine.ts`; every place it differs from the Python engine is listed in `openspec/changes/complete-bar-ordering/design.md`, Decision 5, and each is a default D35 asks the team to confirm.

### 10.18 Owner calendars

A location’s own calendars (D33): each an imported `.ics` file or calendar CSV (D58), a subscription link, or a Google calendar connected by signing in with Google (D39). Eleven routes in `TOWNWISE_ROUTES`. Five are the calendars’ (`org.owner_calendars.list`, `org.owner_calendars.events`, `org.owner_calendars.create`, `org.owner_calendars.refresh`, `org.owner_calendars.remove`), each `member` and `openAsAdmin: true`, in `api/src/handlers/owner-calendars.ts`. Three are a member’s own Google connection (`org.google_calendars.connect`, `org.google_calendars.list`, `org.google_calendars.disconnect`), each `member`, not `openAsAdmin` (403 `open_as_admin_refused` from the chain, 8a), with the route limiter `google_calendars` (`townwise:google-calendars`, 10.8), in `api/src/handlers/google-calendars.ts`. Three are a file calendar’s booking labels (D58: `org.owner_calendars.bookings_sort`, `org.owner_calendars.bookings_label`, `org.owner_calendars.bookings_confirm`), each `org_admin`, the label and the confirm `openAsAdmin: true` and the sort not (403 `open_as_admin_refused` from the chain), in `api/src/handlers/calendar-bookings.ts`. The stores are `tw_calendar_sources`, `tw_calendar_events` and `tw_google_connections` (`api/README.md`, Collections). Under view-as staff read the calendars and their events, titles included for files and links (a Google calendar’s, below), and every write is 403 `view_as_read_only`. A calendar of another location or organization answers 404 like an unknown one, and a malformed id is 400.

| Method and path | Policy | Request | Success | Extra errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/owner-calendars` | member | | 200 `{ calendars, google, bookingSort }`, the calendars oldest first; `bookingSort: { available }`, whether Sort with TownwiseAI can run (a model key is set, D58) | 400; 404 |
| `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/owner-calendars/events?from=&to=` | member | exactly `from` and `to`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `from <= to`, at most 92 days counting both ends, `to` at most 400 days after the town’s today | 200 `{ events }`: every stored event overlapping the range, from each calendar’s current events, by start | 400; 400 `bad_range` (any other range); 404 |
| `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/owner-calendars` | member; body `2mb` | `{ kind: 'file', label, ics }` (`ics` the file’s text, an `.ics` file or a calendar CSV (D58), at most 1 MB of its own bytes) or `{ kind: 'link', label, url }` (`url` at most 2,048 characters), `label` 1 to 60 characters after trimming, either with optional `titlesNotice: 1` (exactly 1; sent only by the popover that shows the weekly sentence, D53); or `{ kind: 'google', googleCalendarId }` (1 to 1,024 characters: an id the picker answered, or `primary`), named from Google | 201 `{ calendar, skippedRows }`, `skippedRows` a calendar CSV’s rows whose start could not be read (0 otherwise, D58) | 400 `invalid_request`; 400 `too_large`, `not_calendar` (the file, or what a link answered); for a link 400 `bad_link`, `blocked_address`, `unreachable`, `timeout`, `http_error`; 404; 409 `calendar_limit`; 413; 429 `rate_limited` (the account’s link adds); 503 `calendar_links_unavailable` (a link, with no calendar key or the link adds not countable). For a Google calendar, in this order: 403 `open_as_admin_refused`; 503 `google_calendar_unavailable` (off); 409 `google_not_connected`, `google_reconnect` (the connection revoked, or a token the key no longer opens); 409 `calendar_limit`; 429 `rate_limited` (the account’s link adds) or 503 `google_calendar_unavailable` (not countable); 400 `google_not_found` (not in the caller’s own Google calendar list), `google_forbidden` (free and busy only), 409 `google_reconnect` (Google refused the token) or 503 `google_unavailable`, from Google’s calendar list; 409 `calendar_already_added` (any Google calendar of the location has the id Google answered); then the events read (400 `google_not_found`, `google_forbidden`; 409 `google_reconnect`; 503 `google_unavailable`, Google busy, down or refusing the client); last, 409 `google_not_connected` when the connection ended while it was stored, which removes the new calendar |
| `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/owner-calendars/:calendarId/refresh` | member | none (no body is parsed) | 200 `{ calendar }` after one read: a success replaced the events; a failure kept them, its code now the `status` | 400; 400 `not_a_link` (a file); 404 (also a Google calendar whose connection is gone, or whose person no longer holds a seat in the organization, which the read removed); 429 `rate_limited` with `retryAfterSeconds` (refreshed in the last 5 minutes; nothing is fetched); 503 `calendar_links_unavailable` (a link); 503 `google_calendar_unavailable` (a Google calendar while they are off), `google_unavailable` (its person’s seat here removed less than a minute ago: nothing read or written, the 5 minutes spent) |
| `DELETE /api/org/locations/:locationId/owner-calendars/:calendarId` | member | | 204: its events, then the calendar; a Google calendar’s connection is marked for a check first, and ended after when it backs no other calendar of the organization | 400; 404 |
| `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/owner-calendars/:calendarId/bookings/sort` | org_admin, not open as admin; no body | none | 200 `{ calendar, sent, labeled, batchesFailed }` (D58): the calendar’s unlabeled events sent, how many TownwiseAI labeled and how many batches failed | 400; 403 (a member; `view_as_read_only`; `open_as_admin_refused`); 404; 409 `not_a_file_calendar`; 503 `chat_unavailable` (no model key, or the sort count not countable); 429 `rate_limited` with `retryAfterSeconds` (3 sorts a calendar an hour); 409 `chat_budget_exhausted` (the month can’t cover every batch’s ceiling; no call is made) |
| `PATCH /api/org/locations/:locationId/owner-calendars/:calendarId/bookings` | org_admin; body `2kb` | strict `{ uid, booking }`: `uid` 1 to 1,024 characters (in the body, never the path or query), `booking` `buyout`, `party`, `own_event`, `other` or null (no label; a sort still leaves it) | 200 `{ calendar, noteMade, noteKept }` (D58): on a confirmed calendar an upcoming event set to buyout or party gets its note (`noteMade`), and one moved off a label with a linked note keeps it (`noteKept`) | 400; 403; 404 (also an unknown uid); 409 `not_a_file_calendar` |
| `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/owner-calendars/:calendarId/bookings/confirm` | org_admin; no body | none | 200 `{ calendar, notesMade, notesLeft, calibration }` (D58): Use for forecasts, the upcoming bookings’ notes made and left, and `calibration` `{ status, id }` (`started`, or why not: `lab_unavailable`, `not_enough_history`, `budget_exhausted`, `in_progress`, `rate_limited`, `start_failed`, `invalid_regime_start`, `org_not_active`), null on a second press | 400; 403; 404; 409 `not_a_file_calendar` |
| `POST /api/org/locations/:locationId/google-calendars/connect` | member; body `2kb`; limiter `google_calendars` | strict `{ code, agreed: true, titlesNotice? }`, `code` Google’s authorization code, 1 to 512 characters; `titlesNotice` exactly 1, sent only by the explainer that says titles go weekly (D53) | 200 `{ calendars }`, the choices as the next row answers them | 400 `invalid_request` (no `agreed: true`; Google not called); 400 `google_code_invalid` (Google refused the code), `google_scope_missing` (a calendar scope not granted; nothing stored); 404; 409 `google_other_account` (not the caller’s sign-in account; nothing stored), `google_connect_again` (no lasting access: the access token revoked, nothing stored), `google_reconnect` (Google refused the calendar list for the choices; the connection marked revoked); 429; 503 `google_calendar_unavailable` (off), `google_unavailable` |
| `GET /api/org/locations/:locationId/google-calendars` | member; limiter `google_calendars` | | 200 `{ calendars: [{ id, name, primary, added }] }`: the caller’s own Google calendar list (`minAccessRole=reader`, one page of 250), the primary first, then Google’s order; `name` the calendar’s name in their Google account, answered to them only and never stored; `added` whether it is already one of this location’s | 403 `view_as_read_only` (under view-as, before anything is read); 404; 409 `google_not_connected`, `google_reconnect` (revoked, a token the key no longer opens, or Google refusing it; nothing is written, 7.3); 429; 503 `google_calendar_unavailable`, `google_unavailable` |
| `DELETE /api/org/google-connection` | member; limiter `google_calendars` | none | 204: the caller’s connection in the organization ended, its grant revoked (reason `unused`) | 404 (no connection); 409 `google_connection_in_use` (it backs a calendar); 429; 503 `google_calendar_unavailable` |

A calendar is `{ id, label, kind, host, eventCount, skippedRepeating, status, lastSuccessAt, lastAttemptAt, createdAt, mine }`: `kind` is `file`, `link` or `google`; `host` is a link’s host (`calendar.google.com`), null for a file or a Google calendar; `skippedRepeating` counts the repeating events not imported (0 for a Google calendar); `status` is `ok` or the code of the last failed refresh (`bad_link`, `blocked_address`, `unreachable`, `timeout`, `too_large`, `http_error`, `not_calendar` or `key_mismatch`; for a Google calendar `google_revoked`, `google_not_found`, `google_forbidden`, `google_rate_limited`, `google_unavailable` or `key_mismatch`). No answer carries a link’s address, a Google calendar’s id (the picker’s, to its own person, aside), a Google token or the Google account a calendar came from. `mine` is true only for a Google calendar the caller added, which their own connection reads, and false for a file, a link, a teammate’s Google calendar and to staff under view-as or open as admin (D39’s Reconnect). An event is `{ calendarId, calendar, uid, title, startDate, endDate, startTime, endTime }`: `calendar` is its calendar’s label, `endDate` is included, and the times are the town’s `HH:MM`, or null. The list also answers `google: { available, connected, clientId, canConnect }`: whether Google calendars are on, whether the caller has a Google connection that is not revoked (false under view-as, the staff member’s own state), the public OAuth client id when available, else null (null too while staff have the organization open as its admin), and whether the caller may connect one (false for staff, under view-as or open as admin, and when off; owner decision, 2026-11-17: staff see the option disabled). D61: the list (`GET .../owner-calendars`, only) also answers each calendar’s `fromFile`: `f_<fileId>`, the Your data item it was imported from (D60), while that file is kept (not being deleted, and stored files on), else null, so its page can link to the file Your data now shows as the calendar.

- **What is kept.** At most 5 calendars a location, of every kind (409 `calendar_limit`; each takes one of 5 slots under a unique index, so adds at once cannot pass it), each named by whoever adds a file or a link, and a Google calendar from Google (below). `api/src/calendar/ics.ts` parses a calendar in the location’s town (its today and time zone): single events from 400 days before the town’s today to 400 days after, at most 2,000 a calendar, the first by start (an imported file from 1,096 days before, its upcoming events first, D58); a repeating event (RRULE or RDATE) is counted, not imported; its moved instances and canceled events are left out. An event keeps its UID, its title (cut at 200 characters), its dates (the end included) and its hours, the latter only when it starts and ends on one date or ends by 06:00 the next morning (its start day’s); its description, location, attendees and organizer are never read. A file is parsed once and only its events are kept. A Google calendar keeps each instance of a repeating event (Google expands them), and its 2,000 are those that end on or after the town’s today first, by start, then the earlier ones read, the latest first (below). [CONFIRM: 5 calendars per location, a 6 hour refresh, a 60 character name] [CONFIRM: Google calendars' repeating events are kept, within the 2,000] [CONFIRM: a Google calendar keeps its next 2,000 events first, then earlier ones]
- **A link is a secret.** Its address is sealed with AES-256-GCM under `TOWNWISE_CALENDAR_KEY` (`api/src/calendar/secret.ts`, a fresh IV each time), opened only to fetch it, and shown as its name and host. Without the key, adding or refreshing a link is 503 `calendar_links_unavailable` and the refresh loop does not start, while files still import. A link sealed under another key fails each refresh with `key_mismatch`, keeping its events, until it is added again.
- **Google’s access is a secret too (D39).** A connection’s refresh token and each Google calendar’s id (often an email address) are sealed the same way and stored only as ciphertext; no access token is stored (each read refreshes one and drops it); and none of them, nor an authorization code or an ID token, is ever answered, logged or audited, or put in a URL path or query (codes and ids travel only in JSON bodies). Every use of a stored token is in `api/src/calendar/google-access.ts`. A token or an id the key no longer opens gives the calendar `key_mismatch` (changing the key breaks every Google connection, as every link). Google calendars are on only while `TOWNWISE_GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_ID`, `TOWNWISE_GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_SECRET` and the key are all set (18); otherwise `google.available` is false, the Google routes, adds and Refresh now answer 503 `google_calendar_unavailable`, and a Google calendar’s refresh records `google_unavailable` and keeps its events.
- **Fetching** (`api/src/calendar/fetch.ts`, Section 17): `https:` on port 443 only (`webcal:` is read as `https:`), no user name or password, every resolved address checked and the connection pinned to it, at most 3 redirects each checked again, 10 seconds and 1 MB, no cookies. Adding a link spends one of the account’s 12 link adds an hour (`townwise:calendar-links`) before it fetches and parses it, and a failure refuses the add with its code, so nothing broken is stored. A Google add spends one of the same 12, the account’s adds that fetch, after the location’s count and before any Google call. [CONFIRM: 12 link adds an account an hour]
- **Calling Google** (`api/src/calendar/google.ts`): only `https://oauth2.googleapis.com` (the token exchange, refreshes and the revoke) and `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3` (the calendar list and events), fixed hosts, so the guarded fetch is not needed; redirects refused, 10 seconds a call, at most 2 MB read, and a failure is a code from a fixed list with Google’s HTTP status, never Google’s message or body. The revoke posts the token in a form body, never a URL.
- **Connecting (D39).** On web, “Add a Google calendar” loads Google’s script and asks Google, in a popup from the press of “Continue to Google”, for a code for exactly `openid`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.calendarlist.readonly` and `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly`, with `include_granted_scopes` false, the person’s email address as `login_hint` (in Google’s window only) and a fresh random `state` on every press, which the client checks; the list answer’s `clientId` is the client asked for. The connect route, a cookie-session write behind the kit’s Origin check, exchanges the code with the client secret (the code model has no PKCE), refuses unless both calendar scopes were granted, checks the ID token’s claims (`iss` Google’s, `aud` the client id, `exp` ahead, a `sub`), and refuses 409 `google_other_account` unless `sub` is the caller’s own Google sign-in subject, so one Google account backs at most one person. With no refresh token in Google’s answer it keeps the stored one only while the person’s connection is not revoked and the key opens it; otherwise it revokes the access token it was given and answers 409 `google_connect_again`, so the next press consents afresh. Then it stores the connection, one per (organization, person), with its sealed token, the granted scopes, `agreedAt` (the press of “Continue to Google”, the person’s agreement to what the section says) and `connectedAt`, clears `revokedAt`, makes that person’s Google calendars in the organization due at once (a reconnect heals them), sets the connection’s check 24 hours on (at once instead when the caller no longer holds their seat, as after a removal while the code was at Google), audits `google_calendar.connected`, and answers the choices.
- **The picker and the add.** The choices route lists the caller’s own Google calendars and writes nothing. An add takes one picked calendar and checks it in the order of the table, so a refused add costs no Google call where it can: the duplicate check runs only after Google’s calendar list confirms the caller can see the calendar, against the id Google answered (the `primary` alias matches the primary’s real id), so a member never learns which accounts’ calendars the location holds. It reads the events before storing anything, stores the calendar with its sealed id and its connection, pushes the connection’s check 24 hours on, and checks the connection again: one ended meanwhile takes the new calendar with it. An add that stores while an end of access is revoking answers 201, and its calendar then goes with the connection. Its label is its name in the person’s Google account cut at 60 characters, or “Google calendar” for the primary calendar and for any name containing “@”, since labels are shown to the team and sent to Anthropic. [CONFIRM: Google calendar labels from Google's name, "Google calendar" for the primary or an email-like name] [CONFIRM: the picker lists a person's first 250 Google calendars]
- **Reading a Google calendar.** Access is refreshed once, then `events.list` with `singleEvents=true`, `orderBy=startTime`, `showDeleted=false`, `eventTypes=default`, the town’s `timeZone`, `maxResults=500` and `fields=nextPageToken,items(id,status,summary,start,end)`, so no description, location, attendee or organizer reaches Townwise: first the events ahead (the town’s today less 1 day to today plus 401 days) up to 2,000, then, with what is left of 2,000 events and 8 pages, the events before in slices that begin 30, 90, 210 and 401 days back, newest first, each read to its end or left out. Each item’s id is its UID, and ics.ts’s rules give its title, dates and hours; canceled ones are skipped. Google’s answers map to statuses: a refresh’s `invalid_grant` is `google_revoked` and marks the connection revoked, so its other calendars record `google_revoked` without calling Google; an events 401 is `google_revoked` too; a 403 rate limit or a 429 is `google_rate_limited`; a 403 for the Calendar API not enabled is `google_unavailable` (logged code `api_disabled`); any other 403 is `google_forbidden`; a 404 or 410 is `google_not_found`; a refresh’s `invalid_client` (a configuration fault), a 5xx, a network failure, a timeout, a redirect or an over-cap body is `google_unavailable`. Each failure keeps the last good events and backs off as a link’s does.
- **Replacing events, with no transaction.** A refresh writes the new events under a new generation, switches the calendar to it with a compare-and-set, then deletes the older generations’ events; reads return each calendar’s current generation, so a reader never sees a mix, and rows a crash left behind go with the next refresh or the removal.
- **Refreshing.** A loop in each API replica (`api/src/calendar/refresher.ts`, while the key is set) looks 30 seconds after start and then every 15 minutes. It claims due links and Google calendars together, one at a time across organizations, the longest due first (`claimDueCalendar`), each under a 5-minute lease (one token call and 8 event pages of 10 seconds each, plus writing 2,000 events, fit within it); a success is next due 6 hours later, a failure keeps the last good events, records its code as `status` and backs off 6 hours, then 24. Before a Google read it checks the connection: none left removes the calendar with its events; a person with no seat in the organization ends the access without reading Google (`seat_gone`); a seat removed here less than a minute ago is neither read nor ended and nothing is written (`unsettled`), since a removal refused as the last admin puts it back. Then it claims due Google connection checks one at a time under the same 5-minute lease (`claimDueGoogleConnection`, under `scopeForGoogleCheck`): a person with no seat in the organization ends the access (`seat_gone`); a seat removed less than a minute ago is left due (`unsettled`, nothing written); a connection backing no calendar a day or more after its connect ends (`unused`); any other is checked again 24 hours on (an unused one younger than a day, at a day after its connect), set only while no mark came in during the check. Closing aborts a Google call in flight; nothing is written, and the lease runs out. “Refresh now” reads at once through the same path, at most once per calendar per 5 minutes (a compare-and-set holds it, so two at once read it once). [CONFIRM: an unused Google connection is ended after 24 hours]
- **Ending Google access** (`endGoogleAccess`, D39). In an order that a retry or the connection check completes: mark the connection for a check; remove the Google calendars it backs in the organization, events first; ask Google to revoke the grant with the stored refresh token (best effort, 10 seconds; a 200 or a 400 `invalid_token` counts as done; a failure is logged with its status only), unless the same person holds a connection in another organization, since Google’s revoke ends every grant the account gave the project, sign-in’s included; delete the connection whether or not the revoke worked; then remove the connection’s calendars once more, for one an add stored while the revoke ran. The revoke needs only the token and the calendar key, so access ends with the grant revoked while Google calendars are off too. It runs when the last Google calendar a connection backs is removed, whoever removes it (`last_calendar`); when the picker’s Cancel drops an unused one (`unused`); when its person’s seat is removed, or they leave (`seat_removed`, `left`: the three seat removals mark the person’s connection before the seat is removed, then end it after, and a refusal as the last admin changes nothing); when a location is deleted (it marks the connections backing its Google calendars before the location row goes, then ends each left backing nothing: `location_deleted`); when the organization is deleted (`org_deleted`); and, as backstops, at the refresh loop’s seat check and connection check above, and at a person’s deletion (`person_deleted`). There is no separate “Disconnect Google” control: a person ends Townwise’s access by removing their Google calendars, or at Google. [CONFIRM: no separate Disconnect Google control]
- **Staff (D39).** Open as admin never holds a Google connection: the three Google routes and a Google add answer 403 `open_as_admin_refused`, and the list answers `{ available: true, connected: false, clientId: null, canConnect: false }` while Google calendars are on, so staff see “Add a Google calendar” disabled (owner decision, 2026-11-17). Under view-as the choices route is refused 403 `view_as_read_only` (the person there is the target) and the list answers `google.connected` and `google.canConnect` false. Under view-as and open as admin alike (which outlasts the first join, D25), the list, the events read and Refresh now’s answer show each Google calendar with the label “Google calendar” and each of its events with the title “Google calendar event”, with their dates and hours, and in a TownwiseAI turn staff run open as admin `get_owner_calendar` lists them the same way, so staff never read a Google calendar’s name or an event’s title on the Calendar or through TownwiseAI (Google’s rule that people read its users’ data only with their “affirmative agreement to view specific” data); files and links show as before. A TownwiseAI reply staff read under view-as, in a member’s conversation, may still mention one, which the connect section says before “Continue to Google”. Everyone on the organization’s team sees the location’s Google calendars and their events, as for every calendar.
- **Audit and logs.** `owner_calendar.added`, `owner_calendar.refreshed` (“Refresh now” only) and `owner_calendar.removed` carry ids, the kind (`file`, `link` or `google`), the event count and the status (and, D60, on an add from a stored file, its `fileId`; summarized “Added a calendar file from Your data with {n} events”), never the calendar’s name, a link’s address or host, a Google calendar’s id, or a title. D58: `owner_calendar.bookings_sorted { locationId, calendarId, sent, labeled }`, `owner_calendar.booking_labeled { locationId, calendarId, booking }` (the label set, or `none`; never the uid) and `owner_calendar.bookings_confirmed { locationId, calendarId, buyouts, parties, notes }`, each note also `note.created`; the sort logs `townwise.calendar_bookings_sorted { calendarId, sent, labeled, batchesFailed }` or, when every batch failed, `townwise.calendar_bookings_sort_failed { calendarId }`, never a title, uid, an event’s date or a label per event. `google_calendar.connected { connectionId }` and `google_calendar.disconnected { connectionId, calendarCount, reason }` (`unused` or `last_calendar`; target type `google_connection`) record a connect, the picker’s Cancel and a last calendar removed; a seat loss, a location’s or organization’s deletion and the connection check write no new audit event, since their own events record the cause, and log `townwise.google_access_ended { connectionId, calendars, reason }`. The handlers log only Google’s failures, through one helper, `townwise.google_calendar_failed { op, status, code }`, with a failed revoke as `townwise.google_revoke_failed { status }`; the refresh loop logs the calendar or connection id, the status, counts and the duration only. No audit event or log line carries a code, a token, a Google calendar id, an email address, a calendar’s name, an event’s title or anything of Google’s answer.
- **Deletion.** Removing a calendar deletes its events, then the calendar, then its events again, so a refresh finishing meanwhile leaves nothing. Deleting a location or an organization deletes its calendars and their events, and ends the Google access left unused (above); a person’s deletion deletes their connection rows.
- **Keys and following linked notes (D53).** A stored event row also holds `keyed`: true for every Google event (Google’s id) and for an ICS event whose UID the file stated, appears once among the events the file keeps and is at most 1,024 characters, and whose stored `uid` is that stated UID; never for a made-up `event-{n}`, a `{UID}#{n}` clash or a longer UID, which do not survive a refresh (absent reads false, so a file imported before this is not linked until imported again). A switch of a calendar’s events also answers `keptKeys` and `hadKeys`: how many keyed UIDs of the new generation were among the keyed UIDs of the generation it replaced (counted before the old rows are deleted), and how many the replaced one had. Where it switches (the refresh loop after its “after” check, Refresh now, and an add after the Google `clearCheck`; never after a failed refresh, which switches nothing), `followLinkedNotes` (`api/src/calendar/follow-up.ts`) compares the location’s notes linked to that calendar (6.7) with its current events and writes `move` and `remove` suggestions (6.27, 10.12), with no model and whatever the weekly switches say; a run a newer replace overtook is skipped, and a failure is logged by the calendar id and never fails the refresh. A `move` is made only when the event’s key is present at other dates or hours, the note’s own dates and hours still equal its link’s (as a note holds them, so a late night’s hours, which a note leaves out, compare as none), and the event’s exact new ones pass Section 12’s rules and start after the town’s today. A `remove` is made only when the key is absent, the link ends today or later, the note starts after today, the calendar holds fewer than 2,000 events (a full one may have cut it) and the refresh kept at least one keyed UID whenever the replaced generation had any. A note edited off its link gets neither, and a note whose event is back at its link’s dates has its open follow-up set `expired`. Removing a calendar keeps its notes and their links; its follow-ups and spotted events read as expired (6.27); a file imported again is a new calendar whose events are not linked to the old notes.
- **The weekly notice (D53).** A file or link calendar (`tw_calendar_sources.titlesNotice`) and a Google connection (`tw_google_connections.titlesNotice`) hold 1 when its add or connect came from a screen that said TownwiseAI reads the titles weekly (`WEEKLY_TITLES_NOTICE`, `api/src/calendar/titles-notice.ts`); absent means the person was not shown it. An add sets it on the new calendar; a connect sets it when its body carries it (a reconnect with it sets it again); nothing clears it, neither a refresh nor a reconnect without it. The weekly call sends a calendar’s titles only with it (10.12).
- **A calendar CSV (D58).** `api/src/calendar/csv-events.ts` `parseCalendarFile` picks the format: text with a `BEGIN:VCALENDAR` line is an `.ics` file; otherwise a first record (after any byte-order mark, read by the upload's RFC 4180 reader) holding the headers `event_id`, `title`, `start_at` and `end_at` (trimmed, any case and order, other columns allowed) is a calendar CSV; anything else is 400 `not_calendar`. No model reads it. Each row is read for those four and, when present, `status` only (a `cancelled` row is left out), so no description, location, organizer, attendee, email, attachment, color, calendar id or Google URL is read or kept. A time with an offset or `Z` is the town’s wall time of that instant; one with no offset is the wall time it says [CONFIRM: a calendar CSV time with no offset is the town’s wall time]; a bare date is a date; the `timezone` column is not used. Then the `.ics` rules: an end at midnight closes the day before, an event ending by 06:00 the next morning stays on its start day with its hours, hours only within a day. The uid is the trimmed `event_id` (`event-{n}` when blank, `{id}#{n}` when repeated), keyed when stated once and at most 1,024 characters; each row of a repeating series is a single event, so `skippedRepeating` is 0. A row whose start can’t be read is skipped and counted (`skippedRows`). A file calendar keeps its `format` (`tw_calendar_sources.format`, `csv`, or `ics` when absent), answered on the calendar as `format` (null for a link or a Google calendar).
- **A file calendar’s history (D58).** A file calendar, `.ics` or CSV, keeps the events ending on or after the town’s today minus 1,096 days and starting by today plus 400, at most 2,000, the upcoming ones first and then the latest earlier ones [CONFIRM: a calendar file keeps 3 years of past events and its upcoming events first, at most 2,000]. A link and a Google calendar keep their 400 days. The events read and TownwiseAI’s `get_owner_calendar` already read any past range, so the history shows on the calendar’s page in Your data (36 months back for a file calendar) and in chat; the Calendar page keeps its 12 months.
- **Booking labels (D58).** Each event of a file calendar may carry a label in `tw_calendar_events` (`booking`: `buyout`, the whole restaurant; `party`, a private party alongside regular service; `own_event`, the restaurant’s own public event; `other`, not a booking; or null, cleared by a person), with `bookingBy` (`ai` or `person`) and `bookingAt`; the calendar keeps `bookings: { state: sorted | confirmed, sortedAt, confirmedAt, confirmedBy }` (absent reads unsorted; a deleted person’s `confirmedBy` is nulled). A file is never re-read, so its rows and labels last; link and Google calendars refuse labels (409 `not_a_file_calendar`). The calendar answers `bookings: { state, sortedAt, confirmedAt, counts: { buyout, party, own_event, other, unlabeled } }` (null for a link or a Google calendar) and each event in the events read `booking` and `bookingBy`. Only an org admin sorts, labels and confirms; members see the labels; under view-as the section is read-only; staff open as admin may label and confirm but not sort, which sends customers’ names to Anthropic [CONFIRM: only an org admin sorts, labels and confirms a calendar’s bookings; staff open as admin can label and confirm, but not press Sort]. Labels change nothing until confirmed.
- **Sort with TownwiseAI (D58, `api/src/calendar/booking-sort.ts`).** In the request: the calendar’s events no one labeled, in batches of 250, all at once, one structured-output call each with the chat’s model, low effort and no tools, within 150 seconds overall. Each event goes as a ref only this request knows (`e1`, `e2`, ...), its title with every email address and phone number replaced by `[removed]` (the weekly call’s `sentTitle`), its dates with the start’s weekday, and its hours: never the calendar’s name, id or kind, the event’s uid, or another column. The prompt marks the titles as data, never instructions, and defines the labels from the owner’s defaults: off-site catering, meetings, holds, tentative entries, staff and vendor items, reminders and closures are `other` [CONFIRM: what counts as a buyout, a party, the restaurant’s own event and not a booking, in Sort with TownwiseAI’s prompt]. An answer’s label is kept only for a ref its batch sent, the first time; `unsure`, a missing ref and a failed batch’s events stay unlabeled; a person’s label (or cleared label) is never overwritten; no model words are kept. A sort that labels any event of a confirmed calendar sends it back to sorted, so the new labels train nothing and make no note until an admin confirms again. Every batch’s ceiling (its input at 3 characters a token and 8,000 output tokens at the most expensive model) is reserved from the organization’s TownwiseAI month before any call (409 `chat_budget_exhausted`) and settled to what the calls cost. It runs on an admin’s press with its own words, whatever the weekly titles switch says [CONFIRM: Sort with TownwiseAI sends titles on an admin’s press whatever the weekly titles switch says], at most 3 times a calendar an hour (`townwise:calendar-booking-sorts`, 10.8) [CONFIRM: 3 sorts a calendar an hour].
- **Use for forecasts (D58).** Confirm sets `bookings.state` to `confirmed` by compare-and-set (a second press finds it confirmed and still makes any missing note). Each `buyout` or `party` event that is keyed, ends on or after the town’s today, is linked to no note and is covered by no private-event or closure note gets a note as D53’s accept writes one: a private event with effect closed (buyout) or more guests (party), no guest count, no title or detail, the event’s dates and, when Section 12 allows them, its hours, `fromEvent` set, by the confirming admin, at most 100 a confirm, soonest first, within the 1,000 notes; its id comes from the calendar and uid, so a retry makes none twice [CONFIRM: confirming makes a linked note for each upcoming buyout or party event, at most 100 a confirm]. A later label set to buyout or party on an upcoming event of a confirmed calendar makes its note; one set away leaves it (`noteKept`). The press that confirms also starts a calibration as the admin through the lab’s checks (`via: file`), else answers why not, and the next weekly refresh refits the location anyway, since the input’s fingerprint changes [CONFIRM: confirming a calendar’s bookings starts a refit for the admin who confirmed].
- **A calendar file kept in Your data (D60, `api/src/files/calendar-import.ts`).** A reference file whose upload completes (`org.files.complete`) and that is an `.ics` or `.ical` file starting a VCALENDAR (after a byte-order mark and blank lines, in any case), or a text file whose first record is the calendar CSV profile, is added as a file calendar by the uploader through the same add as `kind: 'file'` (1 MB of UTF-8, `parseCalendarFile`, 5 a location), labeled from its name, with no `titlesNotice`, and keeping the file’s id as `fromFileId` under a unique index on `(orgId, fromFileId)`: the add checks for it first and again after a refused insert, so of two imports of one file one stores it. An `.ics` or `.ical` file that is no calendar is recorded `not_calendar` unread; a file over 1 MB is `too_large` unread; a failure to read the original or store the calendar is `unavailable` and logs `townwise.file_calendar_import_failed { fileId, errType }`. Each outcome logs `townwise.file_calendar_imported { fileId, outcome }`. Importing never fails the upload, whose answer is unchanged. The calendar is an ordinary file calendar: Your calendars lists, refreshes nothing of and removes it, and removing it leaves the stored file, as deleting the file leaves the calendar.
- **Sorting on import (D59 slice 2, `api/src/calendar/auto-sort.ts`).** After a file calendar's add, while `TOWNWISE_AGENT_AUTO`, the organization's `agentAuto` and its `calendarTitlesToAi` are all on, a model key is set, the TownwiseAI reader runs here and the caller is not staff open as admin (who may not sort), the calendar is queued once (`tw_calendar_sources.autoSort: { status: queued | sorting | done | skipped | failed, queuedAt, notBefore, leaseUntil, attempts, reason, endedAt, labels }`, beside `bookings`, whose absence still reads unsorted; never queued twice). The TownwiseAI reader's loop (`files/ai-reader.ts`) claims it when no file read is waiting, one job per organization across both, under the read's 90-second lease and its 1, 2 and 4 minute waits, three attempts. Before any call: the switches and the importer's seat again (`agent_auto_off`, `titles_off`, `requester_gone`), and a calendar someone already sorted, labeled or confirmed is left to them (`already_sorted`: a press or a label while it was queued), then D58's batches of the unlabeled events reserved from the TownwiseAI month (`budget_spent`; the page still offers Sort with TownwiseAI). Every batch failing puts it back. The model's labels are then kept on the queue entry (`autoSort.labels`, by uid; removed when the sort ends; never logged) before any write, so a retry of any later step writes them with no second call. Then one `booking.label` change (6.31) for the calendar: the ledger row first, then every label the model gave (`unsure` stays unlabeled; a label counts as sure, the answer having no confidence of its own [CONFIRM: a label other than unsure counts as sure, so an import's labels are used for forecasts at once]) written as `bookingBy: 'ai'` with the row's planned time as `bookingAt`, only on events nobody labeled, and the calendar confirmed by TownwiseAI (`confirmedBy: 'townwise_ai'`). A label anyone else set meanwhile (a person's, or a press's) or a confirm someone else made, found before the labels are written or just before the confirm, sets the whole sort aside: its labels and confirm are taken back, the row is removed and the sort is skipped `already_sorted`, so TownwiseAI's confirm never covers a label it did not set. The row's `count` and dates are those of the labels written, not of the model's answer. A retry finds the row and the kept labels and finishes it with no second call. Then Use for forecasts' notes for the upcoming buyouts and parties (at most 100, within the note limit), each a `note.add` change by TownwiseAI with its `fromEvent`, written only while the labels' change is still applied, so a person's note that decides the day, a note someone undid or the same note from elsewhere keeps one from being written. No calibration starts; a booking on a past day wants a refit (14.6). Logged as `townwise.calendar_auto_sort_queued { orgId, locationId, calendarId }`, `townwise.calendar_auto_sorted { calendarId, sent, labeled, batchesFailed, notes, notesSkipped }`, `townwise.calendar_auto_sort_skipped` and `_failed { calendarId, reason }`, and `townwise.calendar_auto_sort_attempt_failed { calendarId, errType }`; audited as `agent.change_applied`. [CONFIRM: a calendar file imported while TownwiseAI works on its own is sorted and its labels used for forecasts with no press] [CONFIRM: a calendar file staff import with an organization open as its admin is not sorted on its own]
- **The forecast.** A stored event changes a forecast figure only through notes, scheduled business rules (14.5) and, since D58, a confirmed file calendar’s buyout and party labels on past days in the lab input (14.5).

## 11. Upload format and validation

### 11.1 What leaves the browser

This is the browser path (P13). It stays as the fallback while stored files (11A) are off, and as the visible choice to send only daily totals. On this path, only this leaves the browser, for one location:

```
{ "days": [ { "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "guests": <integer or null>, "netSalesCents": <integer or null> }, ... ] }
```

Nothing else leaves the browser: no file name, column names, row count, other columns or raw values. The file is read with `File.text()`, held in component state only, never written to `localStorage`, IndexedDB or a log, and dropped when the wizard closes or finishes. The client sends no telemetry (expo-shell rule 12, **Exists**).

### 11.2 Browser steps (web)

1. **Choose a file.** `.csv` or `.txt`, up to 50 MB [CONFIRM: 50 MB]. UTF-8 with any leading byte-order mark stripped. The delimiter is detected from the header line (comma, semicolon or tab). A small RFC 4180 parser in the client handles quoted fields, doubled quotes, and CRLF or LF; no CSV library is added. An Excel file gets “Save it as CSV first.”
2. **Match columns.**
   - “What is one row in this file?” One day (a daily summary); One check or order; One item on a check. The third blocks Continue with “Item-level exports aren’t supported. Export daily totals or checks, not items.” Item lines repeat the check’s guest count, so adding them up would inflate guests.
   - Four pickers list the header names, each with a type detected locally from the first 200 non-empty cells (“dates”, “numbers”, “text”). Cell contents are never shown (D11).
   - **Date** (required) accepts `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYYMMDD`, `M/D/YYYY`, `M/D/YY`, any of them followed by a space and a time, which is ignored. For slash dates the user confirms the order: “Month first (03/04/2025 is March 4, 2025)” or “Day first (03/04/2025 is April 3, 2025)”. If a first part above 12 appears, the order is set and shown. The helper reads: “If your export has a business date column, pick it, so a 1 a.m. order counts toward the night before.”
   - **Guests** and **Net sales** are optional, but at least one is required.
   - **Location** is optional. If it is mapped, the user picks which value of that column is this location, from up to 50 distinct values. These are the only cell contents ever displayed, because the user named that column as locations. Only matching rows are used.
   - Header guesses preselect the pickers: date from `date` or `business date`; guests from `guests`, `covers` or `guest count`; net sales from `net sales`. [CONFIRM: header guesses]
3. **Check the totals.**
   - Numbers: strip `$`, thousands commas and spaces. Parentheses or a leading minus (hyphen or U+2212) mean negative, so refunds net out. Guests must be whole numbers. Net sales becomes integer cents, rounded half up once per day.
   - In “one day” mode, a repeated date is an error: “{n} dates appear more than once (rows {list}). Choose “One check or order”, or fix the file.” In “one check” mode, rows are added up per date: “We add up rows that share a date.”
   - The screen shows “{rows} rows became {days} days, {first} to {last}.”
   - Skipped rows by reason, with up to 10 row numbers each and never a value: “{n} rows had no readable date (rows {list}).”, “{n} rows had a number Townwise couldn’t read (rows {list}).”, “{n} rows were for other locations.”
   - Excluded days, listed by date with the reason (up to 10, then “and {n} more”): a date after tomorrow, a date before 2010-01-01, a negative daily total, a total above the caps in 11.3, or a day with neither value.
   - Totals for the file (guests, net sales), with “Check these against your point-of-sale system.”, and a table of the first 7 and last 7 days.
   - If the location already has data, for an org admin: “You already have {first} to {last}. Days in both will be replaced by this file.” For a member: “You already have {first} to {last}. Days you already have stay as they are. Only an admin can replace them.” The range counts only days that are on; a day held by a turned-off upload (D28) is still an existing day to the write (11.4), so when `offDayCount` is above zero a second line says so, and shows even with no days on. For an org admin: “{n} days are held by turned-off uploads. Any of them this file covers will be replaced, and will show again.” For a member: “{n} days are held by turned-off uploads. Any of them this file covers stay as they are, and stay hidden.” (“1 day is held …” for one.)
   - More than 3,660 days: “This file covers more than 10 years. Upload up to 10 years at a time.”
4. **Send.** One request. On success, all file state is cleared, and the result reads, for an org admin: “Saved {days} days for {location}: {inserted} new, {replaced} replaced.” For a member: “Saved {inserted} new days for {location}.”, then, when `kept` is above zero, “{kept} days already had data. Ask an admin to replace them.” It is followed by the calibration line and the links “Add notes for unusual days” and “See your sales data”.

### 11.3 Server rules (zod `.strict()` at every level)

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Body | exactly `{ days }`; any other key is 400 |
| Day | exactly `{ date, guests, netSalesCents }`; any other key is 400 |
| `days` length | 1 to 3,660 [CONFIRM: ten years per upload] |
| `date` | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`, a real calendar date, not before 2010-01-01, not after the server’s UTC date plus one day (covers every US zone) [CONFIRM: earliest date] |
| `guests` | integer 0 to 20,000, or null [CONFIRM: cap] |
| `netSalesCents` | integer 0 to 100,000,000 (one million dollars a day), or null [CONFIRM: cap] |
| Per day | at least one of `guests` and `netSalesCents` is not null |
| Dates | unique within the request |
| Size | a 256 KB parser on this route only. 3,660 days at the largest allowed values serialize to 230,590 bytes (measured for this spec), under 262,144 |

Any failure is 400 `invalid_request` with no field details (**Exists**). The client applies the same rules first, so a 400 means a client bug.

### 11.4 Write

1. Insert the `tw_uploads` record with `status: 'applying'`.
2. One unordered `bulkWrite` of upserts keyed by `{ orgId, locationId, date }`. Days not in the upload are untouched.
   - **Org admin:** each upsert `$set`s `guests`, `netSalesCents`, `uploadId` and `updatedAt`, so an uploaded day replaces that day in full, nulls included.
   - **Member:** each upsert writes those four fields with `$setOnInsert` only, so a day that already exists is never changed. A member’s upload therefore cannot overwrite or zero out history, which matches the matrix reserving deletion for org admins (Section 3).
   
   [CONFIRM: replace by day for org admins; members add new days only. If members should replace data too, the matrix must say that a member’s upload can overwrite all of a location’s history.]
3. Set the record to `applied`, with `inserted` (upserted count) and, from the matched count, `replaced` for an org admin or `kept` for a member.
4. Audit `sales.uploaded`. Log `townwise.upload_applied { orgId, locationId, uploadId, dayCount }`.

A crash leaves `applying`, which the Sales data tab shows as “This upload didn’t finish. Upload the file again.” Sending again is safe, because every write is an upsert on the day; a member’s resend keeps the days that already saved. The request body is never logged: server-core logs no bodies (**Exists**), and Townwise code adds no body logging.

Delete all sales for a location removes its `tw_sales_days` and `tw_uploads`; the audit log keeps the history.
