### 14.4 Forecast runs

The API never computes a forecast and never holds a model. [Build note: since D27 the forecast lab computes forecasts too. A job on Townwise's Azure servers (`modeling/lab`, not the API) refits a location's model from that location's own uploaded days and notes, returns its outputs to the API's callback (10.15) and keeps no model; the API still computes nothing and holds nothing but outputs and the code version, parameters and input hash that reproduce them.] Staff export a run's outputs on the team's computers (`modeling/export_forecast_run.py`, from the frozen files in `modeling/forecasts/`, written to the gitignored `modeling/outputs/`), import the run file for one location from P21, and publish it. [Build note: owner decision 2026-11-05: staff may import and publish Sawtooth's frozen v3 forecast once Sawtooth is an organization in Townwise and the owner confirms its consent to see it and to its being sent to Anthropic through TownwiseAI. The build ships the machinery only; nothing is published.]

- **The run file** (`townwise.forecast-run/1`, `api/src/forecasts/file.ts`, at most 256 KB as sent: P21 reads the file in the browser, refuses one over 2 MB on disk unread, and checks the 256 KB on the parsed file as compact JSON, so the exporter's indenting doesn't count; strict at every level): `schema`, `metric: 'guests'`, `model { family, version, notebookCommit }`, `trainingSource: 'files_from_owner'`, `trainedFrom`, `dataThrough`, `madeAt`, `frozen`, `interval { level: 0.8, widened }`, `backtest`, `days` (1 to 400: `date`, `status`, `low`, `mid`, `high`, `baseline`, up to 6 `reasons { kind, ref, effectPct }`) and `weeks` (up to 60: `from`, `to`, `openDays`, `low`, `mid`, `high`). No location id, name, note, URL or other free text. Rules: `trainedFrom <= dataThrough <= madeAt <= today`; every day after `dataThrough` and within 400 days of it, each once; an open day has `low <= mid <= high` (0 to 20,000), a closed or booked day no numbers; only term, event and holiday reasons may carry a `ref`; each week lies inside one Monday-to-Sunday week, on days the file has, without overlap, with `openDays` between its open days and its open and booked days. A refusal is 400 `invalid_forecast_file` with at most 50 `{ path, code }` issues, never a value.
- **Import** (staff, 10.7): the run is upserted on `{ orgId, locationId, fileSha256 }` as `importing`, its rows upserted on their key (a duplicate key from a concurrent import of the same file is a row the other one wrote, not an error), and it becomes `draft` when every row is there. The same file again answers 200 with the run; a run left `importing` finishes on the retry. Publish is a compare-and-set from `draft`; withdraw from `draft` or `published`. Each is a staff action (9.2), written before the effect and listed in the org's Townwise staff activity.
- **Lab runs** (D27). Org admins (through TownwiseAI's `start_calibration`, or a TownwiseAI read of a file that wrote notes or days, `via: 'file'`, 11A.9) and staff (the console's Calibrate button) start a calibration for a location. Its job returns a draft run with `trainingSource: 'townwise_lab'` and a `lab` block (6.20), plus a scorecard on held-out weeks (WAPE, typical-week error, weeks over 20% off, the worst week, 80% range coverage, weekday bias). It publishes itself only when staff have switched the organization's forecasts on (`POST .../forecasts-switch`, which needs the staff member's word that the owner agreed) and the gate passes (10.15); otherwise the draft and its scorecard stay for staff, who see percentages and counts only (D7). Staff publish a draft with the existing Publish, which also answers 409 `forecasts_off` while the switch is off, and withdraw any run, lab or imported, with Withdraw. A lab run is frozen with its training cutoff, input hash, code version and parameters, scored prospectively like any published run, and never overwritten. Each calibration costs the organization's TownwiseAI month $0.10 and is limited to 4 a day per organization and one live per location. Since 2026-11-19 a person’s start needs a 230-day span, as the weekly refresh’s does (14.6), and under 595 days the lab runs the baseline engine alone. Privacy: the job sees only the one location's days, and nothing about a calibration reaches a log or an audit event except ids, codes and counts. TownwiseAI's three lab tools (`tuning-chat.md` section 4) give the model the scorecard as chart data and cards, never a draft forecast day; no chat view draws them yet [DECISION NEEDED: how lab results render in the redesigned chat].
- **Who sees it.** Owners, view-as and TownwiseAI read published runs only: drafts, unfinished imports and withdrawn runs never show. For each date the reader uses the newest published run whose `dataThrough` is before it, so no forecast is shown for a day its model saw. Week rows come only from a run that supplied every day of the week, and are the run's own, never sums of days. [Build note: since D52 (release A, 2026-11-17) the reader chooses each date’s run from run metadata for a run with no gap in its days (`dayCount` equal to its range’s length, every lab run), and from rows for a run with gaps (an imported file may skip days), then reads rows only of the runs it chose: over the read’s days and a week either side, and each run the read’s days use over its own past days, for its live accuracy; the model card reads the newest run’s rows only. Answers equal a reader that reads every row, with 52 year-long runs (`api/test/estimates.int.test.ts`).]
- **Labels** are made in code (`api/src/forecasts/reasons.ts`): the weekday; the term from the town calendar's term state on the day; an event or holiday by the calendar entry its `ref` names (by id, or a group with one entry that day), a federal holiday on the day, or plain words ("Town event", "Holiday"); "Your recent level", "Closed", "Private event booked". A partner's text can never reach a label.
- **Effects** (`api/src/forecasts/effects.ts`, pure). From the town's today on, each of the run's reasons says whether it pushes guests up or down: `effect: { direction: 'more' | 'fewer' | 'same', pct, basis, days, averageGuests }`. Where the run recorded `effectPct`, the effect is the model's (`basis: 'model'`, `days` null). No run records one yet (the forecast lab writes none: its quantile-linear base plus xgboost doesn't estimate an effect per reason; a later lab change may), so otherwise it is the location's own history (`basis: 'history'`), which every reader words as "usually", never as the forecast's cause: the 52 weeks of stored days before the town's today, with closed and likely-closed days (D32) left out of every comparison. A weekday is that weekday's mean guests against the mean over every open day, with at least 8 of that weekday. A term reason holds each day in the day's term state against the mean of the same weekday in the other known term states, with at least 6 days on each side. A holiday holds each past occurrence (its calendar group) against the same weekday in the 4 weeks before and after it, other holidays left out, with at least 1 occurrence. An event holds each day with its calendar group against the mean of the same weekday without it, with at least 3 days on each side. `days` is how many days the effect rests on. `averageGuests` (D40) is, on a weekday’s history effect, the mean guests of the open days it is compared against (the comparison’s denominator), rounded to the nearest guest, which the Calendar prints after “your average day”; it is null on the model’s effects and on every other kind. `pct` is the size rounded to the nearest 5 (never negative), and 5 or less is `same`. Below a minimum, for "Your recent level", "Closed" and "Private event booked", for an event or holiday the reason doesn't name or one with no calendar group, for a term state that is unknown, on a note's or a rule's reason (its outcome says what it did) and on every day before today, `effect` is null. The read computes effects from its own reads (the stored days, read once from the history's start, and the notes and rules it reads anyway, which mark the history's closed days), stores nothing and logs nothing. [CONFIRM: a reason's effect is the model's when the run records one, else the location's own history, worded "usually"] [CONFIRM: the history is the 52 weeks before today; a weekday needs 8 of its days, a term state 6 days in it and 6 same-weekday days outside it, a holiday 1 past occurrence, an event 3 days with it and 3 without; holidays compare with the same weekday 4 weeks either side; 5% steps, and 5% or less is about the same]
- **Accuracy.** Each past day carries its stored guests and whether they landed in the range. Live accuracy is per run: it counts the open days that have passed which that run supplied (the reader chose it for them), booked days left out, as WAPE with the in-range count, misses included, and is null under 5 of its own scored days. A day that was closed or likely closed (D32: a closure note, a rule's closure that holds, an all-zero row, or guests under the likely-closed line, read from the same notes, rules and stored days, reaching 8 weeks before the first scored day) is a closure, not a forecast miss, and is left out too (`api/src/forecasts/score.ts`). [CONFIRM: live accuracy leaves out closed and likely-closed days] A newer run is never credited with an older run's days, so a run published today reads "not scored yet" even when older runs have been scored. A day is past once it has ended in the town (its local date, `localDay`, 10.13), on the forecast route, the model card and in TownwiseAI alike. Scored weeks are not listed separately: a week row in a read carries its `actual` and `inRange`. A week's actual is summed only when all its open days have passed and none was booked. [Build note: since D52 (release A) an outlook day (Read view) is left out of each run’s `live` and the window’s `accuracy` too, and reads `scored: false` while still carrying its `actual` and `inRange`, so live accuracy keeps scoring only the forecast tier (`api/src/forecasts/score.ts`, pinned by `api/test/forecast-score.test.ts`). [CONFIRM: outlook days are left out of live accuracy, so it keeps scoring only the forecast tier]]
- **Read view** (`ForecastWindow`): `{ available, reason: 'no_published_forecast' | 'not_covered' | null, runs: (ForecastRunView & { live: LiveAccuracy | null })[], days: ForecastDayView[], weeks: ForecastWeekView[], notCovered: { from, to }[] }`, each run with its own live accuracy. `ForecastRunView` is `{ id, metric, model: { family, version, label }, trainingSource, trainedFrom, dataThrough, madeAt, frozen, interval, backtest }`; a day `{ date, weekday, status, low, mid, high, baseline, reasons: { kind, label, effectPct, sources }[], runId, madeAt, madeAfterDay, actual, inRange }`; a week `{ from, to, openDays, low, mid, high, runId, madeAt, actual, inRange }`; `LiveAccuracy` `{ days, inRange, typicalErrorPct, from, to }`. Numbers are raw; clients and TownwiseAI round low down and high up. [Build note: from the calendar change (D30) a day also carries `model`, `noteGuests` and `moreNotes`, a reason `note`, and a week `noteGuests` (10.13, 14.5).] [Build note: a reason also carries `effect` (Effects, above), and a read covers at most 42 days (10.13).] [Build note: since D42 (phase 1 of `autonomous-forecasts`) a read covers at most 92 days (10.13). `ForecastRunView` adds `engine`, `'baseline'` for model family `seasonal_baseline` and `'model'` otherwise, derived and never stored, and a baseline run’s `model.label` is “Townwise's baseline from your recent weeks and the town calendar” (a model run keeps “Townwise demand model v{n}”); the model card, the Calendar’s provenance, `get_forecast` and the console’s runs list use these words. A day adds `scored`, true when live accuracy counted it. The window adds `accuracy`: live accuracy (`liveAccuracy`, `api/src/forecasts/score.ts`) over the window’s own days, each from the run the reader chose for it, booked, closed and likely-closed days left out, null under 5 scored days, exactly as a run’s; each run’s own `live` is unchanged. Pinned by `api/test/forecast-score.test.ts` and `api/test/estimates.int.test.ts` (92 days answer 200, 93 answer 400).] [Build note: since D52 (release A, 2026-11-17) a day adds `outlook`, true when the date is after the forecast tier (`tierEnd`, 14.6) of the run the reader chose for it, and a week `outlook`, true when any of its days is; derived, never stored, and false on every day while runs are 91 days. Notes and scheduled rules adjust an outlook day exactly as a forecast day (14.5). Pinned by `api/test/estimates.int.test.ts` (`year-long runs and the outlook (D52)`).]
- **TownwiseAI** reads it through `get_forecast { from, to }` (at most 31 days, its own limit under the route's 42, from at most 92 days back), which answers "Townwise has no forecast for this location yet." when none is published; its prompt gives every forecast as a range, never the middle alone, uses week rows for weeks, names the model when asked, mentions accuracy and misses when the owner is deciding, and never makes up a forecast (`tuning-chat.md` section 4). Each reason carries its `effect`, and the tool's description has it say "usually" for a history effect, name how few days it rests on when they are few, never call it the forecast's cause, and say so plainly when the history is too short. ### 14.5 Notes in the forecast

From the calendar change (D30), the location's notes adjust each published forecast day on read (`api/src/forecasts/adjust.ts`, pure, called by `api/src/forecasts/reader.ts`). The adjustment is computed on every read and stored nowhere: runs and their rows (`tw_forecasts`) are never rewritten, so frozen and published runs stay exactly as made, and an added, edited or deleted note shows on the next read everywhere (the forecast route, Home, the Calendar, `get_forecast` and `show_visual`). The reader reads the notes overlapping the window once (`NoteStore.overlapping`, under the caller's `OrgScope`) and takes, for each day, the notes that cover it (dates and weekdays), oldest first. It reads the location's business rules with a schedule once too (`BusinessRuleStore.scheduled`, at most 30, under the same scope, D31), and a rule's schedule covers a day as a note does, an end of null meaning no end; a yearly schedule (D46) covers a day on or after its start, on its weekdays, whose month and day are in its season (crossing the new year when `to` is before `from`), every year. One function decides coverage (`noteCovers` in `api/src/agent/questions.ts`, mirrored in the client's `analytics/days.ts`), so the forecast, the lab's input, the questions, the day classes, the chat's day tools, the weekly pass and the Calendar all apply a season the same way, and a rule with no season covers exactly what it did before. A suggested closure rule (D46, 10.12) is not a rule until someone confirms it: the reader never reads `tw_agent_suggestions`. A rule's schedule is applied exactly as a note with the same fields: everything below about a note holds for a rule (its closure, its buyout, its private event with a guest count, and every outcome), and rules and notes on one day all apply together, so their guests add up, except that a note covering the day beats a rule's closure or buyout (rule 2). Another location's or organization's rule never reaches the read. Rules, in order:

1. **Past days.** A day before the town's today (the reader's `today`, 13.2) keeps the model's figures, and every note covering it has outcome `past_day`. Past days keep the forecast as it was made, so `actual`, `inRange` and live accuracy stay comparable with what the model said. [CONFIRM: notes change the forecast from today on, never a past day]
2. **Status.** A closure (a closure note, or any closed note but a buyout) makes the day `closed` whatever the model said (outcome `closed`). Otherwise a buyout (a private event with effect `closed`) makes it `booked`, even a day the model closed (outcome `booked`; `day_closed` under a closure). Otherwise the model's status stands (`row.status`, open when none), except that on a day the model closed (a learned closure, such as a weekday or a holiday, not a note) a private event with effect `more_guests` and a guest count opens it (rule 3). A closed or booked day has `low`, `mid` and `high` null, as the run file's booking rule says. A note covering the day beats a business rule's schedule (D31): when a covering note decides the day (a closure, a buyout, or one that says it is open: an opening, a private event, or more or fewer guests; `notesDecide` in `api/src/closed-days.ts`), every covering rule's closure and buyout is set aside (outcome `overridden`) and the day's status comes from the notes and the model, so a one-day opening or party note opens a day a standing closure rule would close. A rule's private event with a guest count still adds its guests on a day that ends open. [CONFIRM: a buyout books the whole day] [CONFIRM: a closure note beats every other note, and a note that decides the day beats every rule's closure and buyout; on a day the model closed, a buyout books it with its guests and a private event with a guest count opens it with only those guests]
3. **Guests.** On a day that ends `open`, each private event with effect `more_guests` and a guest count adds its guests to `low`, `mid` and `high`, and the guests are summed (outcome `added`). On a day the model closed, which has no figures of its own, `low`, `mid` and `high` are all the summed guests. The exception is a day whose run reasons include `kind: 'booking'`: the notebook exporter (`modeling/export_forecast_run.py`, `EVENT_REASONS`) marks open private-event days that way, so every such note there gets `already_in_forecast` instead of counting the party twice.
4. **noteGuests.** On an open day, the guests the counted private events add; on a booked day, the sum of its buyouts' guests (0 when none gave a count); on a closed day, 0.
5. **Every other note** is listed with why it changed nothing: `no_guest_count` (a private event with more guests and no count, unless a closure note closed the day), `not_counted` (an opening, an other note, fewer guests or unknown), `day_closed` (a private event on a day that stays closed), `day_booked` (a private event, not a buyout, on a booked day) or, for a rule only, `overridden` (its closure or buyout, set aside by a note that decides the day, rule 2).
6. A model day that is open with null figures can't happen (`file.ts` refuses it), so it needs no rule.

- **Day fields.** `status`, `low`, `mid` and `high` are the adjusted values; `model` keeps the run's own `{ status, low, mid, high }`; `noteGuests`, `moreNotes` and `moreRules` as in 10.13. `inRange` is computed on the model's figures and status, and `baseline` is null when a note changed the status.
- **Reasons.** Notes with outcome `added`, `booked` or `closed` come first, then the run's reasons in run order, then every other note, with at most 6 note reasons in all; `moreNotes` counts the rest, whose guests still count. A note's reason (`kind: 'note'`) is labeled in code from its kind, guest count and hours, never its detail: "Your private event, 70 guests, 6 pm to 9 pm"; "Your private buyout, 70 guests" (the count left out when null); "Your closure" (or "Your note: closed" for another closed note); otherwise "Your {opening | note | private event}{, N guests}{, hours}". A rule's reason (`kind: 'rule'`, D31) carries `rule: { id, guests, outcome }` (and `note: null`; every other reason has `rule: null`), and is labeled in code from its schedule without its dates, never the rule's text: "Your rule: closed on Mondays", "Your rule: closed Jan 1 to Mar 31 every year" (a season, D46), "Your rule: adds 40 guests on Fridays, 6 pm to 9 pm", "Your rule: private buyout, 70 guests on Saturdays", "Your rule: other, fewer guests than usual on Tuesdays". Rules that changed the day come before the notes that did, and the rules that didn't before the other notes; rule reasons have their own cap, at most 6 a day (`MAX_RULE_REASONS`, the ones that changed the day first), apart from the six-note cap, and `moreRules` counts the rest (their guests still count), so a day's reasons and `get_forecast`'s result stay bounded however many of a location's 30 rules cover it. [CONFIRM: at most 6 rule reasons a day, apart from the six-note cap (moreRules counts the rest), and they come before the notes' in each group] `REASON_KINDS` in `file.ts` is not extended, so a run file still can't carry a note or rule reason. A note's or a rule's reason has `effect` null (14.4): its guests and outcome say exactly what it did, and the Calendar and Home size it from that outcome against the model's middle figure and order it among the run's reasons by that size (P28's Why, D40). The notes and rules this read already loads also mark which of the history's days were closed for those effects, so the read loads nothing more for them.
- **Weeks.** The reader never sums days: a week starts from the run's own week row. From today on, each of its days whose notes or rules changed it shifts the week's `low`, `mid` and `high` alike by the day's adjusted `mid` less the model's (a newly closed or booked day takes its model `mid` off; guests notes and rules add are added, exact since a party is a fixed number; a day the model closed or booked counted nothing in the week), floored at 0, and `openDays` gains the days they opened and loses the days they closed or booked. The week is left out only when a changed day has no model `mid` to take off (an open model day without figures, which `file.ts` refuses). The row carries `noteGuests` (the guests notes and rules add on its open days), and its `inRange` stays the model's. So a vacation closure note or a new “Closed Mondays” rule keeps every week's range on Home and in `get_forecast`. [CONFIRM: a week's range shifted by its days' note and rule changes]
- **The lab's input** (`api/src/lab/input.ts`, 10.15): on days after `dataThrough` (the forecast horizon) the notes this read applies are left to it. `closed` and `booked` are false, so a closure or buyout note never becomes the run's own day status (`statuses()` in `modeling/lab/townwise_lab/forecast.py`), which editing or deleting the note could not undo until the next calibration; closures the lab learns from the history (weekdays, closing holidays) still come from the model. `privateEvent` is true only for covering private events this read will not count, that is, any but a buyout or one with effect `more_guests` and a guest count; otherwise a lab run would apply its learned private-event lift and this read would add the headcount on top. History days (on or before `dataThrough`) keep all three flags, for training, except for a counted party (a private event with effect `more_guests` and a guest count): this read adds its guests on every day it covers, so on a history day it sets no `privateEvent` and the day's guests go out less its guest count (never below 0). Training sees the day's base demand and the read adds the party back, so a recurring counted party (“40 more guests every Friday”) is never counted twice through a `privateEvent` flag collinear with its weekday. [CONFIRM: on a history day a counted party's guests are taken off the day's guests and set no privateEvent] A business rule's schedule (D31) sets the three flags as a note with the same fields does, on history and future days alike (`buildLabInput` reads `BusinessRuleStore.scheduled` under the calibration's scope), and its more or fewer guests say a near-empty history day was open, as a note's do (D32), but its closure and buyout hold only as the day classes say (D31, D32): never over a covering note that decides the day, and on a history day before today a closure only when the day's guests are missing or under the likely-closed line, so a standing rule never drops real recorded guests from training. Today's row, which may be partial, is never likely closed. A rule's text never reaches the input. The lab (`modeling/lab`) reads the same booleans and needs no change. A lab run made before these changes keeps the statuses and lifts it baked in for its future days (a deleted closure or buyout still closed or booked there) until the location is calibrated again.
- **Confirmed booking labels (D58).** `buildLabInput` also reads `bookingsBetween`: the current `buyout` and `party` events of the location’s file calendars whose bookings are confirmed, as dates and label only, never a title or uid. On a day on or before `dataThrough` they cover, with no private-event or closure note covering it (the note decides, so a counted party is never counted twice), a buyout sets `booked` (training drops the day) and a party sets `privateEvent` [CONFIRM: a confirmed buyout label books a past day and a party label marks it a private event, unless a note on the day decides]. They never change `closed`, the likely-closed test, a rule’s closure or the guests sent [CONFIRM: labels never change a day’s closed or likely-closed status or its guests], and after `dataThrough` they set nothing: an upcoming booking reaches this read as the linked note confirming made (10.18). `own_event` and `other` set nothing. The schema (`townwise.lab-input/2`), the lab and `LAB_MODEL_VERSION` are unchanged; the fingerprint changes, so the weekly refresh refits that location. The backtest reads these history flags on fold days as known ahead, since the export has no created times [CONFIRM: past bookings on the calendar were entered before their day, so the backtest may read them]. Since labels touch only days before every run’s `dataThrough`, D49’s scoring needs no change.

The lab's reasons carry no `booking` on open private-event days (`modeling/lab/townwise_lab/forecast.py`), so rule 3's exception does not catch it.
- **Privacy.** A note's reason carries its kind words, guest count and hours, never its detail; TownwiseAI's `get_forecast` sends each note reason's guests and outcome, never its detail or id. A rule's reason carries its schedule's words, guest count and hours, never the rule's text, and `get_forecast` sends its `rule: { guests, outcome }`, never the text or id. The read logs nothing and stores nothing, as before.
- **Rules in the day classes (D32).** A covering rule schedule with effect `more_guests` or `fewer_guests` says a near-empty day was open exactly as a note does, in TownwiseAI's `get_sales_days` and `get_day` (both read `BusinessRuleStore.scheduled`), in `classOfDay`, `closureOfDay` and `yourHistory` of `api/src/people-in-town/history.ts` (a `rules` parameter, default none) and in the client's `dayContext` (`rules`, default none; `ruleSchedules` maps rules to schedules). A rule changes only the closed and likely-closed checks, and no rule makes a day `noted`, since it is no note. A rule's closure or buyout closes the day as a closed note does, except that a covering note that decides the day sets it aside, and before the town's today a rule's closure holds only when the day's guests are missing (no row, no guest count or 0) or under the likely-closed line, so a past day's real guests beat a standing rule (`closingRules` in `api/src/closed-days.ts`; `get_sales_days`, `get_day`, `classOfDay`, `closureOfDay` and `yourHistory` take the town's `today`, and the client's `dayContext` takes it as `today`; without one every day counts as past). The people in town reader (`api/src/people-in-town/reader.ts`) passes the location's scheduled rules to `yourHistory` (pinned by `api/test/chat-estimate-tools.test.ts` > "counts a near-empty day in that history only when a business rule’s schedule says it had fewer guests"), and Analytics (P24) fetches the rules and passes them to `dayContext`. The forecast, the lab's input and the Calendar read rules too.

### 14.6 Weekly refresh, engines and publish policy

D42 (OpenSpec change `autonomous-forecasts`; contract: its `design.md` and spec deltas). Every location of an organization whose forecasts are on (G1) keeps a published forecast reaching 91 days past today, refreshed weekly by a background worker (a scheduled Container Apps job, not a timer in the API). The change lands in phases, each on by default (owner directive, 2026-11-16) and inert while the lab runner is off (its `design.md`, decision 15). **Built in phase 1:** the reads (92 days, `accuracy`, `scored`, `engine` and the baseline’s label; 14.4, 10.13), `seasonal_baseline` as a model family (6.20), and the client and the staff view accepting every new state, field, requester and gate reason below before the API sends them. **Built since:** the lab’s two engines and input version 2 (phase 2); the publish rules, the system requester, the fingerprint, the ranged read and the `calibrated` and `stale` states (phase 3a); the weekly refresh and its worker, its collections, the staff pause, the env vars, the `engine_switched` reason and forecasts on by default (phase 3b, 2026-11-16); Home’s Last week, its tile and the model card’s engine and `stale` words (phase 4, P11, 2026-11-16); the public and privacy copy, drafted for the owner’s approval before any push (phase 4b, 2026-11-16); the worker’s scheduled job `caj-townwise-forecasts`, its alerts (two, and a third for a killed execution since the 2026-11-17 review) and the explicit `TOWNWISE_WEEKLY_FORECASTS=true` in `api/production.env` (phase 5, 2026-11-16; created with the lab, `infra/README.md` step 20). **Decided, not built yet:** an end-to-end test and a local demo before any push (phase 7). Until a phase lands, 10.15 and 14.4 say what runs.

- **The weekly refresh** (`api/src/lab/schedule.ts`, run by the worker `api/src/workers/weekly-forecasts.ts`; the API's server process starts no loop). While the lab runner is on (18) and `TOWNWISE_WEEKLY_FORECASTS` is true, the worker runs one pass and exits: in production a Container Apps scheduled job, `caj-townwise-forecasts` (the API image with a command override, hourly, parallelism 1, its own managed identity), starts it every hour, and locally `npm run worker:forecasts -w @townwise/api` runs one pass (`--loop` ticks hourly). Only the pass that claims the lease on `tw_forecast_schedule` (6.25) by compare-and-set acts, so overlapping executions do no harm. The lease lasts 10 minutes and is renewed by compare-and-set before each location; when a renewal fails (another replica holds it, or the store is down) the holder stops the pass at once and starts nothing more, and a later pass continues. With the runner off, the switch false or the schedule paused, no calibration is started. [Build note: phase 3b. The worker is a second composition root that reads the same `config.ts` schema; its `--now` (development only, refused in production) decides only which locations are due, while what a pass records keeps the real clock. Locally the worker and the API share `TOWNWISE_LAB_LOCAL_SECRET` (18) so a job the worker started can call the API back.] Mongo holds the lease, as for the file sweep (6.14), because the record that a week was done must outlive a cache flush; the worker needs no Valkey (Valkey is the API's sidecar, and a scheduled start uses no limiter).
- **Which locations start.** The lease holder considers each location of an active organization whose forecasts are on, found through `stores/cross-tenant.ts` with its scope minted by `access/policy.ts`, one at a time. It starts a calibration only when it is Monday at 03:00 or later in the location’s town time zone, or a later day of that week up to the end of Sunday; the location has no `tw_forecast_weeks` row (6.26) for that Monday; its history span (first to last day with guests) is at least 230 days; fewer than 3 scheduled calibrations are live across all organizations; and its fingerprint differs from its reference calibration’s, or the published run would lapse first (below). The fingerprint (`dataSha256`, 6.23) is the sha256 of the lab input without `calibrationId`, `today` and `champion`, with the input schema version and `LAB_MODEL_VERSION` (an API constant held equal to `modeling/lab/townwise_lab/version.py`’s `MODEL_VERSION` by a contract test), so a change to the lab’s model refits every location once. The reference is the location’s newest calibration whose gate published its draft or refused it on its own data; a failed calibration, or one refused `forecasts_off` or `champion_changed`, is never one, so switching G1 on after a `forecasts_off` draft gets a fresh calibration the next Monday, and a calibration from before D42 has no fingerprint and counts as changed. The calibration carries the `regimeStart` of the calibration that made the current published run (null without one), so the owner’s pattern change is not dropped; when the history no longer holds that date (before its first day or within 8 weeks of its last, as after an upload is turned off, D28) the start drops it (null, logging `townwise.weekly_refresh_regime_dropped { orgId, locationId }`) rather than being refused every week. A start blocked by a live calibration of the location (a person’s) writes no row and is tried each tick until that week ends in the town; one past the live cap writes no row either and waits for a later tick, as live ones finish. [Build note, 2026-11-17 review: at 3 live at once and one pass an hour, Monday alone (03:00 to midnight) starts at most 63, so a location with no row is considered on every pass of its week, not only on Monday, and the locations the live cap held back (the newest, by the candidates’ order) are caught up on Tuesday or later instead of missing the week; the weekly cap of about 200 is then reachable.] Unchanged data is still refit when no published run will be current (28 days ahead) at the next Monday’s pass and the run its reference published ended at its today plus 91 days, since a refit on the same days ends later (a run’s end moves with today; `refitExtends` in `schedule.ts`, since the 2026-11-17 review): without it a location with no new uploads lost its forecast 63 days after the last refit. Nothing in the schedule names a town, an organization or a location. [CONFIRM: a scheduled calibration starts from 03:00 on Monday in the town's time zone] [CONFIRM: at most 3 scheduled calibrations live at once across all organizations]
- **Week rows.** Before starting, the holder inserts the week row as `starting`, then sets it `started` with the calibration id, or `start_failed`. When the runner refuses the job (an outage), the row is removed so a later tick that week tries again, until 3 of the location’s system calibrations have failed to start in the last day, when it records `start_failed` (`SCHEDULE_START_TRIES`). [CONFIRM: a scheduled start the runner refuses is tried again each hour that Monday, up to 3 times] A tick that finds a `starting` row older than the lease looks for a calibration of that location requested by the system at or after the row was written, and sets the row `started` with it or `start_failed`. Skips are recorded as `unchanged`, `not_enough_history` or `cap_reached`. A started calibration is never retried that week, even when it fails.
- **Who pays, and the bounds.** A scheduled calibration’s requester is `{ userId: null, role: 'system', via: 'scheduled' }`. It is not charged to the organization’s TownwiseAI month (`chargedMicroUsd` 0), does not count toward its 4 a day, is not refused for a spent budget, may start from a 230-day span, and still holds the location’s one live slot. Roughly `TOWNWISE_WEEKLY_FORECAST_CAP` (default 200) week rows across all organizations are `starting` or `started` in one week; past it, rows record `cap_reached` (approximate only in that a stopped holder’s `starting` rows count until resolved). At about $0.03 of compute a run that is roughly $6 a week at most, paid by Townwise. Each start records the audit event `calibration.scheduled` (actor `system`; location id and calibration id only). A calibration a person starts keeps D27’s charge and limits; since 2026-11-19 it may start from a 230-day span too (its refusal under that says “Calibration needs at least 230 days from the first to the last day of sales history, for Townwise’s baseline. Its demand model also runs from 595 days, which a location needs while its current forecast is from the demand model.”), and the lab, handed the same input, picks its engine as for a scheduled one. [CONFIRM: a calibration a person starts may also start from a 230-day span and then runs the baseline engine alone under 595 days, still charged $0.10 and one of the 4 a day] [CONFIRM: scheduled calibrations are paid by Townwise, not the organization's TownwiseAI month, and do not count toward its 4 a day] [CONFIRM: roughly 200 scheduled calibrations a week across all organizations]
- **Three ways to stop it.** `TOWNWISE_WEEKLY_FORECASTS`, true by default, is the deploy-level off (18). Staff pause and resume every scheduled start from the console (P21, `POST /api/admin/forecast-schedule { paused }`, policy `staff`, audit `forecast_schedule.paused` or `forecast_schedule.resumed`), which sets `paused` on the schedule document and takes effect at the next tick; it pauses the whole weekly worker, TownwiseAI’s weekly suggestions included (`weekly-forecast-suggestions`). Switching an organization’s forecasts off (G1) stops its scheduled starts at once, since only switched-on organizations are considered. None of the three cancels a calibration already live.
- **The pass’s time.** [Build note, 2026-11-17 review.] A pass has 8 minutes from its start (`SCHEDULE_PASS_BUDGET_MS`), inside the job’s 600-second replica timeout, so an execution is not killed mid-location (a killed weekly suggestions call would otherwise be recorded failed for its whole week by the next pass, its reservation handed back though the call may have been billed). It takes another calibration location only with at least a minute left (`SCHEDULE_STEP_MS`), and another weekly suggestions location only with the call’s whole 2 minutes and that minute left; otherwise that part ends `deadline` and the rest wait for the next hour’s pass, whose week stays open until Sunday ends.
- **Visibility.** Each pass ends with one log line, `townwise.weekly_refresh_pass { started, failed, skipped, capped, ms }`, counts and time only, never an id or a figure. The console’s Forecasts section (P21) shows each location’s latest week row. [Build note: phase 3b adds `state` (`ran`, `off`, `paused`, `lease_held`, `lease_lost`, and since the 2026-11-17 review `deadline`) to the line, a code; a location whose turn throws logs `townwise.weekly_refresh_location_failed` with its organization and location ids, as other lab lines do, and the pass goes on.] `infra/README.md` adds a log search alert, like the daily-cap alert, for a pass reporting `failed` above 0 or no pass line for 8 days while the switch is on. [Build note: built as three alerts (phase 5, and the 2026-11-17 review): `townwise-forecasts-failed`, hourly, for a pass or weekly suggestions pass with `failed` above 0, a location whose turn threw (`townwise.weekly_refresh_location_failed`, `townwise.weekly_suggestions_location_failed`), a worker that stopped on an error, or a pass on a Sunday (UTC) with `capped` above 0; `townwise-forecasts-killed`, hourly over two hours, for an execution whose start line (`townwise.weekly_worker_started`, first in the worker) has no pass or error line from the same replica after 15 minutes, which is one the job’s 600-second timeout killed or that crashed; and `townwise-forecasts-missing`, every 6 hours, for no pass line in a day (not 8 days: a pass logs a line every hour, and log search windows stop at two days). Since the 2026-11-17 review a fourth, `townwise-forecasts-held`, hourly, fires when the API logs `townwise.calibration_finished` with gate `jump_held` (ids and the code only), so staff learn of a draft the jump guard holds for them (14.6) and publish or withdraw it; after a real level shift every weekly refit is held until they do. Since the second 2026-11-17 review `townwise.calibration_finished` also carries the requester’s `via`, and `townwise-forecasts-failed` also fires on that line with `via` `scheduled` and `status` `failed`: a scheduled calibration whose lab job crashed, timed out, or answered a failure or a result the API refused, which is not retried that week, so a broken lab image is seen within the hour, not when forecasts lapse. A pass counts the scheduled calibrations it times out in `failed`.]
- **Two engines** (`modeling/lab`). Every calibration runs the baseline engine, and also the trained model when the history span is at least 595 days. Both are backtested on the same weeks, each scored from a cutoff at least 28 days before its Monday. The lab returns the current engine’s run (`champion.engine`, 10.15) unless the other engine’s backtest weekly WAPE is at least 0.5 points lower on those weeks and the other engine passes the gate’s absolute checks (12 or more weeks with an 80% range, 65% to 95% of them inside it, a backtest weekly WAPE under that engine’s own weekday median’s on the same days, at least 0.5 points under for the model and strictly under for the baseline, for the baseline a weekly bias within 5 points, and for the model a mean absolute weekday bias no more than 2 points over the current run’s recorded backtest, `champion.recordedWeekdayBiasMeanAbs`, when it has one); with no current run, the model’s when it is at least 0.5 points lower than the baseline’s, else the baseline’s, but the other engine’s when that one fails those checks and the other passes them (`pipeline.passes`). A tie keeps the current engine, so close engines do not flip-flop, and a current engine that fails its checks is kept while its run stays published. When the current engine is the model and the model did not run, the lab returns the baseline’s run, which the gate holds (`model_not_run`). The scorecard carries `engine` (the run returned) and `engines` (each engine’s backtest metrics, the model’s null when it did not run).
- **The baseline engine** (`modeling/lab/townwise_lab/baseline.py`). Each open day is its weekday’s recent level times last year’s seasonal shape times the location’s own calendar effects. The level is the median guests of the last 8 open same weekdays on or before the cutoff, needing at least 3. The shape is last year’s same-weekday guests in the 3 weeks around the date less 364 days over last year’s level at the cutoff less 364 days, leaving out event and holiday days, clamped to 0.5 to 2, and 1 when last year has fewer than 3 such days. Each event or holiday group on the day multiplies by the median ratio of its past days to the same weekday without it (an event needs 3 days with it and 3 without; a holiday 1 past occurrence against the 4 weeks either side). Day statuses (closed, booked) come from the same rules as the model’s; notes and scheduled business rules act only through the input’s flags and the read (14.5), never inside the engine. Its run has `model.family` `seasonal_baseline`, the model’s reason kinds, and `effectPct` from the engine’s own multipliers (so 14.4’s effects read `basis: 'model'` for a baseline run). Its minimum history is 230 days, the span that always gives 12 backtest weeks with an 80% range, pinned by a lab test; it applies to scheduled calibrations only. [CONFIRM: scheduled calibrations, which can only use the baseline engine below 595 days, may start from a 230-day span of history; this supersedes the owner's 2026-11-10 decision of 595 days for the baseline engine on scheduled calibrations only, while a calibration a person starts and the model engine keep 595 days]
- **Publish rules, for every calibration** (`api/src/lab/gate.ts`). After G1 (forecasts on and the organization active, else `forecasts_off`), every draft is judged the same way, whoever started it. With no current published run, a model draft needs today’s first-forecast rule (10.15) and a baseline draft its absolute checks. With a current lab run of the same engine that has a recorded scorecard, the draft needs its engine’s absolute checks and the refresh tolerance. With a current lab run of the other engine, the lab’s same-weeks comparison stands and the draft needs its engine’s absolute checks; the gate makes no second cross-engine comparison against a recorded backtest from different weeks. With a current run that has no recorded lab scorecard (an imported run), the draft keeps 10.15’s comparison on held-out weeks after that run’s `dataThrough`. A baseline draft made because the model did not run while the current run is a model run stays a draft (`model_not_run`), so a model run is never replaced by a baseline for want of data. `GATE_WORDS` words every new reason. [CONFIRM: a same-engine draft is compared with the current lab run's recorded backtest instead of held-out weeks after that run's cutoff, and an engine switch is decided by the lab on the same backtest weeks with a 0.5-point margin, a tie keeping the current engine]
- **The refresh tolerance.** A same-engine draft publishes (`refreshed`) when its backtest weekly WAPE is no more than 0.5 points above the best (lowest) recorded backtest weekly WAPE among the runs of the current streak (the consecutive published lab runs of that engine for the location that still reach 28 days past today, newest first, back to the first one of another engine, imported or lapsed); otherwise it stays a draft (`refresh_worse`). A tie publishes, the one exception to G2’s “ties do not publish”. Measuring against the streak’s best keeps the tolerance from compounding: refits of 9.1%, 9.5% and 9.6% hold a fourth at 9.7%. [Build note, 2026-11-17 review: the streak stops at a run that has lapsed, so after a lasting rise in backtest error refits are held only while the last run before it is current (about 9 weeks), and then publish again, instead of a best that has lapsed holding every later refit.] [CONFIRM: a same-engine refit publishes when it passes its absolute checks and is no more than 0.5 points of weekly WAPE worse than the best recorded backtest in the current streak]
- **Absolute checks.** A model draft: coverage 65% to 95% on at least 12 backtest weeks with an 80% range, weekday bias no more than 2 points worse than the current run’s recorded backtest (when there is one), and weekly WAPE at least 0.5 points under the weekday median (`weekdayMedianWeeklyWape`). A baseline draft: at least 12 backtest weeks with an 80% range (`too_few_weeks`), coverage 65% to 95% (`coverage_out_of_band`), weekly bias (forecast less actual over actuals, summed across the backtest weeks) within 5 points either way (`biased`), and weekly WAPE lower than the weekday median’s (`baseline_not_beaten`; a tie fails). [CONFIRM: baseline publishes when the model is not eligible or does not win] [CONFIRM: a baseline's absolute checks are 12 backtest weeks with an 80% range, coverage 65% to 95%, weekly bias within 5 points, and a lower weekly WAPE than the weekday median]
- **The jump guard.** When a draft passes every other check and there is a current published run (or, with none, a published run that has lapsed: the newest one, so a draft after a lapse is not published unseen), the gate sums both runs’ middles over the 28 days from the calibration’s `today`, on the days both forecast open. When the draft’s sum differs from the current run’s by more than 25% either way, it stays a draft (`jump_held`) for staff to publish or withdraw (a draft summing 5,200 guests against the current run’s 4,000 is held; one summing 4,300 is not), so a data error such as a doubled upload never reaches owners unseen. [CONFIRM: a draft whose next 28 days' middles differ from the current run's by more than 25% is held for staff]
- **Horizon.** A lab run carries the days from the day after `dataThrough` through the calibration’s `today` plus 91 days, capped at 182 days after `dataThrough`, and only the Monday-to-Sunday weeks wholly inside them, so a location whose sales lag still sees 91 days ahead. The scorecard keeps `horizonDays: 28`, which alone the gate judges, and adds `horizon91` (the backtest weeks forecast from a cutoff at least 91 days before their Monday, `{ weeks, weeklyWape, coverage80 }` or null) and `horizonReach` (the same at the run’s longest lead in whole weeks, when sales lag past 91 days, or null), reported to staff and TownwiseAI. Days with a lead of 29 to 91 take the 80% range widened by the ratio of the 91-day to the 28-day backtest weekly band, longer leads by the reach’s ratio, never less than 1; weeks likewise by their first day. When a horizon’s backtest has fewer than 8 weeks, the run stops at the last day the shorter horizon covers (28 or 91 days of lead). A run needs 28 days left to stay the current run (`gate.ts`), so a 91-day run stays current for about 9 weeks without a refresh. [CONFIRM: runs reach today plus 91 days, capped at 182 days after the last day of sales; ranges past 28 days of lead widen by the backtest's longer-horizon bands; a run stops where fewer than 8 backtest weeks back the next horizon] [Build note: D52. Built in phase 3a: the reader reads rows by range (`ForecastStore.rows`’ `range`): the window and a week either side, and the past days of each run reaching them, which live accuracy and `accuracy` score, instead of every row of every published run, so about 52 weekly runs a year stay fast. Its answers do not change, pinned with 52 published runs.
- **The engine’s words** (built in phase 1). A baseline run’s label is “Townwise's baseline from your recent weeks and the town calendar”; a model run’s keeps “Townwise demand model v{n}” (14.4).
- **`calibrated` and `stale`** (14.3; `api/src/calibration.ts`). For a location with a published run, `calibrated` when the newest published run’s `dataThrough` is on or after the last day with guests, and `stale` when it is before it, both with the run’s `dataThrough`, `newerDays` (days with guests after it) and `nextRefresh` (the Monday the weekly refresh will next consider the location, that same day on a Monday before 03:00 in the town [build note, 2026-11-17 review], or null while the lab runner is off, `TOWNWISE_WEEKLY_FORECASTS` is false, the schedule is paused or the organization’s forecasts are off, or while the location’s guest span is under the weekly refresh’s 230 days, which the schedule only records `not_enough_history` for, as for a run a staff import published [build note, 2026-11-17 review]; and, for a stale location, null when its reference calibration already read every day with guests, since that refit was refused and the next Monday finds the data unchanged, so the words never promise a refit the schedule will skip [build note, 2026-11-17 review]). Derived on every read and never stored; notes and rules are left out of `stale` on purpose, since they act on the forecast at read time (14.5). Where it shows (the model card and TownwiseAI), `stale` reads “Forecast made from your sales through {Sun, Nov 15}. Townwise refits on {Mon, Nov 23} with the {6} days since.”, or with `nextRefresh` null “Forecast made from your sales through {Sun, Nov 15}. The {6} days since aren't in it yet.” A location with days and no published run stays `not_calibrated`.
- **Privacy.** The lab input never carries a calendar entry’s title, URL or source label, a note’s text or a name (10.15); the week rows, the pass’s log line and `calibration.scheduled` carry ids, codes and counts only (G4). The training data stays on Townwise’s infrastructure.
- Tests: built in phase 1, `api/test/forecast-score.test.ts`, `api/test/estimates.int.test.ts`, `api/test/chat-estimate-tools.test.ts`, `api/test/forecast-file.test.ts`, `api/test/lab-views.test.ts`, `client/test/portal/estimates/forecast-schema.test.ts`, `client/test/portal/console/calibrations.test.web.tsx` and `client/test/portal/console/forecasts.test.web.tsx`. Later phases add `api/test/lab-gate.test.ts` (one test per publish scenario), `api/test/lab-input.test.ts`, `api/test/calibration.test.ts`, `api/test/weekly-refresh.int.test.ts`, `api/test/forecast-weeks.int.test.ts`, `api/test/forecast-schedule.int.test.ts` and the lab’s `modeling/lab/tests/test_baseline.py` and `test_pipeline.py` (the change’s `tasks.md`).

---


**Refits after training changes (D59).** Whatever `TOWNWISE_AGENT_AUTO` or an organization's `agentAuto` says, a change that can move the lab input marks the location: `tw_locations.refit.wantedAt`, set with `$max` (`api/src/agent/refit.ts`): an applied or undone TownwiseAI change touching a day on or before the location's last stored sales day, every applied sales upload (the route, staff setup, the file reader, a TownwiseAI read), a file read's undo, and a person's note or scheduled rule created, edited or deleted on such a day. On any day, after the week's locations, the hourly worker pass takes each location of an active organization with forecasts on whose mark is at least 15 minutes old and that started no refit in the last 24 hours (`refit.startedAt`), and with no live calibration of its own: it fingerprints the lab input as above; unchanged (or under the baseline's 230 days) clears the mark; changed starts a calibration as the system (free, not one of the 4 a day), inside the live cap of 3 and counted in the weekly cap with the week's rows and the refits started in the last 7 days, records `calibration.scheduled`, sets `refit.startedAt` and keeps the start in `refit.starts` (the last 8; Monday's pass counts them in the weekly cap too). A location the caps hold keeps its mark; a start the lab refused sets `startedAt` too, so it is tried again a day later. The mark is cleared by compare-and-set on the value read, so a change landing during the pass keeps it. Logged as `townwise.refit_pass { started, cleared, held, failed }`. The gate and the forecasts switch still decide publication. [CONFIRM: a training change refits as the system after 15 quiet minutes, at most once a day per location]
## 15. App shell

Mockup builders work from this section in parallel, so every page uses exactly these frames, bars, tabs, banner and patterns. Tokens are from `townwise-ds/project/tokens.json`. Class names are from `components/bundle.css`.

### 15.1 Four frames

| Frame | Used by | Top bar | Nav items |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Public** | `/sign-in`, `/totp` | the marketing Nav and footer, as on the SignIn artboard (**Exists**) | the marketing links |
| **Gate** | `/request-access`, `/waiting`, `/no-access`, `/joining`, the staff notice on `/settings/security` | `ground` fill, 64px; wordmark left; right: “Signed in as {email}” (`mono`, `text3`, hidden below 641px) and “Sign out” (text link) | none |
| **Client app** | members and org admins, and staff in view-as | `ground` fill, 64px | per role (15.3) |
| **Staff console** | staff | `panel` fill, 64px | Overview, Requests, Organizations, People, Audit log |

Every signed-in frame ends with a slim footer: a 1px `border` rule, then one `mono`, `text3` row: “Townwise is a student project. It is not an official Dartmouth product.” and the links Privacy and Terms, `space-6` apart.

### 15.2 The client app layout

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| VIEWING AS  {email}, {Role} at {org}. Read-only until {time}.        [End view-as]   |  view-as only (15.5)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Townwise | {Org}  Home Calendar Orders Analytics TownwiseAI More v   Team Settings  {email} Sign out |  top bar
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| {LOCATION NAME}, HANOVER, NH                            Location [{name} v]  All locations |  page header
| {Page title}                                                                         |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| content, 12 columns                                                                  |
|                                                                                      |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Townwise is a student project. It is not an official Dartmouth product.  Privacy Terms |  slim footer
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

- **Grid.** Content max `content-max` (1280px), centered. Side margins `margin-fluid` from 1024px, `margin-tablet` (32px) from 641px, `margin-phone` (16px) at 640px and below, plus safe-area insets as on the SignIn artboard. Columns: 12 from 1024px, 8 from 641px, 4 below; gutters `gutter` (20px) and `gutter-phone` (16px).
- **Top bar.** At least `nav-height` (64px), with a 1px `border` rule below. In order:
  - the wordmark “Townwise” (`wordmark`, `white`), which links to `/dashboard`;
  - a 1px `border` vertical rule, 20px tall, then the organization name in `ui`, `text2`;
  - the nav links in `ui`, `text2`, `space-6` apart (`space-5` in the client app’s bar when it carries a location’s sections, so from 1280px the organization name and the email keep their room; D38), turning `white` on hover and with `aria-current="page"`, as Nav does. On the client app they are the location’s sections (15.3), with Notes, Rules, Town and Your data under More (D38), and Location settings after them for org admins, then Team and Settings as a group at the nav’s far end;
  - **More** (D38), in the sections’ place after Analytics: a button in `ui`, `text2` with the select’s drawn chevron (pointing up while open), turning `white` while open, on hover, or when one of its sections is current, with `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls`. On web above 640px its links drop down under it inside `<nav aria-label="Main">`, so Tab runs from More into them: a square `panel` box with a 1px `border`, each link at least 44px tall, over the page (while it is open the bar is lifted over `main`, and only then, so a layer drawn in `main`, such as TownwiseAI’s file drop, still covers the bar). Escape, with focus on More or one of its links, closes it and returns focus to More; a press or focus outside More and its links closes it. In the native apps above 640px its links take a row under the bar, under a `border` rule, as a navigation of their own named “More” (Android delivers no touch outside a view’s box); it stays open until More or another page closes it. Moving to another page or location closes either. At 640px and below there is no More: its links are in the phone menu (D51);
  - right (`margin-left: auto`): the signed-in email in `mono`, `text3`, then the light and dark switch, then “Sign out” as a text link.
  - **The light and dark switch** (web only; owner request, 2026-11-12): a 44px square button with a sun or moon icon, named for what a press does (“Switch to light mode” or “Switch to dark mode”), with a `raised` hover inside its square and the portal’s focus ring. It is in every bar (gate, client and console, at every width) and in the public pages’ header beside Sign in. Every page follows the system’s `prefers-color-scheme` until the person presses it; the pick is then kept in this browser (localStorage `townwise.theme`, the client’s one stored preference) and wins on every page and on later visits. The light palette keeps every token’s role: `white` is the main text (near black in light), the primary button is dark with a light label, and mint darkens to #136a53 so lines and text keep their contrast (dark mint stays #7bd2b4). Native apps stay dark and show no switch.
  
  `<header>` holds `<nav aria-label="Main">`, and the skip link is the first focusable element (Nav, **Exists**).
- **Below 900px** (`bp-nav-wrap`; below 1280px when the client app’s bar carries a location’s sections, which need the room), the nav links wrap to a second row under a `border` rule. Above 640px they never hide, apart from the ones under More (D38), one press away: the app has no footer that repeats them. At 640px and below the email hides and the organization name stays and truncates with an ellipsis.
- **The phone menu** (D51). At 640px and below the client app’s bar has no second row, no More and no Sign out in the bar. After the light and dark switch sits **Menu**: a 44px square button (`raised` on hover) named “Menu”, with `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls`. It draws two `white` lines, 20px by 2px, 8px apart. Opening, each line slides to the icon’s center in the first half of the motion, then turns 45 degrees in the second, one each way, so the two cross at their midpoints as an X; closing runs the same path back, and each half eases in and out. The panel moves with them: it fades in and drops 8px, coming out from under the bar (a box clips it, so it never draws over the bar’s rule), and fades out and lifts as it closes (280ms in all; with reduced motion the change is immediate). The panel is `panel` under a `border` rule, as wide as the screen: `<nav aria-label="Main">` with every link at least 44px tall, one to a row, in groups under `border` rules (the location’s sections; the ones the wider bar keeps under More; Team and Settings), the current page’s link `white` with its `aria-current`, then Sign out as the last row (disabled under view-as, as in the bar). It scrolls inside itself on a short screen. On web it hangs under the bar, over the page (the bar is lifted over `main` only while it shows), and closes on a link (the current page’s too; focus goes to Menu, as the link is about to leave), on Menu, on Escape with focus on Menu or in the panel (focus returns to Menu), and on a press or focus outside; in the native apps it is in the flow, and closes on a link or on Menu. A menu left open closes when the window passes 640px, and does not open More there. While it closes it takes no press and is hidden from assistive technology. The gate bar and the console bar keep their phone layouts.
- **Page header.** `space-8` above, `space-6` below.
  - Left, columns 1 to 8: the eyebrow (`tw-eyebrow`, `text3`), then the page title as the page’s one `<h1>`, styled `tw-h2` (40/44, then 32/36 below 1024px, then 28/32 at 640px and below), `text-wrap: balance`.
  - Right, columns 9 to 12, aligned to the title’s last baseline: the page’s actions (at most one primary), or on location pages the location switcher and “All locations”.
  - On location pages the eyebrow is the town alone, “{Town}, {ST}”, when the organization has one location (D29: with one location the UI never shows the location’s own name), and with several it names the location: “{Location name}, {ST}” when the name already ends with its town (“Sawtooth Kitchen, Hanover, NH”), else “{Location name}, {Town}, {ST}” (`locationEyebrow` in `client/src/portal/locations/naming.ts`). The title is the page’s own: Home “Welcome back, {name}.” or “Welcome back.” (P11), Calendar “Calendar” (P28), Analytics “Analytics”, Sales data “Sales data”, Upload “Upload”, Notes “Notes”, Town “Town”, Business rules “Business rules” (P29), Location settings “Location settings”. TownwiseAI has no page header: no eyebrow, title or side links (P25). The switcher and “All locations” (a text link to `/dashboard`) show only with more than one location, so with one location the header has no side links; Location settings is under the top bar’s More (15.3), not in the header.
  - Below 1024px the two stack.
  - Gate pages use the same header with the lead paragraph (`sub`, `text2`) under the title, in columns 1 to 7, and an optional side column 9 to 12, as on the SignIn artboard.
- **Location switcher.** Shown only when the organization has more than one location. It is a labeled select (“Location”) styled like a FormField input, and changing it navigates to the same page of the other location.
- **No location tabs.** The location’s sections are in the top bar (15.3); Sales data is reached from Analytics and from Upload’s result, and Location settings from More, for org admins.
- **Scrolling between pages** (D40; owner request, 2026-11-15). Every portal frame that scrolls (the client app, the gate pages, account settings and the staff console) is one scroll view that stays mounted while pages change (`shell/Frame.tsx`), and a change of path scrolls it to its top, without animation, on web and native, whether the move came from a link, a button, the top bar, a redirect, or back or forward, in a browser or on native, so a new page opens at its top. A change of query on the same page (the Calendar’s `?day=` and `?view=`, Orders’ `?day=`) keeps the scroll, and so does a page’s own scroll into view (the Calendar bringing its day panel into view below 1024px). Home’s This month opening a day in the Calendar (`?day=`) opens the Calendar at its top too, so below 1024px and on native its day panel stays under the grid. TownwiseAI’s frame, which fills the screen and does not scroll, and focus handling are unchanged.
- **Content.** Sections are separated by a 1px `border` rule with `space-8` between them. Panels have a `panel` fill, a 1px `border`, square corners, and `space-5` padding (`space-4` at 640px and below). Never put a `raised` fill inside a `raised` surface; outline the inner element with `line` instead. Reading width for forms and prose is columns 1 to 7; the side column 9 to 12 holds help text and summaries.

| Member | Home, TownwiseAI, Calendar, Orders, Analytics, More (Notes, Rules, Town, Your data); then Settings | All locations (more than one location) | No Team. Upload and notes are allowed (D16). [CONFIRM: Orders in every member’s top bar, after Calendar] |
| Org admin | Home, TownwiseAI, Calendar, Orders, Analytics, More (Notes, Rules, Town, Your data, Location settings); then Team, Settings | All locations (more than one location) | |
