The sections are Home (`/locations/[id]`), Calendar (`/locations/[id]/calendar`, P28, D30), Orders (`/locations/[id]/orders`, D35, which is also marked on its Ordering setup page, P31), Analytics (`/locations/[id]/analytics`), TownwiseAI (`/locations/[id]/agent`), Notes, Rules (`/locations/[id]/rules`, P29, D31, for every member), Town and Your data (`/locations/[id]/data`, D28, which replaces Upload; the upload page stays at `/locations/[id]/sales/upload` and marks Your data current, as an item’s page, P27, does). They open the location in the path; on a page outside a location (Locations, Team, Settings), the last location opened in this sign-in, held in memory only and never in storage, else the organization’s first. With no location the bar has only Team and Settings, and no More. Notes, Rules, Town and Your data sit under More (D38), and after them, for org admins only, Location settings (`/locations/[id]/settings`, P16); More turns `white` whenever one of them is current, or a page below one; the link inside keeps its `aria-current`. [CONFIRM: Notes, Rules, Town and Your data under More] `aria-current="page"` marks the section of the current page; Analytics is also marked (`aria-current="true"`) on Sales data, which lives under it, and Location settings marks its own link under More. The wordmark goes to `/dashboard` (Locations), which redirects to the only location’s Home when there is one. Settings is the account page, `/settings`. Two-step sign-in (`/settings/security`, **Exists**) is reached from Settings.

### 15.4 How the staff console differs

- **Unmistakable chrome.** The console top bar has a `panel` fill (the client app’s is `ground`). After the wordmark comes a kind tag, “Staff console” (`tw-tag` with no square: the StatusTag kind form, so no new status is invented).
- **Right side of the top bar:** “Verified until {time}” in `mono`, `text3`, then the staff email in `mono`, `text3`, then “Sign out”. The time is `staff.verifiedUntil`, a real time, not a live counter, and the page does not tick.
- **No organization name and no location tabs.** Console pages are full-width tables: NumbersTable styling (`mono` 12/16, tabular figures, 1px `border` rules, heads in `text3`, values in `text2`, row hover `raised`, rows at least 44px), each inside a focusable, named scroll region.
- **Overview first** (D48). The nav is Overview, Requests, Organizations, People, Audit log. Staff land on Overview (`/admin/overview`, P32) after sign-in and when a view-as or open as admin ends, and the console’s wordmark opens it. `/admin` stays Requests, and the frame keeps reading the pending count off it on every other console page.
- **Requests** shows its count in the nav as “Requests {n}”, with `{n}` in `mono`. The count is a number, not a dot or badge, and it is never animated.
- **Detail panels.** A selected row opens its detail in a panel: on the right from 1200px (columns 8 to 12), below the table under 1200px. The selected row takes the selected-row idiom (raised, border outline, 6px mint square, mint name).
- **No client figures.** Location rows show counts and date ranges only, with the line “Sales figures and notes are visible only through Open as admin or View as.” (D7, D25).
- **Web only by layout.** The console is designed for 1024px and up and stays usable at 641px. At 640px and below, tables become stacked rows. Native builds do not include console routes. [CONFIRM: console on web only]

### 15.5 The view-as banner

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| VIEWING AS   {email}, {Admin|Member} at {org}.   Read-only until {time}.  [End view-as]|
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

- **Position.** First in the page, above the top bar, full bleed, `position: sticky; top: 0`, above every other layer. At least 52px tall (`toolbar-height`). It is the second focusable element, after the skip link.
- **Look.** A `raised` fill with a 1px `line` rule below. `line` is a mark color, so the edge reads as a boundary, not decoration. Inside the content grid:
  - “Viewing as” as `tw-eyebrow` in `text3`;
  - “{email}, {Admin or Member} at {org}.” in `ui`, `white`;
  - “Read-only until {time}.” in `mono`, `text2`;
  - right: an outline button (`tw-ob`), “End view-as”.
  
  For a target with no organization, the middle reads “{email}, signed in, no organization.”
- **Never color alone.** No mint (mint is data and selection), and no `warning` or `error` (proposed, not adopted). The words carry the meaning.
- **Not dismissible.** It is `role="region"` with `aria-label="View-as"`. The document title is prefixed “Viewing as {email} · ”.
- **Phone (640px and below).** Two rows: the text, then “End view-as” at full width.
- **Read-only controls.** Every write control stays in place, so the layout matches the client’s, but renders disabled (15.7). Each form or section with writes shows one helper line: “Read-only while viewing as {email}.” Sign out in the client top bar is disabled too; End view-as is the way out. It sends `{ grantId }`, the grant the banner shows, so a tab left on an ended view-as never ends a grant the session started since (8a).
- **On expiry**, or when the target’s organization changes (Section 8), the next `GET /api/me` returns staff access without `viewAs`. The client goes to `/admin/overview` (D48) and shows the notice “View-as ended at {time}.”

### 15.5a The open-as-admin banner

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| You’re setting up {org} as Townwise staff. Its admins see each change you make in their Townwise staff activity. [End] |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

- **As 15.5.** Same position, look, never-color-alone rule and phone layout (two rows: the text, then “End” at full width), shown on every portal page while `openAsAdmin` is set. It is `role="region"` with `aria-label="Townwise staff setup"`, not dismissible, and the document title is “Setting up {org} · Townwise”.
- **No time.** The mode has no timer of its own (D25), so the line has none.
- **Every control is enabled**, Sign out included: signing out ends the staff sign-in, and with it the mode. Sign out first sends End with `{ grantId }`, so `open_as_admin.ended` is recorded at the sign-out; a failed End never stops the sign-out. Nothing is read-only and there is no helper line.
- **End** sends `POST /api/admin/view-as/end` with `{ grantId }`, the grant the banner shows (8a), and applies the answer, the staff member’s own access, so the client goes to `/admin/overview` (D48).
- **When it ends** (End, a suspension; never a join), the next `GET /api/me` returns staff access without `openAsAdmin`. The client goes to `/admin/overview` (D48) and shows the notice “Setting up {org} as Townwise staff ended at {time}.” once. A read that finds it ended sends End once, naming the grant it showed (4.3). When the staff sign-in ends, `GET /api/me` answers `staff_reauth_required` instead and the client signs out to `/sign-in` (P8), with no End; the next start or End records the end (8a).

### 15.6 Visual language

- **Dark, one theme.** The page is `ground` (#080a0d). Surfaces step to `panel` (#101317) and then `raised` (#181c21). Depth comes only from the fill step and 1px `border` (#34383e) rules: no shadows, gradients or blur. Exception (D40): a popover’s card (15.7) carries the `shadow` token, as a select’s open list on web does, so it reads above the page.
- **Swiss.** A visible grid, flush-left sans, objective labels, asymmetric headers. Square corners everywhere (`radius-none`); the app frame’s 8px edge belongs to the homepage console, not to app pages. Round shapes only for data marks. Exception (D26): on TownwiseAI only, the composer (radius 28), the person's message bubbles and the file chips (16) and the chips and the composer's button (22) are rounded; everything else there stays square. Exception (D40): the source chip (15.7) is a fully round pill wherever a source is linked.
- **Type.** Instrument Sans: display 600, UI 500, reading 400. Geist Mono for every numeral, with `tabular-nums`, for labels (`label`, uppercase, through `tw-eyebrow` and `tw-tag`) and for table cells. Sentence case. Fonts are self-hosted in the app (**Exists** on `feature/townwise-web`); mockups may link Google Fonts as the design system previews do.
- **Color roles.**
  - `white` (#eff2f6): primary text.
  - `text2` (#b5bbc2): secondary text.
  - `text3` (#9a9fa6): mono labels and fine print.
  - `line` (#7b8187): outlines and controls.
  - **Mint (#7bd2b4) is for data and selection only**: chart series, the selected tab or row (6px square and label), pressed controls, the focus ring and the skip link. It never fills a button, never colors a message, and never marks a warning.
  - Labels on a mint fill are `ground` (`on-mint`), never `white`.
- **The primary button is white** (`cta`): `white` fill, `ground` label, `text2` fill on hover. It is square, at least 44px tall, with a 15px `button` label and 18px side padding. **One primary per page**, for its main action; everything else is an outline button (`tw-ob`) or a text link (`tw-tl`). [CONFIRM: extends the Button rules to app screens, where labels vary by page]
- **StatusTag only for build status and kinds.** In progress (6px mint square) and Planned (6px outlined square) describe Townwise features, as on the homepage; College town, Seasonal town and Event town describe towns. A client’s own data state (“Not calibrated yet”, “Active”, “Invited”) is plain words, never a tag.
- **Charts** follow the design system: every chart has a text summary and “Show the numbers”, prints its scale and year, and keeps its SVG `aria-hidden`. Client sales series are `mint`, solid, 2px (`stroke-series`), with “Scale fitted to this location.” Town charts keep the Northeast dashed and the county solid.
- **Motion.** State changes only, 150 to 200ms with `--ease-out`. No spinners, shimmer or counters, and no pulsing but a loading skeleton’s opacity (15.7), save one exception the owner asked for: the ring by Replying on a TownwiseAI conversation in History (P25), still under reduced motion. One reduced-motion switch zeroes everything. The one exception is the two statement moments of 15.8, whose words fade in over 200ms each, 80ms apart, and which end within 5 seconds; reduced motion shows them whole and still.
- **Voice.** Second person to the operator, first person plural for the team, short declarative sentences, no exclamation marks. Say what exists, and only that. U+2019 apostrophes and curly quotes in every visible string, no em dashes, ranges as “80 to 115”, a true minus (U+2212) for negatives.

### 15.7 Shared patterns

- **Forms (FormField).** The label is `ui`, `white`. The input has a `ground` fill, a 1px `line` border, square corners, at least 44px height, and 16px typed text. The helper is `small`, `text2`, tied by `aria-describedby`. Focus is a 2px `mint` outline offset 2px, plus a `mint` border. Selects, number inputs, date inputs and textareas use the same anatomy. A select's open list is drawn in the app's style on every platform, never the operating system's: on web a `panel` list under the control (over it when the room below is short) with a 1px `line` border, square corners, 44px choices, group labels in `label` type, the highlighted choice `raised` with a 3px `mint` bar, and the current choice `mint` with a drawn check; on native the sheet. On web it is an ARIA select-only combobox (Down, Up, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down move; Enter or Space picks; Escape closes; typing jumps to a choice). Field messages print in white in the numbered, ruled list (`tw-msgs`), with `aria-invalid` on the field. [CONFIRM: error and notice colors stay unadopted, as the design system proposes]
- **Notices are toasts** (D55; `ui/toast.tsx`, one file for web and native). What an action the person just took did (“Saved.”, “You joined {org}.”, “View-as ended at {time}.”) shows as a toast, not in the page: wherever this spec says a page shows a notice for an action’s result, that notice is a toast. A toast is one line of `small` `white` text, with the notice’s link when it has one, in a `raised` box with a 1px `border`, square corners and the `shadow` token, at most 480px wide, centered 24px above the bottom of the window (above the safe area on native, and 144px higher on TownwiseAI, clear of its composer), with a 44px “Dismiss” button (×). No color carries meaning. The newest is on top; three show at most and the rest wait their turn. Each leaves by itself after 6 seconds; the time waits while the pointer is over it or focus is in it and starts over after. A toast with a link (“You joined {org}… Leave {org}.”, “See rejected requests”, “Open {org}”) never leaves by itself, since the region is last on the page and a keyboard or a screen reader may need longer than any timer to reach the link; it goes with its Dismiss button. Escape with focus in a toast dismisses it, and focus that was in a dismissed toast moves to the page’s h1 (or `<main>`), never to the body. While a statement moment (15.8) covers the frame, toasts wait unseen and show once it ends. The same words again within a second are ignored, and the same words again while their toast is up keep the one toast and start its time over. It slides up 8px and fades in over `fade`; with reduced motion it is simply there. The toasts sit in one polite live region (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, not atomic) that is in the page before the first toast, and iOS is told each one; a toast never takes focus, and its controls take the portal’s focus ring. When the action took away the control that had focus, focus moves to the page’s h1 (on the Calendar, to the day panel), never to the toast. A toast is drawn under an open dialog or popover, so a result that arrives while a popover stays open (Your calendars) stays a line in it. **What stays in the page**, in the ruled message style in `white` until the page changes it: every error and field message, anything the person has to read to fix something, and standing state that is no action’s result (`role="status"`): the view-as and open-as-admin banners, the read-only line, “This location isn’t available.”, no forecast published yet, a file read’s status lines, an upload’s summary and result steps, per-address results of adding people, results inside a TownwiseAI card, and a line that says the action did not happen or why something left the page (“This note isn’t available.”, “{location} was deleted meanwhile.”, why setup closed). [Build note: `<Notice>` is the toast, `<Notice stays>` the line for an action that did not happen, and `<InlineNotice>` the standing line (`ui/feedback.tsx`); the host is mounted once in `app/(gate)/(app)/_layout.tsx`. Pinned by `test/portal/ui/toast.test.web.tsx`, `toast.test.native.tsx` and `test/app/toasts.test.web.tsx`.]
- **Disabled controls** are not defined in the design system. Here they get `aria-disabled="true"` (not the `disabled` attribute), so they stay focusable and screen readers reach them and their helper line. They use a `text3` label with a 1px `border` outline and do nothing when pressed. A disabled primary has a `raised` fill, a `text3` label (6.43:1) and a 1px `border` outline, with no hover change. [CONFIRM: disabled style]
- **Destructive actions** have no red. Each is an outline button that opens a confirm dialog. Deleting data asks the person to type the location name, and the dialog’s action stays disabled until it matches.
- **Dialogs** have a `panel` fill, a 1px `border`, square corners, at most 560px width, and `space-6` padding. The title is `tw-h3`, the body is `small` and `text2`. Actions sit flush left: the dialog’s one primary, then “Cancel” as a text link. The backdrop is `ground` at 80% opacity. Focus is trapped while open and returns to the opener on close; Escape closes. [Build note: while a dialog’s action is pending, Cancel and Escape wait for its answer.]
- **Popovers** (`ui/Popover.tsx`, one file for web and native; D40). A card that floats over the page, anchored to the button that opened it, so nothing under it moves: a transparent `Modal` with no animation, as Dialogs use, whose card is `role="dialog"` named by its heading, a `panel` fill, a 1px `border`, the `shadow` token (as a select’s open list), square corners and 16px padding, at most its own width (Your calendars 440px, the note form 400px) and never wider than the window less 32px, its content scrolling inside it. The area outside the card is transparent (no dim) and is neither a tab stop nor a screen reader stop. From 641px it opens 8px below its button when the room below is at least 320px or at least the room above, else 8px above it, at most that room less 24px tall; its right edge lines up with the button’s when the button’s center is in the right half of the window, else its left edge, at least 16px from either window edge. Below 641px, or with no button to measure, it is pinned 16px from the top (under the safe area on native) and 16px from the left; below 641px it is the window’s width less 32px. While a keyboard shows (iOS, Android and web) the window’s bottom is the keyboard’s top, so no part of the card is under it and its own scroll brings the focused field into view; placement is measured on open and again on every window size change and every keyboard show or hide. On open focus moves to the card’s first control and stays in the card; Escape on web and Android’s back button close it, as does a press outside where that popover allows one, and focus then returns to its button, which carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` while it is open. While the action it started runs, it waits: its Close or Cancel disabled in place, and Escape, the back button and a press outside doing nothing, so the answer lands in it. Used by “Your calendars” and the note form on the Calendar (P28).
- **Source chips** (`ui/SourceChip.tsx`, one file for web and native, and on the public pages its DOM sibling `src/marketing/SourceChip.web.tsx`; D40). Every link to a source in the portal, TownwiseAI and the public pages is a pill at least 24px tall, fully round (12px corners), a `raised` fill with a 1px `border` outline and 8px side padding, holding the site’s logo in a 16px circle on `logoGround` (#f5f6f8 in both palettes, so a dark logo shows on the dark theme), 6px, then the site’s name in 12px sans `text2`, never cut or ellipsized. A chip moves to the next line whole; only a chip wider than its whole row wraps its name inside the pill. The link is a 44px target on web and native with the pill centered in it and no `hitSlop`, so in a row of chips the pills sit 8px apart across and a wrapped row’s 20px below the row above, and no two targets overlap. The logo is decoration, hidden from screen readers. The link’s name starts with what it shows: “{Dartmouth Registrar}. Source: {its label}” when the source’s own label differs from the site’s name, else “{name}. Source”; a second chip in one row with the same name is numbered (“Dartmouth Registrar 2”); and on web the label is the link’s `title`. Names and logos come from the committed manifest `client/src/portal/sources/logos.ts`, by the URL’s host without `www.`, then its parent domains down to two labels (a site without a logo of its own takes its nearest parent site’s); a host found nowhere, or a site with no logo, shows a plain globe in `text3`, with the host as the name when the site is unknown. The names are written by hand in `client/scripts/source-logos/sites.json`, and the logos are PNGs fetched once by `client/scripts/source-logos/fetch.mts`, run by hand, reviewed and committed under `client/assets/sources/`, so no chip loads an image from another site and the CSP is unchanged (`client/MODULE.md`, Security); a test fails when the shipped source data cites a host `sites.json` lacks. Plain-text citations (the Town profile’s “Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, QCEW, …”) stay text, and TownwiseAI’s row words keep their hosts (P25).
- **Tables** use NumbersTable styling in a focusable, named region. At 640px and below, rows become stacked label and value pairs. A table in a TownwiseAI reply scrolls sideways inside its own region instead (D26).
- **Loading** is a skeleton of the page in place of its content (`client/src/portal/skeleton/`): the page’s own sections, columns and tables (stacked at 640px and below, as the tables are) as square shapes, each the size of what it stands for, so nothing shifts when the content arrives. Text and figures are `raised` blocks as tall as their type and line, controls 44px `line` outlines, panels the `panel` surface. No mint and no sample values, so no skeleton suggests a number. The shapes pulse in opacity alone, from 1 to 0.5 and back over 1.6s on the ease-in-out curve, and are still under reduced motion (on native, also until the system answers). Screen readers hear one polite status line with the page’s loading words (“Loading your locations”), and the shapes are hidden from them. A part of a page that loads on its own (a month’s days, a place from Google, the audit log’s Load more) keeps a text line in place of that part, in `small`, `text2`, inside a box that keeps its height. [CONFIRM: loading skeletons, and their opacity pulse]
- **Errors** reuse the SignIn artboard’s strings word for word: “Can’t reach Townwise. Check your connection and try again.”, “Townwise isn’t responding. Try again in a minute.”, “Something went wrong on our side. Try again in a minute.”, “Something went wrong with that request. Reload the page and try again.”, “Too many attempts. Try again in {minutes} minutes.” Each comes with an outline “Try again”.
- **Empty states** say what is missing and what to do next, in one or two sentences, with the action as the page’s primary or a text link.
- **Numbers and dates.** Every numeral is `mono`, tabular. Guests print as whole numbers with thousands commas (“{n} guests”). Money prints in whole dollars with a `$` and thousands commas, rounded half up [CONFIRM: whole dollars in v1]. Dates always print their year (“Mar 2, 2026”), and times as “3:42 PM” in the viewer’s time zone. Day counts print as “{n} days”. No sample values ever appear in mockups: use `{slots}` (Placeholder data slot) for every number that comes from data.
- **Hit targets** are at least 44px. Every control shows the focus ring.
- **Phone (640px and below).** One column, 16px side margins, the top bar and banner as above, tables stacked, dialogs full width with 16px margins. There is no horizontal page scroll.

### 15.8 Statement moments

Two full-screen statements reveal word by word, hold, then dissolve into the page underneath. [Build note: `MomentProvider` (`client/src/portal/moments/`) is mounted in `PortalGate` and decides both moments from each access answer with `momentFor` (`moments.ts`).]

| Moment | When | Lead (`white`) | Follow (`text2`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Request received | right after a request is sent: the access goes from `no_org`, `rejected` or `removed` to `pending` in this session | We’ve received your request for {orgName}. | We’ll let you in soon. |
| Welcome | the first visit after approval, while `GET /api/me` carries `welcome` | Welcome to Townwise, {firstName}. (Welcome to Townwise. when `firstName` is null) | {restaurant}, ready to set up. |

- **Who gets the welcome.** Only the person whose approved request created the organization, while the organization has no sales day, never under view-as. Invited teammates and admins of organizations staff created have the Joining notice instead. `firstName` is the first word of the request’s contact name, or null for an honorific (`Mr`, `Mrs`, `Ms`, `Mx`, `Dr`, `Prof`), an initial or a word over 40 characters. The client calls `POST /api/me/welcome` once when the moment starts, so it plays once across devices. [CONFIRM: welcome for the requester only]
- **Copy.** No doubled full stop when a name already ends a sentence. The follow line of the request moment repeats the held page’s own sentence, so it stays true whether or not the approval email has shipped.
- **Layout.** A `ground` layer over the portal frame, the top bar included, with no shadow, gradient or blur. The wordmark sits exactly where the top bar draws it. The statement is flush left in the content column, at most 760px wide, vertically centered, both lines at the h2 scale for the breakpoint, 12px apart. Every word is laid out at full size from the first frame and only its opacity changes, so nothing shifts. No horizontal scroll at any width.
- **Timing.** The first word starts at 120ms. Each word fades in over 200ms (`--ease-out`), 80ms after the one before, closer together when a line would take longer than 640ms. A clause or a sentence inside a line holds 140ms more (at most twice a line). The follow starts 360ms after the lead lands, holds 1.4s once it lands, and the layer fades out over 200ms. Request received for a two-word name is gone at about 3.3s, and every moment ends within 5 seconds.
- **Reduced motion.** Both lines whole at once, still for 2.4s, then gone at once.
- **Any input ends it.** A press, touch or wheel is absorbed (it never reaches the page under the opaque layer) and fades the layer out; once that press is over, presses reach the page. On web a press is over when its click has landed on the layer, or 350ms after it lifts if no click comes, because a touch's click is aimed when the finger lifts; under reduced motion the layer goes at that point too. A key removes it at once and still does its job on the page (Tab moves focus). Repeats and lone modifier keys are ignored, and so is any input in the first 300ms, so the press that sent a request can’t end its moment. Android back dismisses it and is consumed. A moment that would start in a hidden tab keeps its ground up and waits until the tab is visible.
- **Screen readers.** The visual words are hidden from assistive tech, and the statement is said once, as plain text: on web through a polite live region that exists before any moment (`aria-live="polite"` without `role="status"`, so it never competes with a page's own status notice), on native through an announcement. On native with a screen reader running there are no visuals at all. The layer never takes focus.
- **One player.** `MomentProvider` in `PortalGate` plays one moment at a time; a page may call `useMoment().play(statement)` for its own statements and hold its own entrance while `useMoment().playing`.
- **When it decides.** On every new access answer (`GET /api/me`, or an answer applied in its place), in the same render, so the layer and `playing` are up before the page paints. Request received needs this session's previous answer in `no_org`, `rejected` or `removed` and the new one `pending`: a fresh load or Check again on Waiting plays nothing, and neither does a decline that returns an invited person to Waiting. Each moment is keyed (the request's id; the person and the organization for the welcome) and plays once in a session, so a later re-read that still carries `welcome` (its `POST` failed) does not replay it. Under view-as, or on the first answer after it, nothing plays and nothing is posted. Nothing is stored on the device.

It is used up when you continue, even if you don’t finish.”; back with “Use your authenticator app instead”). An accepted proof shows the notice “Your current authenticator app keeps working until you confirm a code from the new one.”, then setup’s Step 1 (titled “Add Townwise to your new authenticator app”) and Step 2, with the outline “Cancel and keep my current app”; a confirmed code shows the new recovery codes with “Other devices were signed out.” A wrong proof prints under its field (“That code didn’t work. …” or “That recovery code didn’t work. Each one works once.”), a timeout reads “That took too long, so nothing changed. Your current authenticator app still works. **P8. Staff sign in again (no page of its own).** When `GET /api/me` answers `staff_reauth_required` on any portal path but `/settings/security`, the client signs out at once (kit `POST /auth/logout`) and the gate opens the ordinary sign-in page, whose notice gives the reason:

- `session_before_codes`: “Two-step sign-in is on. Sign in again with your code.”
- `session_too_old`: “Staff sessions need a fresh sign-in with your code every 60 minutes.”

Until the sign-out answers, the gate frame shows “Signing you out”. A sign-out that fails shows “Couldn’t sign out. Check your connection and try again.” with Try again. `/settings/security` stays open in this state, so the recovery codes after enrollment (P7) are never cut off; P7's own “Sign in again” signs out from there. |---|---|

Add location (`/locations/new`, org admins).** Fields: Name, and Town (as P3); while the Google Places search is on, the form starts with the places checklist instead (as P3’s Step 1, 10.2a, with “Search Google Maps for the location”), and each checked place has a Name field that starts as “{Google name}, {Town}”, or “{Organization name}, {Town}” for a street address, with the town not repeated when the name holds it and the name cut so the town stays within 80 characters (D29, 10.3). While the organization has no location yet, a single checked place has no Name and is added with that default, and “Can’t find it? Enter it yourself” shows Town alone and names the location “{Organization name}, {Town}”; with a location already, Name shows on every row and is required, and existing locations are never renamed. Staff setup (P21) follows the same rules with the organization’s name and location count. Primary: “Add location”, or “Add {n} locations” with two or more checked, disabled with none checked or while one is loading. A Name left empty says “Enter the location’s name.” on its row, and nothing is sent. Otherwise it adds the checked places one after another, each with its place (the Names read-only and “Can’t find it? Enter it yourself” disabled meanwhile), and each row says how it went: an added row leaves the list; a name another location uses says “Another location already uses that name.” under that row’s Name, and the rest go on; a place Google now answers differently says “Google Maps answered differently this time. Search for the place again, or enter it yourself.” on its row, and the rest go on; the location limit stops the rest with “You’ve reached 25 locations. Write to hello@townwise.tech for more.”; a 503 says “Google Maps isn’t answering right now, so the place wasn’t added. Check the town, then add the location without it.” on its row and stops the rest; any other failure stops the rest with the error and “Try again”, which adds the rows left. Once every row is added, it opens the Home (P11) of the first location that press added. “Can’t find it? Enter it yourself” adds one location by hand, with Name and Town (after a row’s 503, filled in from that row) and “Search Google Maps instead” back to the checked places. Errors by hand: “Another location already uses that name.” and “You’ve reached 25 locations. Write to hello@townwise.tech for more.” On success it opens the new location’s Home (P11).

**P11. Home (`/locations/[id]`, the location’s first page)**

Home replaced the Forecast page here (owner decision, 2026-11-05); its data checks live in P24’s Your data. It is built around the Monday decisions: what is on this week, the bar order, last week against what happened, and this month in town. Until forecasts exist it shows only history and the calendar, never an unpublished guess: every figure is a sum, an average or a share of the location’s own stored days, always of a past day, apart from Who’s in town’s headcount range, which is printed only where public counts with stored sources support it (13.2; none is researched today). No figure from the location’s days is shown for a day after the last day of data or after today. It reads `GET .../sales/history`, `GET .../notes` and `GET .../calendar` (10.4, 10.10) in parallel, from two years and four weeks before this week’s Monday to the later of this month’s last day and today plus 6 days (This week’s last day), then on their own `GET .../agent` (the questions count) and `GET .../people-in-town` for this month (10.13), and writes nothing. “Today” is the device’s date; This week runs from today, as do Who’s in town’s This week and the month grid’s This week, Last week is the seven days before today, and the bar-order line reads last year’s Monday-to-Sunday week (all twelve towns are Eastern). Built from `client/src/portal/home/` and `client/src/portal/analytics/week.ts`. A status word (“Closed”, “Booked”, or “Likely closed” on a past day under a tenth of its weekday’s typical guests, D32) is its own line under the number, in mono uppercase that shrinks with a narrow cell to at most 10px so its longest word fits (at 375px a cell holds about 30px of text), “Likely closed” wrapping between its words; its label keeps the full words, “Likely closed ({1} guest recorded).”. A rule schedule with more or fewer guests says such a day was open, as a note does (D31), so Home reads the location’s business rules on their own, as none while they load or if the read fails. Each day’s label says everything it shows, the figure with its range (“Wed, Nov 11, 2026. Veterans Day.”, “Fri, Nov 6, 2026. This week. 1 note.”, “Sat, Nov 7, 2026. This week. Forecast about 282 guests, 250 to 310. Includes 70 guests from your notes. Sample game.”, “Tue, Nov 3, 2026. This week. 110 guests.”). Today is selected at first. On web the grid is `role="grid"`, named by its month, and one tab stop, each day as wide as its column and at least 64px tall from 641px (52px at 640px and below), growing with what it holds: Left and Right move a day, Up and Down a week, Home and End the row’s Monday and Sunday, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End the month’s first and last day, never leaving the month; the selection follows focus; a click, Enter or Space opens the day in the Calendar (`/locations/[id]/calendar?day={date}`); a mouse or pen over a day previews it and shows the Calendar’s tooltip (`aria-hidden`: the date, “About {212} guests ({180} to {240})”, “Includes {70} guests from your notes”, and the day’s three reasons with the largest effect either way, in P28’s Why order and short words (D40), “Saturday: usually more guests”, or its events and notes), and leaving the grid restores the selection and hides it; touch shows none. On native each day is a 52px button with its label and selected state, and a tap opens the day in the Calendar. The detail (region “Selected day”): the date as an h3 (“Today, {Thu, Nov 5, 2026}” for today); from today on, with a published forecast day, Forecast (“About {282} guests, likely {250} to {310}.”, plus “Includes {70} guests from your notes.” when notes added guests (“from your rules” or “from your notes and rules” when business rules with a schedule added them, D31); “Booked: a private buyout, {70} guests. No walk-in forecast.”; “Closed.”) and Why (the day’s three reasons with the largest effect either way, shown in P28’s Why order, D40: a run reason with short words for which way it usually moves guests, “Saturday: usually more guests”, “Thanksgiving Day: fewer guests last time”, “Sample game: more guests in Townwise’s model”, after its mark in its grade’s color (`aria-hidden`), or its label alone when it has no effect; a note’s or a rule’s by its label alone with no mark, since there the mark would be the only sign of its direction; 14.4), each row followed by its sources as chips; Reorder (D35: how an order is built, then how the next order relates to the day, from Home’s one read of `GET .../orders`: “The order from {supplier} arriving {date} lasts until its next delivery, {date}, so it plans for {day}.”, or that the day is outside it, or the board’s reason with no setup; “Checking the next order.” while it loads and “Townwise couldn’t check the next order.” if it fails; then the text link “Open this day on Orders”, P30 with `?day=`); On the calendar (each holiday and town event as “Veterans Day. Federal holiday.” with its sources as chips, less one Why already names, as P28’s panel leaves it out, each note in words with its detail, or “Nothing on the calendar this day.”, “Nothing else on the calendar this day.” when Why named them all; term and season periods are left to the list); then, with any history, This day (the day’s own figure for a past day with data, or “No sales stored for this day.”; a day after today has no line, ever), Same weekday last year (as This week’s Last year cell) and Two years ago (only with data).
- **On the calendar in {November}** (block, eyebrow “{November 2026}”): every event and note on the month in date order with its sources as chips (“Veterans Day. Federal holiday.”, “Your note: Private event, more guests than usual.”), or “Nothing on the calendar in {November}.”.
- **Who’s in town** (block, eyebrow “{Hanover}, {November}”): the month’s people in town from today on (13.2, `GET .../people-in-town` for the month, read on its own; `client/src/portal/home/InTown.tsx`), laid out for a glance (2026-11-12, owner request: “make the who’s in town easier to read”). With no headcount on any day of the month it opens with “Townwise can’t put a number on how many people are in {town} yet.” beside a Planned tag. Then the term by time, each group an h3 in `label` type over a 1px `border` rule. **This week** leads with today’s run of days: its headcount first where every input has a source (“{9,500} to {10,500} people in town”, the figure in 40px `value` type with its unit, then “Fall term classes until Tue, Nov 17.”), otherwise the term as one sentence at h3 size (“Fall term classes until Tue, Nov 17.”; “… for the rest of {November}.” when the run reaches the month’s end; “Townwise has no term dates until …” without a term); then a row for each run that starts by Sunday. **Later in {November}**: a row for each run that starts after this week, the dates in mono beside the words (“{Nov 20 to 25}”, “Fall term finals”; “From {Nov 26}”, “Townwise has no term dates”; “Between terms”), the dates over the words at 640px and below, and, when any day of the month has a headcount, the run’s figure (“{9,500} to {10,500} people”, mono 18px) or “No headcount”. Days before today are left out, and events are left to On the calendar. Under the groups, “Between terms is worked out from the term dates.” when a run shown is between terms, and the sources of the runs shown, once each, as source chips (15.7, D40; none of the holidays’ sources). **Your sales by term**: “Your Saturdays averaged …” when the location has days both in term and between terms, with its “From your sales, …” line. A town Townwise hasn’t researched says so. While the read is out, “Loading who’s in town…” keeps about the groups’ height (15.7), so the jobs under it don’t move. A failed read shows its error and Try again in that place only. Then, for one of the twelve towns, **Food-service jobs in {Grafton County}**: “{4.5% fewer} jobs in {November} 2025 than in an average month that year.” (“more”, or “About as many jobs … as …” when the gap rounds to 0.0; the figure in mono 18px), with “County, not town. Employment is a stand-in for demand.” and its source as a chip, “U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics”, labeled “U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, QCEW”.
- **Your {November} in past years** (block, eyebrow “Past {November}s”, only with a past year): one line per past year, newest first, at most three (“{118} guests a day over {30} days in 2025, {9%} below your 2025 daily average over {364} days.”, closed days left out; the year’s day count shows how much of that year the history covers), and “Averages leave out closed days.”.
- **Your history** (panel, root `nativeID` “home-history” for the Reading screen’s animation): “{n} days”, “{first} to {last}. {n} missing days in between. Last upload {date} by {email}.”, the newest year as a heatmap that takes no focus (web; `role="img"` named by its summary), where a mouse or pen over a day (never touch) rings it and shows the Calendar's day tooltip with its label's words, and a click on a day opens it in the Calendar (P28, `?day=`) when the Calendar shows it (12 months either side of today's; older days only hover) (owner request, 2026-11-17), and links “See it in Analytics” and “Upload sales history” (web; native says where to upload).
- **While onboarding’s `needsHistory(org, locations)` is true** (agreement 1 with session 54: the organization has locations and none has a stored day) and this location’s own history has no day: step 3, below, takes the place of At a glance, Bar order, Last week and Your history; This week (calendar only), This month and Who’s in town still show.
- **Step 3, Your history** (`client/src/portal/onboarding/`, `HistoryStep`; the Home2-Drop and Home2-Reading boards; 11A, 10.11). Mono “Step 3 of 3: Your history”, then “Drop in everything you have” and “Drop your exports as they are, as many as you have. Townwise reads the date, guest count and net sales for each day from them on its server.” Two columns from 1024px: the drop on the left; on the right the location card (“Your restaurant”, the name, the town and its kind) and “What Townwise keeps” (the files, stored privately with no public internet address, each original deleted after 365 days or sooner when deleted; from each file the three values a day and a cleaned copy; from a file the person let TownwiseAI read, what it found and adds, until undone on the file’s page (D34); download or delete them on Sales data). On the first view of a fresh step the card moves from the left into the rail once (280ms) while the drop fades in; with reduced motion, on narrower screens and on native it is simply in place. Nothing is kept in browser storage.
  - **Drop** (web): a dashed zone, “Drop files here”, “Many files at once is fine, by dragging them here or choosing them.”, the accept hint (11A’s cap from the create answer, never a constant) and “Choose files” (`multiple`, any type). Files dragged anywhere on the step drop there (“Drop to add {n} files”); one dropped elsewhere on the page is ignored, so the browser never opens it over the app and stops the uploads. Each file is its own row through the upload queue (storage2 15.2): name, size, a progress bar, “{speed} · About {t} left” or “Estimating”, “Waiting to upload”, “Reconnecting…”, the refusal’s words, and Cancel or Remove; above the rows “{n} files, {size} · About {t} left to upload”. Files from an earlier visit still uploading show “Upload interrupted. Drop it again.” with Remove. Primary “Read my history”, disabled with “Add at least one file.” until a file is stored. Then “What to drop in”: daily sales summaries; sales reports as Excel, CSV or PDF (a PDF needs a table, scans can’t be read); ZIPs of exports; check-level exports (item-level don’t work); as many years as you have; closures and events go on the Notes page (the sales reader takes only daily totals; TownwiseAI adds a file’s dated events as notes only for a file the person lets it read, D34).
  - **TownwiseAI opt-in** (web, while stored files are on; D34, 11A.9; `onboarding/useHistoryAi.ts`): under “Choose files”, the checkbox “Let TownwiseAI read these files and use what it finds”, off by default, described by the same help line and followed by the same link as P26’s. A file that finishes uploading while it is checked is sent to be read once, and only after Townwise has read it for sales (before that the request answers 400): as soon as the import’s status read lists it read, kept or failed, `org.data.ai_read` goes to its upload, `u_<uploadId>`, when it wrote days (its `f_` ref answers 404), else to `f_<id>`. One that finished while the box was unchecked never is, and a kind TownwiseAI can’t read is never sent. The file’s row then adds P26’s line: “Added. TownwiseAI is reading it; open it on Your data to see what it finds.”, “Added. {why TownwiseAI can’t read it}” or “Added, but TownwiseAI didn’t start reading it.” and why (a refusal never undoes the upload); nothing shows while it waits for the sales read. A 503 `ai_unavailable` hides the box for the visit. The step itself sends the request, so a checked file still being read for sales when the person leaves the step (Go to Home now, or closing the page) is never sent; it can be let in later from its page on Your data (P27). Under view-as it is disabled in place; native has no drop and no box, and the browser path never offers it.
  - **The browser path** (11.1) is always linked under the drop as “Prefer to send only daily totals? Read the file in your browser instead.”, and after a refusal or a failed status read as “Or read a CSV file in your browser and send only the date, guest count and net sales for each day.” While stored files are off (503 `files_unavailable`, from the status read or a create) the drop is replaced by “Read a file in your browser” and P13’s “Upload sales history”.
  - **Reading** (“Reading your history”, “You can close this page. Townwise keeps reading on its server, and Home shows your history when it’s done.”): “{done} of {n} files read · {About {t} left to read, Estimating, Waiting for a turn or Waiting for your answer}”; each file’s line (11A.6) with its own time left to read or “Estimating”, a bar when the server knows the total, a ZIP’s count and “See what’s inside” (its files inside, each with its status and reason, as on Sales data); the question (ImportQuestion) when the reader needs an answer; every file kept and not used with its reason; “Found so far” from the import’s counts; and the calendar of days read so far (the analytics heatmap, one picture named by its summary, unread days of the drawn years up to yesterday as “Not read yet”), re-read when the import applies more days. New drops join the started import. Native shows the same in words, with no calendar and no drop (“Drop your files from a computer at townwise.tech.”).
  - **Done**: “Done. {n} days, {first} to {last}.” and “Opening Home.”; after 2.5 seconds, or on “Go to Home now”, Home and the organization load again and the step leaves; on web Home’s history card grows from where the calendar was (280ms; reduced motion: it just appears), and focus moves to it when the step held focus. While this screen still has uploads running it waits (“Some files are still uploading. Going to Home now stops them.”). An import that found no day says “Done. Townwise found no days it could use in these files.”, keeps every file’s reason listed and the drop zone open.
  - **View-as**: no drop and no upload (no file input, the queue never created), “Choose files”, “Read my history” and the browser path’s link disabled with the read-only line, file names shown as their kind; the status reads run as any GET does.
  - A screen reader hears one status line when the step changes (reading, a question, done), never a time left or a byte count.
- No primary button of Home’s own.

**P12. Sales data (`/locations/[id]/sales`)**

- Coverage line: “{n} days, {first} to {last}. {missing} days missing in between.” With missing days, it adds: “Missing days might be closures. Add a closure note.” as a text link that opens C6 prefilled (closure, closed).

The line is `mint`, solid, 2px. On web a mouse or pen over the plot (never touch) marks the nearest calendar day with a 1px `line` rule across the plot and a `mint` dot on the line, and shows the charts’ shared tooltip (as TownwiseAI’s daily chart does): the day (“{Sat, May 30, 2026}”) and its value (“{486} guests”, or the net sales in dollars on the net sales series), or “No data” and no dot on a day without a value; the rule, the dot and the tooltip are `aria-hidden`, since the summary and “Show the numbers” carry the same numbers (D40; owner request, 2026-11-16). The y scale is printed with “Scale fitted to this location.” and the x ticks are months with their year. Text summary: “Daily guests, {first} to {last}. Highest: {value} on {date}. On native (D21), the page shows the text summary and the table, plus “See the chart at townwise.tech.” [CONFIRM: daily chart on Sales data]

Each point is P24 Year over year's own: the month's average over its days with a value that are not closed (Analytics' default filters, from the sales history, notes and rules), so both pages show the same numbers and a short month does not read as a drop, and a month the history does not run through from its first day to its last, such as the month so far, is a hollow point. Above the chart its line: “Average {guests | net sales} per day in each month, one line per year.”; under it P24's basis line (“Based on {n} days with a guest count. Leaves out {n} closed days.”). **P24. Analytics (`/locations/[id]/analytics`)**

Every figure is a count or an average of the location’s own stored days that the filters keep, from `GET .../sales/history`, `GET .../notes` and `GET .../calendar` (10.4, 10.10); the model card reads `GET .../estimates/about` (10.13). Nothing is estimated, nothing is shown for a day after today, and a figure with too few days behind it says so instead. The page writes nothing; its filters live in the page’s state only (never the URL or storage) and reset when it closes. Built from `client/src/portal/analytics/`.

- Lead: “{n} days, {first} to {last}.”
- **Filters**, one block that drives the page (labeled groups in a row on desktop, stacked on phones; a change never animates or moves focus):
  - Color by: Guests (default when any day has guests) or Net sales, a radio group with one tab stop whose arrows move the choice. A metric with no data is disabled, with “No guest counts in your history.” or “No net sales in your history.”
  - Show on the calendar (checkboxes, all on): Town events, Holidays, Your notes, Closures. They change only the heatmap’s marks and labels.
  - Include in the numbers: Closed days (off), Days with a note (on; closures follow Closed days only), Holiday and event days (on). They change every average, chart, type of night and the heatmap’s levels; a value they leave out is drawn as “Left out”.
  - Years: one per year with data, all on. Unchecking the last is refused: the box stays checked and “Keep at least one year.” describes it.
  - The checkbox is a shared control (`ui/Checkbox`): a real `<input type="checkbox">` in its `<label>` on web, a Pressable with the checkbox role and state on native; checked takes the `mint` fill with an `on-mint` check; disabled keeps its focus with `aria-disabled`.
- **Every day.** The heatmap (web): one grid per checked year, newest first, 7 weekday rows (Monday first) by week columns of square cells; four `mint` levels from the quartiles of the kept values, “No data” `raised`, “Left out” `state`, closed outlined, a white corner square for a holiday or town event and a `text2` one for a note. A visible legend above; under it the summary (“{Daily guests}, {first} to {last}. Busiest: … Quietest open day: … {n} closed days.” and what the town calendar covers) and the basis line; “Show the numbers” is the month table (Month, Days with data, Total, Average; every value in the checked years, kept or left out). Each year is `role="grid"` named “{year}, daily {guests}”, with row headers; each cell’s label says everything its fill and marks show. One tab stop for the whole heatmap, starting at the selected day or the last day with data: arrows move a day (up and down) or a week (left and right), Home and End the week’s Monday and Sunday, PageUp and PageDown 52 weeks across years, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End the first and last day with data; Enter or Space selects, Escape clears, and while a day is selected the selection follows focus. On web the selected day is in the address (`?day=`), so a refresh keeps it; with no `?day=` the heatmap can focus, the last day with data starts selected (owner request, 2026-11-17). Native starts with none selected. Days after today are blank and never focusable. A mouse or pen over a cell previews it; leaving the grid restores the selection. Native (D21): a month list, newest first (“{month}, {n} days with data, {average} on average”); a month opens its days as 44px rows (date, value, marks in words), and a day opens the Day panel under its row.
- **Day panel** (columns 9 to 12 and sticky from 1024px; under the heatmap below): the date and its status (Closed, No data for this day, Left out of the numbers by your filters, Today); Your numbers (Guests, Net sales, Usual for a {weekday} with the day count and the day’s change, Same day last year); On the town calendar, each event with its kind, dates and sources as chips (15.7, D40), and the line when the town’s research doesn’t cover the day; Your notes in words with “Open Notes”; Where it came from (“From the upload on {date} by {email}.”, “This upload didn’t finish.”, “Upload record not found.”) and, for an upload read from a stored file (F4), “File: {name} ({kind}).”, “Download cleaned CSV” (web, a finished upload; never under view-as, where the line reads “File: {kind}. Its name is hidden in view-as.”; native says “Download from a computer at townwise.tech.”) and “Open Your data” (P26); Previous day and Next day (they move the selection, and on web focus the matching cell); “Ask TownwiseAI about this day”, which opens P25 at `?about={YYYY-MM-DD}` to fill its composer with the day (it never sends by itself). Empty: “Point at or select a day to see everything Townwise has for it. Use the arrow keys to move between days.”
- **Weekly shape**, **By month**, **Year over year**, **By type of night**: each a text summary, the chart (web: inline SVG, `aria-hidden`, `mint` 2px marks with square ends, printed scale “Scale 0 to {n} guests. **P25. TownwiseAI (`/locations/[id]/agent`, members; `/locations/[id]/chat` redirects here)**

The location's chat with TownwiseAI (server contract: `docs/portal/tuning-chat.md` and 10.12), a chat page (D26). The page has no page header at any width: no eyebrow naming the location, no greeting, no location switcher or “All locations” (those stay on the location's other pages). Its one h1 is visually hidden and reads “TownwiseAI”. The chat header (the conversation's title, History, New chat and Questions and activity) is the first thing under the top bar, and the chat, the thread with the composer docked over its bottom edge, fills the rest of the screen's height. The page asks for no name; the name comes from Settings (P18) and greets on Home (P11). Messages and the composer sit in one centered column at most 760px wide. **Questions and activity** shows only on the new chat page (build note “Questions and activity on the new chat page”, 2026-11-18): from 641px a right column beside the landing, under the header (the landing takes columns 1 to 8 while it is open, 1 to 12 while it is closed), and at 640px and below a collapsed row under the suggestion chips that opens in place; inside a conversation neither it nor its button shows. The composer's button is the page's one primary; the composer, the person's bubbles and the chips are rounded (15.6, D26). Under view-as everything reads and versions still switch, by reading; every write control stays in place, disabled, described by the one read-only line.

- **Header**: no title and no rule under it, so the thread gets the height (History's list marks the open conversation); at the right **Questions and activity** (on the new chat page from 641px only; “Questions and activity ({n})” while n questions and weekly suggestions are open together, as P11’s link counts them; `aria-expanded`), **History** and **New chat**, wrapping on narrow phones. History is a disclosure over a small square dropdown, at most 360px and 60% of the window tall and scrolling inside, drawn over the thread on web (on iOS and Android it opens under the header, since Android does not deliver a touch outside its parent's box): each row is the title and date (mono), the open one marked with a mint 6px square and `aria-current`, with **Rename** (the title becomes the field “Conversation name”: Enter saves, Escape cancels; “Use 1 to 60 characters.”) and **Delete**, which asks “Delete this conversation?” with “TownwiseAI’s replies and your messages in it are deleted. Notes you saved from it stay.”; with none, “No conversations yet.” Escape, or opening a conversation from it, closes it and returns focus to History; on web a press outside it and History closes it and leaves focus where that press put it (not while a Rename field or the delete dialog is open). On web focus never falls to the page: a Rename field that closes returns it to that row's **Rename**, and after a delete it goes to History; when New chat, or opening or deleting a conversation, swaps the landing and the thread and focus went with the control used (on phones the header is drawn in each), the composer takes it. Optional.” with Got my numbers wrong, Made something up, Missed something I told it, Didn’t answer my question, Too long, Something else, and Skip), and under the row the **Based on** line, built in the client from that reply's tool cards and never written by the model (“Based on your sales from Oct 1 to Oct 31, 2026, your 12 notes, and Hanover’s town profile (bls.gov).”; no reads: “Based on this conversation only.”). Under it, when the reply's text cites web pages (D37, `sources` in `done` and in the conversation's GET), **Sources**: the label of a group of source chips (15.7, D40), one per page, each with its site's name and logo, or for a site `sites.json` lacks its host without `www.` and the globe, https links only, opening in a new tab on web (`noopener noreferrer`) and in the browser on native; live and read back from history alike. A failed or stopped reply keeps what arrived, says it wasn't saved, and offers **Try again**, which sends the same message as a new turn. A reply survives a refresh (D45): reloading the page, opening it in a second tab or bringing a phone back to the foreground opens the conversation with the running turn, shows the person's message and the reply so far, follows it to its end and then shows the saved reply; a stream that drops is read again from where it stopped, with no text twice. A reply whose replica restarted or died keeps what arrived and reads “TownwiseAI was interrupted. Your message and this reply weren’t saved. Try again.”, with **Try again**.

Regenerate streams a new version of the newest reply in its place; if that one isn't saved, the earlier one comes back. **P26. Your data (`/locations/[id]/data`)**

- Header: kicker “Everything your team added”, title “Your data”, and the lead “Sales uploads, calendars, files and text your team added for {location}. Open an item to turn it off and leave it out of your numbers, forecasts and TownwiseAI without deleting it.” (D61; it said “newest first” before the folders). With more than one location, a “Show” select (“{location}” or “All locations”) widens the list to the organization.
- Actions: the primary “Upload sales history” (P13; native says “Upload from a computer at townwise.tech.”), then “Add a file” (any kind of file up to 200 MB, kept as it is for the team; Townwise doesn’t read it for sales) and “Paste text” (a title of up to 120 characters and text of up to 10,000), both web only (D20). Under Add a file, the TownwiseAI opt-in (D34, 11A.9), off by default: a checkbox “Let TownwiseAI read these files and use what it finds”, described by “Each file you add is sent whole to Anthropic’s Claude to read. You can undo what TownwiseAI adds from a file on its page.” and followed by the link “How Townwise handles your data” (`/privacy`). While it is checked, each file that finishes uploading is sent once to be read (`org.data.ai_read` on `f_<id>`); one that finished while it was unchecked never is. A kind TownwiseAI can’t read is not sent, and the line beside the file says why (“Added. TownwiseAI can’t read old Excel files (.xls). …”); a sent one reads “Added. TownwiseAI is reading it; open it on Your data to see what it finds.”; a refusal reads “Added, but TownwiseAI didn’t start reading it.” and why, and never undoes the upload. Nothing says beforehand whether reading with TownwiseAI is on, so the box shows whenever stored files are on and hides for the rest of the visit once a request answers 503 `ai_unavailable`. Under view-as it is disabled in place. Add a file, with its opt-in and its files, stands on its own above its help line and Paste text, so the taller opt-in never pushes Paste text out of line. The help line reads “Any kind of file up to 200 MB, kept as it is for your team. Townwise doesn’t read it for sales; use Upload sales history for that. With the box above off, TownwiseAI reads a file only when you ask, in a chat or on the file’s page. With it on, TownwiseAI reads each file you add and uses what it finds.” Once TownwiseAI takes a file (or answers 409 `ai_read_running`), the list loads again, so its row says so. The page never guesses that a file is sales. Org admins, with one location shown and a sales file’s original stored, also get “Delete all originals for this location” (11A.7), whose dialog says “This deletes the original of every sales file for {location}. Cleaned copies and days stay, and so do items kept for reference. Files still uploading or being read are skipped. This can’t be undone.” and whose outcome reads “Deleted {n} originals.” (with “{m} files were busy and kept.” when some were).
- **Table** (`ui/DataTable`, “Your data for {location}”): Item (the name, “Daily totals” or the kind’s label; under view-as the API sends no name), Location (all locations only), Added (date and who: an email, “Townwise staff”, “Deleted person”, or “Saved from TownwiseAI”), Kind, Size, Status (On or Off, then what Townwise did: Used, Kept for reference, Kept, not used with the reason, Couldn’t read it, Reading, Waiting for an answer, Uploading, Didn’t finish; then, once someone let TownwiseAI read the file (`ai.status`, D34), “ · TownwiseAI is reading it” while queued or reading, “ · Read by TownwiseAI”, “ · TownwiseAI couldn’t read it” (failed) or “ · TownwiseAI didn’t read it” (skipped), and nothing once undone or for a status the client doesn’t know), Days (“{inUse} of {count} in use, {first} to {last}”, or None).
- **Rows open their item**: a press anywhere on a row opens its page (P27), where its actions are; the row's one link, for the keyboard and screen readers, is the item's name, named for the item (an item with no name by its kind and its days, “Daily totals, May 1, 2026 to May 10, 2026”, else by when it was added, “PDF, added Nov 5, 2026”). The row is raised on hover and while its link has focus. An item still uploading has nothing to open, so its row is not a link. Opening is a read, so rows stay links under view-as. A ZIP's “See what’s inside” in a row still only opens its list. “Show older items” loads the next page.

When the file states the days you’re regularly closed, it suggests them as business rules for your team to confirm. When an org admin asks, it may also start updating the forecast. Everything it adds can be undone, except a suggested rule someone has confirmed.” (D46), the link “How Townwise handles your data” (`/privacy`) and the outline “Let TownwiseAI read this file” (“Asking TownwiseAI…” while it asks). A kind TownwiseAI can’t read has no button and says why: old Excel (“TownwiseAI can’t read old Excel files (.xls). Save it as .xlsx and add it again to let TownwiseAI read it.”), old Word, Numbers, and any other file that isn’t a PDF, a CSV or text file, an Excel workbook, a Word document, a ZIP or a file named as a picture. Nobody who may ask and no read: no panel. Queued or reading: “TownwiseAI is reading this file. It’s next in line, and this page updates when it’s done.” or “… This can take a few minutes, and this page updates when it’s done.”; the item is read again 3 seconds after each answer until the read settles, and leaving the page stops it; a read the page saw running ends with “TownwiseAI finished reading this file.” (or its reason). Done: what TownwiseAI read it as (“TownwiseAI read this file as a calendar of events.”), the summary, the facts as a list (“What it found”), “This file was too long to read whole, so TownwiseAI read only the start of it.” when the input was cut; then what it added: “It added {n} notes to Notes:” with each note’s title and dates and “Open Notes”, or “It added no notes.”; “It added {n} days of sales.” with “Open the days” (its upload), or why none in plain words (`daysReason`: not a sales file; no totals day by day; days already read from the file; a picture, whose figures can’t be checked; not sure enough; too few dates and figures found in the file’s text; the last three add “To add them yourself, use Upload sales history.”); “It kept a summary on Your data that TownwiseAI can read later.” with “Open the summary”, or why not (`itemReason`); and the forecast line (`calibration.status`): “Started updating the forecast. It goes live once Townwise turns forecasts on for you.”, “An org admin can update the forecast from this.”, or “The forecast wasn’t updated: …” with the reason; and when it suggested rules (`rulesSuggested`, D46), “Suggested {n} rules on Business rules.” with the link “Open Business rules” (P29). An unknown code reads as the general line for its place. Failed or skipped: the reason in plain words (the budget spent, too big, a kind it can’t read, a password, the original deleted, too complex, couldn’t be opened; “TownwiseAI declined to read this file.”; something went wrong), with the button again. For `canUndo`, the outline “Undo what TownwiseAI added” opens a dialog, “Undo what TownwiseAI added?”, that names what goes (the notes it added, even edited since; the sales upload with the days it still holds; its summary; “the {n} suggested rules still waiting”, `rulesWaiting`, D46), says a started forecast update keeps running, that the file stays and can be read again, and that this can’t be undone; Undo (“Undoing…”) sends `org.data.ai_undo` and says “Removed what TownwiseAI added from this file.” (with “The forecast update it started keeps running.” when `calibrationKept`). Refusals say why in this section's words (503 `ai_unavailable`, 409 `ai_read_running`, 400 `nothing_to_undo`, else P26's), and the item is read again. Focus moves to the line that says how an action ended. Under view-as the API sends no summary, facts, note titles or rights, so only the statuses, kinds, dates and links show, with no buttons. An upload or a summary item a read made (`fromAiRead`) has the link “Made by TownwiseAI from a file” to the item it was read from under its header lines, and no panel of its own.
- **Rename** (web): an inline form, “Name”, holding the name without its extension, which the API keeps (“The name keeps its .txt ending.”); it takes focus. Save sends `PATCH { title }` and reads the item again, saying “Renamed to {name}.”; the same name just closes; an empty one says “Add a name.” A refusal shows under the field in P26’s words, with “This item is changing right now, maybe because someone is saving an edit of it. Try again in a moment.” for 409 `item_busy` (Townwise is still reading it, or an edit of it is being saved) and “Townwise couldn’t rename this item. Try another name, or go back to Your data in case its file was deleted.” for 400 (a title that makes no file name, or an original deleted since the page opened).
- **Edit** (web) puts an editor in the viewer’s place: text up to 200,000 characters as a textarea named for the item (in its last 10,000 a line says how many characters are left); a CSV or TSV read whole, up to 1,000 rows and 50 columns (its widest row), as a grid of cells named “Row 3, column 2”, with Delete on each row and Add a row and Add a column at the end (a ragged row stays ragged except where the person types past its end); an Excel workbook read whole whose every sheet fits the same, as that grid per sheet under the sheet tabs, cells named “Row 3, column B”. A PDF, Word document or picture has no Edit. Text, a table or a workbook too long or wide to edit, or read only in part, has no Edit and says why: “This file is too long to edit here: Townwise edits text up to 200,000 characters.”, “This file is too big to edit here: Townwise edits tables up to 1,000 rows and 50 columns.” or “This workbook is too big to edit here: Townwise edits up to 50 sheets of 1,000 rows and 50 columns.”, each followed by “Download it, edit it on your computer, and add it again.” Save stays disabled until something changed, line endings aside (a browser reports a textarea’s line breaks as LF); Cancel with changes asks “Discard your changes?” (Discard changes). While saving, Save reads “Saving…” and the cells are read-only.
- **Saving.** Text and a CSV save in place: UTF-8 (with a byte-order mark when the file had one or wasn’t UTF-8, so Excel reads it right), the file’s own line endings (text’s line breaks as CRLF when every one in it was, else LF; a CSV’s unchanged cells as they were and an edited cell’s line breaks as the table’s) and a CSV’s own delimiter and quoting, stored as a new reference file named exactly as the item through the stored-files upload (11A), then `POST .../replace` puts it in the item’s place (10.14). The page opens the item’s new ref and says “Saved.” A workbook saves as a copy, “{name} (edited).xlsx”, with no replace; above “Save as a copy” the page says “Saving makes a new Excel file beside this one. The copy keeps each cell’s value; formatting, formulas and charts stay only in the original.”, and then it opens the copy, saying “Saved a copy. The original is still on Your data.” [CONFIRM: Excel edits save as a values-only copy beside the original]
- **When a save fails**, the line says what happened and what to do, and focus moves to it. An upload refused or failed changes nothing, and the edit stays open to save again, each line ending “Your changes are still here.”: storage full (“…saving an edit needs room for both copies until the old one is removed. Delete some files on Your data, then save again.”), today’s upload limit, too many uploading, “This is the same as another item on Your data, so there’s nothing new to save.”, an empty file, stored files off, the network. A replace that fails after the upload leaves the edit as its own item: 409 `item_changed` says “Someone else saved an edit of this item first. Yours is kept on Your data as a new item.” with “Open it”; a failure that may not have reached the API (network, 5xx, 429) says “Townwise saved your edit, but couldn’t put it in this item’s place. Try again. If you leave, your edit stays on Your data as a new item.”, with Try again (the same file id, retry-safe) and Close.

| State | Shows |
|---|---|
| Loading | “Loading this item”; for a stored file “Downloading {size} to show it…”, then “Opening {size} file…” for one frame before it is read |
| Gone | “This item isn’t here anymore. It may have been deleted, or replaced when someone saved an edit of it.” and “Back to Your data” |
| Error | Network copy with Try again |
| Files off | A stored file is gone from the list, so its page answers as gone; an upload shows its days |
| View-as | No name, no download, no Rename or Edit; a stored file says files don’t open; an upload shows its days; TownwiseAI shows statuses only, with no buttons |
