**P28. Calendar (`/locations/[id]/calendar`, members; D30)**

One month of the location, as a grid of six weeks, or a week, the 7-day block counted from today that holds the selected day, as day columns of cards: each day’s published forecast with what drives it, the town’s calendar, the owner’s notes and the events of the location’s own calendars (D33), with a day’s panel to add, change or delete notes, which change that day’s forecast on the next read (14.5). Built from `client/src/portal/calendar/` (`model.ts` is pure: cells, the day panel, the tooltip, the filters and the months; `grid.ts` is pure: the grid’s 42 days, its cell sizes, its keys, the week view’s blocks, days and cards, and `readRangeFor`, the one range every read of the page covers; `api.ts` holds the owner calendar routes and `calendars.ts`, pure, the words of “Your calendars”; no calendar is parsed in the client). It reads seven member routes: `GET .../notes` (10.5) with `GET .../rules` (10.16, read and read again together; a failure of either is the page's load failure), `GET .../owner-calendars` (10.18, the location’s calendars, part of the first load; its failure leaves the page showing), `GET .../calendar` for the range’s days (10.10), `GET .../sales/days` for the range’s days before today and the 8 weeks before them, which likely closed reads (10.4, D32), `GET .../owner-calendars/events` for the range’s days (10.18, read with the town calendar and the sales days, one read of at most 42 days; its failure leaves the page showing), and `GET .../forecast` for the range’s days (10.13, one read of at most 42 days); notes are written through 10.5 and calendars through 10.18’s add, Refresh now and remove, which carry `openAsAdmin` and the `writes` limiter. The range (`readRangeFor`) is, in the month view, the grid’s 42 days clamped to the first day of the first month the page shows and the last day of the last (`gridRange`), and in the week view the same while the shown block’s days inside the 25 months (the block so clamped, `weekRange`) all lie inside it, and otherwise that clamped block itself, which keeps every read within 396 days of today. Reads are keyed by the range’s first and last day, so selecting a day, or switching between the month and the week, reads nothing while the range stays the same: a week inside the grid reads nothing, and a block that runs past the grid’s days reads its own 7 days (D40). “Today” is the device’s date.

- Header (15.2): the location’s eyebrow and the title “Calendar”; the top bar marks Calendar (15.3).
- **Header row** (one 44px row under the title, its items centered, wrapping; no item taller than 44px): the text button “Today”, the “Previous month” and “Next month” icon buttons (“Previous week” and “Next week” in the week view), then the month or week in words (“November 2026”, “Nov 15 to 21, 2026”; `aria-live="polite"`; 216px wide from 641px, which holds the longest week label, “Dec 27, 2026 to Jan 2, 2027”, so nothing after it moves in either view, and flexible at 640px and below), then the “Calendar view” switch (a group of “Month” and “Week”, one segmented pair of `.tgl` buttons with `aria-pressed` on web and a checked state on native), then the “Your calendars” button, which opens a popover over the page (Your calendars, below; D40), on web and native, so nothing the row holds takes a line of its own and no line sits under the row. From 1024px the switch and the button sit at the right of the row, and at the right of the next line if they wrap; below that they start their own line at the left, together. The page shows 12 months before the current one to 12 after it; Previous and Next step from the grid’s month and are disabled in place at either end, which keeps every read inside the API’s 400-day bounds; in the week view they move the selected day 7 days, a whole block, clamped to the 25 months, and are disabled in place when that block lies wholly outside them. After Previous, Next, Today or the view switch, focus stays on the button and the label announces the new month or week. **Filters** (“Show on the calendar”), a ToggleGroup of chips, all on at first: “Holidays”, “Town events”, “Term dates” (term and season periods), “Your notes”, and “Your calendar” (only when the location has a calendar). From 641px they head the grid’s column, above the grid (from 1024px the day panel’s top is level with their legend); at 640px and below they come after the grid and before the day panel. Filters hide marks, entry lines and list items only; forecast figures and the forecast’s reasons always show. Filter state is the page’s, never stored.
- **Banner** (only when the forecast read answers `no_published_forecast`): “Townwise hasn’t published a forecast for {location} yet. Days show your history, your notes and {Town}’s calendar. Notes you add now count as soon as a forecast is published.” ({location} is the shown name, D29). A month the run doesn’t cover (`not_covered`), or covers in part, has no banner: those days show no figure, and the panel says “No forecast for this day.”
- **Month grid** (columns 1 to 8 from 1024px, full width below; 2026-11-12, owner request: a full grid that doesn’t move, with more of each day on it): always 42 days in 6 rows of 7, Monday first, from the Monday on or before the month’s 1st, with weekday heads, so every month is the same height. The days of the months before and after that complete its first and last weeks show everything an in-month day shows, from the same reads, muted: no `raised` fill but a 1px `border` outline, and the number, figure and entries in `text3` (today keeps its own number style and the selected day its `mint` outline). Clicking one, or Enter or Space on it, selects it in place: the grid stays on its month. [CONFIRM: clicking a leading or trailing day selects it in place] A grid day outside the 25 months is inert: its number only in `text3`, no click, hover or keys, `aria-disabled`, labeled “{Sun, Dec 5, 2027}. Outside the months the calendar shows.”, and never read (native: a disabled element with that label). Each cell has a fixed height by width alone, 104px from 1024px, 64px from 641px and 52px below (native the same), so a busy day never grows its row and the grid is 658px, 418px or 346px tall every month. [CONFIRM: 104px month cells with three entry lines] From 1024px a cell shows its day number (mono 13px; today `white`, bold) with “Booked” or, under a past figure, “guests” (or “forecast”) at its right; then its figure, centered (22px tabular): from today on, the published forecast’s middle figure rounded, with a `mint` “+{70}” beside it when notes added guests, or a booked day’s buyout party; before today the day’s stored guests (`text2`), and with no guests stored the forecast made for the day, as the run made it, captioned “forecast” (data wins over a forecast, owner request, 2026-11-17); on a closed or likely-closed day the status word in its place (“Likely” over “Closed”, uppercase), a past day the run had closed or booked included; every day shows something (owner request, 2026-11-17): once the forecast read answered, a past day with neither reads “No data” and a day from today on that the read doesn’t cover “No forecast”, in the status word’s place (nothing while it loads or after a failure); the row kept even when empty; then up to three one-line entries (holiday and town event titles, a note’s kind words such as “Private event, 70”, an imported event’s title), or the first two and “+{n} more” past three. From 641 to 1023px the same top row, then the 18px figure or the status word, and corner marks as on Home (white for a holiday or town event, `text2` for a note, a `mint` outline for an imported event) instead of entries. At 640px and below the number, then the 15px figure or any status word (Booked too) in its place, and the corner marks; “+{70}” and the caption leave the cell and stay in its label, the tooltip and the panel. Term and season periods mark no cell, since they span weeks; the day panel lists them. The selected day is outlined `mint` over the `state` fill, its weekday column a little wider (D64); today’s week `line`. Each cell’s label says everything it shows, the range with the figure (“Sat, Nov 21, 2026. Forecast about 212 guests, 180 to 240. Dartmouth home football. 1 note.”, with “Includes {70} guests from your notes.” when notes added guests). On web the grid is `role="grid"` named by its month and one tab stop with a roving tabIndex. Left and Right move a day and Up and Down a week, across rows and months; Home and End go to the row’s Monday and Sunday, and with Ctrl or Cmd to the grid month’s first and last day; PageUp and PageDown show the month before or after the grid’s (as a date picker does, from the grid’s month, since the selected day may be a leading or trailing one), on the same day number clamped to that month’s length: PageDown from Jan 31, 2027 gives Feb 28, and from a trailing Dec 6 in November’s grid, December with Dec 6 still selected. A key whose move would leave the 25 months is consumed; Home and End clamp to them instead. Enter, Space or a click selects a day. The cell a key moved to takes focus. Home’s month grid keeps P11’s keys. A mouse or pen over a day (never touch; never over an inert day, or a day whose reads are still in flight) shows an `aria-hidden` tooltip: the date, “About {212} guests ({180} to {240})”, “Includes {70} guests from your notes”, and the day’s three reasons with the largest effect either way, shown in Why’s order (D40), in short words (“Saturday: usually more guests”, “Thanksgiving Day: fewer guests last time”, “Sample game: more guests in Townwise’s model”; a note’s, a rule’s or one with no effect by its label), or its entries. - **Week view** (`?view=week`; 2026-11-12, owner request): the 7-day block counted from today that holds the selected day (D40): it starts on today plus 7 days times the whole weeks from today to the selected day, rounded down (calendar dates only, `weekStartFor`), so with no `?day=` it opens on today in its first column, and a reload or a link at `?day=` shows the block that holds that day; from there it scrolls a day at a time (D64, below), and the label, the reads and Home and End follow the 7 days in view. It reads over the grid’s range when its days inside the 25 months lie inside that range, so a week inside the grid shows its data at once and reads nothing, and otherwise over the grid of the month that holds its first or last day (D64), so a run of one-day scroll stops reads once: with today Sun, Nov 15, 2026 and November’s grid (Oct 26 to Dec 6), the block of Dec 6 to 12 reads December’s grid (Nov 30 to Jan 10), Dec 6 showing its data while Dec 7 to 12 are pending, and Month then reads November’s grid again. Then every item on the day as a card, not focusable (the panel keeps the actions): holidays and town events, including those Why names (which On the calendar leaves out), notes, business rules (whatever the filters), imported events, and term and season periods, as the filters allow. A card has a `panel` fill and a 2px left rule (`white` for a holiday or town event, `text2` a note or rule, `mint` an imported event, `line` a term or season): a timed one’s hours first (“6 pm to 9 pm”), the title in full (a note’s kind words such as “Private event, 70”, a rule’s text, an event’s title), then its kind words in `text3` (“Holiday”, “Federal holiday”, “Town event”, “Term”, “Season”, “Your note”, “Your calendar”, or a rule’s schedule summary, “Your rule” when it has none) with a multi-day item’s span (“Town event, Nov 20 to 22”). Every card wraps its words onto as many lines as they need and nothing in it is cut or ellipsized (D40), a term or season card included, which keeps its title and kind words on one wrapping run, so “Fall term finals” shows whole and its column grows if it needs to. A day outside the 25 months is an inert column (its head line only in `text3`, no click, hover or keys, `aria-disabled`, the inert label, no cards); a day whose reads are still in flight is pending (its head line only, labeled “{Tue, Dec 8, 2026}. Loading.”, no description and no tooltip, still the tab stop when selected) in a dimmed, `aria-busy` box. The keys are the month grid’s (Left and Right cross into the next or previous block, and Up and Down in the columns move 7 days), except that Home and End go to the first and last day in view (a block’s after Previous, Next or a key, any 7 days after a scroll), Ctrl or Cmd with them act the same, and PageUp and PageDown step from the selected day’s own month, since the week view hides the grid’s, the block following the new day (with today Wed, Nov 11, 2026, PageDown from Oct 28 gives Nov 28, in the block of Nov 25 to Dec 1). The column a key moved to takes focus without scrolling. At 640px and below on web, and at every width on native, the week is an agenda of 7 rows, each the day’s head on one line above its full-width cards, its height following what it holds: on web a `role="grid"` named by the week label with 7 rows of one gridcell each, labeled and described as the columns are, where Up and Down move a day; on native each row a pressable element with the day’s label and selected state, which selects the day; a row is one accessible element, so its hint reads its cards in short sentences (a timed one’s hours, the title, then the kind words: “6 pm to 9 pm, Private event, 70. Your note.”), and a day without cards has none.
- **Day panel** (region “Selected day”; a sticky side column 9 to 12 from 1024px, under the grid below, scrolled into view on web when a day is clicked or entered). The heading (h2) “Today, {Wed, Nov 11}” or “{Sat, Nov 21, 2026}”. **Forecast**: “About **{212}** guests”, then “Likely {180} to {240}. About 8 in 10 days land in the range.”; when notes changed the day, “Likely {250} to {310}.” and “Townwise’s model: {180} to {240}. About 8 in 10 days land in that range. Your notes add {70} guests.” (“Your rules add …” or “Your notes and rules add …” when business rules added guests, D31, and the same words in a cell's label, “Includes {40} guests from your rules.”, and the tooltip) (the 8 in 10 sentence goes only with the model’s own range); “Booked: a private buyout, {70} guests. No walk-in forecast.” (“Booked for a private event.” when the model booked it); “Closed.” with “From your closure note.”, “From your business rule.” (a rule's schedule closed it) or “Townwise’s model expects you closed.”; a day the model closed that a private event opened (14.5), “Townwise’s model expects you closed. Your notes open the day with {70} guests.” with no range; a past day “{138} guests” and, when a run covered it, “Townwise’s model forecast {120} to {150}, and the day landed in that range.” (or “outside it”; the run’s own range and `inRange`); otherwise “No forecast for this day.” with the reason in one line. **Why** (2026-11-12, owner request: make it easier to read, and say whether each reason brings more or fewer guests): one row per reason, the label (`white`) over a line in `text2` that says what it does, then its sources as source chips (15.7, D40) on their own wrapping line. Order (D40; 2026-11-15, owner request: “organize the items from most positive to most negative”), from today on, by each reason’s signed size in percent: a run reason’s effect, its pct for more, minus its pct for fewer and 0 for about the same; a note’s or rule’s outcome against the model’s middle figure for the day, `added` 100 times its guests divided by that figure (100 with no figure), `closed` minus 100, `booked` 100 times the party less the middle, divided by the middle (0 without either), each rounded to the nearest 5, with 5 or less either way counting as 0, and any other outcome 0; a run reason with no effect has no size. Why lists the reasons above 0, the largest first; then the run’s about-the-same reasons, the notes’ and rules’ reasons at 0, and the run’s reasons with no effect, each group in the read’s order; then the falls, the smallest first and the largest last. At an equal size notes and rules come before the run’s reasons, then the read’s order. A day before today keeps the read’s order, since no reason has a size. A run reason’s line, from today on (14.4): “▲ Usually about {35}% more guests than your average day ({210})” (a weekday, with the average open day’s guests, `averageGuests`, 14.4, D40; no number when the read has none), “▼ Usually about {10}% fewer guests than the same weekday at other times of the year” (a term state), “▲ Usually about {20}% more guests than the same weekday without it” (an event), “▼ Last time, about {70}% fewer guests than the same weekday in the weeks around it” (a holiday seen once; “Usually” from two), “= Usually about as many guests as your average day ({210})” (5% or less), “▲ Townwise’s model: about {10}% more guests” (an effect the run recorded); “Not enough of your history to say yet” for a weekday, term, event or holiday below its minimum; nothing for the other kinds or on a day before today. The mark (▲ more, ▼ fewer, = about the same) is hidden from screen readers, which hear the same words, and only the mark is colored (D40): by its size’s magnitude, 10 to 15 step 1, 20 to 35 step 2, 40 and over step 3, ▲ in `effectUp1` to `effectUp3` (greener with each step) and ▼ in `effectDown1` to `effectDown3` (redder), = in `text2`. - **URL.** `?day=YYYY-MM-DD` is the selected day; choosing a day sets it, so a reload or a link from Home (P11) opens that day. A missing or invalid day, or one outside the 25 months, falls back to today. The grid’s month is the page’s state, not the URL’s: it starts at the selected day’s month, follows `?day=` only when the day leaves the grid’s 42 days (a key past its first or last row, browser back or forward, a link), and otherwise moves only on Previous, Next, Today, PageUp and PageDown, so the selected day is always in the shown grid. `?view=week` is the week view; any other value, or none, the month. “Week” sets `view=week` and keeps `?day=`; “Month” takes `view` out of the URL. Choosing a day keeps the view, and switching keeps the grid’s month, so Month, Week, Month returns to the same grid unless the selection left it. A switch reads only when the shown block runs past the grid’s days: Week then reads the block’s own 7 days, and Month the grid’s range again (D40). Links from Home (P11) open the month view. On web, when focus was on a cell or column that such a change removes (browser back or forward across `?day=` or `?view=`), it moves to the selected cell, never to the page body; focus anywhere else is left alone.

**P29. Business rules (`/locations/[id]/rules`, members; D31)**

The location's standing facts, which TownwiseAI reads with every message the person sends (10.16, `tuning-chat.md` section 3), each with an optional schedule that changes Townwise's forecast (D31, 14.5). Built from `client/src/portal/rules/` (`rules.ts` mirrors the API's text rule and says whether a schedule changes the forecast; `useRules` holds the list with the page's own writes applied in place) and the note form's fields and checks (`client/src/portal/locations/NoteFields.tsx`, `checkSchedule` in `noteRules.ts`).

- Header (15.2): the location's eyebrow and the title “Business rules”. The page is the top bar's Rules section, right after Notes, for every member (15.3); Location settings (P16) also links to it.
- Lead: “Standing facts about how {location} runs, like “Closed Mondays” or “Brunch only on weekends”. TownwiseAI reads them with every message you send. A rule changes Townwise’s forecast only when you give it a schedule under Change the forecast: a closure, a buyout or a private event with a guest count, on the days you choose. For one day that’s different, add a note.” ({location} is the shown name, D29), then the text links “Open Notes” and “Ask TownwiseAI”. TownwiseAI suggests closure rules only in the group below (D46), and no copy says it saves a rule by itself: a suggested rule is saved only when someone on the team confirms it.
- **Suggested by TownwiseAI** (D46, 10.12), above Add a rule, only while GET .../rules’ `suggested` holds any: the eyebrow “{n} to decide” and the lead “TownwiseAI found these in your files and sales history. Each changes nothing until someone on your team confirms it.” Each card (one shared card, web and native, which P25 also shows): the rule’s words (the view’s `text`, with no client copy of the wording) as its heading; “Changes the forecast: {scheduleSummary}”; where it came from, “From {file title}” linked to that item’s page (P27), “From a file TownwiseAI read” under view-as (no title), “From a file you deleted” once the file is gone, or for the sales history “No sales on any Monday since {Sep 7, 2026}. In all, {n} of {m} Mondays had no sales.” (“In your sales history, {n} of {m} Mondays had no sales.” when the weekday never had sales); the help “Confirm saves it as a business rule, and the forecast uses its schedule from then on. Edit changes it first. Dismiss and TownwiseAI won’t suggest it again.”; and Confirm, Edit and Dismiss, disabled in place under view-as, described by the read-only line. Edit opens the rule form inside the card, prefilled (the words, Change the forecast and Every year), and Save sends the accept with `rule`; `?suggestion={id}` (P25’s Edit) opens that card’s edit. Confirmed, the card leaves the group and its rule appears in the list, with the notice “Added the rule “{text}”.”; dismissed, it leaves with “Dismissed. TownwiseAI won’t suggest it again.” Errors on the card: 409 `rule_limit` “This location has 30 rules, the most it can hold. Delete one to confirm this.”; 409 `rule_exists` “A rule with these words is already saved. Edit that rule, or change these words with Edit.” with “Edit that rule”, which opens the saved rule with those words for edit (“Open Business rules” on P25). A Confirm or Edit another tab won (409 `already_decided`) moves that tab’s rule into the list with the notice “Already confirmed as: {text}” (on P25 the card says it); a suggestion gone in the meantime (404) says “That suggestion was already decided, or its dates have passed.” and loads the page again.
- **Add a rule:** a one-line field “New rule” (placeholder “Closed Mondays”, helper “One line, up to 200 characters. Leave out guest names.”), with “{n} of 200 characters” under it from 180 characters; then the optional **Change the forecast** section; then the page's one primary, “Add rule”. Enter submits on web. The page checks the API's text rule before it sends (“Write the rule.”, “Keep it to 200 characters.”, “Take out the special characters.”). Added: the field empties, the section closes and the page says “Added the rule.” At the limit the field is read-only and Add rule and Change the forecast disabled, all described by “This location has 30 rules, the most it can hold. Delete one to add another.”
- **Change the forecast** (in the add form and in a row's edit). Closed, the outline button “Change the forecast” and “Optional. Without it, TownwiseAI reads the rule and the forecast doesn’t change.” Open, a group named “Change the forecast”: “Townwise applies this to its forecast as it applies a note: a closure, a buyout or a private event with a guest count changes the days it covers.”, the note form's fields (C6: Kind, closure first; Starts; Ends (optional), helper “Leave it empty to keep it going.”; Starts at and Ends at; Only on these days; Effect; Expected guests, whose helper says the guests count “on each day the rule covers”), with no Details, and the link “Remove from the forecast”, which closes it. Either button goes when pressed, so focus moves to what takes its place (web focus, the screen reader on native): opening, to the group’s heading “Change the forecast”, from which Tab reaches Kind; closing, to the line “Optional. Without it, …” under the button that comes back. A form as it starts (the page, an edit opened, the add form after Add rule) moves no focus. The page checks the note form's rules before it sends, with its messages under the fields (an empty end means no end). Add sends `schedule` only with the section open; Save sends the schedule when the section is open, `null` when the section was closed on a rule that had one, and nothing about it otherwise. A row's edit opens the section, filled in, when the rule has a schedule. Under Starts and Ends, a checkbox “Every year” (rules only, web and native; D46) with the helper “Closes the same days every year from Starts on, until you delete the rule.”: checked, Ends drops “(optional)” and is required (“Enter the season’s last day.”), and a season over a year or starting or ending Feb 29 gets “Pick a season shorter than a year that doesn’t start or end on Feb 29.” The form then sends `season` from the two dates’ months and days, `startDate` as Starts and `endDate` null. Editing a yearly rule prefills Starts and Ends with its first season on or after its start. At phone width the fields stack as on the note form. [CONFIRM: a rule's schedule may have no end date ("ongoing"); one with an end keeps a note's 366-day span]
- **Rules** (eyebrow “{n} of 30”): a list, oldest first; each row is the rule's text, then what it does to the forecast (“Changes the forecast: {scheduleSummary}” in white for a schedule the forecast applies, a closure, a buyout or a private event with more guests and a count; “On the calendar: {scheduleSummary}. Only closures, buyouts and private events with a guest count change the forecast.” for any other schedule; “TownwiseAI reads this. It doesn’t change the forecast.” with none), then “Added by {email}, {Mar 2, 2026}” or “Saved from TownwiseAI by {email}, {date}” (“Townwise staff” for a rule staff added in open as admin, “a deleted person” when the author is gone), then text buttons “Edit” and “Delete” when `canEdit`. Edit turns the row into the field “Edit rule” and its Change the forecast section, with the outline “Save” and the link “Cancel”; saved, the page says “Saved.” Delete asks “Delete this rule?”, “TownwiseAI stops reading it from your next message.”, with “Delete rule” and “Cancel”; deleted, the page says “Deleted the rule.”
- Write errors where the write happened (the add form, the row's edit, the dialog): 409 `rule_exists` “That rule is already saved.”; 409 `rule_limit` the limit line; 403 `forbidden` “Only the person who added this rule or an org admin can change it.” on an edit, the shared copy in the dialog, and either re-reads GET /api/me (4.3); 404 on an edit or a delete “This rule was deleted.”, and the list loads again; 404 on an add loads the list again, which says the location isn't available; 400 the page's text rule; anything else the shared copy (15.7).

**P30. Orders (`/locations/[id]/orders`, members; D35)**

- Read with `org.orders.get` (10.17), never the sample unless the person asks for it. The h1 is “Orders” and the top bar marks Orders (`aria-current="page"`); on Ordering setup (P31) it is marked `aria-current="true"`. Nothing here is sent to a distributor, and the page says so wherever it speaks of an order.
- **With a board**: one section per supplier, soonest order-by first. Each has the supplier’s name as its heading, its deadline in a sentence (“Order by Wed, Nov 18, 2:00pm. Thursday’s delivery lasts until Monday’s.”), a table (Item, Order, Other deal, Why) and “Explain the {supplier} order”, which opens TownwiseAI (P25) with the order. A line shows the item (with “Never run out” when it is), the quantity in its unit (“3 cases”, “1 keg”; the line’s saved change when it has one, and then, when that differs from Townwise’s quantity, the why line ends with it in the owner’s words, “You changed this order to 16 cases: a home game weekend.”), the other deal size when there is one (a dash otherwise), the reason in a sentence and “Ask why {item}”. Above them: “Townwise still can’t see {item sales and a recent count}.” when the board lacks them, **Enter a count**, **Edit ordering setup** (to P31) and **Preview with a sample bar**.
- **Will it last?** (h3, under a supplier’s table; owner request, 2026-11-17): a bar per item, from the numbers the line’s quantity came from, so it never disagrees with the why line. The bar is the count (`line` gray) then what the line orders (`mint`; the owner’s saved change when there is one), with a `white` mark at the use Townwise expects before the following delivery and a `text3` mark at that use with Townwise’s cushion, each row scaled to its own largest quantity. Under each bar a sentence carries the same numbers (“5 cases on hand + 8 ordered = 13 cases. Expected use: about 14. That is less than the expected use.”), in `white` when the stock is under the expected use; rows under the expected use come first, then rows under the cushion, then the rest. The bars and the key are hidden from screen readers. A line has a row only with a count at most 7 days old and item sales for the window, and a supplier with no such line (and so the sample bar) has no chart. Drawn with plain views, on web and native alike.
- **A line’s edit** sits under its section, one per line: a quantity (a whole number from 0 to 999, checked before anything is sent, else “Enter a whole number from 0 to 999.”) and a reason (“Say why, in a few words.”, at most 280 characters), saved with `org.orders.decision`. **Remember this** adds the saved change to every later order of the item (the copy says so, with the amount in the item’s unit and the reason in the owner’s words), through `org.orders.rule`; a reason whose rule the owner turned off answers “You turned that rule off. Save this line with a new reason to remember a new one.” Each rule that applies is listed on its line (“Adds 2 cases to every order: “a football weekend””) with its own “Turn this rule off”, through `org.orders.rule_off`.
- **Enter a count** opens a form with one field per item, grouped by supplier, empty to start. Only filled fields are sent, as today’s count (0 to 9,999 in whole or half units; a bad field is named and nothing is sent); a save reloads the board and says “Saved today’s count for {n} items.”
- **With no board** (no setup, or one with no supplier delivery or no item): the reason, “Townwise still needs {the supplier schedule and the items}.”, **Set up ordering** (to P31) and **Preview with a sample bar**. The preview asks for the labeled sample (“Sample bar. These lines are not {location}’s stock, and nothing here can be saved.”): every line starts with “Sample.”, and it has no edit, rule or count controls.
- **From Home** (P11) a calendar day may open this page with `?day={date}`; it then opens with a sentence on which order covers that day (`orderCoverSentence`), and the board below.
- States: loading “Loading orders for {location}”; error with Try again. View-as: the board reads, every write is disabled in place and described by the read-only line.

**P31. Ordering setup (`/locations/[id]/orders/setup`, members; D35)**

- Read with `org.orders.setup.get`, saved with `org.orders.setup.save` (10.17). “Back to Orders” returns. Every member edits it. [CONFIRM: every member may edit the ordering setup]
- **Suppliers.** A name (1 to 60 characters) and 1 to 7 deliveries, each a delivery weekday, an order-by weekday and an order-by time (in the town’s time zone); up to 20 suppliers, one delivery per weekday.
- **Items.** A table of up to 300 items: name (1 to 80), supplier, category (bottles and cans, draft, liquor, cocktail ingredient), unit (cases, kegs, bottles, units), servings per unit, par (0 to 999), deal size (1 to 999, or none), never run out, and up to 10 point-of-sale names with the servings one sale uses (default 1). **Import a sheet** reads a CSV or Excel file in the browser with the template’s columns (Item, Supplier, Category, Unit, Servings per unit, Par, Deal size, Never run out, Point-of-sale names), creates the suppliers it names and shows the rows unsaved, with any row that fails a check marked, for the person to review before saving. The page offers the template as a CSV. Saving sends the whole setup with the version the person loaded; if someone saved first (409 `setup_changed`) the page says so and nothing is overwritten.
- **Read a file with TownwiseAI** (web and native, D41), only while the GET's `canReadWithAi` holds, after the sheet import. Drop or choose one file (a PDF, an Excel `.xlsx` or Word `.docx` file, a CSV or text file, or a picture), then **Read the file**, or paste text, then **Read the text**; nothing is sent before. Pasted text that is only links is refused before anything is sent (“TownwiseAI can’t open links. Download the sheet or page as a file and choose it, or paste what it says.”). The lead says it is sent once to Anthropic’s Claude with the names of the suppliers and items already there and isn’t kept, that TownwiseAI never sets a par or never run out and that nothing saves until Save, and a second line that a register export read this way sends its item names and quantities to Anthropic, unlike the item sales upload; then “How Townwise handles your data” (the privacy page). The browser refuses, with the cap in words and before anything is sent, a file over 5 MB, a picture over 3.75 MB, an empty file, an old Excel or Word file, a ZIP, a Numbers, Pages or OpenDocument file, or a TIFF, each with the way to a kind it reads, a saved email or web page (which says to paste its text, since a saved email carries its headers and a page mostly markup), any other kind (which also says the text can be pasted), and two files at once; the file's name never leaves it. A HEIC photo (`.heic`, `.heif`) of up to 5 MB is drawn in the browser when Read is pressed (by the browser itself where it draws HEIC, as Safari does, else by `libheif-js`) and sent as a JPEG made from its pixels, so without its metadata, with a long side of at most 4,096 pixels; the picture caps are checked on the JPEG (“That photo is more than TownwiseAI reads once it is a JPEG: up to 3.75 MB and 8,000 pixels a side. Save a smaller copy and choose it again.”), and one the browser can’t decode says “Townwise couldn’t open that HEIC photo in your browser. Save it as a JPEG, or take a screenshot of it, and choose that.” While it reads: “TownwiseAI is reading the file. This can take up to three minutes.” (“the text” for pasted text) with **Cancel**, which stops the request and adds nothing (“Stopped. Nothing was added to the setup.”). The answer merges into the unsaved draft (D41), and a status says what it found and what to do: “TownwiseAI found 14 items: 11 new, 3 replaced by name. Nothing is saved yet: check them below, then save the setup.”, “Set the par of the 11 new items.”, that replaced items keep their par and never run out, “Check the servings per unit of 4 items: TownwiseAI estimated them.”, “TownwiseAI didn’t find 2 of these names in the file: check them.”, the new suppliers with the delivery days it found (or those still needing them), suppliers whose empty deliveries it filled, a cut or partial read, and the suggestions left out, one per line (“Item 3, {name}: {reason}”). An estimated servings value and a name not in the file take their field's helper (“TownwiseAI estimated this: {note}. Check it.”, “TownwiseAI didn’t find this name in the file. Check it.”), tied by `aria-describedby`, until the field changes or a save goes through. Each refusal from the API is one alert in plain words (the budget spent, reading off or busy, a file too large, of another kind than its name, with a password (or an old Excel or Word file under a new name) or unreadable, a refusal, an answer too long, a failure, the 150-second limit or the page's 230-second wait). Under view-as every control is disabled in place and described by the read-only line, with no file input and no drop. Native (2026-11-18) draws the same section without the drop zone: the lead begins “Choose a file”, the register line says the item sales upload is “on a computer”, and the zone’s line reads “Choose a file: a PDF, an Excel (.xlsx) or Word (.docx) file, a CSV or text file, or a picture.” **Choose a file** opens the system file picker, which copies the file into the app’s cache; the app checks it by name and size as the browser does before anything is read, reads the copy as base64 when **Read the file** is pressed and then deletes it, whether or not that worked (so another try chooses the file again; on iOS the system picker also keeps its own temporary copy inside the app’s sandbox, which the app can’t reach and iOS clears), and deletes it too when the file is removed, replaced or refused or the page closes. A HEIC photo is refused before anything is read (“The app can’t read HEIC photos yet. Choose a JPEG or PNG, or read it at townwise.tech on a computer.”), and a copy the app can’t open says “Townwise couldn’t open that file. Choose it again.” Under view-as the picker never opens. Native’s line for the rest reads “Use a computer to download the template, import a sheet or upload item sales.”
- **Opened from a TownwiseAI card** (web and native, D56). With `?proposal={conversationId}.{toolCallId}` (two ids, checked by pattern before anything is asked) the page shows **Suggestions from TownwiseAI** first, above the sheet tools and Suppliers, reads the card and, while it is open, merges its suggestions into the unsaved draft once, as a read above does, and says what that did in the same words, with the chat’s own line when the file listed more than 60 items; the section takes focus once the merge lands, so it is in view. The same list says “Townwise couldn’t check these names against the file’s text, because it was read as a picture.” when no name could be checked, and “The TownwiseAI reply behind these suggestions also read web pages, which Townwise didn’t check. Look over each change before you save.” when it did. Under it, “N items already in your setup by name change when you save:” leads a row for each such item, field by field with both values quoted (Sample Lager: unit: “cases” becomes “kegs”; servings per unit: “24” becomes “124”). A second card named in the same page merges too; a card a save went through for is not merged again in that page. Nothing saves until Save, which names each new item’s blank par. After “Load their changes” the suggestions merge into the reloaded draft again, and the toast says “Loaded the setup as it was last saved, then added TownwiseAI’s suggestions again.” Once a save goes through the section goes and the query is dropped, so a reload never merges over what was saved. A card set aside says “You set these suggestions aside in TownwiseAI, so nothing was added here.”; one no longer served says “These suggestions aren’t available any more, so nothing was added here. The file they came from may have been turned off or deleted.”; either leaves the draft alone. Under view-as nothing is asked or merged, and the section says so.
- **Item sales.** An upload of a point-of-sale export (CSV or Excel), read and matched in the browser: it proposes the date, item and quantity columns (presets for Toast’s Business Date, Menu Item and Item Qty, and Square’s Date, Item and Qty), lets the person change them, counts a time before 4 a.m. toward the day before, and matches each item name (trimmed, case-folded) to the items’ point-of-sale names. Unmatched names are listed with “Add to an item” and never sent. The page shows the first and last covered day, the covered days, and for each item the covered days of the last 8 weeks with any sales, “No sales matched” when it has none. An org admin’s upload replaces the dates it covers; a member’s adds only dates not already saved, and the page says so before sending and how many dates it kept after. An org admin can delete a location’s item sales.
- **Count.** The same count form as P30.
- States: loading; error with Try again. View-as: every field and button disabled in place. Your data (P26) carries one line pointing here.

**P32. Overview (`/admin/overview`)** (D48) [Build note: `client/app/(gate)/(app)/(console)/admin/overview.tsx`, with its parts in `client/src/portal/console/`: `overview.ts` (the words), `StatTiles.tsx`, `AttentionList.tsx`, `ActivityChart.tsx` and `ActivityChart.web.tsx`, `OverviewOrgs.tsx`; `OverviewSkeleton` in `client/src/portal/skeleton/console.tsx`.]

- Title “Overview”, the first item in the console’s nav and where staff land (15.4). Web only, as every console page.
- **Window switch**: tabs styled as Requests’ (15.2), links to `?days=7`, `?days=28` and `?days=90`, “7 days”, “28 days” and “90 days”; no query is 28. Under the tabs, a line in a slot whose height is kept in every state (one line from 641px, two on phones), so nothing moves when it changes: “The last {days} days, {from} to {to} (UTC).”. A change of window keeps the last answer on the page until the next arrives, so the figures never flash and the tabs never move, but dimmed, `aria-busy` and inert, and the line says “Loading the last {days} days… Below: the last {held days} days until then.”. The skeleton shows only before the first answer (the line then says “Loading the last {days} days…”). A failed read shows the shared error with Try again in place of the figures, so no figures stay under a tab they are not for; Try again moves focus to the line, since the button goes with the error.
- A line above the tiles: “Days of use recorded since {date}.”, or, with nothing recorded yet, that organizations and people that used the app count from the first day a member or org admin opens it, so they read 0 until then, and that the other figures come from the audit log.
- **Eight tiles** (`panel`, the label as an eyebrow, the figure in the `value` type with its thousands separator in the sans face, four to a row from 1024px, two from 641px, one on phones). Never a bare “active”: Status in the table keeps the console’s word for an organization that is not suspended. First row: Organizations that used the app “{n} of {m} with people in them” (of the active organizations someone has joined), People who used the app “{n} of {m} members and org admins” (of the active seats in active organizations), Forecast days in range (across the locations with a scored window, the days in range of the scored days as a percent, “In range on 37 of 45 scored days”, or “No forecast days scored yet” with no figure), Locations with a published forecast “{n} of {m} locations” (a published run used on the window’s passed days, of every location in the table), “Used on the last {days} days”. Second row: TownwiseAI turns, Sales uploads, Notes written, Order decisions. Under each count its change in words: “Up 3 from the 28 days before”, “Same as the 28 days before”, “Down 2 from the 28 days before”, or “Not enough history to compare”; never by color. Under the tiles: “Used the app: a member or org admin opened Townwise that day (staff never count). Actions are recorded changes, not page views. Days are UTC.”
- **Needs attention** (h2; on phones it comes before the tiles): one ruled row per item, in plain words with a text link to where it is acted on (the request on Requests, or the organization’s page); from 641px the link takes at most 40% of the row, so a long organization name in it wraps. “An access request has waited since {date}.”, “{org} has had no upload since {date}.”, “2 invitations to {org} are unanswered, the oldest since {date}.” and so on; the staff pause says “Staff paused the weekly refresh for every organization on {date}. Resume it under Forecasts on any organization’s page.” and opens the first organization not suspended (Organizations with none), since the one switch for every organization is on each organization’s page. “Nothing needs attention.” when empty. Organization names come from the answer’s rows; the server sends ids only. [CONFIRM: Needs attention's thresholds: 2 days, 14 days, 7 days, 80%]
- **Activity by day** (h2): on web, inline SVG with no library on the analytics charts’ scale rules: people who used the app each day as mint bars above (mint is theirs alone), and the day’s actions as bars stacked in the groups’ order below (uploads and data; notes, rules and calendars; TownwiseAI; orders; team and settings), each band on its own printed scale, segments kept apart by a 1px `ground` rule, with a key drawn the same way. The groups differ by mark, not shade alone, in both palettes, with existing tokens only: uploads solid `white`, notes a diagonal hatch, TownwiseAI solid `line`, orders dots, team an outline. At 90 days on a screen under 480px each bar is a week counted back from the newest day (the week’s actions, the most people on one of its days), and a caption says so. A mouse or pen over a bar shows its counts in the chart tooltip. The SVG is hidden from screen readers; a summary line (“{n} actions recorded in the last {days} days (UTC): uploads and data {n}; notes, rules and calendars {n}; …. The most people who used the app on one day: {n}, on {date}.”), the line that an action is a recorded event, not a click, and “Show each day”, a table of each day’s counts, newest first, carry the same numbers. Native draws nothing (D21).
- **Organizations** (h2): a table whose rows each open the organization (P21), stacked as on phones below 1024px, where its ten columns would not fit. Each head says its span: Organization, Status (“Active” or “Suspended”, with “, in setup”), Last day used, People who used the app ({days} days), Actions ({days} days), Days of sales (all time), Last upload, Forecast ({days} days) (per location, named when there are several, the short figure first, “81% in range (17 of 21 days)”, “No scored days yet” or “No published forecast on these days”, and under it in `text3` “Typical error 12.4%. Newest run used: made {date}, {engine}, data through {date}.”; “Forecasts off” when the switch is off), Weekly refresh (latest week) (per location: “Week of {date}: {outcome}”, with a failed or running scheduled calibration), TownwiseAI (this month, UTC) (“$4.10 of $20”). The forecast column names the newest run used on the window’s days, which may be older than the newest published. [CONFIRM: the console shows a published forecast's live accuracy as a typical error percent with its scored-day and in-range counts, never a guest or sales figure]
- No sales figure, guest count, note text, chat text or member email reaches the page: the client’s schema keeps only these fields (D7).

## 17. Logging and privacy

- Townwise server code logs ids and counts only: `userId`, `orgId`, `locationId`, `memberId`, `requestId`, `grantId`, `uploadId`, `routeId`. It never logs emails, names, organization or location names, note text, request notes, view-as reasons, figures, file content or request bodies. This matches the privacy page’s promise for sign-in logs (“its own log lines carry your account ID, never your email address”).
- Product log lines: `townwise.view_as_read`, `townwise.upload_applied`, `townwise.audit_write_failed` (error level), `townwise.access_denied { policy, code }`, `townwise.email_sent { kind, requestId, orgId? }` (info), `townwise.email_failed { kind, requestId, orgId?, code, status, upstreamCode, errType }` (warn; D14), and the stored-files lines in `api/README.md` (Audit and logs), which carry ids, kinds, sizes, counts and codes. An email’s log line never holds its address, subject or body. A stored-files line never holds a file name, header, sheet name, location value, cell, figure or the storage SDK's message; the SDK's own logger stays off.
- TownwiseAI’s visuals (`show_visual`) carry figures computed from the location’s sales days and published forecast, and its suggested next questions (`suggest_next`) are text the model wrote. Both reach only the author’s browser (and staff in view-as, who can read the conversation), in the turn’s stream and the conversation GET; neither is ever logged or put in an audit event, and their tool cards have no views (`docs/portal/tuning-chat.md` section 4).
- A rating of a TownwiseAI reply logs `townwise.chat_feedback { orgId, rating, reason }` (info), with no conversation, node or person id and no audit event; the rating itself (`up` or `down` and one of six fixed reasons, no text) lives in the conversation document and goes with it (10.12).
- The welcome’s first name and organization name travel only in the `GET /api/me` body, never in a URL, log line or audit event. The welcome marker (6.15) is deleted with the organization and with the person.
- The display name (6.22) travels only in the `GET` and `PATCH /api/me/profile` bodies, never in a URL, log line or audit event; there is no audit event for setting it. It is deleted with the person (10.7), never with an organization.
- A business rule's text (6.24, D31) is the team's own words. It travels only in the rules routes' bodies (10.16) and in TownwiseAI's conversations, never in a URL, log line or audit event. It reaches Anthropic inside the person's messages: a turn adds the location's rules to the person's message only when the list changed since the last one on the conversation's path, and the conversation stores that block with the message (`tuning-chat.md` section 3), so a rule's text stays in a conversation after the rule is edited or deleted, until the conversation goes.
- A suggested closure rule (D46, 10.12, 6.27) holds Townwise's words for its schedule, never the file's or a model's, and a sales suggestion's evidence is counts and one date. Its words, schedule, evidence date and file name never reach a log line or an audit event: `file.ai_read`, `file.ai_undone`, `agent.suggestion_accepted`, `agent.suggestion_dismissed`, `townwise.ai_read`, `townwise.ai_read_undone` and `townwise.agent_suggestion` carry ids, the source, whether it was edited and counts only. Nothing new reaches Anthropic: a file read asks one more question of a file already sent whole, the sales history calls no model, and the weekly pass leaves file and sales suggestions out of its request (`alreadySuggested`, `tuning-chat.md` section 9). TownwiseAI's chat reads a suggested rule only once it is confirmed, as any rule. Undoing a read removes its suggestions still waiting; confirmed and dismissed ones are kept until the location is deleted, and the privacy page says so in “Files you let TownwiseAI read.”.
- Forecast runs (14.4) log `townwise.forecast_imported { orgId, locationId, runId, days, weeks }` and `townwise.forecast_status { orgId, runId, status }`, never a figure or the run file; their audit events carry the model version, dates and day count only. The run file holds no free text, and the model, its features and its training rows never reach the API.
- A stored file is read only by the file reader and returned only to its organization; TownwiseAI and every model read `tw_sales_days` (days that are on), notes and the town calendar, never sales files (6.10 rule 9). The exceptions are a text item the team kept for reference on Your data, which TownwiseAI reads only when asked and only through `ctx.items.readText` (D28), a file a person attaches to a TownwiseAI message (D36, below), a file its uploader or an org admin let TownwiseAI read, which is sent whole to Anthropic, a picture without its metadata (D34, 11A.9; no file nobody opted in), the AI column step (11A.4), which sends Anthropic a redacted profile of one table (header text and value tokens), never a row, a figure, a file name or an entry path, and a file or text a member gives Ordering setup to read (D41, below), which is no stored file at all: it is sent once in the request and never stored; only `chat/model.ts` and `files/extract/model.ts` construct a model client (test-enforced). Your data’s audit events and log lines (`data.turned_off`, `data.turned_on`, `data.renamed`, `data.edited`, `sales.upload_deleted`, `file.uploaded`, `townwise.file_stored`) carry ids, kinds, sizes and counts, never a file name, an item’s title or text, or a figure.
- A file attached to a TownwiseAI message (D36) stays on Your data. Only the person who added it or an org admin can attach it, as only they can download it. Its content, a text file's first 20,000 characters, a PDF's, Word file's or Excel file's text (at most 20,000 characters, made on Townwise's server; never the file's bytes), or a picture's bytes without its metadata (where and when it was taken, the device, an author or a caption), goes to Anthropic in that turn's requests only, and again when the person regenerates that reply, read through `ctx.items.readForModel`; it never enters the stored conversation, a log line or an audit event. The conversation stores the file's ref and a kind word, never its name; the conversation view shows the name to the conversation's author only (never under view-as), read from Your data at that moment. A later turn reads a file again by its ref, only while it is on and its original is kept, and a picture, PDF, Word or Excel file only while a message of that conversation attached it. Log lines count a turn's files by kind and `chat.turn_completed` their number; a PDF, Word or Excel file whose text thread failed is logged by its id, kind and the error's type, never the error's message. The privacy page must say so before stored files go on in production (`infra/README.md`, step 18). [CONFIRM: attaching a file and pressing Send is consent to send it to Anthropic for that turn and later re-reads, separate from D34]
- A file or text a member gives Ordering setup to read with TownwiseAI (D41) is the one content Townwise sends to a model without storing it. It travels in the request body only and goes to Anthropic once, with the saved setup's supplier and item names and nothing else (never a point-of-sale name, the file's name, the organization's or location's name, or an email), a picture without its metadata, and a PDF byte for byte, its document properties included (they can hold a title or an author's name); the server drops it when it answers. It never reaches `tw_files`, a blob, Your data, a log line or an audit event: `townwise.setup_read`, `townwise.setup_read_failed` and `order.setup_read` carry kinds, codes and counts only, never a name from the content or the answer, and the answer's email addresses and formatted ten-digit phone numbers are replaced. Pressing Read is the consent; the privacy page says so in “Files and text you give TownwiseAI for ordering.”. [CONFIRM: a file or text given on Ordering setup is sent once to Anthropic and never stored, separate from D34] [CONFIRM: pressing Read with TownwiseAI is consent to send it, with the setup's supplier and item names]
- TownwiseAI's web search (D37), while `TOWNWISE_CHAT_WEB_SEARCH` is on: a search runs at Anthropic, which sends the query the model wrote to its search provider; Townwise never fetches a page. The system prompt limits a query to the town's name and the public fact, never a guest's or staff member's name, the owner's sales or figures, or words from notes, rules, files or messages, but nothing on the server can check a query before it leaves. The results come back inside the model's reply and are stored in the conversation as Anthropic returns them: titles, URLs and page ages, the pages' text only encrypted, and in the reply's citations up to 150 characters of a page each; they go back to Anthropic with every later turn of the conversation and go with it when it is deleted. A search's query, titles, URLs, cited words and pages never reach a log line or an audit event, which carry a count of searches only (`webSearches`); the conversation view shows a search's result count and up to 5 sites, never its query, and the pages a reply cites. The privacy page must say so before the release that turns it on (client stage). [CONFIRM: web search on in production; off by default in code]
- The audit log (a database record) holds emails, organization names and view-as reasons. It never holds figures, note text, request notes or decision messages.
- The client never logs (expo-shell rule 12, **Exists**) and never persists the file or the parsed rows.
- The location’s own calendars on the Calendar (P28, D33) are kept on Townwise’s server (10.18), each an imported `.ics` file, which the API parses and keeps only the events of, or a subscription link: of each event only its UID, its title (at most 200 characters), its dates and its hours, never its description, location, attendees or organizer, until the calendar is removed or its location or organization deleted. A link’s address grants read access to the whole calendar, so it is sealed with AES-256-GCM under `TOWNWISE_CALENDAR_KEY` (a Key Vault secret) before it is stored, opened only to fetch it, and never answered, logged or audited; a link shows as its name and host. Townwise fetches a link itself, when it is added, about every 6 hours and on “Refresh now”, through one guarded fetch (`api/src/calendar/fetch.ts`): `https:` on port 443 only, no user name or password, every address the host resolves to checked against loopback, private, CGNAT, link-local (the managed-identity endpoint included), multicast, documentation and reserved ranges in IPv4 and IPv6 (an IPv4-mapped address by its IPv4 address), the connection made only to the address checked, at most 3 redirects each checked again, 10 seconds, 1 MB, no cookies. A Google calendar (D39) is connected by signing in with Google, on the web, for the person’s own sign-in account only, with read-only access (`openid`, `calendar.calendarlist.readonly` and `calendar.events.readonly`, nothing else): Google’s refresh token and each Google calendar’s id are sealed under the same key and never answered, logged or audited, no access token is stored, and Townwise’s server reads from Google’s fixed hosts only each event’s id, status, title, start and end (each instance of a repeating event included), when it is added, about every 6 hours and on “Refresh now”; the person’s list of Google calendars is shown to them alone to pick from and never stored. The organization’s team and TownwiseAI see a Google calendar’s events; Townwise staff see them only through view-as or with the organization open as its admin, and there only as “Google calendar event” in a calendar named “Google calendar”, with their dates and hours, TownwiseAI’s reads in staff’s own turns included. Townwise’s access ends, its Google calendars and their events deleted, the grant revoked at Google (unless the person holds a connection in another organization) and the connection deleted, when the person’s last Google calendar is removed, when they cancel the picker or leave a connection unused for a day, when they leave or are removed from the organization, and when a location or the organization is deleted and leaves it unused (10.18); the person can also remove Townwise at myaccount.google.com/connections. TownwiseAI reads the calendars’ names and the titles (`get_owner_calendar`), so they can reach Anthropic when the owner asks about bookings, as the privacy page says; its saved conversations keep counts in place of every calendar read, so a title reaches Anthropic only in the turn that read it, though a reply that mentions one keeps it (`tuning-chat.md` section 3). Since D53 titles also reach Anthropic once a week, outside any conversation: while an organization’s weekly suggestions and its calendar titles switch are both on (both on by default; an org admin can turn the titles off, 10.12), TownwiseAI’s weekly call (`tuning-chat.md` section 9) sends each location’s keyed events of the next 91 days (at most 150, soonest first), each only as its title, with every email address and phone number replaced by `[removed]`, its dates, weekdays and hours, and a ref that only that request knows; never a calendar’s name, kind or id, an event’s UID, or the events of a calendar whose add or connect came from a screen that did not say titles go weekly (no stored `titlesNotice`, 10.18; P28, D39), or of a Google calendar whose connection is revoked. A person’s or company’s name written in a title goes as written; only email addresses and phone numbers are removed. The privacy page, the Google connect explainer, the file and link add screens and `estimates.md` section 5 carry the words, which await the owner (18). No title reaches a log line, an audit event, a stored suggestion (code drops any item that repeats a distinctive word of a sent title) or a staff view; a card reads the title from the live event when it shows, and staff read a Google calendar’s as “Google calendar event”. A note’s `fromEvent` and a spotted suggestion’s `event` keep the event’s UID, dates and hours and never its title, and a UID travels only in JSON bodies and answers. The follow-ups’ log lines carry the calendar id and counts only (10.12). A calendar’s name, a link’s address and host, a Google calendar’s id, a Google token or code, and event titles never reach a log line or an audit event; the `owner_calendar.*` events carry ids, the kind, the event count and the status, and the `google_calendar.*` events the connection’s id, a count and a reason. A title is never put into a note; a note made from an event carries only its dates and hours. Note reasons in the forecast read and in `get_forecast` carry a note’s kind words, guest count and hours, never its detail (14.5); the note audit events are unchanged. Since D58 a calendar CSV keeps exactly what an `.ics` keeps (uid, title, dates, hours, keyed), read from its `event_id`, `title`, `start_at`, `end_at` and `status` only, plus a booking label per event with who set it and when; its other columns are never read or kept. Its titles reach Anthropic outside chat and the weekly call only when an org admin presses Sort with TownwiseAI, once per press, as titles with every email address and phone number removed, dates, weekdays and hours under request-local refs, never a calendar’s name or an event’s uid; no word of the answer is kept, and the sort’s log line and audit event carry counts only. The privacy page, the import popover and the Bookings section say so, in words the owner approved on 2026-11-19.

  - how long each is kept, and how to ask for deletion (the staff path in 10.7);

**TownwiseAI working on its own (D59).** What newly reaches Anthropic with no press: each file added to Your data (but a sales export Townwise read into days, a calendar export, a summary or item TownwiseAI kept, and a file whose box was unchecked), whole, as a D34 read sends it, while `TOWNWISE_AGENT_AUTO` and the organization's switch are on; and (slice 2) each calendar file imported then, while its calendar titles switch is on too, as D58's sort sends one (titles with email addresses and phone numbers removed, dates and hours, never the calendar's name); and (slice 3) the weekly suggestions' request again, at most once a day, after a link or Google calendar refresh adds or moves an event in the next 91 days, while the calendar titles switch is on too; and (slice 4) text pasted on Your data with its box checked, as a stored file. A note a person states plainly in a TownwiseAI message is saved for them with Undo (slice 4); the message reached Anthropic anyway, as every chat message does. Never a sales figure on its own. Audit events carry `org.agent_auto_switched { on }`, `agent.change_applied` and `agent.change_undone` `{ locationId, action, sourceKind }`; log lines carry ids, codes and counts (`townwise.ai_read_auto_queued { orgId, locationId, fileId }`, `townwise.refit_pass`, the undo lines of 10.12); a change's why is stored for the log page only, never logged or audited, and hidden under view-as. ## 19. Kit reports (no kit file is edited)

1. **Per-action TOTP** needs a kit export. `api/kit/auth` checks codes only inside its own routes, and its verifier is internal. A staff action that asks for a fresh code would need something like `verifyTotpCode(userId, code)` exported from `api/kit/auth`. This is reported, not made. D2 meets the requirement without it.
2. **No user listing.** `UserStore` has `findById`, `findByEmail` and `findByGoogleSubject`, and no list. People uses Townwise records plus exact-email lookup (10.7), and never reads the kit’s collections.
3. **`normalizeEmail` is not exported.** Townwise repeats `trim().toLowerCase()` then `z.email().max(254)` and pins the rule with a parity test against addresses the kit accepts and rejects.
4. **`onUserCreated` swallows failures** (`auth.on_user_created_failed`), and it never fires for an existing user who is invited later. Townwise does not use it; joining is an explicit POST (F1).
5. **Package manifest for `api/`.** The router, models and tests import `express`, `mongoose`, `vitest`, `testcontainers`, `@testcontainers/mongodb` and `@types/express`. All six are already in `package-lock.json` at 5.3.0, 9.11.2, 5.0.5, 12.2.1, 12.2.1 and 5.0.6 through the kit modules. Declaring them in `api/package.json` at those exact versions adds no new package. [CONFIRM: this counts as no new dependency; if not, the build is blocked on these six]
   
   The lint gate (`eslint.config.js`: `import-x/no-extraneous-dependencies` with `includeTypes: true`) requires every import, type-only ones included, to be declared, and lets only `**/test/**`, `**/*.config.{js,ts}` and `tooling/**` import devDependencies. The kit’s own pattern (`import type { Redis } from 'ioredis'`) would need a seventh package. To stay within six:
   - type the Redis client as `RedisHandle['client']` from `@ckeith26/redis`;
   - take driver types (command-monitoring events included) from `mongoose.mongo.*`;
   - sign in during tests through magic link, so no `jose` is needed for a fake Google signer;
   - turn on command monitoring with the `monitorCommands=true` connection-string option, which the installed `mongodb` 7.7.0 driver accepts;
   - declare `express` and `mongoose` as dependencies, and `@types/express`, `vitest`, `testcontainers` and `@testcontainers/mongodb` as devDependencies;
   - keep every test under `api/test/`, so the devDependencies glob matches.
6. **Gmail and Workspace only.** The kit’s A-L2 rule refuses other email hosts (403 `google_email_not_authoritative`). An owner whose Google account uses a custom domain without Workspace cannot sign in until email delivery and magic links exist. [CONFIRM: accept for the beta]
7. **No user delete.** `UserStore` has `findById`, `findByEmail`, `findByGoogleSubject`, `create`, `linkGoogleSubject` and `updateEmail`, and nothing that deletes. `SessionStore.revokeAllForUser` revokes but keeps the records, and `TotpStore.remove` deletes the factor. The privacy page on `feature/townwise-web` already promises “we will delete your account record, sessions and any authenticator record”. Until the kit adds a user delete, the Townwise path (10.7, Deletion) revokes sessions and removes the factor, and the user record and its revoked session records are deleted by hand in the database, as a runbook step. Kit user records are deleted only after the Townwise path succeeds, so no active seat ever outlives its user and the last-admin rule never counts a missing person. [Build note: the person can still sign in until the manual step, so the runbook first confirms that no `tw_members` row has `activeUserId` equal to the user id (`api/README.md`, Deletion).]
8. **Test helpers are not exported.** The kit’s helpers (`startAuthServer`, `signIn`, `seedTotp`, mail capture, `global-setup.ts`, `images.ts`) live in `api/kit/auth/test/`; the package exports only `./src/index.ts`, and `import-x/no-relative-packages` forbids reaching into it. `seedTotp` also uses internals that are not exported (`createTokenCrypto`, `parseKeyring`, `generateSecret`). Townwise writes its own helpers against the public API (Section 20).

## 20. Tests and verification

Backend gate: from the worktree root, `npm run verify` with no new failures against the first stage’s baseline. `api/package.json` gains a `test` script (vitest), so the root `npm test --workspaces --if-present` runs it. Integration tests use Mongo and Valkey in Docker through testcontainers, as the kit’s do.

**Harness (`api/test/helpers/`).** The kit’s helpers cannot be imported (Section 19, item 8), and `api/src/main.ts` is a top-level-await script, so the tests build the app through `createTownwiseApi` (7.1). The helpers provide:

- `global-setup.ts`, which starts Mongo and Valkey with the same image digests as `compose.yaml`.
- `startTownwiseServer()`, which composes server-core’s `createServer` with `/auth` (the kit’s `createAuth`) and `/api` (`createTownwiseApi`). It passes one shared, mutable test clock as `now` to both, and a capturing `sendMagicLink` (production `email.ts` rejects every magic link). It runs `flushdb` on Valkey per test file, which also resets the kit’s magic-link send limit (`auth:ml-send-ip`, 20 per hour per IP).
- `signIn(email)`, through the kit’s magic-link routes and the captured link, so no fake Google signer and no `jose` is needed.
- `makeStaff(userId, { enabledAt })`, which seeds the factor through the public `TotpStore`: `startEnrollment` with any `secretEnc`, then `confirmEnrollment({ userId, step, recoveryCodeHashes: [], now: enabledAt })`, with `enabledAt` placed before or after the session’s `createdAt`. The resolver reads only `status` and `enabledAt`, so no code is ever generated.
- Command monitoring through a connection opened with `monitorCommands=true` (Section 19, item 5).

Because access tokens last 600 seconds (**Exists**), a test that advances the clock past 10 minutes calls `POST /auth/refresh` before its next `/api` request; otherwise the kit answers 401 before Townwise code runs.

Named tests:

- **Routes:** every Express route on `/api` is in `TOWNWISE_ROUTES`, with no duplicates.
- **Routes:** every GET route issues no write command, checked with Mongo command monitoring. This covers `GET /api/me`, which never joins and never withdraws a request.
- **Routes:** product code answers 401 only from `resolveAccess` when the kit user no longer exists (4.2 step 1), through the one helper `userGone()`.
- **Routes:** a non-GET refused by policy still counts toward `townwise:writes`, and is never body-parsed: a 300 KB body to the upload route from a `no_org` account answers 403, not 413.
- **Access:** each state of 4.2 from fixtures.
- **Access:** an invitation beats a pending request and carries it as `pendingRequest`, and the newer of rejected and removed wins.
- **Access:** a staff email that is also invited resolves as staff, never as member.
- **Join:** five concurrent joins of one invitation leave exactly one active seat.
- **Join:** joining with a different email than the invitation’s is 409 `no_invite`.
- **Join:** a second organization’s join is 409 `already_in_org`.
- **Join:** an invited person with a pending request stays pending until they press Join; “Not my team” deletes only the caller’s own invitation, and the request stays pending.
- **Invitations:** the same email invited by two organizations answers `invited` to both, and the person is offered both.
- **Staff gate:** a session created before `enabledAt` is refused, and one created after is accepted.
- **Staff gate:** after the clock advances 60 minutes and one second and the client calls `POST /auth/refresh`, a staff route answers 403 `staff_reauth_required`.
- **Staff gate:** no factor is `staff_setup_required`, and a member gets `forbidden`, never a staff code.
- **Isolation:** for every `member` and `org_admin` route with an id, organization A presenting organization B’s location, note or member id gets 404, and B is unchanged. The cases are generated from the route table.
- **Isolation:** only `access/resolve.ts`, the join and decline handlers and the staff handlers import `stores/cross-tenant.ts`.
- **View-as:** under a live grant, every non-GET route without the `staff` policy answers 403 `view_as_read_only`. The cases are generated from the route table.
- **View-as:** under a live grant, every route with the `staff` policy, any method, answers 409 `view_as_active`; `view-as/end` is the only staff route excluded. The cases are generated from the route table.
- **View-as:** under a live grant, `POST /api/admin/view-as/end` answers 200, and the next `GET /api/me` is `staff` with `viewAs: null`.
- **View-as:** `end` with a stale staff session answers 403 `staff_reauth_required`.
- **View-as:** a second session of the same staff user has no view-as.
- **View-as:** an expired grant is ignored.
- **View-as:** a grant that expired without End does not block a new Start on the same session.
- **View-as:** view-as ends when the target joins or changes organization.
- **View-as:** the target’s exact access is returned, including Waiting.
- **View-as:** `view_as.started` exists for every grant.
- **Audit:** a staff invite appears in the org admin’s staff activity.
- **Audit:** a staff action whose audit write fails is refused with 503, and nothing changes; a staff role change refused with 409 `last_admin` is followed by `staff_action.not_applied`.
- **Team:** concurrent demotion of the last two admins leaves at least one.
- **Team:** removing the last admin is 409 and the row is restored.
- **Team:** a removed member’s next member request is 403 `no_access`.
- **Uploads:** an extra key in the body or in a day is 400, and nothing is written.
- **Uploads:** a 3,661-day body is 400, and a 257 KB body is 413.
- **Uploads:** replace-by-day counts are right for an org admin.
- **Uploads:** a member upload never changes an existing day, and reports it as `kept`.
- **Uploads:** stored documents have exactly the eight keys of 6.5.
- **Uploads:** a log capture during upload contains no figures.
- **Notes:** range, weekday and kind rules hold.
- **Notes:** a member editing another member’s note is 403.
- **Notes:** `detail` is absent from logs and audit.
- **Deletion:** deleting a person with an active seat is 409 `person_has_seat`; otherwise their requests, invitations and removed seats are gone, and no audit event holds their email.
- **Deletion:** deleting an active organization is 409 `org_not_suspended`; deleting a suspended one leaves no tenant document with its `orgId`, and no audit event holds its name.

## 21. Deferred

| Item | Why it waits | What it needs |
|---|---|---|
| Email for invitations and rejections | D14 sends only request received and you’re in | An owner decision for each; a rejection email would also decide whether it quotes the staff message |
| Calibration, forecasts, model storage | Models exist only in research notebooks | The reserved states and shape (14.3), and `tw_calibrations` |
| AI chat for tuning | The privacy decision about sending client data to an AI provider | That decision, a provider agreement, a redaction step |
| Per-action TOTP for staff | Kit gap 1 | A kit export |
| Hash-chained audit, tenant-guard plugin, ESLint import bans | Heavy for a beta; covered by `OrgScope`, the route table and the generated tests | Revisit with paying customers |
| An org activity log beyond staff activity | Not requested | An org-filtered audit view |
| More than one organization per person | Simplicity (D5) | An organization switcher; organization ids on member routes |
| Native upload, `.xlsx` upload, POS integrations | New dependencies or vendor terms | `expo-document-picker`, a vetted parser, vendor APIs |
| Per-upload undo, a business-day cutoff setting | Not needed for v1 | Per-day history, or a per-location cutoff hour |
| Self-serve deletion of accounts, organizations and data; export; a retention schedule | Privacy decisions pending. Staff deletion on request exists in v1 (D22) | Section 17 decision, then flows and a job |
| Deleting the kit user record in code | The kit has no user delete (Section 19, item 7) | A kit addition; until then, a runbook step |
| An audited staff export of a client’s days for notebook calibration | Waits on the Section 14.1 decision | A `sales.exported` audit event shown in staff activity, and a privacy page line |
| Native charts | No `react-native-svg` (D21) | That dependency, vetted, or a View-based chart |
| Withdrawing or editing a pending request | Staff can fix names at approval | A withdraw action on Waiting |
| Last sign-in times on People | The kit exposes no session listing | A kit addition, or a Townwise `lastSeenAt` |
| Required TOTP for org admins | Friction for owners | [CONFIRM: optional for org admins] |
| Hourly forecasts (P28, D30) | A note’s hours show in its reason, but a timed event changes only the day’s total | [DECISION NEEDED: hourly forecasts. Uploads are daily totals (date, guests, net sales), so Townwise can't say how many guests come during an event's hours; an hourly view needs hourly sales from the owner's POS, a new upload field and a privacy review.] |

## 22. Index of decisions

### 22.1 Lead defaults to confirm

Each is marked inline with “lead default”:

- the three roles (D1);
- staff by `TOWNWISE_SUPERADMIN_EMAILS`, with TOTP for every staff action (D2);
- auto-join for invited emails, Request access for everyone else, and staff approval that creates the organization and its first admin (D3); kept despite the critic’s recommendation of a one-click Join screen for every invitation, which the F1 note explains;
- view-as read-only, audited, bannered, with writes refused by the server (D8);
- browser-side parsing that sends only date, guests and net sales per location per day (D10);
- no fake output (D12);
- tuning as structured notes, AI chat later (D13);
- organizations with one or more locations (D15).

### 22.2 Judgment calls to confirm

1. Per-organization invitations (D4).
2. One organization per person (D5).
3. Auto-join without a click, with Leave as the remedy and the inviter named (F1); a press to join when a request is pending, and “Not my team” to decline (F2b).
4. Role chosen at invite, default member (F5).
5. First location at approval (D6).
6. Town profile while waiting (F2).
7. What “validated manually” means (F3).
8. Rejected people may request again, with an optional message (F4).
9. Staff create organizations directly (F10).

13. Org admins see all staff activity on their organization, with staff emails (D9).
