### 22.3 Decisions needed

- The minimum days of history before calibration (D12, 14.1).
- Whether Waiting states a review time (P4).
- Retention and deletion terms for the privacy page (17, 10.7).
- Whether staff may copy a client’s uploaded days into research notebooks, for that client’s calibration only, and how the copy is recorded, shown to org admins and deleted (14.1).
- What happens to a raw export a client sent directly once that client uploads through the portal (17). Recommended: delete it once its days are in the portal.
- Retention periods for stored files (11A.7). Defaults [CONFIRM]: originals 365 days (lifecycle backstop 400), cleaned copies and reports until the file, its location's sales data or the organization is deleted, never-read drops 30 days, unfinished uploads 24 hours, deleted blobs 7 days in soft delete, storage access logs 365 days.
- What expected guests means on an opening or other note, extra guests or the day's total, before those notes change a forecast; and whether a fewer-guests note with a count lowers it (12, 14.5).
- Hourly forecasts (21, P28).
- Whether business rules should ever be shared across an organization's locations (an organization-wide rule), or stay per location (D31). Today they are per location, as the chat, notes, view-as and deletion are; an owner with several locations repeats a rule.
- [DECISION NEEDED: whether admin-only TownwiseAI tools that act at once ask the person to confirm first] Any member's business rule reaches an org admin's own message (10.16), and `start_calibration` checks only the chatting person's role before it starts a calibration and spends from the monthly budget (D27, D31). Today the model is told to start one only when an org admin asks; the code doesn't ask the admin to confirm.
- Whether TownwiseAI’s weekly rule suggestions should also show in P29’s “Suggested by TownwiseAI” group; they are in P25’s panel only for now (D46).
- Whether a yearly rule suggested from a file should start earlier than the read’s today, so it explains last year’s closed season in the questions; Edit can move Starts back (D46).
- [DECISION NEEDED: whether the restaurant’s own events become a forecast input] A file calendar’s `own_event` label is recorded and changes nothing; a feature would mean `townwise.lab-input/3` and `MODEL_VERSION` v10 (D58).
- [DECISION NEEDED: guest counts from descriptions] A calendar CSV’s descriptions are never read, so a booking’s guest count is not taken from one; an admin can add a count to its note (D58).
- [DECISION NEEDED: updating a file calendar from a newer export] A new export is a new calendar, whose labels are sorted again; the old one is removed by hand (D58).
- [DECISION NEEDED: model reads of big CSVs that are not calendars] Read with TownwiseAI still sends a text file’s first 300,000 characters, and a chat attachment its first 20,000 (D58, 11A.9).
- [Decided (owner, 2026-11-19, of PR #118: “Ship #118 as built”): the outlook's range rule as built in release B ships, though it was chosen after the coverage check had been measured; the R2 fallback (every outlook ratio at least sqrt(lead / 28), no backtest read) and holding release B were the alternatives.] D52 decision 6 set the outlook’s range rule before measuring; the rule first decided failed the check on 2026-11-18, and release B’s build (2026-11-19) replaced it with one chosen after seeing the check (item 160). The check passes unchanged with its control failing, and on 16 held-out seeds only one level-shift history falls under its 65% floor; R2 passes the check too (seeds 0 to 3), with outlook ranges about 15% wider at the median, in log terms, that do not narrow as history grows. Numbers: `forecast-year-outlook` design.md, build notes of 2026-11-19 (D52, 14.6).
- [DECISION NEEDED: automatic reads skipped for budget are not retried when the month resets; a person presses Read with TownwiseAI] (D59, 11A.9).
- [DECISION NEEDED: booking labels on link and Google calendars, whose rows are replaced on refresh (D58 kept labels to file calendars)] (D59 slice 2).
- [DECISION NEEDED: whether repeating events on link and file calendars are expanded so they can answer a closure question] `calendar/ics.ts` counts a repeating event and imports none of its days, so a weekly "Closed" on an iCloud or Outlook link answers nothing; Google expands repeats (D59 slice 5, 10.12).
- [DECISION NEEDED: whether a calendar event that plainly says open answers a likely-closed question] A title like "Open" is rare and close to "Open mic" or "Open bar", and a likely-closed day would still read as closed to D32 without the open-day note (D59 slice 5, 10.12).

### 22.4 Conflicts in existing copy

- The homepage FAQ says the data needed is “what sold, how much, and when”. This spec stores only daily guests and net sales per location. One of them should change.
- The homepage step 02 says “Today: the app has no upload yet.”, and the Privacy page says “The Townwise app has no place to upload sales data yet.” and “That is the whole account record.” All three change when the portal ships.
- The SignIn artboard’s button says “Sign in with Google”. `feature/townwise-web` already says “Continue with Google”, but its sub still says “Your first sign-in creates your account.” (P1).
- The homepage step 03 carries [DECISION NEEDED: confirm step 03 status]. P11 no longer mirrors it: the client’s calibration step carries no StatusTag, whatever the homepage decides.
- More copy on `feature/townwise-web` that becomes false when the portal ships and has to change first:
  - `privacy.tsx`: “We do not keep your name, your photo or the Google token itself.” (false once a request stores `contactName`).
  - `privacy.tsx`, “Where your data lives”: “Account, session, authenticator and email-link records are stored in a MongoDB database.” (the portal adds requests, memberships, locations, sales days, uploads, notes, view-as grants and audit events).
  - `privacy.tsx`, rate limiting: “the server counts requests from each IP address: one limit for the whole service and a tighter one for sign-in” (the portal adds per-account counters).
  - `Home.web.tsx` FAQ: “There is no upload in the app yet.” and “The app has no upload yet.”
  - `security.tsx`, Hosting: “Hosting has not been chosen.” gains the who-has-access facts (17).
- Raw exports sent directly: the privacy page’s “Exports you send us directly” has its own [DECISION NEEDED]; the portal adds the question of what happens to them once the client uploads (22.3).

**2026-11-16, autonomous forecasts (D42).** Owner request of 2026-11-16 (“set this up so it runs autonomously”; OpenSpec change `autonomous-forecasts`): every location of an organization whose forecasts are on keeps a published forecast reaching 91 days past today, refreshed weekly by a background worker with no person starting anything (14.6). Decided: an hourly scheduled job (`caj-townwise-forecasts`, running the worker `api/src/workers/weekly-forecasts.ts`) under a Mongo lease starts one scheduled calibration per changed location a week from 03:00 on Monday in the town, system-paid, at most 3 live and roughly 200 a week, recorded in the new collections `tw_forecast_schedule` (6.25) and `tw_forecast_weeks` (6.26), stopped by `TOWNWISE_WEEKLY_FORECASTS` (18), a staff pause (P21, `POST /api/admin/forecast-schedule`, audited `forecast_schedule.paused` and `.resumed`; each start `calibration.scheduled`) or G1; a baseline engine beside the model, from 230 days on scheduled calibrations only, the current engine sticking unless the other is 0.5 points better; lab input version 2 with the town calendar’s entries (10.15); one set of publish rules for every calibration, with a same-engine tolerance against the streak’s best (a tie publishing, an exception to G2), each engine’s absolute checks, a 25% jump guard and the reasons `refreshed`, `refresh_worse`, `model_not_run`, `biased` and `jump_held` (6.23); runs to today plus 91 days; `calibrated` and `stale` as derived states (14.3); and Home’s Last week showing the published forecast’s error, or the forecast where no guest count is uploaded (P11), Home’s “never a guess” becoming “never an unpublished guess”. Built in phase 1: the forecast route and `get_forecast` read up to 92 days (10.13, a frozen-prefix change, `tuning-chat.md` section 4), with the window’s `accuracy`, each day’s `scored` and each run’s `engine` and the baseline’s label (14.4); `seasonal_baseline` as a model family (6.20); and the client and the staff view accepting the new states, requester and gate reasons. The rest lands in later phases. Owner directive, the same day: every part is on by default (the env switch, and forecasts for every organization, reversing G1, item 94), runs as a background worker, and is tested end to end before anything is pushed; nothing publishes in production until the lab is enabled there. D27, G2, 6.20, 6.23, 10.13, 10.15, 14.2 to 14.4, P11 and P21 carry build notes; D12 and its DECISION NEEDED are unchanged, since a calibration a person starts keeps 595 days. TownwiseAI’s weekly suggestions of notes and rules are the follow-up change `weekly-forecast-suggestions`. Its defaults are CONFIRM index items 83 to 94. Written in `feat/autonomous-forecasts` (openspec change `autonomous-forecasts`).

**2026-11-15, TownwiseAI reads attached PDF, Word and Excel files (D36).** A PDF, Word (.docx) or Excel (.xlsx) file attached to a message is sent as its text, a document titled by its ref after the attachments block, made in the parse thread the file reader uses (`extractAiText`, 11A.9) through `ctx.items.readForModel`: at most 20,000 characters (cut said as for a text file), within that reader's byte caps, never the bytes. The turn waits at most 15 seconds for the shared thread (then the file is listed not read, busy, and its thread never runs; `inThreadSlot` gains that optional wait, which the readers don't use) and gives each file 30 seconds, and the turn's 150-second limit now runs from its claims, so the read counts toward it; every file read of a turn ends 30 seconds before that limit, a message's documents are read one after another (so they never find each other busy; one without the time is listed too much at once), and a tool call runs only while the turn is not stopped. A thread failure lists the file as one that couldn't be opened and logs `townwise.chat_file_read_failed` with the error's type only. A PDF with no text (a scan), a password, a file that can't be opened or one too complex is listed not read with why; old Word and Excel files and ZIPs stay not readable. `read_data_item` reads a picture (an image block in its result), PDF, Word or Excel file again, only while a message on the conversation's path attached it, as its attachment was read; later turns keep a stub, and a re-read marks the turn as one that read a file (`file_turn`); a re-read holds its bytes against the replica's 64 MB, the turn's pictures stay within 7.5 MB, and one without the time left reads nothing and says so. Its description changed, so every conversation's prompt cache and stored thinking blocks are dropped once (release it with the other frozen-prefix changes); the system prompt did not change. `files/items.ts` is the one new importer of `files/parse/ai-text.ts` (`test/isolation.test.ts`). The client's chips read “PDF”, “Word file” and “Excel file”, and an old Word or Excel file's says what to save it as (P25). Privacy: section 17. The privacy page lists nothing by attachment kind, so it is unchanged.

The late-week share still reads Monday weeks.

At a glance gives the busiest and quietest days’ figures in brackets.

Once anyone has joined (D23’s notion), the start asks a reason of 5 to 200 characters, as view-as does (400 `reason_required` without one), stored on the grant and in `open_as_admin.started`, and shown in the staff activity’s Reason column (`openAsAdmin: { reason }`; the summary drops “, to set it up”); P21 asks for it in a dialog. Staff setup (D23) still ends at the first join. P21 shows Open as admin while the organization is active, with one Locations line; the banner and the staff activity intro (P18) drop the setup-only wording. The privacy page and the homepage FAQ have drafted wording awaiting the owner’s approval (17).

**2026-11-15, a driver’s days (P24).** Biggest drivers’ names open each driver’s days under the table (owner request): the effect, each day’s figure against its usual and the change, the event that day and a link to it in the Calendar.

**2026-11-15, bold key figures on Home (P11).** In Home's sentences the key figures are bold, in the text's own font (owner request): Your {Month} in past years (the daily figure and its change), This week, last year's change against usual, Last week's total and change (card and tile), the late-week share, last year's and two years ago's figures and changes in This week, and a day's own figure. Each line is built in parts (`client/src/portal/analytics/phrase.ts`); joined, the parts are the sentence the tests and screen readers read.

**2026-11-15, This week from today (P11).** Home’s This week in {Town} shows the seven days from today, today first, in place of Monday to Sunday (owner request); At a glance’s This week, last year totals the same seven days last year (“Same 7 days last year, …”), This month’s grid marks them as This week, and Who’s in town’s This week group ends with them. Last week, its comparison and the late-week share still read Monday to Sunday.

**2026-11-14, TownwiseAI web search (D37).** While `TOWNWISE_CHAT_WEB_SEARCH` is on (off by default; on in `api/production.env`), every TownwiseAI request sends Anthropic's `web_search_20260209` server tool last, with `max_uses` 3 and direct calls only (`api/src/chat/web-search.ts`). The turn streams each search as a `tool` event named `web_search` with no input (never the query) and `{ pages, sources }` or `{ code }`, resumes `pause_turn` within the 8 calls, runs client tools from a message that also searched, never saves a search without its result, treats text before a search as an aside, strips citations from a declined model's text at a fallback, and refuses `start_calibration` with `web_turn` in any turn whose requests carry a search's results. `done` and every reply entry of the conversation view gain `sources` (the pages the reply cites, at most 10). Each search adds $0.01 to the call's cost. `chat.turn_completed` and the turn's log lines gain `webSearches` (its allowlist in `api/src/stores/audit-events.ts`). The system prompt gains four lines and names public web pages among the kinds of figures, and the switch changes the tools, so each changes every conversation's prompt cache and stored thinking blocks once: release them with the other frozen-prefix changes. Runbook: `infra/README.md` step 16, Web search. Privacy: section 17. The client (P25) shows each search as a card (“Searching the web”, “Searched the web” with its page count and sites, “Couldn’t search the web”, or “Stopped before the search finished”), names “public web pages” in the Based on line, words `web_turn`, and lists a reply's sources under that line; the privacy page gains “Web searches by TownwiseAI.” (section 17).

**2026-11-14, the top bar’s More (D38).** The client app’s top bar keeps Home, Calendar, Orders, Analytics and TownwiseAI and puts Notes, Rules, Town and Your data under one More button (15.2, 15.3): a dropdown over the page on web above 640px, a row under the bar on phones and native. `NavItem.more` marks the four in `clientNav`; no route, page or API changes. 15.3’s open-as-admin row now reads Your data, as the bar has since D28. A browser check at 1280px then found the organization name and the email 19px short, so that bar’s links sit `space-5` apart, not `space-6` (15.2).

**2026-11-14, owner calendars (D33).** A location keeps up to 5 calendars on Townwise’s server, each an imported `.ics` file or a subscription link, with only each event’s title, dates and hours (owner decision, 2026-11-12, issue #10). Five member routes, 10.18 (`org.owner_calendars.*`): the list, the events over a range of at most 92 days, add (a file posted as text and parsed by the API, `api/src/calendar/ics.ts`, which replaces the Calendar’s in-browser parser; or a link, fetched first through the guarded fetch and stored sealed under the new `TOWNWISE_CALENDAR_KEY`), Refresh now and remove. A refresh loop reads each link again about every 6 hours. TownwiseAI reads the events with `get_owner_calendar` and proposes notes from them; events change the forecast only through notes the owner saves. On the Calendar (P28) the header row’s import button and “How importing works” become one “Your calendars (N)” button on web and native whose panel lists the calendars (Refresh now, Remove) and holds the import, Add a link and the help; the stored events are read once per grid and show as “Your calendar”; a failed list or stored-events read leaves the page showing with its own notice; under view-as the panel’s writes are disabled in place; the skeleton’s Row A ends in one 170px block. Section 17 and the privacy page say calendars are kept, links are fetched by Townwise, and titles can reach Anthropic through TownwiseAI. D33 settles 21’s questions on a live link and on keeping an imported calendar. [CONFIRM: 5 calendars per location, a 6 hour refresh, a 60 character name] [CONFIRM: 12 link adds an account an hour]

**2026-11-13, chat attachments (D36).** A message to TownwiseAI may attach up to 5 files of Your data: the turn's `attachments` (10.12), refused before any claim for a file not at the location, a sales file, one still uploading or stored files off. The stored message gains a code-made attachments block (refs and kind words, never a name) after any `business_rules` block, and the files' content (a text file's first 20,000 characters, a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP picture of at most 3.75 MB) goes into that turn's requests only, read through `ctx.items.readForModel` (6.10 rule 9), by the person who added the file or an org admin, after the claim and within 7.5 MB of pictures a message and 64 MB a replica, a picture without its metadata and listed unread over 8,000 pixels a side; a turn that sent content saves no thinking blocks, and no turn that read a file's content (attached, or by `read_data_item`) can start a calibration. Replies write each link's host after it. The conversation view lists each message's files with their name and state (P25). `chat.turn_completed` gains `attachments` (its allowlist in `api/src/stores/audit-events.ts`), and the system prompt gains two lines (attachments, and no link from a file, an attachment or a web page unless the owner asks), so every conversation's prompt cache and stored thinking blocks are dropped once (release it with the other frozen-prefix changes). Privacy: section 17. The composer's chips and the bubble's file chips come in the next stage.

**2026-11-12, reading with TownwiseAI (D34), the read.** A stored file can be let in to TownwiseAI, per file, by the person who added it or an org admin (`POST .../data/:ref/ai`, 10.14). A reader beside the file reader (11A.9) sends it whole to Claude Opus 5.5 (a PDF as a document, a picture as an image, anything else as text cut at 300,000 characters), with the date and time zone and no names, checks the structured answer again and saves it on the file (`tw_files.ai`, 6.11), within the files AI budget. Items show `canAiRead` and `ai`; audit adds `file.ai_read_requested` and `file.ai_read`. 6.10 rules 2, 8 and 9, 11A.4 and 11A.8 carve the opt-in out of “never sent to a model”, which still holds for every file nobody opted in. Acting on the answer comes next.

**2026-11-12, reading with TownwiseAI (D34), the actions.** A done read now acts on its answer (11A.9): events become notes by the person who asked, marked with the file (`tw_notes.source`, 6.7); daily totals the file's own text bears out (95% or more, a picture never) become one upload through the upload rules (`tw_uploads.source`, 6.6); the summary and facts become a reference text item (`tw_files.source`); and an org admin's read that wrote notes or days starts a calibration as them (`via: 'file'`, 6.23). The ids are planned first and saved on the read (`ai.actions`, 6.11), so a retry writes nothing twice. `DELETE .../data/:ref/ai` (10.14) undoes it all but a started calibration. Items gain `fromAiRead` and the filled `ai` fields; notes gain `source`; audit adds `file.ai_undone` and counts on `file.ai_read` (9.2). A ZIP is now read too: up to 20 entries as text, labelled by place, never by path.

**2026-11-13, bar ordering (D35).** Locations get an ordering setup, item sales and counts, and the Orders page (P30) shows one next order per supplier from a TypeScript port of the reorder engine's core, with the owner's edits and rules; Ordering setup (P31) holds the setup, the item sales upload and the count. New: nine `order.*` audit actions, six collections (`tw_order_setups`, `tw_item_sales`, `tw_order_counts`, `tw_order_decisions`, `tw_order_rules`, `tw_order_cards`), the routes of 10.17 (the first `PUT` with a 1 MB body, 10.11), five TownwiseAI tools with their cards (`tuning-chat.md` section 4), Home’s Bar order card (P11) and the Orders item in the top bar (15.3). Item sales are removed with the location’s sales data; the setup, counts, edits and rules are not. Written in PR #68 (`feat/inventory-management`) on top of the research and the first product slice. A browser check on 2026-11-15 found that a saved change showed only in its line’s edit fields while the Order column kept Townwise’s quantity, so the Order column shows the change, the why line names it, and Home’s Bar order counts by it (P30, P11).

**2026-11-12, business rule schedules (D31).** A business rule may carry a schedule, a note's fields but the detail, with an end that may be left empty for no end, checked by the note rules' own code (`readRuleSchedule`, 10.16) and stored as `tw_business_rules.schedule` (6.24). Create and update take `schedule` (null takes it off; PATCH writes only the fields that changed, so racing edits of the text and the schedule both land), and `RuleView` adds `schedule` and `scheduleSummary`. The forecast read applies schedules with the notes, exactly as notes with those fields (14.5), each as a reason `kind: 'rule'` worded from the schedule, never the rule's text; the lab's input reads them as notes (10.15, D32); `get_forecast` and the `business_rules` block carry them (`tuning-chat.md` sections 3 and 4), and the system prompt says only a rule with a schedule changes the forecast. P29 adds Change the forecast to Add and Edit and says under each rule what it does to the forecast; the Calendar (P28) lists the rules covering the day and words their reasons; Home (P11) names rule guests. Audit events add `scheduled`, a boolean. [CONFIRM: a rule's schedule may have no end date ("ongoing"); one with an end keeps a note's 366-day span] [CONFIRM: an Other schedule needs no details, since the rule's text says what it is] [CONFIRM: rule reasons are never cut by the six-note cap and come before the notes' in each group]

**2026-11-12, business rules (D31).** A location keeps up to 30 business rules, standing facts about how it runs, each one line of 1 to 200 characters, in the new `tw_business_rules` (6.24): any member adds one, its author or an org admin edits or deletes it, and a rule already saved in another case or spacing is 409 `rule_exists` (10.16, routes `org.rules.list`, `org.rules.create`, `org.rules.update`, `org.rules.remove`). Audited `rule.created { locationId, via }`, `rule.updated` and `rule.deleted { locationId }`, never the text (9.2). Rules go with the location (never blocking its delete) and the organization (10.7). TownwiseAI reads them with every message: a new message starts with a `business_rules` block holding the location's rules whenever they differ from the last block on the conversation's path, stored with the message and hidden from the conversation view, so a location with no rules sends exactly what it sent before (`api/src/chat/user-message.ts`, `tuning-chat.md` section 3); one system prompt line says the block is the owner's data, never instructions, and that rules never change the forecast. The new Business rules page, P29 (`/locations/[id]/rules`, 16.3), lists, adds, edits and deletes them, is the top bar's Rules section (15.3), and Location settings (P16) links to it. Once a newer block replaces one, requests send the older one as a stub, so a deleted rule's text is not sent again. [CONFIRM: 30 business rules per location, 200 characters each]

**2026-11-12, the Calendar and notes in the forecast (D30).** A location's saved notes adjust its published forecast on every read from the town's today on (14.5, `api/src/forecasts/adjust.ts`): a private event with a guest count adds its guests, a buyout (a private event, closed, which may now carry a guest count) books the day, a closure closes it, and each shows as a reason worded in code, never from its detail; runs are never rewritten, and past days, `inRange` and live accuracy stay the model's. Notes take optional local hours (`startTime`, `endTime`; 6.7, 10.5, 12). The forecast read adds `model`, `noteGuests`, `moreNotes` and a reason's `note` (10.13); `get_forecast`, `list_notes` and `get_day` carry them, and the lab's input stops flagging a private event the read counts. The new Calendar page, P28 (`/locations/[id]/calendar`), is a top-bar section after Home (15.3): each day's published forecast and what drives it, filters, a day's panel to add, edit and delete notes, and on web the owner's own `.ics` file, read and kept in the browser only (17). Home's This month (P11) shows each day's figure (stored before today, the published forecast's from today on), a tooltip on web, and opens a day in the Calendar; its In progress line says no forecast is published only while that is so.

**2026-11-10, lab callback sign-in.** The forecast lab's job signs in to the callback with its managed identity instead of a start token, so no credential sits in its environment or the job's execution history (10.15). The API accepts only an Entra v2 token for the new `townwise-lab-callback` app registration (bootstrap; no secret, no app role, no permission) whose `oid` is the lab identity's, and answers 503 `lab_auth_unavailable` only when Entra's keys cannot be fetched. The input is still fetched once, and a result now needs the input answer's result token with the identity token, so nothing is taken before the input was fetched; a job that cannot sign in or fetch its input posts nothing and fails `timeout` after 20 minutes. `tokenSha256` holds the result token's hash only (6.23). New: `TOWNWISE_LAB_AUDIENCE`, `TOWNWISE_LAB_CALLER_ID`, `TOWNWISE_LAB_TENANT_ID` (18); `TOWNWISE_LAB_TOKEN` is a local job's only. Known risk, deferred by the owner (2026-11-10, re-confirmed 2026-11-11): code running as the lab identity that fetches a sibling calibration's input before that calibration's own job does can read it and post a forged result for it, a published forecast if its scorecard passes the gate and that organization's forecasts are on; no worse than before, since a compromised lab image already runs every calibration and can forge any result it computes (`infra/README.md`, known risks).

**2026-11-10, PR leftovers.** (1) A calibration that publishes a first forecast says what it beat, “Better than the weekday average on its backtest weeks, so Townwise published it.” (`gateWords`, `api/src/lab/gate.ts`, 10.15); one that beat a published model keeps “Better than the current forecast on held-out weeks…”. (2) `GET .../sales` and `.../sales/history` carry `uploadsOff` (10.4, 10.10), true when no day shows because every upload holding days is turned off (D28); Home, Analytics and Sales data then say “Every sales upload for this location is turned off. Turn one back on in Your data to see its days.” instead of “No sales history yet” (P11, P12, P24). (3) `LocationSummary` carries `offDayCount` (also used so Home does not show the history step, P9 says “Uploads turned off” with an Open Your data link, and TownwiseAI’s landing says the uploads are off, when every upload is off) (6.4, 10.1) so the upload check says what happens to days a turned-off upload holds: an org admin’s file replaces those it covers, a member’s leaves them hidden (11.2, 11.4). (4) Keeping text TownwiseAI proposed (`org.chat.item_proposal`) is limited by `townwise:files`, as Paste text is; setting the card aside shares that budget (10.14, Section 10 limits). (5) Owner calls: the 595 days of history before a calibration starts is decided (2026-11-10) and no longer awaits confirmation (D27); open as admin asks staff TownwiseAI’s name question, saved to their own profile, and the Your data page works fully there (8a).

**2026-11-09, forecast lab.** Org admins (TownwiseAI's `start_calibration`, `get_calibration`, `compare_forecast_models`) and staff (the console's Calibrate button) retrain a location's forecast model in an Azure job on the location's own days and notes (D27). The job returns a draft run (`trainingSource: 'townwise_lab'`, 6.20) and a scorecard through two callback routes at `/lab` (10.15), stored in `tw_calibrations` (6.23). The system publishes a draft that passes the gate only for an organization whose forecasts staff have switched on; staff can withdraw it. New: the forecasts switch, the calibration list and start routes, 409 `forecasts_off` on publish (10.7), the `townwise:calibrations` limiter (10.8), actor role `system` and four audit changes (9.2, 9.3), `TOWNWISE_LAB_*` configuration (18), the privacy page's Forecasts paragraph, and the training sentence on the privacy page and in Terms, whose effective date is now November 9, 2026. Person deletion also clears the staff id on an organization's forecasts switch (6.1, 10.7). Calibration status now shows in TownwiseAI and the console (14.2), and the dashboard no longer says calibration isn’t built.

**2026-11-09, Your data.** One page per location, P26 (10.14, D28), lists every upload, stored file and text item. An upload or a reference item can be turned off, which leaves it out of every sales read through one rule on `SalesDayStore` (6.5), or deleted; deleting an upload deletes the days it still holds (org admins). `tw_files` gains `purpose: 'reference'`, `disabledAt`, `disabledBy` and `addedVia` (6.11), `tw_uploads` gains `disabledAt` and `disabledBy` (6.6), and `tw_chat_proposals` gains `kind: 'item'` (6.16). TownwiseAI lists items and reads text items kept for reference through `ctx.items.readText` (6.10 rule 9, 11A.8) and proposes keeping pasted text on a card (10.12). The Upload top-bar section becomes Your data (15.3), and P12’s Uploads table and Your files moved to P26. The privacy page says so before stored files go on (`infra/README.md`, step 18). The chat composer's + adds a file to Your data (P25).

**2026-11-09, TownwiseAI redesign.** P25 becomes a chat page (D26): its h1 greeted the person by the name they gave Townwise (`tw_profiles`, 6.22; `GET` and `PATCH /api/me/profile`, 10.2; asked once on the page and kept in Settings, P18) in place of “TownwiseAI” (15.2) (since 2026-11-11 the greeting is Home's title, the page has no page header and asks for no name); an empty conversation is a centered landing whose composer docks under the thread on the first send; replies are Markdown, with charts, tables and totals Townwise draws from its own data, and end with Copy, Regenerate, Helpful and Not helpful and three suggested next questions; a conversation is a tree, so an edit or a regenerate is a new version with a ‹ n/m › navigator (10.12); and the side column and the phone's three-way switch give way to Questions and activity, a column from 1024px and a sheet below. On this page only the composer, the person's bubbles and the chips are rounded (15.6), and a table in a reply scrolls inside its own region (15.7). **2026-11-09, open as admin (D25).** While an organization is in setup, staff can open its real portal as its admin from its console page (P21, `POST /api/admin/orgs/:orgId/open-as-admin`), with no reason and no timer of its own, and see and change everything an org admin can except people (Team, invitations, roles, leaving, joining). The grant is a second kind in `tw_view_as_grants` (6.8), live only while the organization stays in setup and the staff window lasts, one per session (8a). A route runs in the mode only when the route table marks it (7.2); the rest answer 403 `open_as_admin_refused`, and staff routes 409 `open_as_admin_active`. The start is recorded before the grant exists, the changes after their effect with actor role `superadmin` and the grant id (9.3), and what staff create reads “Townwise staff”. Rename and Add location carry the organization the page shows, and End the grant it shows, so a tab left on an earlier organization never writes into or ends the current one; a grant that expires with the staff window is recorded as ended, at the time it expired, by the next start or End. A suspension ends a grant for good (`lastSuspendedAt`, 6.1), whether or not End was sent; Sign out sends End first; the view-as banner’s End names its grant too; and Settings’ staff activity pages with “Show older staff activity” (10.3), since every change made in the mode is a staff event. D1, D7, D23, Section 3, 4.2, 6.4, 6.6 to 6.11, 10.1, 10.3, 10.7, 10.9, 15.5a, P18’s staff activity line, Section 17, the privacy notice and the homepage FAQ say so.

**2026-11-06, staff setup.** While an organization is active and nobody has ever held a seat in it, staff add, rename and delete its locations and upload or delete their daily totals (D23, F10b), through five staff routes that reuse the org routes’ checks and writes (10.7). Each write is recorded before its effect and shown in the organization’s staff activity once someone joins (9.2, 9.3); answers carry no figure (D7). Approval copies it to the first location. `access_request.created` records only `hasPlace` (9.2). The two Places routes, the `places` limiter and their error codes are in 7.2, 10.2a, 10.8 and 10.9.

**2026-11-04, critic review.** Twenty-three findings applied. Where one conflicted with a lead default, the default stayed and the conflict went into its [CONFIRM] note.

- **Auto-join (F1, D3, F2b, P6).** The lead default stays: one invitation and no pending request still joins on load. The F1 [CONFIRM] now describes the stranger-enrollment attack and the declined alternative (a one-click Join screen for every invitation). Within the default: the inviter is named on `/joining` and in the notice (`invitedBy`); a person with a pending request presses Join, and only then is the request withdrawn; “Not my team” (`POST /api/me/decline`, audit `member.declined`) deletes an invitation.
- **View-as (4.2, 6.8, 7.2, 8, F8).** A grant is live only while the target’s resolved organization equals `grant.orgId`. `resolveAccess` returns `self`, `effective` and the grant. The new `staff_self` policy lets End pass during view-as, while `staff` stays strict. The principal carries the staff actor. Start clears any grant still holding the session, expired or not (`endReason: 'expired'`). The guard answers 409 for staff routes first, then 403 for other writes.
- **Staff activity (D1, D7, D9, 9.3, 10.1, P17, P18, P21).** Org admins see every staff action on their organization, not only view-as. `MemberView.addedByStaff` marks addresses staff added. Staff events are written before the effect and refused on a failed write, with `staff_action.not_applied` when the effect then fails.
- **Request chain (7.2, 10.8).** `townwise:writes` runs right after `requireAuth`. Bodies are parsed only after the guard and the policy pass.
- **Member uploads (D16, 3, 11.2, 11.4, P12, P13).** A member’s upload adds new days only (`$setOnInsert`, counted as `kept`); org admins keep replace-by-day.
- **Deletion (D22, F13, 9.3, 10.7, P21, P22, Section 19 item 7).** Staff delete a person (after removing their seat) or a suspended organization. Each deletes the Townwise records and redacts emails or names in the audit log, which is otherwise still append-only. The kit has no user delete, so the user record is deleted by hand.
- **Honest copy (14.1, P9, P11, P12, P14, 13).** No research-notebook or future-forecast promises. The upload copy says what the upload sends, not what Townwise keeps. Step 03 has no StatusTag. The illustrative block sits under the homepage’s “In development” qualifier. Notes copy says nothing reads them yet. Town progress comes from the bundled data.
- **Privacy (17, 22.3, 22.4).** Says exactly who sees what, including console metadata and Atlas project access, neither of which is recorded. The privacy checklist gains notes, locations, invited addresses, grants and counters. New decisions cover research notebooks and raw exports. 22.4 lists five more sentences on `feature/townwise-web` that become false.
- **Build facts (7.1, 13, 19, 20, D21).** New `api/src/app.ts` with one shared clock. A test harness contract written against the public kit API. A way to stay within the six packages. Named OrgScope mint functions and `stores/cross-tenant.ts`. Town components extracted from `TownPanel.web.tsx`, with charts on web only. Town ids pinned as a literal list on each side. Two tests reworded to match the body (eight sales-day keys; the one 401 from `userGone()`).
